the configured retention periods. [About AI in refiroo](/docs/run/ai/) explains access, costs
and retention in full. Check your organisation's policy before sending a file.

## Describe and review

1. Open the intended workspace. Open its **⋯** menu beside the workspace selector and choose
   **Change this model…**. Check the workspace named in **Change this model**.
2. Enter **What should change?**. Say which types or fields change and what should happen to
   existing records. The field allows up to 4,000 characters. Use **A workbook (optional)**
   to attach an XLSX or CSV file when it helps explain the change.
3. Read the disclosure of what is sent. Choose **Ask the assistant**, or **Cancel** to leave
   without starting a task. Wait on the task page; **Stop** pauses the work without discarding
   the task. Before a proposal exists, the journey bar and trail say **Change with the assistant**
   for a task without a workbook. They become **Change this model** when the proposal changes
   the model, or **Change records** when it leaves the model unchanged.
   For words alone, the task heading gets a short title with the assistant’s first answer;
   any draft it makes is named **Assistant:** followed by that title. Your full instructions
   stay under **You said:** on the proposal. Until the title arrives, including after a stop
   or failure before an answer, the heading uses your words, shortened at a word boundary
   with “…” if needed. With a workbook, the heading keeps the file name.
4. Read **The assistant’s proposal**. Check every type it adds or changes, **Checks**, questions
   and the records that move. For a whole-type move, check both the destination type and the
   number of records. Open **Show the model change**. **No type, attribute or relationship
   changes** does not mean the draft is unchanged: it can still change views or layout. Use
   **Open in the model editor** to inspect those changes. A task without a workbook or a
   model draft instead says **No change to the model.**
   Do not accept merely because the summary sounds plausible.
5. Answer questions and use **Tell the assistant what to change** for corrections. Choose
   **Open in the model editor** to inspect or edit the draft directly. Return to the task;
   the assistant rereads the draft when it continues. For a workbook proposal, inspect
   **What the load does**, open each type's row for examples with source cells, and read any
   repeated-name finding. A draft changed after that check is checked again before loading.
6. For a model-only change or a record move, choose **Accept the model** only when the proposed
   structure and treatment of records are right. **Accept the model** in the journey bar
   takes you to the page’s acceptance button; choose that button to confirm.
   A workbook load showing **What the load does**
   uses **Accept and load to change set**: the engine installs a changed model and loads exactly the checked
   records and relationships into a change set as one batch, without another assistant turn.
   It does not activate or publish. Follow
   [Review the assistant's workbook design](/docs/guide/model/review-an-assistants-workbook-design/)
   for loading, refusals and publication. **Discard this proposal** removes the proposal and its
   draft instead. **Close** keeps the proposal for later.

*Example: a model for transport stops might split a general stop type by a field that distinguishes
bus and rail stops. The instruction should say whether the old type remains and which values
select each new type. These choices belong to the model, not to a built-in transport feature.*

![Change this model dialog with the workspace, instruction and optional workbook](/docs/screens/model-assistant-change-dialog.png)

## Finish a model-only change or a whole-type move

When only the model changes, such as adding a view, acceptance installs a release and prepares
a migration that moves no type. Preview and confirm it as below to put the workspace on the
new model. No change set is created and every record stays as it is.

Whatever you ask the assistant to reshape, all your data comes through: every record, value,
relationship and translation. The only exception is what your own words explicitly ask to
remove. The assistant lists that removal with your words, and the proposal states it in plain
words with the engine's counts before you accept, for example "As you asked, the Drug list is
deleted, deleting 16 records." If the change would lose anything else, the assistant does not
offer it: the task ends with a note naming what would be lost per type, and nothing is changed.

1. For a whole-type move, review the list under **Move the records to the new model** of what
   becomes what, or which application each type moves to when its key stays. The migration
   takes what the draft changes against the workspace's model, together with the moves the
   assistant named. For a model-only change, there are no type moves to review. Accepting has
   installed a release; nothing has moved yet.
2. Choose **Preview the migration**. The migration page opens with the assistant's type choices.
   Follow [Migrate a workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) to inspect converted,
   removed and blocked items. **Back to the proposal** returns to the task.
3. If a mapping is wrong or the engine refuses it, return to the task and use
   **Tell the assistant what to change**. The assistant can revise the model before confirmation.
4. Confirm only the reviewed migration, with **Model release** in this workspace. This changes
   live records and the running release together. There is no change set or separate change-set
   approval for this path. Return to the task to see that the workspace runs the new model.

![Accepted whole-type move with record counts and Preview the migration](/docs/screens/model-assistant-whole-type-move.png)

## Finish a partial move

Before accepting, read how the proposal moves the selected records and what acceptance
prepares: a release with the old types beside the new ones, a change set that moves the
records, and the final release that removes the emptied types. The removal note names the
record moves and their destination types; removing the emptied types does not delete those
records. You do not need to prepare the releases or move the records by hand.

Choose **Accept the model** when this matches your request. Once preparation finishes, the
task links the releases and change set under **Three steps are yours**, with **Next** beside
the available step.

1. Under **1. Add the new types to the workspace**, choose **Open the release**. Activate the
   release holding both the old and new shapes in the intended workspace. No records move.
2. Return to the task. Under **2. Review and publish the change set**, choose
   **Review the change set**. Inspect its record changes and validation, then submit for approval
   and publish according to the workspace's rules. Publication moves the selected records.
3. Return to the task. Under **3. Remove the emptied types**, choose **Open the release** and
   activate the final release. This removes the old types only when they are empty. If new
   records were added to one meanwhile, resolve them and check again.

If the accepted model keeps the old types, **Two steps are yours** omits the removal step.
Someone without **Model release** is told that a holder of that right must activate the release.
A split of thousands of top-level records can take time; avoid starting a duplicate task while
it is working.

![Partial move showing the three steps, with the first complete and review next](/docs/screens/model-assistant-partial-move.png)

## If you cannot continue

Read the reason on the task. A refused migration or next activation is also reported there.
Tell the assistant how to correct the proposal; an explanation cannot waive an engine rule.
After a failure, **Try again as it was** continues without a new instruction. A stopped task
can **Go on as it was**. See [Stop, correct or discard](/docs/model/ai-model-changes/#stop-correct-or-discard)
for what is kept or removed at each stage.

If an action disappears because your permissions changed, ask an administrator to restore the
needed right or give the task link to the person named by the page. An expired or missing task
leads back to the workspaces; start a new task if its proposal is no longer kept. A confirmed
migration has no automatic undo; inspect its history before planning a further model change.

---
title: Change a workspace’s model
description: Choose an installed release and read its data and consumer compatibility checks.
reader: model-admin
---

Choose an installed release for one workspace with **Model release** there. The release must
be usable on this instance. See [Releases](/docs/model/releases/) and [Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/).

1. Open **Settings › Model**, select the model and its **Overview**. Beside the workspace choose
   **Change model…**. Alternatively open a release and choose **Activate in a workspace…**.
2. Check **Workspace** and its current model. Under **Release**, choose the target version.
   Expand another model only if you intend to replace the workspace's definitions with it.
3. Wait for the check and read its result:

   | Result | What to do |
   | --- | --- |
   | Compatible with the workspace's data | No record, value or relationship needs migration. Review the destination before activating. |
   | A migration is needed | The same model's definitions require data changes. Use the offered migration preview. |
   | A different model | The different model does not fit the data unchanged. Review its reasons and the migration preview where available. |
   | A consumer API needs a higher contract version | Correct or version the named contract in a draft before activating. |
   | Could not be checked | Correct the stated failure and check again. This is not a compatible result. |

4. Read the listed open change sets left on the old release and other workspaces left unchanged.
   If compatible, confirm activation. If conversion is needed, use **Preview the migration…**
   and follow [Migrate a workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/).
5. After success, reopen the workspace and inspect its applications. Reload a page reporting a
   model change before editing. A bookmark to a missing application or type shows **Not in this
   model**; choose a collection declared by this workspace's current model.

![Activation dialog selecting a release for one workspace](/docs/screens/model-release-activate-dialog.png)

**Not activated** means the switch failed. Read why, refresh the workspace and check again.
Choosing an older version runs the same checks; it does not restore older record values.


## Check which consumer versions stay available

Compare the target release with the workspace’s current contract, including any earlier
versions it serves. A higher current number does not itself prove every existing consumer
can continue: the target release must retain the earlier definitions. An older installed
release or publication does not keep their live routes available.

A finding ending **a kept version is served as it was: restore it, or stop serving it**
means an earlier contract would read differently. Prepare a corrected draft that restores
that definition and its sources, or coordinate stopping it, then install a new release.
Raising the current contract again does not repair the retained version.

The activation dialog shows blocking consumer differences, and a warning when an earlier
version **stops serving**, naming the version and that its consumers get
`CONTRACT_VERSION_NOT_FOUND`. Agree that removal with all consuming teams
before activating. That version’s reads and feed stop. Webhooks bound to
it can suspend; the integration administrator must check the receiver before resuming on
the current contract. If the version remains retained, its consumers and webhooks continue
in its own shape. A **Sunset day** announces an end but never stops service automatically.

To change which versions the target release retains, use
[Raise a contract version](/docs/guide/model/raise-a-contract-version/) or
[Stop serving an earlier contract version](/docs/guide/model/stop-serving-an-earlier-contract-version/)
in a draft. Releases themselves are immutable. **Cancel** leaves the workspace on its
current release; a draft undo does not reverse an activation already completed.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/check:
---
title: Check a workbook with a dry run
description: Read each source’s predicted changes and inspect refused rows before loading.
reader: model-admin
---

A dry run reads every mapped row without writing records. Model validity and row acceptance
are separate checks. Open a workbook draft with **Model authoring** and see
[Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/#issues-and-the-dry-run-answer-different-questions)
and [Issues and dry runs](/docs/model/issues-and-dry-run/) for the different results.

1. Expand **Issues, history and dry run**. Resolve blocking **Issues** in the model or profile
   first, then choose **Dry run**.
2. Check the draft version and comparison workspace. Wait for **Checking…** to finish.
   **Checked** is a completed check; **Failed** or **Stopped** is not. Read any failure and
   correct its cause before retrying or making the next mapping change.
3. Open each source tab. Read records created or updated, values, relationships, related
   records created and refused rows. These are different units, so do not add them as a row total.
4. Select a figure to inspect the rows behind it. Open the refused-row figure to read sheet,
   row number and reason. Correct an unresolved reference, wrong type or missing required value
   at its source or in the mapping. A valid draft can still refuse source rows.
5. After editing, wait for the new check. **was** compares with the previous result; it is not
   a count from an actual import. Use the result for the current draft version.
6. Account for every source and any remaining refusal before
   [loading into a change set](/docs/guide/model/load-a-workbook-into-a-change-set/).

![Dry run showing per-source predicted records, values and relationships](/docs/screens/use-wb-dry-run.png)

![Refused workbook rows with their sheet positions and reasons](/docs/screens/use-wb-dry-refused.png)

The eventual load can meet newer records or different workspace data. Review its actual result
and change set too; a dry run is neither an import nor a publication.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/choos:
---
title: Choose table columns, filters and sort
description: Choose a table's fields, related-record columns, available filters and initial order.
reader: model-admin
---

Choose what a type's table shows and how it starts when people open it. You need
**Model authoring** and an open draft. The choices become the table's model defaults after
activation; they do not change stored records or save one person's search.

See [Record pages and tables](/docs/model/record-pages-and-tables/) for how table columns
differ from the columns inside a record-page panel.

## Open the table layout

1. Select a type in the model editor and choose **Preview**, then **Edit layout**.
2. Choose **Table**. If there is more than one table view, use **View** to select it.
3. Check that you have a declared table view to arrange. **The draft declares no table view**
   means there is none for this type. Return to the application and use **Add a view…**,
   **Table: the records of one type in rows** to [add one](/docs/guide/model/add-a-view/).

![Table layout with column frames and the Columns, Filters and Default sort controls](/docs/screens/model-layout-table-tab.png)

If the draft is invalid, use **Show issues** and correct the definitions before opening
the layout. Follow [Preview a type](/docs/guide/model/preview-a-type/) for the workspace and
record choices.

## Choose columns, including fields of related records

1. Choose **Columns…**. The dialog lists **Name**, the type's fields and its relationships,
   including its parent relationship where applicable. Check the columns you want to show.
2. Check a relationship to show the names of related records as a column. To show one of
   their fields, open **Fields of** followed by the relationship's name beneath that choice.
   Opening the list does not select the relationship or its fields.
3. Select a field of the related records. Each checked field becomes a separate column;
   you can keep the relationship's name column as well, or leave it unchecked.
4. To show information from a containing record, look under **Where they sit ·** followed
   by a type's name. Choose its **Name** or one of its fields. These choices include types
   further up the related records' hierarchy. Fields holding JSON are not offered here.
5. Choose **Apply**. Check the resulting column frames. A field column's heading combines
   the relationship name and the field label. Its cells show the related records' values,
   with **—** where a related record has no value. These columns cannot sort.
6. Reorder frames by their grips, or open a column's menu and use **Move left** or
   **Move right**. **Remove column** takes it out of this view without deleting any values.

![Table Columns dialog with Has name translation unfolded and Language code selected](/docs/screens/model-table-columns-related-fields.png)

Above: the Stops table in the guide's Graubünden model. **Fields of Has name translation**
shows the translation fields and **Where they sit · Language**. Selecting **Language code**
adds **Has name translation · Language code**, showing the language of each related translation.

These choices read fields of records at the other end, or of their containing records.
Fields stored on the relationship itself cannot be columns. If you need the containing
record's name inside a record-page panel, use that panel's
[Columns… menu](/docs/guide/model/edit-a-record-page/#choose-a-panels-columns-and-sort).

## Choose available filters

1. Choose **Filters…** and select the fields and relationships people may filter by.
   Choose the relationship itself to offer a relationship filter. The dialog does not unfold
   its fields: a related-field column does not provide a filter on that field.
2. Choose **Apply** and check the selection. This defines available filters; it does not
   restrict everyone's table to particular values. In the live table, a relationship filter
   can find records linked to selected records, linked to any record, or with no link.

Keep at least one column and one filter field. An ordinary field must allow filtering and
must not hold JSON. If **Not applied** appears, read its reason, adjust the choices and apply
again; a refused step changes nothing.

## Choose how the table marks inactive records

1. In the **Table** layout, choose **Inactive records…**, beside **Filters…** and
   **Sort menu and page size…**. The dialog is titled **Inactive records of** followed by
   the view's name.
2. Under **A record is inactive when this is No**, select a Yes/No field of this record type.
   Choose **None** if this table should have no inactive mark or switch. If the field you
   need is missing, check that it belongs to this type and is Yes/No. A field of another
   type, or a field with another kind of value, is refused for this setting.
3. Choose **Apply**. This saves a draft step; it does not change any record's value or make
   a read-only field editable. The field does not need to be selected in **Filters…**.
   If **Not applied** appears, read the reason, correct the choice and apply again. Use
   **Undo** to reverse an unwanted draft step.
4. Review **Issues** before [installing and activating the release](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/).
   In the active table, records with **No** stay in their usual order with a quieter name
   and a grey **Inactive** pill if the field is called Active. For another field name,
   the pill says **Not** followed by that name in lower case. Records with no value have
   no inactive mark.
5. Check **Hide inactive (N)** beside **Filter**. It starts off unless the page address
   already applies its filter. Turn it on and check the added pill, such as **Active: not No**:
   only marked records disappear, and records with no value stay visible. Turn it off or
   remove the pill to restore the results. The number counts **No** values after the list's
   search and other filters, including **0** when none match. Choosing **Yes** in the ordinary
   **＋ Filter** menu instead excludes records with no value; it does not turn this switch on.

The setting belongs to the selected table view. The same mark and switch use a change set's
or publication's own values; publications remain read-only. See
[Mark inactive records in a table](/docs/model/record-pages-and-tables/#mark-inactive-records-in-a-table)
for the rules and [Lists, search and filters](/docs/use/lists-and-filters/#show-or-hide-inactive-records)
for the reader's controls.

## Set the initial order and check the table

1. Choose **Default sort**, whose control shows the current field and direction arrow.
2. Select **Sorted by** from the view's allowed sort fields. Check **Descending** to reverse
   the order. Related-field columns cannot be chosen as the initial sort.
3. Choose **Apply** and check the arrow on the control.
4. Return to preview and inspect real records, including ones with several related records
   and ones with none. An empty table explains what it will show; it does not mean the view
   is broken. Use **Undo** for an unwanted step and review **Issues** before
   [installing and activating the release](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/).

![Table default sort dialog with Sorted by and Descending choices](/docs/screens/model-layout-sort-dialog.png)

People continue to see the active layout until activation. Tree and mapping-grid settings are
in the application’s view menu; see [Add a view](/docs/guide/model/add-a-view/).

## Set the sort menu and reading size

1. In the Table layout, choose **Sort menu and page size…**.
2. Select **Fields a reader can sort by**. Name, existing choices and attributes marked
   Sortable are offered. To add another attribute, first enable Sortable on its shared
   definition. Ordinary field columns can still sort from their headers.
3. Keep at least one choice. If the current default is removed, the first selected field
   becomes the default; if you uncheck everything, the current list is retained.
4. Choose **Rows on a page** and **Apply**. The choices are 10, 20, 25, 50 and 100, plus an
   existing different size. This is the amount read at once, not a total-result limit.
5. Review **Default sort** again, and check the preview and Issues before activation.

![Table Sort menu and page size dialog](/docs/screens/model-table-menu-size.png)

---
title: Choose what moves
description: Select mapped types, filtered types, a whole workspace or a contained branch for a dry run.
reader: model-admin
---

Open a mapping for the source and target workspaces. Choose **Copy** to keep source data or
**Move** to also prepare source deletions. See [Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/).

1. Check the source and target, then choose **Change…** beside **What to copy** or **What to move**.
2. Under **Records**, choose the scope:

   | Choice | What it includes |
   | --- | --- |
   | Every mapped type | Records of each source type the mapping handles. |
   | The whole workspace | All source types, with excluded types reported as not copied or moved. |
   | Chosen types | Selected types and, where set, only records matching their filters. |
   | One record and everything under it | A starting record and all its contained descendants. |

3. For **Chosen types**, tick the types and review their filters. For a branch, set **Type
   of the record**, then find **The record** in the source workspace. A similar name elsewhere
   does not identify the same branch.
4. Choose **Dry run this selection**. Cancel keeps the previous selection. Wait for the fresh
   report and inspect creates, updates, records refused and relationships carried or dropped.
5. Open **What cannot be copied** or **What cannot move** for reasons and affected items. A
   relationship whose target cannot be resolved may be dropped even if a record can go.
   Inspect **Values not carried** too. Correct the mapping or deliberately narrow the scope.

![Selection dialog with type, whole-workspace and contained-branch options](/docs/screens/model-mapping-selection-dialog.png)

Changing the selection runs the check again. Nothing eligible prevents starting. When ready,
follow [Move records to another model](/docs/guide/model/move-records-to-another-model/) for
confirmation and publication of the resulting change sets.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/compa:
---
title: Compare releases
description: Choose a baseline and read the definitions added, changed or removed in an installed release.
reader: model-admin
---

Open **Settings › Model**, select a model, **Releases**, then the release to inspect.
See [Releases](/docs/model/releases/) for immutable definitions and permissions.

1. In **Release history**, find **Changes in this release**. Read **Before** and **After**;
   After is the open release. The suggested predecessor comes from activation history or the
   earlier installed release. It is not necessarily the workspace you currently have open.
2. Use **Compare with** to choose another baseline. A comparison may cross model families,
   so check both names and versions rather than assuming they share a lineage.
3. Read the changes table's **Kind**, **Path**, **Before** and **After**. These describe model
   definitions, not a history of record edits. Inspect removals as well as additions.
4. **No semantic changes** means the two documents define the same model. **No earlier release**
   means no predecessor is available; select another baseline if offered.
5. If **Comparison unavailable** names an unsupported model language, choose another release.
   Its metadata and **Export JSON** remain available for specialist inspection. A loading or
   failed comparison is not an empty comparison.

![Release history with baseline selector and semantic before and after changes](/docs/screens/model-release-compare.png)

The separate **Activation check** reads each workspace's data. A small or empty comparison alone
does not establish that activation in a chosen workspace is safe.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/creat:
---
title: Create a model draft
description: Start editable model work from an installed release or an empty model.
reader: model-admin
---

Create a draft to shape definitions without changing a workspace yet. You need **Model authoring**.
Read [Models](/docs/model/models/) for the difference between a draft, release and activation.

## Start from a release or an empty model

1. Open **Settings**, then **Model**. Find the model you intend to extend. Check which workspace
   runs it; another workspace may use a different model.
2. Choose **New draft**. Enter a **Draft name** that identifies the work rather than an installed
   version. The draft name can differ from the model's name.
3. For **Starting document**, choose **Installed release** to retain its applications, types and
   views, then select the intended **Base release**. Choose **Empty model** for a new model with
   no applications or types. An empty draft needs those elements added before people can use it.
4. Choose **Create draft**. Wait for the editor and check its name, base release and version in
   the header. If creation is refused, read the reason and correct the named problem. A missing
   base release or empty draft name prevents creation. **Cancel** closes the dialog without
   creating a draft.

![Create draft dialog with a name, starting document and base release](/docs/screens/model-draft-new-dialog.png)

*Above: Guide draft is named and an installed Graubünden release is selected. This captured dialog
was cancelled; it did not create a draft.*

From a model's overview, **New draft from** its release starts the same flow. On an installed
release's own page, use **Create draft from release**. On **Drafts**, select a saved draft to
continue existing work instead of creating another.

## Start from a workspace

1. Open **Settings**, **Workspaces**, then the workspace you intend to change.
2. On **Overview**, check **Model**, then choose **Edit model**. This opens its existing current
   draft where one is available, or prepares one from its running release.
3. Check **Applies to** in the editor header. Its main action is **Apply to this workspace…**;
   opening the editor has not applied anything.

![Workspace model editor identifying the workspace it applies to](/docs/screens/model-workspace-edit-model.png)

*Above: Guide draft applies to Graubünden and offers Apply to this workspace….*

This route needs model authoring and release access for that workspace. If it is unavailable,
ask an administrator to check access and whether the workspace is retired.

## Continue the draft

Choose an application or type in the model pane, or add one with the plus button. Follow
[Add a record type and fields](/docs/guide/model/add-a-record-type-and-fields/).
**Close** leaves the saved draft available for later; it does not discard your work or activate it.

If the starting material is a spreadsheet, choose **New from a workbook** instead and follow
[Load a workbook](/docs/guide/model/start-a-draft-from-a-workbook/). That guide covers the source and proposals.

For an existing model document, choose **Import JSON** under **Starting document**. A specialist
model author can paste it in **JSON document** or use **Or choose a JSON file**, then create the
draft. Read validation issues before installing; importing does not activate it. For ordinary
changes, starting from a release and using the model editor keeps the work in named controls.

---
title: Create a workspace
description: Create an empty dataset and choose its installed model release.
reader: model-admin
---

You need **Workspace administration** and workspace administration enabled on the instance.
See [Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/) for permissions and lifecycle.

1. Open **Settings › Workspaces**. Search for the intended dataset before creating another.
   Choose **New workspace**.
2. Enter **Name** and review **Key**. The suggested key follows the name until you edit it.
   Use lowercase letters and digits separated by single hyphens. The key is permanent and
   identifies this workspace in links; renaming later does not change it.
3. Under **Model**, choose **The default workspace’s model** or **Another installed release**.
   For the latter choose **Installed release** and check the model name and version. The
   picker initially shows each model's newest usable release; reveal older versions if needed.
4. Confirm creation. The new workspace starts empty. It copies the selected definitions,
   not the default workspace's records, change sets or publications. Changing the default
   workspace later does not change this workspace's selected release.
5. Check its **Overview**, model and applications. Use **Open workspace** to browse its data.
   Arrange data access separately; workspace creation does not grant every person access.
   To start an empty hierarchy, open its tree view and choose **Add …** for its top-level
   type. Create that record first, then add children beneath it; see
   [Arrange records in a tree](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/#add-the-first-top-level-record).

![New workspace dialog showing name, key and model choice](/docs/screens/workspaces-new-dialog.png)

**The workspace was not created** explains a refusal, such as a duplicate key or unusable release.
Correct that cause before retrying. **Cancel** leaves the list unchanged.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/defin:
---
title: Define a consumer API
description: Choose what other systems read and review how each editor choice changes their answers.
reader: model-admin
---

Define a consumer API when another system needs an agreed view of your workspace's data.
Open a model draft with **Model authoring** and agree the required information with the
consuming team. You choose the public record shape, the operations and the filters;
a security administrator separately grants a client access in each workspace.

See [Consumer APIs in the model](/docs/model/consumer-apis/) for the rules. The marked
examples below use the reference Stops API. They explain the result of your choices; the integrator’s request examples are linked separately.

## Choose the records and their public shape

1. Select **Consumer APIs** in the model pane, then the add button's **Consumer API…**.
   Enter **Name**, review **Key** and choose **Types to expose**. A blank key is made from
   the name. Create the API. The initial definition includes identifiers, names, attached
   attributes, Get by ID and a list per type. Inspect these starting choices before sharing
   the contract: exposing a type does not mean every attached field belongs in a public API.
2. On **Types and related**, inspect each type's public name. Use **Expose a type…** to add
   another type. Consumers receive that public name as the object's type. Choose only the
   types they need as business objects; related blocks can carry information from other
   types without exposing those records as business objects in their own right.
3. On **Fields**, open **Parent, path and hierarchy…** if consumers need containment information. The
   parent is the immediate containing record; a path or hierarchy names ancestors from
   the root down, excluding the current record. Review those outputs as part of the contract.
4. Use **Add related…** to include information reached through a relationship. Set
   **Output name**, **Via** and **Fields**. Each related field pairs a public name with a
   value on the related record. Check the relationship's direction and whether it serves
   one record or several: the answer is respectively an object or an array. A missing
   relationship gives null or an empty array, rather than an invented related record. The
   field picker's group **Attributes of the relationship** lists the values stored on the
   relationship itself, when the relation's binding carries any. Give each selected value a
   public output name and check its served type in **Schema**. A connection without that value
   answers null; the same value can differ on two connections to the same related record.
5. To add these values to an existing block, use its **Fields…** and select from **Attributes
   of the relationship**. If the group is empty, review **Via** and the pair's **Carries** in
   [Add a relationship](/docs/guide/model/add-a-relationship/#choose-what-each-relationship-carries).
   Do not add connection values to the main object's Fields: they need the related block's context.

![New consumer API dialog with name, key and types to expose](/docs/screens/model-consumer-add-dialog.png)

Above: creating a consumer API in the reference model.

**Example result.** Stops API exposes Stop, Municipality, Operator and Mode. Its Stop
object includes an `operator` object and a `modes` array. The parent names the municipality;
the path is `Graubünden/Plessur/Chur` for the Chur stop. These are outputs chosen in
**Types and related** and **Fields**, not extra records copied into the stop. Compare the
[complete business object](/docs/model/consumer-apis/#the-business-object-consumers-read).

![Related-block field picker with the Attributes of the relationship group and selected outputs](/docs/screens/model-consumer-relationship-field-picker.png)

*Above: Stops API’s Add related dialog in a reference-model draft, with output operatorLinks
and Operated by (forward), from Stop to Operator. The fields are name, localName and isPrimary.
The open source list for isPrimary separates Built in, Attributes of the exposed types and
Attributes of the relationship. Primary contact is selected beside the Local name and
Inspected on choices. This dialog has not been applied.*

## Add values and related records to the parent

Use this when a consumer needs the containing record's values alongside each child. For
example, a catalogue item can return its category's approval flag and external codes. This
avoids a second read, but a parent's related block repeats for every child in a list.

1. On **Fields**, choose **Parent, path and hierarchy…**, select **Serve the parent
   (objectType, id, code, name)** and apply the choice. The **Parent** section appears below
   the object's fields. If it is already served, open that section directly.
2. Review the parent's **Output name**. Select **Fields**, or choose **Parent fields…**,
   to open **Fields of the parent**. Each row pairs a public name with the source it reads.
   Choose built-in values or attributes from **Attributes of the parent types** and review
   the proposed camelCase name. Edit that name if consumers need another one, then apply.
   The Parent table shows name=source where they differ. These sources belong to types that
   directly contain exposed records, rather than to the child. A missing or unbound value
   answers null unless a default supplies a value; with no parent, the whole output is null.
   Existing short lists remain valid: built-in fields keep their role's output name, and
   other sources become camelCase words, such as categoryCode for category-code. Editing
   writes the parent fields out with explicit output names.
3. Under **Parent's related records**, choose **Add related**, or open the consumer API's
   ⋯ menu and choose **Add related to the parent…** to open the same dialog. Give the block an **Output
   name**, choose **Via**, and select **Fields**, including their public output names.
   The offered relationships start from the possible parent types. Apply and inspect the
   new row. Its block sits inside the parent's answer; do not add a parent prefix to its
   output name here.
4. In **Served**, choose **Always** to return that block in ordinary answers, or **On request**
   to return it only when a consumer asks. You can also set Served in the add dialog.
   The related table on **Types and related** has the same choices for the object's blocks.
   Use **Fields** on a parent block to adjust what it shows.
5. Open **Operations**. If any block is on request, **Include** shows the accepted choices,
   with the parent's blocks distinguished by a parent prefix. This list is generated from
   Served; there is nothing to enter here. Share it with the consuming team. An omitted
   block is absent, rather than null or an empty list; when requested it uses the usual
   object-or-list shape.
6. To filter through the parent's block, open **Filters**, choose **Add filter…**, set
   **Verb** to **On related**, and select the parent's entry in **Related block**. Choose
   **Name** and **Matches on**. Select **Keep only matching records** if children whose
   parent has no matching item should disappear. Leave it clear to trim only the block.
   The filter still works when the block is not requested. Leave **Crosswalk** clear:
   a parent's block cannot be a crosswalk target. The parameter used by Include is
   reserved for requesting blocks; choose a different filter name.
7. Review **Issues**, **Schema**, **Message example** and compatibility. The parent has
   one level; another parent, path or hierarchy cannot be added inside it. Values from the
   parent's ancestors are supported through specialist editing, rather than new choices
   in the parent field picker. An invalid field or relationship must be corrected before
   activation. Changing **Always** to **On request** on a released block needs a higher
   contract version because the block leaves the ordinary answer.

![Consumer API Operations tab with Include choices for an object block and a parent block](/docs/screens/model-consumer-include.png)

The Include list is generated from the two related tables' **Served** choices.
See [the parent's rules](/docs/model/consumer-apis/#the-parent-can-carry-its-own-values) and
[requests with optional blocks](/docs/integrate/reading-business-objects/#ask-for-a-related-block)
when reviewing the contract with integrators.

## Choose the fields and fallbacks

1. On **Fields**, inspect **Output name**, **Role**, **Sources (first non-empty)**,
   **Served type** and **Default**. Output names are the names consumers receive;
   sources are where their values come from. Use **Add field…** to add a public field.
2. Use **Sources…** on an existing field to order its fallbacks. The first non-empty
   value wins. Zero and false count as values. **Move up** and **Move down** order
   supported items; **Remove** takes an item out.
3. Choose **Role** for an identity, code, name or validity output where needed. The identity
   reads the record's stable ID. Keep any business identifier as a separate field. Check
   **Served type** after changing sources; incompatible types or conflicting roles appear
   in **Issues** and need correction.
4. Select an editable **Default** cell to provide a fallback only when all sources have
   no value. Save the value or cancel. Use the served type: a text fallback cannot stand
   in for a number. A default changes the consumer answer, not the stored record.

![Public field dialog with output name, sources and role](/docs/screens/model-consumer-add-field.png)

Above: adding a public field to a consumer API in the reference model.

**Reference-data example:** the code field tries the stop identifier, then the operator code, then the mode code. Chur’s stop shows its stop identifier while its operator shows SBB. The stop number is an integer. A default abbreviation applies only to a record without one; Chur’s existing CH takes precedence. See [Sources and defaults](/docs/model/consumer-apis/#sources-and-defaults).

## Offer the operations and filters

1. On **Operations**, review **Get by ID**, **XREF** and **Resolve**. Get by ID reads a
   stable record ID; XREF matches values such as a code or name. Resolve performs many
   such reads in a batch and needs both Get by ID and XREF. Leave off operations the
   contract does not need: consumers cannot use an undeclared operation.
2. Use **Add list…** and set **Key**, **Of**, **Within the filter** and **Sorted by**.
   **Of** selects a type; sorting selects its order. None for Within gives the list no
   special parent parameter. With an Under filter, a consumer can supply a parent ID to
   list records below it. Omitting that parameter still returns the whole type.
3. Enable XREF if needed, then use **Add XREF rule…**. Review the fields with
   **Matches on…** and **Fields…** where offered. **Exact** and **Contains** are numeric
   weights, not mutually exclusive modes. Give reliable identifiers stronger weights
   than broad name fragments. Contains applies to text terms of at least three characters.
4. Use **Add a match through a related block…** when related data should help identify an
   exposed record. Review **Also match through**, **First of** and **Prefers**. A match
   through a system code can identify its owning record; a shared code can identify several.
   Use that row’s **Preferred types…**, select **Prefer records of these types**, and Apply
   to prefer exposed owner types; select none to remove the preference. Review ties with the
   consuming team rather than relying on the first result.
5. On **Filters**, choose **Add filter…**, **Name** and **Verb**. **By type** selects types;
   **Under** reads containment; **Linked to** selects **Through**; **On related** selects
   **Related block**. Review **Matches on** and the offered **Options**. **Keep only
   matching records** narrows the returned records. A related filter also narrows the
   related block's items; **Score only matching items** limits which items contribute
   lookup scores. **Crosswalk** lets consumers ask for a target representation from
   that block. Enable only the choices the contract needs.
6. For a filter on connection values, use **On related**, choose the block, then **Matches on…**
   and a field under **Attributes of the relationship**. Keep only matching records if objects
   without a matching connection should disappear too. To score a carried value instead, use
   a text attribute in the related match's **First of**. Review **Schema** and **Message example**:
   only the connection with that value supplies a match, even when other records share its target.

![Filter dialog with verb-specific matching options](/docs/screens/model-consumer-add-filter.png)

Above: adding a filter to a consumer API in the reference model.

**Reference-data example:** the all-stops list can use an ordinary municipality filter to match Chur’s FSO number 3901. The stops list uses that filter name as its special parent scope and requires the municipality’s stable identity. Omitting the parent selection returns all stops. Review this distinction with the consuming team.

The stop number Exact rule scores Chur at 900 for its number 8509000. Matching Q663869 through its Wikidata system code instead scores 90. A tied top score stays ambiguous. The mode filter can further restrict results to Train. See [Lookups and batch answers](/docs/model/consumer-apis/#lookups-and-batch-answers) for how these choices fit together.

## Define notifications and review the contract

1. If every exposed type needs standard notifications for creation, update and deletion,
   enable **Events per type**. For a named event, use **Add custom event…**, then choose
   **Key**, **Types**, **Changes** and **Watches**. No Watches means any change to what
   consumers read, including related blocks. To report edits of carried values, include their
   related block in Watches and expose those values in the block. The reference event watches
   only main fields; it needs this extra choice to report connection-value changes.
   To report changes to the parent's selected values or related items, watch the parent
   output or leave Watches empty. One parent edit can update every child that shows it.
   Full event and webhook objects omit on-request blocks; notifications have no Include choice.
   This defines an event, not a delivery subscription.
2. Use **Describe…** to explain the API's purpose to consuming teams. Review **Issues**,
   **Schema**, **Message example** and the compatibility result. A **Not applied** notice
   means the attempted step was refused: correct its named problem, then review again.
   Specialist editing does not bypass validation.
3. If the editor says **Needs contract version …**, inspect the contract changes and
   [raise the contract version](/docs/guide/model/raise-a-contract-version/). The contract
   version is separate from the model release version. Renaming a public field, changing
   a related block's shape, removing an operation or reducing event coverage can require
   a higher version.
4. [Review and share the generated documents](/docs/guide/model/see-a-consumer-apis-documents/)
   before installing and activating the release. Draft edits do not change the live API.
   Agree changes with integrators and ask a security administrator to grant the consuming
   client this API in the workspaces it needs. Model authoring and other roles do not
   substitute for that grant.

**Reference-data example:** the reference notification watches code, name and validity dates. A name change produces an update naming the affected name output; changing latitude alone does not. See
[the event example](/docs/model/consumer-apis/#events-describe-changes-to-the-output).
The reference contract is version 1. When a draft based on its released definition raises it to 2, the editor keeps version 1 in **Earlier versions** by default. After activation both read current data, each in its own shape. Check the retained row and agree the changeover with consumers; see [Raise a contract version](/docs/guide/model/raise-a-contract-version/).

## Plan the earlier version’s lifetime

On **Types and related**, review **Earlier versions** after raising a released contract.
The editor keeps the base release’s definition even if you made breaking edits before raising;
it does not keep an unserved draft version. Review **Superseded** and optionally edit
**Sunset day** to announce an agreed end. Every retained version must still have the model
sources it reads. Keep those types, fields and relationships while its consumers need them.

The model administrator chooses the notice period. A sunset day does not stop service.
When the consuming teams are ready, follow
[Stop serving an earlier contract version](/docs/guide/model/stop-serving-an-earlier-contract-version/)
to remove the row, review the warning and activate the change. **Undo** restores a removal
in the draft; it does not reverse an already activated release.

## Refine a released API safely

Turning XREF off can ask **Stop offering XREF?** because its rules are removed and Resolve
stops too. Cancel to retain them, or confirm and inspect the contract difference. **Undo**
restores the step; switching XREF on again alone does not restore the old match rules.

Use **Rename…** for a display-name change. A new API shows **Key editable**; a released API
shows **Released: a new key moves its address**. Its key is the access point consumers
already use. **Change key…** is still offered, but after activation the old address answers
404, as if the API were removed, and the contract check warns about it. Removing the API
stops those reads after activation too. Coordinate any deliberate replacement and its access
grants with the consuming team.

*Source for the reference examples: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0.*

To remove an entire contract, choose **Remove consumer API**, read the warning and confirm
only when consumers are ready to lose that access after activation. Cancel keeps it. Undo
restores a saved draft removal. **Edit as JSON…** is a specialist alternative on the whole
API or an individual row; it saves one step and still needs validation and contract review.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/delet:
---
title: Delete a draft
description: Remove an editable draft while keeping installed releases.
reader: model-admin
---

Delete a draft only when its saved design work and attached source are no longer needed.
You need **Model authoring**. See [Models](/docs/model/models/) for the distinction between a draft and a release.

1. Open the draft and inspect **About this draft** and **History** to identify it. If you need
   a copy of its model document, use **JSON**, then **Export JSON**, before deleting.
2. In the editor's **More actions** menu choose **Delete draft…**.
3. Read **Delete this draft?**. This removes the editable draft, its proposals, history and
   attached workbook. Installed releases are not changed. Choose **Cancel** to keep it.
4. Confirm deletion only for the intended draft. Return to **Settings › Model** and check the
   remaining drafts. If deletion fails, read the notice and reload the list before retrying.

![Editor menu with Delete draft and workbook actions](/docs/screens/model-more-actions.png)

Deletion is not an undo of activation or a removal of records. To stop offering a release for
new use, see [Retire or delete a release](/docs/guide/model/retire-or-delete-a-release/).

---
title: Delete a model mapping
description: Remove a reusable copy-and-move mapping while keeping work already produced.
reader: model-admin
---

Delete a saved mapping when you no longer need its conversion choices. You need **Copy and move**
access. This removes its saved editing history and proposals too. Read
[Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/) before deleting one still used by other people.

1. Open **Settings**, **Workspaces and models**, **Copy and move**. Find the mapping under **Mappings**;
   check **From model**, **To model**, **Version** and **Updated**.
2. Choose its **Delete…**. The confirmation asks **Delete the mapping …?** and names both models.
3. Read the warning: copies and moves already made remain; new work needs a new mapping.
   Choose **Cancel** to keep it, or **Delete the mapping** to remove it. There is no Undo here.
4. Wait for the row to disappear. If deletion fails, read the message in the dialog. If another
   editor changed the mapping, refresh and review its new version before deciding again.

![Mappings list and Delete the mapping confirmation](/docs/screens/model-delete-mapping.png)

Deleting a mapping does not publish, undo or discard any change set from an earlier copy or
move. Review those change sets separately. When the Delete action is absent, ask an access
administrator about Copy and move access rather than trying to delete data to remove the mapping.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/edit-:
---
title: Edit a draft as JSON
description: Save and validate a model document in the specialist draft workbench.
reader: model-admin
---

Use this task only when you maintain model documents. Ordinary browser modelling does not
require document syntax. You need **Model authoring**. See [The JSON view](/docs/model/json-view/).

1. Open the draft's **JSON** or **Open as JSON**. Check **Draft name** and the editable draft
   version before changing the **JSON model** text. Use **Export JSON** for a copy if needed.
2. Make the intended specialist edit. If **JSON syntax:** reports an error, correct it first.
   The summary alone is not proof that all references resolve.
3. Read **Authoritative validation**. Select a diagnostic to reach its location. Correct unknown
   references or conflicting definitions. Do not replace a referenced definition merely to silence an error.
4. Choose **Save draft**. This saves your text as a draft step, shown as **JSON edit** in
   History. If **A newer draft version exists** appears, choose **Copy local JSON** before
   **Reload saved version** when you need to keep your work. Review and reapply changes manually.
5. After saving, choose **Compile and compare**. Review **Canonical model**, its **Ready for
   review** or **Invalid** state and all semantic changes. Unsaved edits must be saved before compiling.
6. Choose **Open in editor** to inspect the same draft visually. To install without activating,
   use **Install immutable release…** where your permissions allow it and read **Install this
   model release?**. Confirm **Install release** only after review. It creates an inactive release.

![Syntax error in the specialist document editor](/docs/screens/model-json-syntax-error.png)

![Workbench actions including Save draft, Compile and compare and Export JSON](/docs/screens/model-json-workbench-actions.png)

For activation, follow [Install and activate a release](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/).
A successful save or compile alone does not check every workspace's data.

---
title: Edit a mapping row
description: Set a target type, field, relationship or typed default and review its dry run.
reader: model-admin
---

Open a copy or move in **Settings › Copy and move** with the necessary workspace access.
See [Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/) for how mappings and record matching work.

1. On **Mapping**, check **From**, **To**, the saved mapping and its version. **Change…**
   beside Mapping selects another mapping; it is different from changing one row.
2. Focus or select a row and read **Why this step**. Evidence and alternatives explain a
   **Proposed** choice. No numeric score is displayed. Select an alternative only if its
   meaning is right, not simply because its labels look similar.
3. Choose the target type for a source type. For an excluded type, use **Map … to…**. Then
   inspect each attribute, parent, relationship direction and matching rule under it.
4. Select a target field or **Not carried (reported)**. Review **Records already in the target**:
   finding only previously moved records differs from matching by a unique target field.
5. For a target field without a source value, use **Set a default…** and enter a value of its
   declared type. Use **Change…** to edit it or **Clear** to remove it. Supply a meaningful
   default rather than an arbitrary value just to satisfy a required field.
6. Read any problem beside the row. A refused step leaves that choice unapplied. **Undo** and
   **Redo** revisit mapping steps. A manual row says **This row is yours**; Undo can restore
   the proposal where available.
7. Wait for the new dry run. Inspect **Values not carried**, dropped relationships and records
   that cannot go. **The dry run waits for the mapping** is not a successful check; correct
   mapping problems first. After **The dry run did not run**, read why and **Dry run again**.

![Mapping choices and the evidence for a selected row](/docs/screens/model-mapping-why.png)

![Typed default editor for a target field](/docs/screens/moves-set-default.png)

If the mapping names releases other than the workspaces run, choose **Use the releases the
workspaces run**, inspect the choices and check again. A read-only notice means this deployment
or your access prevents edits. Saving rows alone copies or moves no records.

---
title: Edit a record page
description: Add panels and arrange fields, columns and regions on a draft record page.
reader: model-admin
---

Arrange a type's record page so people can read its fields and related records together.
You need **Model authoring** and an open draft. These changes affect the draft; people see
them after its release is activated in their workspace.

See [Record pages and tables](/docs/model/record-pages-and-tables/) for the page a type gets
before you arrange it.

## Open the layout

1. In the model editor, select the type in its application and choose **Preview**.
2. Choose **Edit layout**, then **Record page**. The layout shows **Main** and **Side**
   regions with frames for panels and fields.
3. If the type has no declared page, choose **Declare its page** first. This saves the
   generated page as a draft step so you can edit it. It includes **Details**, hierarchy
   where applicable, contained records and a panel for each relationship.

![Record layout with panels and field frames in Main and Side](/docs/screens/model-layout-record.png)

If the draft has errors, use **Show issues** and correct them before opening the layout.
For help choosing a workspace and record, follow [Preview a type](/docs/guide/model/preview-a-type/).

## Add a panel

1. At the foot of **Main**, choose **Add panel…**, beside **New field group**.
2. In **Add panel**, choose **What the panel shows**:
   - **Related records** lists the records reached through one relationship. It is offered
     when this type has relationships other than containment.
   - **Contained records** lists records inside the open record. It is offered only when
     the type contains types that this application lists. Select at least one **Contained types** choice.
   - **Fields** creates a group of this type's fields. Select **Fields**; chosen fields move
     from their current groups into the new one.
3. For **Related records**, select **Relationship**. The names read from this type's side
   of the relationship, including relationships pointing towards it. **(on the page)** means
   an existing panel already lists that relationship; it does not prevent another panel.
   Read the **Columns:** line beneath the choice to see the columns the new panel gets.
4. Choose **Region**: **Main** or **Side**. Review **Title**. For related or contained records,
   it starts from your choice and you can change it. For a field group, enter a title.
5. Choose **Apply**. The panel appears in the chosen region as one draft step. Use **Undo**
   if it was not what you wanted. Adding the panel does not create or change records.

![Add panel with a relationship chosen, its proposed columns, region and title](/docs/screens/model-add-panel-relationship.png)

Above: a Stop page in the guide's Graubünden model, with **Is represented by system code**
chosen. The proposed columns include **Name**, **System**, **External code** and **Description**.

An existing page keeps its arrangement. To give an older page separate panels for its
relationships, add each one here rather than expecting **Declare its page** to replace it.

## Choose a panel's columns and sort

1. Open the menu of a related-record, contained-record or table panel and choose **Columns…**.
2. Select **Name** and the fields you need. Under **Where it sits**, select a containing type
   to show the containing record's name. This can be an ancestor further up the hierarchy,
   not just the immediate parent. **Type** is also offered when the panel lists several types.
3. Choose **Apply** and inspect the column frames. Keep at least one column.
4. On a related-record panel whose menu offers **Sort…**, choose it, select **Sorted by**
   and choose **Apply**. The choices come from the panel's allowed sort fields.

![Panel Columns dialog with containing types under Where it sits](/docs/screens/model-panel-columns-where-it-sits.png)

Above: the **Has name translation** panel on a Stop page offers **Language** under
**Where it sits**. It shows each translation's language name. To show a field of that
language, such as **Language code**, use a
[table's related-field columns](/docs/guide/model/choose-table-columns-filters-and-sort/) instead.
Fields stored on the relationship itself cannot be columns.

## Arrange panels and fields

1. Open a panel's menu. **Move up**, **Move down** and **Move to Main** or **Move to Side**
   change its position. A grip can also drag it within a region or into the other region.
   On a phone, or with a keyboard, use the menu.
2. Choose **Rename…** to change **Title**. **Hide** keeps a panel in the layout but hides it
   from the record page; **Show** restores it. **Remove from page** takes it off the page,
   with **Undo** available afterwards. Stored records and values remain.
3. For a field, use **Move up**, **Move down** or **Move to …** to place it in a field group.
   **Remove from panel** takes it off that group. Dragging a field onto another group or
   field is another way to move it.
4. To make a field group in **Main**, choose **New field group**, give it **Title** and select
   **Fields**. Choose **Apply**. Selected fields move into it from their current positions.
   To add an omitted field to an existing group, use its **Add fields…** menu and select
   from **Fields not on the page**. This does not create a new field definition.

![Panel menu with ordering, visibility and field actions](/docs/screens/model-layout-panel-menu.png)

## Check the result

Return to preview and inspect a populated record and an empty record. Check the page with
records that have different relationships or parents. Review **Issues** before
[installing and activating the release](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/).
If an action shows **Not applied**, it has changed nothing: read the reason, correct the
choice and try again.

## Set the header and breadcrumbs

1. In **Record page**, choose **Header and breadcrumbs…**.
2. Select **Title of the record** from Name or an attached field. **Line under the title**
   adds a second field; choose **None** to remove it.
3. Choose **Show the type’s name in the header** as needed. **Breadcrumbs name the type**
   also shows the type in the header; **Breadcrumbs name the records above it** shows parents
   in the line above the title. That line starts with the list link when opened from a list,
   without an application entry. These choices do not change a record’s parent or name.
4. Apply and inspect the preview with a record that has parents. Undo restores the saved step.

![Record page Header and breadcrumbs dialog](/docs/screens/model-header-breadcrumbs.png)

## Change what a panel lists

1. Open the panel’s menu and choose **Settings…**. Fields groups have no extra settings.
2. For related records, select **Relationships listed** and **Listed from**. Choose **This
   record to the others**, **The others to this record**, or **Both ways**. Tick **Show which
   relationship joins each record** when one panel combines several meanings.
3. Select **Fields a reader can sort by** if people need a sort menu. Leaving these unchecked
   lists related records by name. A default sort no longer in the list moves to the first
   remaining choice, or is cleared when the list is empty.
4. For hierarchy, set **Show the parent** and **Show the records above the parent**. For a
   contained-record or table panel, choose **Rows on a page**. A table also offers **List
   only the records under this one**; clear it only when the page should show that type’s
   records beyond the open record’s direct children.
5. Apply and review columns, sorting and Issues. Changing settings does not rewrite stored
   connections. A panel with no matching records is empty; check its direction and selection
   before concluding that data is missing.

![Related-record panel Settings with relationship selection, direction and sort fields](/docs/screens/model-panel-settings.png)

---
title: Edit a workspace’s model
description: Reopen its saved draft and apply the reviewed definitions to that workspace.
reader: model-admin
---

Use this path when changing the model for a particular workspace. You need **Model authoring**,
**Model release** there and **Browse**, with model administration enabled. A retired workspace
does not offer this action. See [Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/).

1. Open **Settings › Workspaces**, then the workspace. Check its current model and choose
   **Edit model**. The workspace's menu also offers this action where your access allows it.
2. Read **Applies to** in the editor. It identifies the destination. Later visits reopen the
   saved workspace draft; closing keeps the work rather than applying it.
3. Make the intended changes and review **History**, **Issues** and preview. No live record
   or active definition changes merely because a draft step was saved.
4. Choose **Apply to this workspace…**. Read the model changes, data and consumer checks,
   old change sets left behind and other workspaces left unchanged.
5. **Not valid** needs model fixes. **Nothing to apply yet** means no applicable change.
   **Your records stay as they are** means no data conversion is required. **Some records
   must move first** offers **Preview what happens to the records…**; follow
   [Migrate a workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) for the separate review.
6. Confirm only after checking the named workspace. On success inspect its model and applications.
   On **Not applied**, read the reason, reload the current state and check again before retrying.

![Workspace overview with Edit model](/docs/screens/model-workspace-edit-model.png)

![Apply dialog listing the workspace, changes and compatibility](/docs/screens/model-workspace-apply-dialog.png)

To choose an already installed release instead, follow
[Change a workspace’s model](/docs/guide/model/change-a-workspaces-model/).

A workspace remembers at most one current draft. If its model changes elsewhere, that older
draft is detached from the workspace rather than deleted. Reopen **Edit model** to obtain the
current draft instead of applying an old tab without review. If installation succeeded but
activation failed, the flow retries against the installed release; inspect the reported state
rather than installing the same release again.

## Ask for a change in words

The workspace menu also offers **Change this model…** when the assistant and your rights
allow it. Follow [Change a model with the assistant](/docs/guide/model/change-a-model-with-the-assistant/)
to review its draft and complete the record moves. Apply can separately
[explain the change](/docs/guide/model/explain-a-model-change/) through the configured provider.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/expla:
---
title: Explain a model change
description: Ask for an account before activation and follow its statements back to the engine's facts.
reader: model-admin
---

Use this task before activating a release or applying a draft to a workspace. You need
**Model release** and **Use AI proposals** in that workspace, and a configured AI provider.
The Claude Code assistant alone does not provide this explanation.

Your request sends the model's changes and record counts, without record values or names.
It may incur provider charges. Successful accounts are reused for the same inputs for up to
an hour; call records remain, with content kept only if enabled by the operator. See
[About AI in refiroo](/docs/run/ai/) for full costs, access and retention details, and
[Accounts of model changes](/docs/model/model-change-accounts/) for how the facts are prepared.

1. Open the release under **Settings › Model** and choose **Activate in a workspace…**, then select the
   workspace. Alternatively, open the workspace's draft and choose **Apply to this workspace**.
   Check the workspace, release and comparison before proceeding.
2. Wait for the data and consumer API checks. Opening the dialog does not ask the provider
   or spend AI usage. Read any compatibility notice first.
3. Find **What this change does**. Read the line saying what goes to the provider, then choose
   **Explain this change**. Wait for the account; asking does not activate or apply the model.
4. Read the statements and their AI-written note. Select a numbered citation to move to the
   fact it rests on. A citation to a hidden fact opens the rest of the list. **+** refers to
   the other facts of a kind.
5. Review **The facts**, including counts and blocking reasons. Choose **Show the other …**
   when more facts are available. Check the original compatibility and consumer notices too:
   the account cannot certify that a change is safe.
6. Decide what to do using the dialog's normal action. Cancel if the result is wrong, fix the
   draft, or follow the migration route if needed. Ask again after a new check; the old account
   is cleared. For migration, follow [Migrate a workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/).

![Activation dialog showing What this change does before an account is requested](/docs/screens/model-account-before-request.png)

![Activation dialog with an AI-written account, numbered citations and the engine's facts](/docs/screens/model-account-facts.png)

If **The account could not be written** appears, read the facts below it. **Try again** asks
the provider again; it is not required to continue reviewing the model. If the account could
not be asked for, use the reason shown to resolve the request failure. Fix an invalid draft's
issues or reload a newer draft version before another attempt.

![Provider failure with facts still available and Try again](/docs/screens/model-account-provider-failure.png)

If the section is absent, ask an administrator to check provider setup and your workspace
permissions. It is absent from the install dialog and migration page by design. You can still
read those screens' checks and outcomes without an AI account.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/expor:
---
title: Export a release
description: Download the immutable model document and identify its exact release.
reader: model-admin
---

Use export to hand a model document to a specialist author or keep a copy of its definitions.
It exports the model, not workspace records. See [Releases](/docs/model/releases/).

1. Open **Settings › Model**, the model's **Releases**, then the intended version. Check its
   name, version and **Immutable release** state rather than opening a similarly named draft.
2. Choose **Export JSON** and keep the downloaded document. The installed release is unchanged.
   Export is also available for historical definitions the current editor cannot interpret.
3. If you need to identify it precisely, open **Technical details**. Use **Copy** beside
   **Release ID** and **Content hash**. The hash identifies the content; the displayed version
   is a human-facing release label.
4. To edit a copy, use **Create draft from release** or the draft creation dialog's **Import
   JSON** option. Importing a document does not activate it. For data backup, use the operator's
   backup procedure instead of treating this file as a workspace export.

![Immutable release with export and draft creation actions](/docs/screens/model-release-detail.png)

![Technical details identifying the release and its content hash](/docs/screens/release-technical-details.png)

If the download fails, read the displayed failure and retry after correcting its cause.
The downloaded file alone does not include records, access grants or publication history.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/find-:
---
title: Find your way around the editor
description: Select definitions, open their actions and navigate the editor with the keyboard.
reader: model-admin
---

Open a [model draft](/docs/guide/model/create-a-model-draft/) in the editor. You need
**Model authoring**. See [The model editor](/docs/model/the-model-editor/) for saved steps and states.

1. Read the draft title. Select it to rename the draft. Open **About this draft** to check its
   base release, whether it is a new model, draft version and errors or warnings. The version
   increases with each step; **Close** keeps the saved draft.
2. In **Model**, unfold an application and select a type. Its centre panel shows **Attributes**
   and **Relations**. Selecting the application instead shows **Object types**, **Views** and
   **Navigation groups**. The same type can appear in more than one application.
3. Select **Attribute types** or **Relation types** to inspect reusable definitions. Select
   **Relationship matrix** to see permitted type pairs, with the from end down the rows.
   Use arrow keys in the grid and Enter to select a pair; its panel offers the pair's actions.
4. Use **Add** for **Application…**, **Object type…**, **Attribute type…**, **Relation type…**
   or **Navigation group…**. An empty draft asks you to add an application first.
   The **Consumer APIs** tab has its own add action.
5. Open an element's operations menu to change it. In the model pane, Up/Down and Home/End
   move focus, Enter or Space selects, Right/Left unfolds or folds, and Shift+F10 or the
   context-menu key opens that row's operations. A type an application lists only because one of its
   relation views needs it is shown with a dashed icon, in its group or under **From other
   applications**, and opens on the application that holds its records; types no view uses come last. A disabled action is not applied.
6. Expand **Issues and history** to inspect errors or saved steps. With a workbook, use
   **Issues, history and dry run** and the additional **Source** pane. Resize the pane dividers
   for space. On a phone, use the pane tabs; dragging is unavailable, so use the menus.

![Model editor showing the model pane, selected definition and history drawer](/docs/screens/model-editor-overview.png)

If an edit reports **Not applied**, read the reason before trying again. For a newer saved
version, follow [Work on a draft with others](/docs/guide/model/work-on-a-draft-with-others/).
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/fix-i:
---
title: Fix issues before installing
description: Follow validation messages to their elements and check data compatibility before applying a draft.
reader: model-admin
---

Use this check before installing or applying a draft. **Model authoring** lets you correct it;
release access is needed to activate it. [Issues and dry runs](/docs/model/issues-and-dry-run/)
explains why a valid model, compatible stored data and accepted source rows are separate results.

## Follow and correct model issues

1. Open the draft and read the header's status. Expand **Issues and history**, then choose **Issues**.
   Read each message and its severity.
2. Use an issue's **Go to** link to open the affected type, application or view. Check the named
   setting against what that element actually contains.
3. Correct the cause using the element's controls. For a view referring to an unavailable field,
   remove that field from its selected columns, or attach the intended existing attribute to its
   type if it belongs there. If the last edit was a mistake, use **Undo** instead.
4. Save the correction and wait for validation. Reopen **Issues** and resolve the remaining errors.
   If **Another change came first** appears, read the newer steps, then choose
   **Apply mine again** or **Discard mine** after reviewing the current model.

![Draft validation error with a link to the affected view](/docs/screens/model-issues-error.png)

*Above: Guide draft contains a deliberate unavailable-field reference in the Municipalities view.
The issue points to Network's view rather than requiring the reader to search every type.*

Do not treat saving or closing as a successful check. An invalid draft can be saved, but its
errors still prevent installation. Read warnings too, especially when a workbook mapping is attached.

![Corrected draft showing Valid and no issues](/docs/screens/model-issues-none.png)

*Above: Guide draft's issue is fixed. The Issues tab now says the draft is valid and can be installed.*

## Check the selected workspace

1. Choose **Install and activate…**, or **Apply to this workspace…** in a workspace draft.
   Opening the confirmation performs checks without applying the model.
2. Check the named workspace and the differences from the base release. Read the stored-data
   result. If data does not fit, read the affected records and rules before deciding whether to
   correct data, revise the model or open the offered migration preview.
3. Review **Consumer APIs**. If a contract needs a higher version, coordinate that change and use
   the offered version action before checking again. A model release version increase alone does
   not resolve a consumer contract incompatibility.
4. Read the open change sets left on the current release. Plan how to move or discard them before
   their next publication. Use **Cancel** while further work is needed; the draft stays saved.

For an attached workbook, also wait for the latest **Dry run**, open refused-row figures and
resolve or explicitly account for them. **No issues** does not mean every source row is accepted.
Follow [Load a workbook](/docs/guide/model/start-a-draft-from-a-workbook/) for that check.

Once the intended model is valid and the target is suitable, follow
[Install and activate a release](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/).

Where an issue offers a fix, inspect its meaning before choosing it. **Use as the profile's key**
resolves a profile identity choice; it is not a change to a record's identifier. An issue for a
panel naming a removed field can offer to remove that panel. Recheck after either action. In a
workbook dry run, select each source tab, open refused-row counts and compare the **was** figures
with the previous check. A fix to one source does not establish that the other sources load.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/group:
---
title: Group collections in navigation
description: Group collections and relation matrices in the sidebar, order entries and choose opening views.
reader: model-admin
---
