Arrange an application's sidebar so people can find related collections and open a matrix directly.
Work in a draft with **Model authoring**. See
[Applications and views](/docs/model/applications-and-views/) for grouping rules.

## Create and open a group

1. Select the application. Choose **Add a navigation group…** from its menu, or **Navigation
   group…** from **Add** and choose **Application**.
2. Enter **Label** and choose whether it is **Folded when the sidebar opens**. Apply and check
   **Navigation groups** in the application panel. An empty group is allowed.
3. Choose the group's name in that table, or select it in the model pane. Its panel shows the
   application it belongs to, its starting state and entry count. The **Entries** table lists
   **Entry**, **Kind**, **Opens on** and **State**. A new group has no entries yet.

![Application navigation groups with their entries and starting states](/docs/screens/model-application-groups.png)

## Add collections and matrices

1. In the group panel, choose **Add to group…**. The dialog lists **Collections** and
   **Relation matrices** separately. Entries already in this group are left out.
2. Use **Search collections and matrices** to find entries by name. Tick all the entries you
   want to add. Beside each, **Top of the sidebar** means an ungrouped collection;
   **Inside** followed by a type's name means a matrix available through that row collection.
   **In** followed by a group name means the entry is in another group. Ticking it changes
   that note to **Moves from** followed by the old group name.
3. Review those moves, then choose **Add** with the selected count. The entries appear in
   the group's table. A collection or matrix belongs to at most one group in this application;
   choosing a new group replaces its old placement. This does not move records under a parent.
4. Check the result. Adding several entries at once is one saved step: one **Undo** takes
   the whole addition back.

![Add-to-group dialog with collections and relation matrices selected and their current locations](/docs/screens/model-group-add-entries-dialog.png)

From the application panel, **In no group:** lists ungrouped collections. Its **Add to a group…**
opens the same dialog with those collections ticked; choose **Group** and adjust the selection
before adding them.

You can also place one entry at a time. On a type listed in the application, choose
**Move to group…**. Select **Application** if offered, then **Group**.
**No group: the top of the sidebar** leaves the collection ungrouped. For a relation matrix,
find it in the application's **Views** table and choose **Move to group…** from its menu.
Choose a group, or the **No group: inside** option to keep it within its row collection.
Create a group first if the matrix's menu does not offer this action.

A grouped matrix has its own entry in the sidebar and on the group page. It uses the view's
name and a matrix symbol in its row type's colour, and opens the matrix directly. The row
collection stays where it was, and its view tabs still offer the matrix.

## Order entries and choose what opens

1. In **Entries**, drag a row by its grip to a new place, or open its menu and choose **Move up** or
   **Move down**. Collections and matrices share one order. The first entry cannot move up; the last cannot move down.
2. Choose **Move to another group…** to select a different **Group**. This action is available
   when another group exists. **Take out of the group** returns a collection to the top of the
   sidebar; a matrix returns to being available only through its row collection.
3. For a collection with several views, select its **Opens on** cell. Choose the view people
   should see when they open that collection, then **Save**. **Cancel** leaves it unchanged.
   With only one view there is no choice to edit. A matrix entry shows **Itself** and always
   opens that matrix.
4. Check the chosen view's name and kind in **Opens on**. It sets the collection's opening
   view in both the sidebar and the group page; people can still switch to its other views.
   Without a collection choice, refiroo uses the application's default view if it belongs to
   this collection, otherwise its table, otherwise its first view.

![Navigation group panel with a collection, a relation matrix and their opening views](/docs/screens/model-navigation-group-panel.png)

*Above: a group in the Graubünden model contains a collection and the Municipalities by system
relation matrix.*

## Adjust or remove the group

1. Use **Rename…** and **Start unfolded** / **Start folded** in the group panel to change its
   label and initial state. A person's later folding choice is remembered in their browser.
2. Drag a group's row by its grip in the application table, or use the group menu's **Move up** or
   **Move down**, to order groups. The table also lets you edit **Label** directly, and **Starts
   folded** is a box you click to change. **Change key…** is for unreleased keys only.
3. To remove the grouping, choose **Remove group**, read the confirmation and confirm.
   The confirmation says that its collections return to the top of the sidebar and, when the
   group holds relation matrices, that they go back inside their row type's entry; matrices
   remain available through their row collections. The views and records are kept. Check **Issues** and use **Undo** if needed.

![Navigation group menu with ordering and initial-state choices](/docs/screens/model-group-menu.png)

These are model defaults. The active workspace keeps its current navigation until the release
is activated. If an action says **Not applied**, correct the stated problem before retrying.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/insta:
---
title: Install and activate a release
description: Review a draft, choose one workspace and confirm installation and activation safely.
reader: model-admin
---

Apply a checked model to one workspace. You need model authoring to prepare the draft and
**Model release** in the target workspace; creating a new workspace also needs **Workspace
administration**. Read [Releases](/docs/model/releases/) and
[fix draft issues](/docs/guide/model/fix-issues-before-installing/) before confirming.

## Install from the editor

1. Open the draft and choose **Install and activate…**. Read the confirmation; opening it alone
   installs nothing.
2. Check **Release key**, **Version** and **Name**. Keep the key when releasing another version of
   the same model. The dialog proposes a version no release of this model holds. If you type one that is taken by
   different definitions, the refusal offers a **Use** button with the next free version. The draft's edit
   number is not this version.
3. Under **Activate into**, choose **An existing workspace** and select it, or **A new workspace**
   and complete its details. Read the workspace name carefully: another workspace may run another
   model. The choice affects this target alone.
4. Review **What changes against** the base release, **Valid**, stored-data compatibility and
   **Consumer APIs**. Resolve blocking issues before continuing. A different-model workspace may
   be checked only when activation is attempted; its selection is not a promise its records fit.
5. If **Activation needs a migration** appears, read the steps and what each part does.
   Review where records go, **records move**, **records created**, **relationships created**
   where shown, and **refused**. For a changed key, the warning names consumer APIs of the base
   release using it and says integrations naming the key must change. Coordinate those changes.
6. When a migration is needed, choose **Install … and preview the migration…**. This installs
   the release and opens the migration page with the draft's proposal filled in. The release
   is not active yet. Review **What the draft proposes**, its **Proposed** rows and all outcomes,
   including **Created** for a split or list conversion, then
   [confirm the migration](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) when acceptable.
7. Otherwise confirm **Install … and activate in …**, or **Install … and create …** for a new
   workspace. Wait for the outcome. **Cancel** in the install dialog leaves the draft saved
   without installing or activating it.

![Install and activate confirmation with release identity, workspace and compatibility checks](/docs/screens/model-install-dialog.png)

*Above: Guide draft proposes release 1.0.1 for Graubünden, adding Step-free access and Inspected by.
The captured dialog was cancelled: neither installation nor activation happened.*

![Install review with Activation needs a migration, moving-record counts and a preview action](/docs/screens/model-install-migration.png)

*Above: the draft proposes moving 12 Stop code records to the top level of Systems in Stops tidy-up, with zero refused. Install … and preview the migration… opens the record review; this captured dialog was cancelled.*

A successful installation fixes the release's content; the draft continues as the next editable
version. If the result says **Installed, not active**, keep the installed release and resolve the
reported activation problem. Do not assume installation was undone.


## Review earlier consumer contracts before activation

In **Consumer APIs**, check both the current version and every **Earlier versions** row in
the draft. Raising a contract normally keeps the base release’s previous definition. That
version continues reading current data in its original shape after activation. Installing
an older release alone does not keep any contract served; the workspace’s active release
must retain it.

A finding ending **a kept version is served as it was: restore it, or stop serving it**
means the retained contract would change. Restore that definition and its model sources,
or agree to stop serving it. Raising the current version again does not fix the finding.
The install review shows this explanation instead of a raise action for that retained version.

In the install review, and in the activation dialog of each workspace, a warning that
an API **stops serving version …** means that earlier version disappears
on activation. The review names the version and says its consumers get
`CONTRACT_VERSION_NOT_FOUND`; it does not say **Compatible** for that API. Confirm the removal with consuming teams, including webhook owners. Its
reads stop and affected webhooks need review before resuming on the current contract. A
**Sunset day** alone never stops a version. See
[Stop serving an earlier contract version](/docs/guide/model/stop-serving-an-earlier-contract-version/).

Read the removal warning in the install review before opening the confirmation. The API’s
**Schema › Against what consumers read now** lists the same finding.

Review the destination workspace’s contract check even when the draft’s base comparison
passes: another workspace may serve a different release or retain different versions.

## Apply from a workspace

1. On **Settings**, **Workspaces**, open the intended workspace and choose **Edit model**.
   Confirm **Applies to** in the editor header, make the changes and choose **Apply to this workspace…**.
2. Read the workspace's current model, **What changes in the model**, data compatibility and
   **Consumer APIs**. Expand **Becomes release** to review the release identity where shown.
3. Read **Change sets left on** the old version. They stay pinned to that release and cannot be
   published until moved to the new one or discarded. Check **Not changed** for the other workspaces.
4. If **Your records stay as they are** is shown, confirm **Apply to** the named workspace when ready.
   If **Activation needs a migration** appears, review the steps, destinations, counts and warnings
   about changed keys and the consumer APIs naming them. **Some records must move first** can
   appear when the compatibility check finds a migration without a draft proposal.
5. Choose **Preview what happens to the records…** when a migration is needed. It installs the
   release and opens a migration preview with the draft's choices where available. Inspect
   **What the draft proposes**, the **Proposed** rows and outcomes, including **Created** when
   records and relationships are created. The workspace keeps its current release until you
   [confirm the migration](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/).

![Workspace apply dialog showing changes, compatible data and change sets left behind](/docs/screens/model-workspace-apply-dialog.png)

*Above: applying Guide draft to Graubünden leaves Default unchanged and names December 2026 timetable
change as remaining on release 1.0.0. The dialog was cancelled.*

![Workspace Apply review with a proposed type move and Preview what happens to the records action](/docs/screens/model-apply-migration.png)

*Above: Apply to Stops tidy-up shows the same move of 12 Stop code records, with zero refused. Preview what happens to the records… opens the migration review. The captured dialog was cancelled.*

## Activate an already installed release

1. Open **Settings**, **Model**, choose the model, then **Releases** and the intended version.
2. Check its identity, workspace use and installation details. Use **Create draft from release**
   if its definitions need changing; the release itself is immutable.
3. Choose **Activate in a workspace…**, select the target and read its compatibility result and
   change sets left behind. A release can be activated only when that workspace's existing data fits.
4. Confirm **Activate** with the displayed version and workspace when ready. If activation is
   refused, correct the named issue and recheck. A stale-state refusal needs a refreshed workspace
   state and another review, not repeated confirmation of the old result.

![Installed release page with workspace use and activation and draft actions](/docs/screens/model-release-detail.png)

*Above: release 1.0.0 of the Graubünden model is immutable and already run by Graubünden.*

![Activation dialog checking one selected workspace and listing other workspaces unchanged](/docs/screens/model-release-activate-dialog.png)

*Above: the selected target is Default, which runs RDM Starter Model; Graubünden stays unchanged.
The captured activation was cancelled.*

After success, open the target workspace and check its applications and a changed type's page.
Other workspaces keep their models. If an already open page says its model changed, reload it
before editing records. Review any left-behind change sets through the
[change-set process](/docs/use/change-sets/) before their next publication.

## Read the activation result

| Result | Next action |
| --- | --- |
| Compatible with the workspace's data | Review the named workspace and confirm activation when ready. |
| A migration is needed | From installation, choose **Install … and preview the migration…**; from Apply, **Preview what happens to the records…**. Review proposed destinations, created items, conversions, removals and items to fix before confirming the migration. |
| A different model | Review this destination carefully; compatibility is checked when activation is attempted. |
| A consumer API needs a higher contract version | Coordinate the contract change and raise its version in a draft before rechecking. |
| Could not be checked | Read the failure, correct its cause and check again; it is not a successful compatibility result. |

The install dialog says **Comparing with the base release** where the draft has one. That
comparison can differ from the target workspace's current release; read the separate data and
consumer checks too. Cancelling a migration preview leaves workspace data unchanged; a release
installed to start that preview remains installed. After a stale preview, review a fresh
one instead of confirming the old counts.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/load-:
---
title: Load a workbook into a change set
description: Apply the workbook's model and profile, load its rows and review the unpublished result.
reader: model-admin
---

Use this for the manual workbook route in the model editor, which loads through an import
profile. For an assistant's proposal, use
[Review the assistant's workbook design](/docs/guide/model/review-an-assistants-workbook-design/):
**Accept and load to change set** loads its checked records and relationships without saving an import
profile or activating the model. The steps below apply to the manual route.

First [start a draft from a workbook](/docs/guide/model/start-a-draft-from-a-workbook/) and
check every source's mapping and dry run. See
[Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/) for the separate model and data stages.
You need the release permissions for any activation and the import and change-set permissions
in the destination workspace. Loading does not publish the records.

## Load and review


1. Choose **Load into a change set…**. Check the dry-run version and summary at the top.
2. Read stage 1. If the model changed, check the release's **Release key**, **Version** and
   **Name**. Installing and activating changes the target workspace's model before loading rows.
   If the model is unchanged, this stage keeps it and saves the profile.
3. Under **Open a change set**, set **Change set name** and **Workspace**. Verify the destination
   before proceeding, especially if it differs from the comparison workspace.
4. Review **Load the rows**. Found records are updated through the saved profile. Choose
   **Install, activate and load**, or **Load** when no activation is needed. **Cancel** leaves
   the dialog without starting these stages.
5. Wait as the stages run in order. Completed steps are marked; the button shows **Installing…**,
   **Opening the change set…** or **Loading…**. During the row load, read the processed-item count
   under **Load the rows**. The dialog's actions are unavailable while it works.
6. If it stops, read which stages completed and why it stopped. An installed release can remain
   installed after a later failure; inspect the reported state before retrying. If the profile
   or model has issues, return to **Issues** and resolve them.
7. At **Loaded into the change set**, read all four counts: **created**, **updated**, **unchanged**
   and **refused**. They cover records and relationships. A finished load with refused items is
   not a complete import of every source row. Compare the result with the dry run and resolve
   unexpected refusals before publishing.

![Load dialog showing release details and the chosen change-set workspace](/docs/screens/wbload-dialog.png)

*Above: the fictional operator workbook is about to install release 1.0.1, open a change set in
Guide workbook test and load the rows. This is the destination chosen for this example.*

![Load in progress with completed installation and change-set stages](/docs/screens/wbload-running.png)

*Above: the first two stages are done. Loading has begun at 0 of 420 items; the button says Loading….*

![Completed load with its four counts and Open the change set review](/docs/screens/wbload-finished.png)

*Above: the fictional workbook load created 258 records and relationships, updated 108, left 45
unchanged and refused 9. The result is in a change set, ready to review.*

## Inspect the loaded changes

1. Choose **Open the change set review**. Check its workspace and change-set name against the
   destination you chose. On **Records**, read the kinds of change and expand entries to inspect
   the loaded details. Use **Filter** if needed, then remove it to check the rest.
2. Open **Relationships** and inspect the connections. Compare the proposed changes with what
   you intended to load. Unchanged records do not count as differences; refused rows have not
   become successful record changes. The dry run's refused-row details explain its known refusals.
3. Choose **Back to change set**. Open a collection and inspect the records' fields and
   relationships. Check the orange **Change set** banner before correcting anything; the load
   has not published the records.
4. If the result is ready, [review, validate and publish the change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/),
   or [submit it for approval](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/#submit-your-work).
   **Close** in the finished load dialog leaves the loaded proposal unpublished; it does not undo it.

![Review changes showing added records from the workbook load](/docs/screens/wbload-review.png)

*Above: the load's review in Guide workbook test includes new lookup values and local codes.
Each arrow opens the record's details; Relationships has its own tab.*

![Loaded collection of records inside the load's open change set](/docs/screens/wbload-records.png)

*Above: Haltestellens lists 51 proposed records in the fictional workbook's application. The
change-set banner remains visible above the list; the records have not been published.*

Keep the draft if you need to revisit its mapping. To remove it, choose **Delete draft…** on the
editor menu and read the confirmation. Deletion removes its proposals, steps and attached workbook
permanently; installed releases remain. Cancelling deletion keeps the draft.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/make-:
---
title: Make a workspace the default
description: Select the default destination without changing other workspaces’ models or data.
reader: model-admin
---

You need **Workspace administration** and the deployment must allow workspace changes.
See [Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/) for the default workspace's role.

1. Open **Settings › Workspaces**, then the active workspace you want as the default.
   Read its name, permanent key and model in **Overview**.
2. Choose **Set as default**. Check the success notice and **Default** mark afterwards.
   The previous default remains a separate workspace with its own records and model.
3. If another administrator changed the default while your page was open, read the notice,
   reload the state and choose again only if your intended change is still correct.
4. Inspect new-workspace creation choices when relevant: **The default workspace’s model**
   now refers to this workspace's release. Existing workspaces keep their selected releases.

![Workspace management showing the Default mark](/docs/screens/use-workspace-default.png)

Making a workspace default copies no records and grants no access. The default cannot be retired
or deleted. To take it out of use later, first select another active default.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/map-a:
---
title: Map a workbook column
description: Choose what a column feeds, how references match and which values are ignored or replaced.
reader: model-admin
---

Open a draft with an attached workbook and **Model authoring**. See
[Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/) for the source and profile.

1. Select the sheet, then a column in **Source**. Read its status, **Feeds**, **Read as**,
   **Matched by** and **Statistics**. Filled and distinct values help assess a mapping; they
   do not prove the column's meaning. Review frequent values, placeholders and delimiters.
2. Choose **Map to…**, or drag the column onto a type. Select the type whose rows are being
   read and **What the column holds**: a name, attribute, parent, lookup, related record,
   relationship flag, or an ignored column. The form changes with this choice.
3. For a new attribute, review **Attribute name**, proposed **Value type** and **Unique**.
   For a parent or relationship, choose the offered destination. A missing parent type or
   relationship must be modelled first; the form explains when there is none.
4. For a lookup, set **Matched by**. A unique attribute can find existing records; only name
   matching can create missing named records. Enable **Create the records a cell names that
   do not exist** only when those names really define records you want to maintain.
5. For a related record, choose what the column fills and its parent. Choose a fixed named
   parent or **The one each row names in** and **The column naming it**. A fixed parent and
   a column cannot both supply the same source's parent. Name matching for that record is
   under the chosen parent, rather than a search across every parent.
6. For a flag, check **The record a Y relates the row to**. Its default comes from the header;
   change it if that is not the intended record. For a multi-value lookup, set **Split a cell
   on** only when each part names a separate record; **Do not split** keeps the cell whole.
7. Choose **Map**. **Not mapped** leaves the attempted mapping unapplied; correct the stated
   problem. **Ignore** or **Ignore the column** excludes values you do not intend to load.
8. Back in the column panel, use **Add a value map…** or **Edit value map…**. Pair **Text in
   the file** with **Becomes**, including intended placeholder handling. Remove a row to stop
   that replacement. This changes reading instructions, not the original spreadsheet.
9. Choose **Save the value map** to keep its replacements, or **Cancel** to leave them unchanged.
   Check **Key** before **Use as the key of the rows**. A non-unique column explains why it
   cannot serve as a key. Review [the refreshed dry run](/docs/guide/model/check-a-workbook-with-a-dry-run/).

![Workbook column statistics and the model it feeds](/docs/screens/use-wb-source-namen.png)

The mapping form shows the selected source column and its destination. A value map changes
how the file is read before matching or conversion.

![UIC-Nr column mapped to an existing integer attribute, with row type, column meaning and key choice](/docs/screens/model-workbook-map-column.png)

![Value map with an unsaved J-to-true replacement and placeholder entries that become empty](/docs/screens/model-workbook-value-map.png)

If none of a sheet belongs in the load, open its Source menu and choose **Ignore this sheet**.
It removes that sheet’s reading sources, not its cells or live records. Check other sheets’
lookups and the refreshed dry run; use Undo if excluding the sheet was unintended.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/migra:
---
title: Migrate a workspace
description: Review every converted or removed item and confirm a model switch with accepted loss.
reader: model-admin
---

Start from a draft's install or Apply review, or an activation check that says the data needs
migration. You need **Model release**
in the workspace, with model administration and jobs enabled. See [Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/).

1. From **Install and activate…**, read **Activation needs a migration** and choose **Install …
   and preview the migration…**. From **Apply to this workspace…**, choose **Preview what happens
   to the records…**. For an installed release, choose **Preview the migration…** where offered.
   Check the workspace and target release on the migration page. **Nothing has changed yet**
   refers to workspace data: the editor flow has installed the release, but has not activated it.
   Wait for every record to be checked, or **Cancel the preview**. Leaving keeps the job running.
2. For an editor proposal, read **What the draft proposes**. Each row shows **Records of**,
   **Become**, **In**, **Under**, **Records** and a **Proposed** mark for the draft's choice.
   Check the destination type, application and parent placement, plus the split, list-conversion
   or relationship-key lines below. Change **Become** in place if another destination is intended;
   it previews again without changing the draft. Under **What … no longer has**, review any
   remaining missing type or field and select **Became …** only for its genuine replacement.
   Type mappings retain record IDs and history. **Not kept** removes the type's records and
   relationships or the field's values. Each choice previews again.
3. Open each outcome: **Converted**, **Type changed**, **Removed**, **Must be fixed** and, when
   shown, **Created**. Created lists the records and relationships a split or list conversion
   makes. Read the item lists, including before and after values. These count items, not just
   records. Check top-level moves for the removal of the old parent connection; tighter rules
   can leave records under Must be fixed even when their proposed destination is correct.
4. Fix every blocking item in the named workspace or change set. Required values, required
   relationships, parent placement, uniqueness and publication conflicts cannot be waived by
   accepting loss. Choose **Preview again** and review the refreshed lists.
5. If **Removed** contains items, inspect them. While **Must be fixed** contains blocking
   items, the acceptance checkbox is hidden and the migration button is disabled. Resolve
   those items first, then tick **I accept that …** to accept the listed removal.
   Choose **Cancel** to keep the current data; a release already installed remains installed.
6. Check the final action. **Migrate … to …** changes the workspace. **Move change set** changes
   only the named change set onto the workspace's current release. **Migrate and publish** also
   publishes the named change set and needs publication permission and any required approval.
7. Confirm only the reviewed action. If a stale notice appears, **Close** or **Preview again**;
   nothing was migrated by that refusal. Review the new result before another confirmation.
8. Read the success counts and destination. For a workspace migration, inspect its applications
   and arrange to move or discard old change sets. For a change-set move, choose **Open the
   change set** and review and validate it. For migration and publication, inspect the named publication.

![Migration preview with a Proposed destination row and outcome counts](/docs/screens/model-migration-proposed.png)

*Above: the draft proposes moving 12 Stop code records from Network to the top level of Systems. The row is marked Proposed, and Type changed counts 12 records; nothing has changed yet.*

![Migration preview with split and list-conversion proposals and the Created outcome selected](/docs/screens/model-migration-created.png)

*Above: the draft splits Code system from Stop code and turns Code kind values into list records. Created lists 28 new records and relationships across both changes; nothing has changed in the workspace yet.*

![Migration preview with outcomes and choices for missing types and fields](/docs/screens/model-migration-review.png)

![Removed items in a blocked migration preview, with three items to fix and the migration button disabled](/docs/screens/model-migration-loss-confirm.png)

![Stale migration review asking for another preview after the workspace changed](/docs/screens/model-migration-stale.png)

A failed execution leaves data and the release switch unapplied together. Read **Not migrated**
or **Not moved**, correct its cause and preview again. History retains removed content, but
migration has no automatic reverse button.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/move-:
---
title: Move records to another model
description: Review a proposed mapping, check every selected item and copy or move through change sets.
reader: model-admin
---

Copy or move records into another workspace when its model differs. Arrange **Copy and move**
access in the relevant workspaces and the data and change-set permissions needed for review and
publication. Background jobs and model administration must be enabled. See
[Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/) for matching rules and the difference between copy
and move.

## Open a mapping for the two workspaces

1. Open **Settings**, then **Copy and move**. Review **Mappings** and **Recent copies and moves**
   to avoid starting the same work twice.
2. Choose **New copy or move…**. Select **From workspace** and **To workspace**. Check the model
   and release displayed beside each name; source and target must be different workspaces.
3. Under **Mapping**, choose a saved mapping for these models or **A new mapping, proposed**.
   For a new mapping, fill **Name of the new mapping** so it can be recognised later.
4. Choose **Open the editor**. Wait for the proposal and dry run. This prepares the mapping and
   check; it does not copy records. **Cancel** leaves the dialog without starting the flow.

![Copy and move page with saved mappings and recent operations](/docs/screens/model-moves-list.png)

*Above: Guide mapping connects the Graubünden model to RDM Starter Model. Recent entries are dry
runs not started, not completed copies.*

![New copy or move dialog with source, target and mapping choices](/docs/screens/model-moves-new-dialog.png)

*Above: Graubünden is the source and Default the target. Guide mapping is selected, with A new
mapping, proposed offered below. The captured dialog was cancelled.*

## Complete the mapping

1. Review source types on the left and their mapped states. Select each mapping row and read
   **Why this step** and its evidence before accepting a suggestion; choose an alternative
   or change the row if the proposal does not represent your intended meaning.
2. Check the target type, every field and every relationship. **Not carried (reported)** leaves
   a value out. Choose that only when its loss is intended. Map a required target field or supply
   a meaningful default where the editor offers it.
3. Check **Parent** for contained records. A mapped child still needs a permitted parent in the
   target; carrying it under an incompatible parent causes a refusal.
4. Check **Records already in the target**. Decide whether to find only records moved before or
   also match by an offered unique field. Review existing target values before allowing updates.
5. Use **Undo** or **Redo** for mistakes. Wait for the refreshed dry run after a saved change.
   If saving is refused because the mapping changed elsewhere, reload it and review those changes.

![Proposed mapping and dry run with source and target types](/docs/screens/model-mapping-proposed.png)

*Above: the proposed Operators-to-Domains and Modes-to-Codelists choices need human review.
The dry run exposes substantial omissions; this is not a loss-free copy.*

## Choose the records and inspect the dry run

1. Choose **Copy** to keep source records, or **Move** to prepare their later deletion too.
2. Beside **What to copy** or **What to move**, choose **Change…**. Select **Every mapped type**,
   **The whole workspace**, **Chosen types**, or **One record and everything under it**. For chosen
   types, select the types and filters. For a subtree, choose its type and starting record.
3. Choose **Dry run this selection** and wait for the result. Check the source, target, mapping
   version and selection shown above the figures.
4. Review **Create**, **Update**, records that cannot go, and relationships carried or dropped.
   Open **What cannot be copied** or **What cannot move** to see reasons, counts and every affected
   item. Use an item's **Open the mapping** link to correct its choice, then check again.
5. Account for lost values too. A record may be copied without an unmapped value. Do not confirm
   merely because some records can go; resolve or deliberately accept each omission in scope.

![What to copy dialog with mapped types, whole workspace, chosen types and subtree choices](/docs/screens/model-mapping-selection-dialog.png)

*Above: Every mapped type is selected for Guide mapping. The captured selection dialog was cancelled.*

![Dry run reasons and affected items with links back to the mapping](/docs/screens/model-mapping-dry-run.png)

*Above: the example predicts 79 creates and lists missing values, invalid parents and dropped
relationships. Nothing has changed in either workspace.*

## Start and review the change sets

1. Choose **Start the copy…** or **Start the move…**. Read the confirmation's creates, updates,
   relationships and omissions, then fill **Name of the change set of workspace** for the target.
2. Confirm **Start the copy** or **Start the move**. Wait for the operation's result and inspect its
   actual counts and refusals. A changed mapping or model can prevent the start; refresh and review
   a new dry run before retrying. Nothing eligible to copy or move also prevents confirmation.
3. Open the target's produced change set. Review records, values and relationships, correct any
   remaining problems, validate, and publish through the normal approval process. Starting the
   copy alone has not made its records live.
4. For **Move**, also open the source deletion change set. Publish the target copy first, then
   review and publish the source deletions separately. Check any records kept because they changed
   since the dry run or because records staying behind depend on them. Do not assume every selected
   source record was deleted.

Follow [Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) for
review, validation and publication. Publishing either change set needs its own permissions and
any approvals required in that workspace.

Use **Mapping**, **Source**, **Target** and **Not copied** or **Not moved** to inspect the editor's
parts. Read the selected row's **Why this step**; evidence and alternatives explain a proposal,
without a numeric score. If a warning says the mapping names other releases, choose
**Use the releases the workspaces run**, review its rows and obtain a new dry run. Read-only
notices mean the deployment does not allow this flow; ask the operator before attempting a start.

Follow the started job to its result, inspect actual counts and any refusals, and open its
produced change sets. A finished job is not proof that every source item was copied or removed.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/previ:
---
title: Preview a type
description: Check a draft record page and table without changing live records.
reader: model-admin
---

Use preview to check a draft's appearance before applying it. You need **Model authoring**.
See [Record pages and tables](/docs/model/record-pages-and-tables/) for what preview reads.

1. Select the type in the model pane and choose **Preview**. A type listed in several applications
   is previewed in the application whose row you selected (a type another application only borrows
   for a relation view opens on the application that holds its records); when none is selected, in the one
   that holds the workspace's records of the type. Choose the application in the band to switch.
   If **The draft has … issues, so
   it cannot be previewed** appears, choose **Show issues**, fix the errors and return.
2. Choose **Workspace** and **Record**. The record's live values are drawn using the draft's
   definition. Check that the workspace is the one whose records you intend to inspect.
3. Use **Show an empty record** to see unfilled fields, especially for a new type. No value
   in a preview does not itself mean that the field or type is invalid.
4. Inspect **Record page** and **Table**, including long labels and records with missing optional
   values. Controls that would change data are disabled. Previewing does not save a record.
5. Choose **Edit layout** to change the draft's presentation, or **Back to definition** to
   return to the selected type. Review Issues after layout changes.

![Draft type preview over a selected live record](/docs/screens/model-type-preview.png)

Preview shows individual screens. The separate activation check decides whether all stored data
fits the release; a good-looking preview does not replace it.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/propo: --- title: Propose again with a newer workbook description: Replace the draft source and review renewed proposals without losing manual decisions. reader: model-admin --- Use a saved workbook draft when a corrected file needs the same modelling work. You need **Model authoring**. See [Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/) for proposal ownership. 1. Open the draft and read **History** before replacing its source. In **More actions**, choose **Upload a newer workbook…**. A draft without a source offers **Add a workbook…** instead. 2. Choose **Workbook**, an XLSX workbook or CSV file, and review **Compare with the records of**. Upload and wait for the new source to be profiled. If it fails, read the file error and retry with a corrected file; do not rely on the previous source's counts. 3. Inspect every sheet, changed header and list range. Existing reading instructions may no longer fit the columns. Check your row keys and reference matching before accepting proposals. 4. Choose **Propose again…**. Review **A new application**, **A new model**, **Additions to the model** or **Nothing: I will map it by hand**, with **Application name** where offered. Apply the intended choice. **Proposing from the workbook** pauses editing until it finishes. 5. Only elements still as proposed follow the new proposal. Manual edits remain yours and undone proposals stay undone. Review conflicting column choices in **Issues**, rather than assuming the engine replaced your decision. 6. Inspect **Proposed because**, **Evidence** and **History**, then obtain a [new dry run](/docs/guide/model/check-a-workbook-with-a-dry-run/) before loading. ![Draft menu with upload-newer-workbook and propose-again actions](/docs/screens/use-wb-draft-menu.png) For routine uploads through an already installed profile, use **Settings › Import profiles**, **Upload the next version…** and its comparison instead. Review changed or missing columns, unknown values and missing-record choices before accepting the next file. ## Get the example update If you started with the [example workbook](/docs/guide/model/start-a-draft-from-a-workbook/#get-the-example-workbook), download Haltestellen_Busbetrieb_Nord_next.xlsx and select it in **Workbook** in step 2. This fictional update renames **UIC-Nr** to **UIC number** on **Haltestellen** and adds **Capture note**, filled with **Preview only** on the first five data rows. The other two sheets are unchanged. Use it to practise reviewing a renamed column and an extra column. It does not correct the workbook's unresolved references. Check the key and mappings again, decide whether to ignore **Capture note**, and run a new dry run before loading anything.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/raise:
---
title: Raise a contract version
description: Release a changed consumer contract while keeping the previous version available.
reader: model-admin
---

Raise a consumer contract version when consuming systems must read a changed shape or operation.
You need **Model authoring** to edit and **Model release** in the destination workspace to
activate. Read [Consumer APIs](/docs/model/consumer-apis/#keep-an-earlier-version-available)
for the rules. Agree the change and changeover with the consuming teams first.

## Keep the previous version available

1. Open a draft based on the release whose contract you are changing. Select **Consumer APIs**,
   then the API and **Types and related**. Check **Contract version**. If the draft says
   **Checked once the draft is valid**, fix its issues before relying on the contract check.
2. Review your changes to types, fields, related blocks, operations, filters and events.
   **Needs contract version …** lists what existing consumers would notice. Choose
   **Raise to version …**, or open the API menu and choose **Raise contract version to …**.
   Alternatively, edit **Contract version** in **Settings**, enter a higher whole number
   and choose **Save**. The menu advances it by one.
3. Inspect **Earlier versions**. When the draft’s base release served the previous version,
   the editor retains that release’s definition, even if you already made breaking edits
   in this draft. Your edits belong to the new current version. A new API, or a version
   never served by the base release, has no previous definition to retain. Check the row
   rather than assuming every increase adds one.
4. Check the retained **Version** and **Superseded** day. If you have agreed an end date,
   edit **Sunset day**, enter a calendar date in year-month-day form and **Save**. Clear it
   to withdraw the announcement. The date does not stop service automatically.
5. Review **Issues**, **Schema**, **Message example** and the generated operation document.
   [Share the documents](/docs/guide/model/see-a-consumer-apis-documents/) with consuming teams.
   Every earlier version must still have the types, fields and relationships it reads;
   raising the number cannot repair missing sources.
6. Open **Install and activate…** or **Apply to this workspace…**. Review **Consumer APIs**
   for the destination as well as the comparison against the draft’s base. Install and
   activate only when the retained contracts still fit that workspace’s active contract.

![Earlier versions table showing a new current version and its retained predecessor](/docs/screens/model-consumer-earlier-versions.png)

After activation, the new version is available and the retained version keeps reading current
data in its original shape. It is not an old data snapshot. Existing webhooks bound to the
retained version keep delivering in that version’s shape. Installing alone changes no workspace.
Other workspaces keep their own active releases.

## Raise without retaining the previous version

Use this only when consumers are ready to lose the version being replaced. In
**Needs contract version …**, **Raise and stop serving version …** raises the version without
keeping its predecessor. The API menu offers **Raise to … and stop serving …** with a
confirmation. This does not remove other versions already in **Earlier versions**.

Review the draft’s History; **Undo** restores the saved raise step before activation.
After activation, consumers of a version no longer served lose their reads, and its webhooks
need the receiver owner’s review before resuming on the current version. For a separate,
announced removal later, follow
[Stop serving an earlier contract version](/docs/guide/model/stop-serving-an-earlier-contract-version/).

## If the release is refused

- **A consumer API needs a higher contract version**: read the named contract and differences.
  Raise the changed current contract or undo the breaking change, then check again.
- **a kept version is served as it was: restore it, or stop serving it**: the retained
  version’s output would change. Restore that definition and its sources, or agree to
  stop serving it. Raising the current version again does not fix this finding.
- An issue naming an earlier version and a missing type, field or relationship needs that
  source restored or that version removed. A lower version, duplicate retained number,
  retained number at or above the current version, or invalid date must be corrected.

A model administrator chooses the notice period with the consuming teams. refiroo does not
schedule removal or impose its own software compatibility period on your consumer contracts.

---
title: Raise a model language version
description: Review and reopen a workspace whose model uses an older supported conversion path.
reader: model-admin
---

Use this task when a workspace says **Cannot be opened** because its model language is older
than this refiroo version reads. It changes the stored definition format, not the records.
You need permission to install models at the instance level. See
[Model language versions](/docs/model/model-language-versions/).

Before starting, you need an older-language release already stored in this installation,
usually retained through an engine upgrade. New drafts and imports on this version accept
only the current language, **0.10**; importing an older document does not create a release
for this task. The repair affects every workspace sharing the stored release. Arrange a
backup and coordinate with their owners before confirming it.

1. Open the affected workspace and read why it cannot open. A model written by a newer refiroo
   version needs that version; this repair is only offered for an older, raisable definition.
2. Under **Bring it up to date**, choose **Review the change…**. If the page says the model
   cannot be brought up to date automatically, ask the operator or a specialist model author.
3. Wait for the preview, then inspect **Schema language**, **Consumer APIs rewritten**,
   **Workspaces that return** and **Records, change sets, publications: unchanged**.
   Review every named workspace because they share this stored release.
4. Choose **Raise and reopen** only after reviewing that scope, or **Cancel** to leave it.
   This special recovery edits the stored release in place. It is an exception to ordinary
   immutable releases, available before the first stable release.
5. If **The change could not be made** appears, read the diagnostic. An invalid result or one
   equal to another release is refused. **Try again** rereads a failed preview. If the release
   changed after review, inspect the new preview before confirming.
6. After success, reopen the workspace and check its applications. Its records, history, change
   sets and publications stay as they were. This did not migrate or publish its data.

![Model language recovery preview with affected workspaces and unchanged records, change sets and publications](/docs/screens/model-language-raise-review.png)

If no workspace is available, the operator may need the offline procedure in
[Model releases and rollback](/docs/run/model-releases-and-rollback/).
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/read-:
---
title: Read lists in a sheet
description: Check detected list ranges, exclude a list or choose how its cells become records.
reader: model-admin
---

Use this task when a sheet is laid out as several lists rather than one rectangular table.
Open its draft with **Model authoring**. See [Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/).

1. Select the sheet in **Source**. For a sheet laid out as lists, select a detected list
   and read **Under**, **Cells**,
   **Note** and **Loads**. The cell preview shades the loaded range and shows a darker header;
   surrounding cells help you see whether its boundaries are right.
2. For a loaded list, choose **Adjust list…**. Set **Header row**, **Last row**, **First column**
   and **Last column**. Check the displayed range before applying. The cell outline is not
   a draggable range editor.
3. Choose **Don't load this list** to exclude it. A **Not loaded** notice explains why nothing
   reads a range: it may be empty, treated as free answers or interpreted another way.
4. For a range that really is a list, choose **Load as a list…** and review its interpretation.
   Check **Loads** again to see the type, key and any fixed parent it creates records under.
5. Where offered, review **Read these N lists as one list under their headers**. This proposal
   is for at least three same-shaped lists under one title or no title. It creates header records
   and values beneath them; a value beneath two headers becomes two records. Translated category
   names and the role of a second header row are not loaded by this choice.
6. Inspect **Issues** and each source's **Dry run** after changing a range or interpretation.
   **Note** identifies a skipped second header or explanatory row; check that it is not data
   you needed to keep. These edits never rewrite the uploaded spreadsheet's cells.

![Proposed list of fictional local stop codes, with its shaded range, reading instructions and adjustment actions](/docs/screens/model-workbook-list-range.png)

**Example.** The fictional local-code sheet above has its column headings on row 3,
but the proposal uses row 1 as the header. Review **Adjust list…** before loading it;
a detected range is a starting point, not confirmation that the headings are right.

If the cells cannot be read, use the displayed retry after correcting the cause. A reasonable
range alone does not establish that every resulting record passes the dry run.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/remov:
---
title: Remove an element
description: Review the scope and stored-data impact before removing a model definition.
reader: model-admin
---

Remove unused definitions in a draft with **Model authoring**. See
[Types, attributes and relations](/docs/model/types-attributes-relations/) for released-element limits.

1. Select the element, inspect its uses, then open its operations menu. Choose the specific
   removal: **Remove type**, **Remove application**, an attribute's **Detach from …**, or the
   removal offered for that definition. These actions have different scopes.
2. Read the confirmation. Removing a type removes its views, detail page and relationships
   at either end. Detaching an attribute removes its use in that type's views and panels.
   Removing a navigation group leaves its collections available outside the group.
3. Cancel if any named effect is unwanted. Otherwise confirm, inspect the remaining model
   and open **Issues** for references that now need repair. Use **Undo** for an unwanted draft step.
4. A removal of released structure that stored data uses applies to the draft. **History** marks
   it **Needs a migration**, with the records, values and relationships that hold it. The counts
   include Live and open change sets in workspaces running this model. With nothing holding the
   element, the structural step has no migration mark; activation checks stored data again.
5. When installing, review **Activation needs a migration**, then **Install … and preview the
   migration…**. Inspect **Removed** for the records, values and relationships that would be lost.
   Resolve **Must be fixed** items first, then explicitly accept the listed loss only if intended.
   [Migrate a workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) explains confirmation.
   Cancel the review to leave workspace data unchanged.

![Type removal confirmation naming the views, page and relationships removed](/docs/screens/model-type-remove-confirm.png)

![Removal preview with Not kept selected, Removed items listed and loss acceptance ticked](/docs/screens/model-migration-loss.png)

*Above: Stop code is Not kept, and Removed lists 12 items. Must be fixed is zero and the loss acceptance is ticked, making Migrate available. The migration has not been confirmed.*

To hide a collection in one application, use **Stop listing in this application** where offered.
That is different from removing its type and records. A released listing can also need migration.
No removal in a saved draft alone changes the active workspace's records.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/renam:
---
title: Rename or re-key an element
description: Rename a label or change an identifying key with a reviewed migration after release.
reader: model-admin
---

A name is what people read. A key identifies a definition across releases. Changing a released
key needs a migration, even when there are no records; integrations naming it must change too. See [Types, attributes and relations](/docs/model/types-attributes-relations/).

1. Open the element in a draft with **Model authoring**. Read **Key editable until released**
   or **Released: a key change needs a migration** in its facts.
2. To change the displayed words, choose **Rename…** or select the editable title. Enter **Name**;
   a record type also offers **Plural name**. Save, then check navigation and views using it.
   A shared attribute rename appears on every type that attaches it.
3. To change identity, choose **Change key…** and enter the new key. Relation types offer
   **Change keys…**. Save and inspect the affected definitions and **Issues**. The editor follows
   references in the draft; check documents and external systems you maintain separately.
4. For a released key, read **Needs a migration when installed: integrations naming the key must change**.
   The step applies and **History** marks it **Needs a migration**. When installing, review the key
   change and the consumer APIs of the base release naming it. Coordinate integrations before
   confirming the [migration](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/). A label-only rename does
   not change the key.
5. If a save is refused, read **Not applied**. A key already in use needs a different key;
   for a newer draft, review [concurrent changes](/docs/guide/model/work-on-a-draft-with-others/).

![Rename a type with separate singular and plural names](/docs/screens/model-type-rename-dialog.png)

![Change key dialog for an unreleased type](/docs/screens/model-type-change-key-dialog.png)

![Install review naming a changed released key, its consumer API and a blocking contract-version finding](/docs/screens/model-install-key-change.png)

*Above: the key change for Stop number (UIC) names Stops API among the consumers that must change. The Consumer APIs check needs version 2, so installation cannot continue from this review.*

New keys are suggested from labels: lower-case words separated by hyphens, with accents removed.
A clash adds a number such as -2 or -3. Review the suggestion while it is editable; changing a
label after release does not generate a new identity.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/retir:
---
title: Retire or delete a release
description: Stop offering a release for new use or remove an unused release with confirmation.
reader: model-admin
---

Open **Settings › Model**, then the model's **Releases** and the release. These lifecycle
changes need installation permission. See [Releases](/docs/model/releases/).

1. Check its version, workspace use and whether it runs the default workspace. **Retire…**
   stops new selection but keeps existing users on the release. The default workspace's release
   cannot be retired; move that workspace to another usable release first if appropriate.
2. Choose **Retire…**, read the named release and confirm. Cancel keeps it available. Check
   the **Retired** state afterwards. Workspaces and change sets already using it keep working.
3. To offer it again, choose **Bring back** and check that it is available. A model with every
   release retired and no running workspace appears under **Retired** in the model list.
4. Use **Delete…** only for a release with no remaining use or references. **Run by no workspace**
   alone does not prove it is deletable: records, publications, change sets, profiles or mappings
   can still refer to it. Read the confirmation and any refusal before proceeding.
5. Confirm deletion only when the named unused release is no longer needed. Deleting its release
   does not delete editable drafts. If refused, retain it or retire it; do not delete history to
   force a release removal.

![Release retirement confirmation](/docs/screens/release-retire-dialog.png)

If the release changed state elsewhere, reload it and review the current state before retrying.
Retirement is reversible; deletion is not the same operation.

---
title: Retire or delete a workspace
description: Take a dataset out of active use while preserving its history, or delete an eligible empty one.
reader: model-admin
---

Open **Settings › Workspaces** with **Workspace administration**. See
[Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/) for active and retired states.

1. Open the workspace and check its name, key and default status. The default cannot be
   retired or deleted; [make another workspace default](/docs/guide/model/make-a-workspace-the-default/) first.
2. To keep the data but stop changes, choose **Retire…**. Read the confirmation and choose
   **Retire workspace**, or cancel. It leaves the active selector and becomes read-only.
   Records, change sets, publications and history remain readable through workspace management.
3. To resume work later, open the retired workspace in this list and choose **Reactivate**.
   Check the active state. Reactivation does not change its model release. Retirement also
   suspends its active webhook subscriptions; ask their administrator to resume them separately
   after reactivation.
4. Use **Delete…** only for an empty workspace that has never been published and has no change
   sets or webhook subscriptions. Read the page's explanation of anything preventing deletion.
   Even an emptied workspace with past publications must be retired instead.
5. If eligible and no longer needed, read the deletion confirmation's name and key, then
   choose **Delete workspace**. Cancel preserves it. Do not treat deletion as reversible retirement.

![Retire workspace confirmation](/docs/screens/workspace-retire-dialog.png)

If an action fails or reports a newer workspace version, review the current state before
retrying. A missing action can also mean insufficient permissions or disabled administration.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/reuse:
---
title: Reuse and change attributes
description: Attach a shared field and change its local rules or shared definition.
reader: model-admin
---

Work in a draft with **Model authoring**. Read
[Types, attributes and relations](/docs/model/types-attributes-relations/) before changing a shared field.

1. Select the receiving type and open **Attributes**. Choose **Attach an existing attribute…**
   and select the field. Already attached fields are not offered. Choose **Required** only if
   every record of this type must supply it, then apply the attachment.
2. Check **Shared with**. A shared attribute's name, value type and uniqueness are used by all
   attached types. Open **Attribute types** to inspect the common definition and its attachments.
3. In the type's table, select an editable **Required** or **Read-only** cell, choose **Yes**
   or **No**, then **Save**. The menu also offers **Make required** / **Make optional** and
   **Make read-only** / **Make editable**. These choices apply to this type's attachment.
4. To change the shared field, use **Rename…**, **Value type…**, **Make unique** or **Allow
   repeated values**. On the attribute type, **Features…** chooses **Searchable**, **Filterable**,
   **Sortable** and **Unique**. Inspect every attached type before applying a shared change.
5. Use **Move up** or **Move down** to order attributes. **Move to…**, or dragging a field onto
   a type in the model pane, moves the attachment; its columns and panel placement move with it.
   Check the destination rather than creating a duplicate attribute definition. For a released
   field, read **Needs a migration when installed**: moving the attachment removes its values
   from the original type's records. They cannot be carried onto a different type's records.
6. Review **Issues** and **History**. A released field change that affects stored data applies
   and is marked **Needs a migration**, with affected records, values and relationships.
   Installing the draft shows the migration to review. Check conversions, loss and records that
   break tighter rules before [confirming it](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/).
   Use **Undo** if the draft change is unwanted.

![Attach an existing shared attribute to a type](/docs/screens/model-attribute-attach-existing.png)

![Attribute operations including value type, local rules and list conversion](/docs/screens/model-attribute-menu.png)

**Detach from …** removes the attachment and its uses in that type's views and panels; it does
not mean remove the attribute from every type. Read the confirmation, or cancel to keep it.

## Set bounds and field guidance

1. Select the shared definition under **Attribute types**. For Whole number or Decimal number,
   edit **Minimum** or **Maximum** in **Settings**. Both open **Minimum and maximum…**. Enter
   either or both, or leave them empty to remove bounds, then **Apply**. A minimum greater
   than the maximum is invalid. All uses of the shared field receive these bounds.
2. Edit **Hidden** or **Help text** in the same Settings table and **Save**. These are shared
   presentation choices. Hidden leaves the field off record forms without deleting its data.
3. To provide guidance for just one type, select that type’s **Attributes** table and edit
   **Hidden** or **Help text** there. A local help text replaces the shared help; clearing it
   returns to shared help. A field hidden by the shared definition remains hidden even when
   the local cell says No. Review a populated and an empty record in Preview.
4. Check Issues and the release comparison. Bounds apply to stored values too; saving the draft
   does not convert or fill data. Correct incompatible records or review a migration before
   activating the release.

![Shared attribute Settings with bounds, field guidance and a released-key migration notice](/docs/screens/model-attribute-settings.png)

*Above: Height (m) has a minimum of 0, a maximum of 4500, Hidden set to No and help text. Its facts say Released: a key change needs a migration.*

The shared definition’s **Attach to a type…** is another way to reuse it. **Change key…** is
also available after release, with a migration and a warning that integrations naming the key
must change. See [Rename or re-key an element](/docs/guide/model/rename-or-re-key-an-element/). **Remove attribute type** removes the common definition where
allowed; review its attachments and the confirmation. Detaching from one type is the smaller
change when other types still need it.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/revie:
---
title: Review the assistant's workbook design
description: Check the proposed types, source coverage and record changes before accepting an assistant's load.
reader: model-admin
---

Use this task when a workbook needs a new or extended model. The assistant proposes how its
sheets, columns and records fit the workspace. You review that design before anything is
installed or loaded. For the manual editor route, use
[Start a draft from a workbook](/docs/guide/model/start-a-draft-from-a-workbook/).

You need **Use AI proposals**, **Bulk and import** and **Work in change sets** in the workspace.
Model changes also need **Model authoring**, **Model release** in the workspace and permission
to install model releases at instance level. The assistant and job creation must be enabled.

The whole file, your words and the workspace's model go to Claude Code. It reads workspace
records as needed. Assistant turns may incur charges; tasks and files normally remain for
90 days, and session files and transcripts remain while the task can continue. See
[About AI in refiroo](/docs/run/ai/) for the full account of permissions, costs, retention
and data leaving the instance.

## Give the file and its purpose

1. Open the intended workspace and its **⋯** menu beside the workspace selector. Choose
   **Import**. With the assistant enabled, **Load a workbook** opens first.
2. Choose an XLSX or CSV **Workbook**. Check **Into** names the intended workspace.
3. In **Tell the assistant about this file (optional)**, explain whether this updates existing
   records or adds something new. Say which column identifies a record and how new types
   should relate to the existing ones, if you know. A stable key matters more than a row number.
   A list of records not yet held needs a key too; otherwise a later load can create them again.
4. Read what is sent, then choose **Read the workbook**. **Import without the assistant…**
   uses the manual import instead. **Cancel** sends nothing.
5. Wait on the task page. The bar below the top bar shows the current stage and next action.
   It follows you into the model editor and change set. **Stop** ends the current turn;
   it does not discard the task.

*Example: a file of stop names in several languages may extend the existing stop model with
related name records. Check that those names attach to the existing stops and that each
language column is accounted for.*

## Review the model before accepting

1. Read **The assistant’s proposal**, including each type's fields, relationships and record
   counts. The assistant can reuse the current model, extend it or propose a new one. Do not
   assume each sheet should become a separate type.
2. Read **Checks**, especially **Needs attention**, and **What the load does**. Compare new
   records with existing records matched: unexpected new records can mean an intended update
   did not find its records. Inspect **One name twice in one type** if shown; the finding says
   whether those records sit at the top level or under parents. Decide whether they represent
   different things or an unwanted duplicate. Checks and examples do not establish that the
   design means what you intended.
3. Read **Columns left out** and the questions with their assumed answers. Check every
   intentional omission. Conflicting workbook names or values are not automatically errors
   to normalise: explain whether they are intended.
4. Open **Show the model change**. Choose **Open in the model editor** to inspect the draft's
   types, fields and relationships, or edit them. The draft belongs to this task; a second task
   cannot write it while this task holds it. **Close** in the editor returns to the task.
   **No type, attribute or relationship changes** means the summary has no structural changes
   to list; the draft can still change views or layout. Open it in the editor to review those.
   For a task without a workbook or a model draft, the proposal says **No change to the model.**
   and has no model editor button.
5. Answer the questions or use **Tell the assistant what to change** under **Correct the model**.
   The same session revises the design and rereads your editor changes. Check the new proposal
   and its record and relationship counts again.

![Workbook proposal with type counts and an expanded table of model changes](/docs/screens/model-assistant-workbook-proposal.png)

*Above: the reference workbook proposal adds types and relationships, adds Step-free access
and Remark to Stop, and makes FSO number and System key optional. The expanded table shows
these changes.*

The assistant reads the workbook, the model and workspace records, then turns the file into
proposed records and relationships. It changes the draft where needed and asks the engine to
check every proposed record and relationship without saving them. It writes no import profile.
Review the resulting fields and counts: one source row need not mean one output record.
This does not edit your original workbook.

## Check the records and accept

1. Review **What the load does**: new records, existing records matched, new relationships,
   refused items and rows read. New relationships include the links of new records to their
   parents; the summary gives their count separately too. In the type table, compare **New**, **Matched**, **Changed**,
   **Refused** and **Linked to**. Open a type's row with a click, Enter or Space to see example
   records, their values, links and the cells they come from. These are examples, not every record.
2. Expand **Where each part of the file goes** to inspect the sheet and cell ranges that supply
   records or relationships. Compare them with the file and **Columns left out**. Read the
   reasons and source cells of refused items and tell the assistant what to correct.
3. Check how the assistant matched existing records. Explain which fields identify the same
   record when names repeat. Questions ask about choices the file and your instructions leave
   open; they do not ask you to design a loading mechanism.
4. If the draft changed after the check, the card warns you. Accepting checks every record and
   relationship again first. If any is refused, nothing is installed or loaded. Ask for a new
   proposal before accepting if your edit changes the result you want to review.
5. Choose **Accept and load to change set** when the design and proposed records are right. The engine installs
   a release if the model changed and loads exactly the checked records and relationships into
   a new change set as one batch, without another assistant turn. It activates and publishes
   nothing. If the batch refuses any item because the data changed, none of the batch is loaded
   and its change set is discarded. A release already installed can remain installed.
   Whole-type or partial reshapes follow [the model-move steps](/docs/guide/model/change-a-model-with-the-assistant/).
6. On the loaded page, compare the actual counts with the checked result. Both include parent
   links in the relationship total. Choose **Review the change set**, inspect its changes and
   validate. Follow the workspace’s approval rules. If the workspace runs a different model
   version, review offers **Move** followed by the workspace name, the proposed version and
   **and publish…**. Use it to preview the migration, then choose **Migrate and publish** to
   switch the workspace’s model and publish together. You need model-release and publication
   permission and any required approval. A separate activation first is not required; follow
   [Migrate a workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) for the preview and blockers.
   The assistant does not activate, approve or publish.

If the engine cannot apply the proposal, its reason appears on the page. Tell the assistant
what to change rather than accepting an unusable design. A failed turn can **Try again as it was**;
a stopped one can **Go on as it was**. If a required permission is lost, the page names what
is needed and offers a link to copy for the person who can load.

## Load another file, or correct a load

An assistant load saves no import profile. Send the next file of the same layout to the
assistant again, explaining how it should match the records already held.

A separately saved import profile can still let the engine recognise a layout before starting
a session. Its load confirmation can install and activate a changed model before importing;
review that confirmation even though this path makes no assistant call. If the saved layout
no longer fits, **Read it with the assistant** starts its reading. Before loading a saved
layout, **Back to the proposal** and the words box let you reconsider it.

![Loaded task with record counts, change-set review and correction actions](/docs/screens/model-assistant-workbook-loaded.png)

*Above: the reference workbook task has prepared records in a change set. Live data is
unchanged until publication.*

For a wrong load that is not published, enter a correction and choose **Discard and load again**.
Confirm only after reading that this removes the entire change set, including manual edits
in it. The assistant then revises the proposal and checks the records again. Review it and
choose **Accept and load to change set** before reviewing the replacement change set. **Discard the change
set** ends the task instead. A stopped load discards the change
set it was making and returns to the accepted proposal. Once published, the task offers new
work; it cannot discard that publication through this correction flow.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/see-a:
---
title: See a consumer API’s documents
description: Review the output shape, example and operations, then hand over the active contract.
reader: model-admin
---

Review the generated documents before asking another team to build a connection. The
schema describes the business object's fields; the message example illustrates that shape;
the OpenAPI document describes the offered requests and their responses. Together they
show what your consumer declaration produces. See
[Consumer APIs in the model](/docs/model/consumer-apis/) for how each choice affects the output.

You need access to the model draft to inspect its documents. Editing needs **Model authoring**.
Viewing a document is separate from giving a consuming client permission to read workspace data.

## Review the draft's output

1. In the model editor, select **Consumer APIs**, then the API. Check the selected API's
   name and **Contract version**. You are reviewing a draft; its changes are not yet live.
2. Open **Schema**. Compare the field names and types with **Fields**. Check required and
   nullable values, the parent and the shape of each related block. A single related
   record is an object or null; a many-valued relationship is an array. Review the whole
   object, because Get by ID, list items and lookup results share this shape.
3. Open **Message example**. It shows one object generated from the declared field types,
   not a record fetched from a workspace. Check that all intended fields and related
   blocks are present. Do not use the placeholder values as evidence that real records
   have those values, or that a lookup finds a particular record.
4. Use **Copy**, **Download schema.json** or **Download example.json** to share the
   selected document. Check the API and contract version before handing it over. After
   any draft edit, inspect the newly generated documents again.

![Generated schema tab for a draft consumer API](/docs/screens/model-consumer-tab-schema.png)

Above: the schema generated for Stops API in the reference model.

**Reference-data example:** the generated schema describes the stop number as an integer that can be empty. Its public name comes from **Output name** and its type from the selected source. It also describes operator as one object or empty and modes as a list. These are the shapes consuming teams rely on; ask the integrator to review the detailed document.

![Generated message example with placeholder values](/docs/screens/model-consumer-tab-example.png)

Above: the reference API's generated example. Its values illustrate types, not live data.

The example uses placeholder values based on field types. They do not prove that a real record exists or has those values. For comparison, the reference stop Chur has stop number 8509000. Use real records as a separate check when agreeing the contract with its consumers.

## Review the operations as well as the object

1. Return to **Schema** and find **Against what consumers read now**. Read any compatibility
   diagnostics. **Compatible: consumers of version … notice nothing they rely on** means
   this check found no incompatible change; it is not a live connection test.
2. Choose **download the draft's OpenAPI** beneath the compatibility information. This
   document includes the operations, parameters and response shapes, rather than just
   the business object. Share it with the integrator alongside the schema and example.
3. Compare the offered operations with **Operations** and their parameter names with
   **Filters**. Check list scope and ordering, lookup rules, events and contract version.
   An object schema alone cannot tell a consumer which list or filter to use.
4. If a change needs a higher contract version, follow
   [Raise a contract version](/docs/guide/model/raise-a-contract-version/), then download
   the documents again. Agree the new address and changeover with consuming teams before
   activation. Raising retains the base release’s previous definition by default. Check
   **Earlier versions** on **Types and related**; a new, unserved API has no previous
   version to retain. The draft tabs describe the current definition. Give the integrator
   each served version’s own document for the earlier contract review.

**Reference-data example:** an integrator checks that Stops API can read a known stop, list stops, look up its identifiers, resolve several inputs and follow the declared changes. The selected fields, related blocks, filters and notifications should match the agreement. Use [Consumer APIs for integrators](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/) for worked requests and answers. Every organisation’s declaration is its own contract; hand over your generated documents.

## Hand over the active contract
