1. After the release is installed and activated, open **Settings › Connections › Consumer APIs**.
   This read-only page names the active release. Use **Open the release** to check it is
   the release you intended; it does not provide the draft's Schema and Message example tabs.
2. Find the API's section and version. Use **Base URL** and **OpenAPI document** to copy
   its addresses or open the document. The **Route** / **What it does** table lists its
   operations; a route description opens that operation in the API reference.
3. Give the integrator the active API's base address and operation document, the workspace
   they should read, and the agreed contract version. Ask the security administrator to
   confirm the client has this API's grant in that workspace. A model release does not
   create grants, and a role alone does not open consumer data.

![Active consumer API with release, version, base address, operation document and routes](/docs/screens/model-consumer-active-documents.png)

Earlier contracts are marked deprecated in their generated operation documents, with the
announced sunset day when one is set. Deprecated means still served: the administrator must
explicitly stop the version through a model release. Ask the integrator to check the
[version index and generated documents](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/#earlier-contract-versions)
for each required version. Do not assume an installed older release alone serves that version.

Opening the operation document does not require signing in. Reading data still requires the consuming client’s grant in the intended workspace. Share the addresses using the page’s copy controls; see [Consumer APIs for integrators](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/) for discovery and authentication.

## If a document is unavailable

- **The draft has issues** means the documents cannot be generated. Open **Issues**,
  correct the problem or undo the last step, then return to the document. Raising a
  contract version does not repair an invalid definition.
- A document load error is not a successful review. Read the message, correct the cause
  if it names a draft problem, then retry. If copying is unavailable, select the text
  or download the file instead.
- **The active release declares no consumer API** means the active model has none.
  Use **Open model** to inspect its definitions. A draft API is not live merely because
  its documents can be generated.
- If a live read is refused, check the workspace, API grant and active contract with the
  integrator. The OpenAPI document itself is readable without signing in; opening it
  successfully does not prove that the client can read data.

*Source for the reference examples: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0.*
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/split:
---
title: Split, merge and move types
description: Reshape draft types and their containment without confusing definitions with records.
reader: model-admin
---

Use these actions to reshape definitions in a draft. You need **Model authoring**. They do not
move live records merely by saving. Read [Types, attributes and relations](/docs/model/types-attributes-relations/).

## Split a type

1. Select the type and choose **Split…** from its menu. It needs attributes to split.
2. Enter **New type’s name** and, where needed, **Plural name**. Choose **Attributes that move
   to it**. The selected attachments belong to the new type after the split.
3. Enter **Relation name** from the original type, **Reverse name** and **Cardinality** for the
   connection between them. Apply and inspect both types, their relationship and layouts.
4. If stored data uses the released type, **History** marks the step **Needs a migration**.
   Installing proposes related records holding the moved values. In the preview, open **Created**:
   a source record with no moved value gets no new record; with **Many to one**, records holding
   identical moved values share one new record. Its name comes from the first moved value,
   or the source record's name if that value supplies no name.

![Split dialog with moved attributes and the connecting relationship](/docs/screens/model-type-split-dialog.png)

## Merge definitions

1. Select the type to absorb and choose **Merge into…**.
2. Choose **Into** carefully. Its attributes, relations and layout join the chosen type.
3. Apply and inspect the combined type and **Issues**. Use **Undo** if the result is unwanted.
4. When stored data uses the released type, review its **Needs a migration** mark in **History**.
   Installing proposes that its records become the receiving type, keeping their identities
   and history. Check the proposed destination and all outcomes in the migration preview.

![Merge dialog choosing the receiving type](/docs/screens/model-type-merge-dialog.png)

## Move a type

1. Choose **Move to…**. In **Find a target**, type a name, move with Up/Down and select with
   Enter. A destination can put the type under another type or at an application's top level.
2. For a contained destination, choose **Containment relation**, either a new relation or a
   suitable existing one. When several applications list the type, inspect **Take it out of**.
3. For a released type, read **Needs a migration when installed**. The notice explains where
   the records go: a top-level destination releases them from their old parent; under another
   type, records whose existing parent is not allowed are refused in the migration preview.
4. Confirm and check the type and the types under it. Dragging a type onto a type, an application
   or the space beside the tree opens the same decision. Use **Move to…** on a phone or by keyboard.
5. If stored data uses the type, the step applies with a **Needs a migration** mark in **History**.
   Installing shows the proposed destination application and placement. Review the migration:
   moving to the top level removes the old parent and its containment relationship. The records
   go to the named application even when several applications list the type.

![Move dialog with target search and containment relation](/docs/screens/model-type-move-to-dialog.png)

![Move dialog warning that a released type needs a migration when installed](/docs/screens/model-move-needs-migration.png)

*Above: Stop code is moving from under Stop in Network to the top level of Systems. The notice explains that its records move with it and become top-level records when the migration is confirmed.*

Saving any of these steps changes the draft only. Use **Install … and preview the migration…**
to review the proposed changes before [migrating the workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/).
Resolve items under **Must be fixed** and inspect any **Removed** items before accepting loss.
**Not moved** or **Not applied** explains an edit that could not be saved. **Stop listing in this application** only removes a listing;
**Remove type** removes its definition, views, page and relations at either end. Neither is a
shortcut for moving existing data between models; use [Copy and move](/docs/model/model-mappings/).
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/start: --- title: Start a draft from a workbook description: Review a proposed model and its source mapping, check refused rows and load into a change set. reader: model-admin --- Use this task when a workbook needs a new model, an additional application or new fields and types. See [Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/) for what the draft, source and dry run keep. You need the permissions to administer the model, activate it in the target workspace and load records there. ## Get the example workbook You can use your own file. To follow the illustrated example, download Haltestellen_Busbetrieb_Nord.xlsx. Save the file, then select it in **Workbook** in step 2 below. It has three sheets: **Haltestellen** (stops), **Namen** (names) and **Lokale Codes** (local codes). This is a deliberately messy workbook from a fictional bus company. Stop names and numbers come from the guide's [example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/); lines, local codes and fare zones are invented. Review its proposals rather than treating them as an approved model. Dry-run counts and refused rows depend on your mappings and comparison workspace; they may differ from the pictures. For the next-upload exercise, a second file is available in [Propose again with a newer workbook](/docs/guide/model/propose-again-with-a-newer-workbook/#get-the-example-update). ## Start the draft 1. Open **Settings**, **Model**. Choose **New from a workbook**. **New draft** starts model authoring without this workbook proposal task. 2. Enter **Draft name** and choose the **Workbook**, an Excel workbook or CSV file. 3. Under **Propose**, choose **A new application**, **A new model**, **Additions to the model** or **Nothing: I will map it by hand**. Read the explanations: a new application adds to the starting model, while a new model starts empty. Set **Application name** where offered. 4. Choose **Compare with the records of**. The dry run uses that workspace; choose the intended data, not simply a similarly named workspace. Check **Starting document** and **Base release** where offered so the draft starts from the definitions you intend. 5. Choose **Create and propose**, or **Cancel** to leave without creating the draft. Wait for the file to be read and the editor to open. If the upload fails, correct the reported file problem and try again before proceeding. ![Model list with New from a workbook and New draft](/docs/screens/use-wb-model-list.png) *Above: Model lists the releases and drafts installed or saved on the reference instance.* ![Workbook dialog with a selected file, proposal mode and starting release](/docs/screens/use-wb-dialog.png) *Above: Haltestellen_Busbetrieb_Nord.xlsx is a fictional operator file. The capture cancels this dialog.* ## Inspect the source and proposals 1. In the source pane, open each sheet tab. Read the columns, their filled and distinct counts, and the source's header row. Distinguish sheet rows from the data rows actually loaded. 2. Select a proposed type in the model tree. Read **Proposed because** and choose **Evidence** to inspect the values that support it. Check that the proposed key identifies the intended record, and that names, fields, parents and related records have the intended meaning. 3. Select a source column to inspect its mapping. Use its menu's **Map to…** to change what it feeds, or drag it onto a type. Check any splitting of multi-value cells, replacements of placeholders and creation of missing related records. Ignore columns you do not intend to load. 4. Open **Issues, history and dry run**, then **History**, to review the steps. Use **Undo** to reverse an unwanted step and **Redo** to restore it. Closing the editor keeps the saved draft. ![Source pane on the second sheet showing column statistics and Proposed marks](/docs/screens/use-wb-source-namen.png) *Above: Namen is the second sheet of the fictional workbook. Its columns need their own review; a reasonable mapping on the first sheet does not establish that this sheet is correct.* For an explanation of proposal marks and key evidence, see [Proposed steps](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/#proposed-steps-are-decisions-to-review). [How workbook proposals are made](/docs/model/workbook-proposals/) explains the patterns, recognition limits and alternatives behind the evidence. ## Resolve issues and check every source 1. In the bottom panel, choose **Issues**. Fix or undo the steps causing reported issues. **No issues** establishes that the draft is valid, not that every row loads. 2. Choose **Dry run**. Check the draft version and comparison workspace. Wait for the current check to finish; a failed or outdated result is not a result for your latest mapping. 3. Read every source's counts. Select a figure to inspect the rows behind it. Open the red refused-row figure to read each reason. 4. Correct a wrong mapping, unresolved reference or source value. After a source-file correction, use the editor menu's **Upload a newer workbook…**. **Propose again…** can reconsider the file while retaining your edits. Review any new issues and the refreshed dry run. 5. Continue only when you understand the predicted changes and any rows that remain refused. Nothing has been written to the workspace's records by the dry run. ![Dry-run refused rows with their reason and source row numbers](/docs/screens/use-wb-dry-refused.png) *Above: nine Namen rows in the fictional workbook have no matching reference. They would be refused; a valid model does not resolve those references automatically.* When the mapping and dry run are ready, follow [Load a workbook into a change set](/docs/guide/model/load-a-workbook-into-a-change-set/). ## Correct list ranges and column instructions 1. If a sheet contains several lists, choose **Lists** and open each detected list. Read its range and **Loads**. Choose **Adjust list…** to correct the header, last row, first column and last column, then check the range before applying. 2. Use **Don't load this list** for a range to exclude, **Load as a list…** to choose its interpretation, or choose the proposal alternative **Read these N lists as one list under their headers** for at least three lists of the same shape under one title (or no title). These are source instructions; they do not edit cells in the original workbook. 3. Open a column and choose **Map to…**. Review whether it supplies a name, attribute, parent, related record or relationship flag. Check **Matched by**, any naming column and whether missing related records may be created. Select **Ignore** for columns to leave out. 4. Set **Split a cell on** only for genuinely separate values. Open **Add a value map…** or **Edit value map…** to map **Text in the file** to **Becomes**. Check that placeholders are treated as intended, rather than becoming real values. 5. Inspect **Key** and its uniqueness message before **Use as the key of the rows**. Reopen **Dry run** for every source tab. **was** compares a figure with the previous result; open refused rows and use their sheet, row number and reason to make a correction. A workbook describing a model, lists laid out for reading and repeated-parent tables can lead to different proposals. Check the inferred structure rather than assuming one sheet means one type. [Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/) explains those choices. ## Use the assistant instead If the built-in assistant is enabled, you can [review its proposed workbook design](/docs/guide/model/review-an-assistants-workbook-design/) before accepting a model and load. The rules-based draft route above does not call AI or offer AI naming suggestions.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/stop-:
---
title: Stop serving an earlier contract version
description: Announce an earlier consumer contract’s end, remove it in a draft and activate the change.
reader: model-admin
---

Use this task after consuming teams have moved off an earlier version. You need **Model authoring**
to edit and **Model release** in each workspace where you activate the change. Stopping a version
removes its reads without deleting records or stopping the other versions. Read
[Earlier versions](/docs/model/consumer-apis/#keep-an-earlier-version-available) before starting.

## Announce the end date

1. Open a draft based on the workspace’s active release. Select **Consumer APIs**, the API,
   then **Types and related**. In **Earlier versions**, check **Version** and **Superseded**
   to identify the version you intend to retire. This table does not stop the current version;
   [raise it first](/docs/guide/model/raise-a-contract-version/) if it needs a replacement.
2. Agree a notice period with every consuming team, including owners of webhook receivers.
   You choose that period; refiroo does not enforce a minimum for your consumer contracts.
3. Select that row's **Sunset day** value or its pencil. In **Sunset day (YYYY-MM-DD)**,
   enter the agreed calendar date and choose **Save**. Clear it and save to withdraw the
   announcement; the table shows a dash when no day is set. A date that is not a valid
   calendar day stays in the form with **Not saved** and the reason; the previously saved
   value remains unchanged. Correct it and save, or **Cancel**. The date announces the end
   in the response's Sunset header after activation; the version stays served until you
   stop it explicitly, whatever the day.
4. Review and [install and activate](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/) the
   announcement in the intended workspaces. Integrators then see the planned end date in
   the contract’s documents and responses. The date alone never turns the version off.

![Earlier versions with Superseded, Sunset day and Stop serving](/docs/screens/model-consumer-earlier-versions.png)

## Remove the version when consumers are ready

1. Open a new draft from the release that still serves the earlier version. Check the API
   and the intended row in **Earlier versions** again.
2. Choose that row’s **Stop serving**. Read the confirmation naming the version and warning
   that its consumers lose access once the draft is active. Choose **Cancel** to keep the
   row, or confirm **Stop serving** to remove it from this draft. Live workspaces are unchanged.
3. If you removed the wrong row, choose **Undo** or use the draft’s **History** to undo that
   saved step. Check that the version and its sunset day are back before continuing.
4. Review **Issues**, then open **Install and activate…**. Its Consumer APIs list names the API
   and says it **stops serving version …** and its consumers get `CONTRACT_VERSION_NOT_FOUND`,
   not **Compatible**; the activation dialog of each workspace says the same. Confirm that
   this is the removal you agreed. A finding that a kept version changed needs repair;
   raising the current version again does not repair it.
5. Install and activate the release in each intended workspace. Installation alone does
   not stop reads. Check each workspace’s active release; a workspace left on the old
   release keeps serving the version.
6. Ask the integration administrator to review affected webhooks with their receiver owners.
   A webhook whose accepted version stopped is suspended. Resuming accepts the current
   version after its events and filters pass validation; the receiver must be ready for
   that shape. Follow [Find out why a webhook paused](/docs/guide/administer/find-out-why-a-webhook-paused/).

An earlier version’s reads and change feed stop after activation. Keeping an older release
installed or an older publication does not keep that route available. Other served versions
continue reading the same stored data.

## Restore service after activation

Draft **Undo** alone cannot change a live workspace. Prepare a release that retains the original
definition and its model sources again, review its compatibility against the workspace, then
activate it. Do not reuse the earlier number for a different contract. Check suspended webhooks
separately; a restored route does not itself resume delivery. If the required source fields or
relationships have been removed, restore them too or agree a different recovery with the consumers.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/turn-:
---
title: Turn an attribute into a list
description: Replace a field definition with a relationship to a reusable list type.
reader: model-admin
---

Use a list type when people should choose maintained records instead of entering a free value.
For example, a stop's operator may be a relationship to operator records. This is a modelling
choice, not a special value type. See [Types, attributes and relations](/docs/model/types-attributes-relations/).

1. In a draft, select the type and open **Attributes**. Open the attribute's menu and choose
   **Turn into a list type…**. You need **Model authoring**.
2. Enter **List type’s name** and **Plural name**. Enter **Relation name** from the original
   type and **Reverse name** from the list records back to it.
3. Review **Which records may be chosen**. Leave it unrestricted to offer any list record,
   or add the offered criteria. A new list type initially offers criteria on its name.
4. Apply and inspect the new type and relationship. Check the original type's fields and
   layouts and resolve **Issues** before previewing or installing.
5. If the released attachment holds values, the step applies and **History** marks it
   **Needs a migration**. Saving the draft does not populate live list records. Use **Undo**
   to reverse an unwanted draft step.
6. When installing, review **Activation needs a migration** and choose **Install … and preview
   the migration…**. The preview includes the proposed list conversion. Open **Created** to
   inspect the list records and relationships it creates: one record per distinct value,
   named by the value, connected to every source record holding it. The values leave the
   source records. Review any loss or items to fix, then
   [confirm the migration](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) when acceptable.

![List conversion dialog with list names and relationship names](/docs/screens/model-attribute-list-type-dialog.png)

![Migration preview with split and list-conversion proposals and the Created outcome selected](/docs/screens/model-migration-created.png)

*Above: the draft splits Code system from Stop code and turns Code kind values into list records. Created lists 28 new records and relationships across both changes; nothing has changed in the workspace yet.*
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/undo-:
---
title: Undo and review the draft history
description: Inspect saved steps and undo changes with their dependent steps.
reader: model-admin
---

Use history to understand and correct a draft before releasing it. You need **Model authoring**.
The [model editor](/docs/model/the-model-editor/) saves actions as steps; an installed release stays fixed.

1. Expand **Issues and history**, or **Issues, history and dry run** with a workbook. Choose
   **History**. Steps appear newest first with their author, time and state: **Applied**,
   **Undone** or **JSON edit**. One step may include several related changes. A released-element
   change that affects stored data also shows **Needs a migration**, with the records, values
   and relationships that hold the element. A released key change needs a migration even when
   those counts are zero; integrations naming the key must change with it.
2. Use **Earlier steps** to read older entries. **No steps yet.** means there is no saved step
   in this history. A document edit appears as **JSON edit**, rather than a list of visual actions.
3. To reverse the latest step, choose **Undo** in the header. To reverse an older step, use
   its **Undo** action in History. Check the resulting model and Issues afterwards.
4. If **Undo the steps that depend on it too?** appears, read every dependent step. Confirm
   only if all those reversals are wanted. Cancel keeps them. A field added later cannot stay
   attached to a type whose creation is being undone.
5. Choose **Redo** to restore the available undone step. A new edit clears redo history.
   If the draft changes elsewhere, review its newer history before retrying.

![History showing an applied move, its Needs a migration mark and affected data counts](/docs/screens/model-history.png)

*Above: moving Stop code to the top level of Systems is marked Needs a migration, with 12 records, 36 values and 12 relationships holding the type. Undo is available.*

![History after Undo with the move and its migration mark crossed out and Redo available](/docs/screens/model-history-undone.png)

*Above: the move is Undone and its migration mark is crossed out. Stop code is back under Stop in Network in the draft; Redo is available.*

![Confirmation listing steps dependent on the step being undone](/docs/screens/model-history-undo-dependants.png)

Undo changes the draft and takes the undone step's part out of the proposed migration. Redo
restores it; the install or Apply review reflects the steps that stand now. A migration mark
records a step's impact; activation checks the workspace's current data again. See
[Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/) before installing marked steps.

Undo neither changes an installed release nor reverses published records.
For concurrent edits, see [Work on a draft with others](/docs/guide/model/work-on-a-draft-with-others/).
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/work-:
---
title: Work on a draft with others
description: Recover an edit refused because another person saved a newer draft.
reader: model-admin
---

Several model authors can open the same draft. Each save checks the version it was based on,
so an older edit cannot silently replace a newer one. See [The model editor](/docs/model/the-model-editor/).

1. When **Another change came first** appears, stop repeating the original action. Your change
   was not applied. The notice lists steps applied since you opened the draft, and the model
   beneath it shows the newer version. A rename names both the old and new name, so you
   can identify the definition before deciding whether to retry.
2. Read those steps and inspect the affected definitions. Check whether your intended change
   is still needed and whether its target still means the same thing.
3. Choose **Apply mine again** to try your change against that version, or **Discard mine**
   to leave it out. A further edit by someone else can refuse the retry too; review again.
4. Open **History** to confirm the saved result and **Issues** to check its validity.

![Newer draft notice with applied steps and retry or discard actions](/docs/screens/model-conflict-editor.png)

In the specialist [JSON view](/docs/model/json-view/), **A newer draft version exists** preserves
your local text. Choose **Copy local JSON** before **Reload saved version** if you need that text.
Reloading reads the saved draft; it does not merge your local text into it. Review and reapply
only the changes still needed, then save against the current version.

![JSON editor preserving local work after a version conflict](/docs/screens/model-json-newer-version.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/add-a-l:
---
title: Add a language with a workbook
description: Fill empty columns to create owned records under selected parents.
reader: steward
---

Fill in records that belong to each exported row, arranged as columns beneath chosen parents.
This works for any model declaring that ownership and placement; languages are one example.
Read [Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/#a-workbook-for-people).

1. Open the owner records' collection. Choose **Workspace actions › Export** and **For editing in a spreadsheet**.
2. Open **Advanced: columns and sheets**. Select the owned-record relationship and choose
   **Columns per parent** for its layout. Choose the fields to fill.
3. Under **More columns for these …**, search for and select the additional parent records.
   Existing parents arrive automatically; added parents contribute empty columns. The parent
   must already be available to the model and workspace.
4. Choose **Start export**, then download the completed workbook. Check each column heading:
   it identifies the parent and any higher level used to distinguish it.
5. Fill the empty cells for the intended rows. Each filled owned-record entry becomes a record
   under that column's parent, connected to its row's owner. Leave cells blank where you want
   no addition; blank cells do not remove existing ordinary values.
6. Import with **Profile: None**. Check the **Read as exported …** preview, creations and
   refused cells, then choose **Load the file**. Review the actual results and, if working in
   a change set, publish through the usual review process.

**Example:** in the reference data, a parent groups stop names in a language. Adding that parent
as columns lets a steward fill names for the exported stops. This layout comes from ownership
and hierarchy rules, rather than a special language feature.

If the workbook would exceed Excel's 16,384 columns, the export job fails. Choose fewer parents
or fields and export again. If a cell summarises several owned records, edit their sheet instead.

![Workbook export showing Columns per parent, fields and an additional parent](/docs/screens/workbook-columns-per-parent.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/add-a-r:
---
title: Add a record
description: Create a record with its fields, parent and required relationships in one save.
reader: steward
---

Create one item of the type declared by your model. See [Records](/docs/use/records/) for
field rules and [Hierarchies](/docs/use/hierarchies/) for placement.

1. Open the intended workspace, application and collection. Check **Live** or the named change
   set before choosing **Add …**. If you see **Propose a new …**, follow
   [Propose a change](/docs/guide/use/propose-a-change/) first.
2. The **New …** form opens. Enter the name and editable fields. Required fields must have
   values, including at least one field where the form gives that rule. Read-only fields
   cannot be filled through this form. Keep numbers, dates and Yes/No values in their proper controls.
   Read help below the fields before filling them. Fields hidden by the model are omitted;
   ask the model administrator if a required piece of information cannot be supplied.
3. Where **Parent** is offered, select the allowed parent type and search for the record.
   Some types require a parent and cannot be created at the top. **No parent available** means
   you must first provide an allowed parent. Open the hierarchy view and use **Add …**
   for its top-level type, then add the child records beneath it. If that action is absent,
   check your editing access and ask the model administrator about the view’s actions and placement rules.
4. Complete required relationships in the same form. Search only offers eligible records in
   this workspace and context. A general search result elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility.
5. Choose **Create**. Fields, parent and required relationships save together. A refusal leaves
   no partially created record: correct the named missing value, duplicate value, invalid date
   period, placement or relationship and try again.
6. Check the new record's path, fields and save notice. A Live save takes effect immediately;
   a change-set save stays proposed until publication.

If the workspace's model changed while the form was open, reload and review the new form.
Do not remove required information merely to get past a refusal.

![New record form with name, typed fields, required parent and relationship, Create and a visible context.](/docs/screens/new-record-required-connections.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/approve:
---
title: Approve a change set
description: Submit proposed work, review a request and publish it or send it back.
reader: steward
---

Use this task when a proposal needs someone else's decision. You need **Approve publications**
to decide a request. A workspace can require a second person, even if the submitter holds that
permission. See [Inbox and approvals](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/) for the policy and notices.

## Submit your work

1. [Prepare the change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/), then check its
   workspace in the sidebar and name in the band. Open **Details** for its version.
   Review the proposed records and relationships.
2. Choose **Submit for publication** where offered. The dialog explains that refiroo validates
   the change set and that it cannot be edited while it waits. Add a comment if the approver
   needs context, then choose **Submit**. **Cancel** leaves it unsubmitted.
3. If validation fails, fix the reported problems and submit again. Success says
   **Submitted for publication. It waits for approval.** The approvers receive a notice.
4. Check that the band now says **waits for approval**. Open **Details** for the submitted
   version and your name; read your comment in the review’s **Decision** panel. To change your proposal while it waits, choose **Withdraw request** first. The proposed work
   stays in the change set and becomes editable. After correction, submit a new request.

![Submitted change set showing Waiting for approval, version, comment and Withdraw request](/docs/screens/appr-submitted.png)

*Above: Guide Admin's Guide approval example waits in Graubünden. Its submitted version is 2;
the proposed height correction is still separate from Live.*

If **Publish change set** is offered instead, your permissions and the policy allow direct
publication. Use the [publish steps](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/#publish).
Do not change workspace policy merely to make a button appear; ask an administrator if the
available actions do not match your responsibility.

## Open and review a request

1. Open the bell and choose **Waiting for your approval**, or open the request from Home's
   **Waiting for your approval** section using **Review**. The Home list shows the change-set
   name, workspace, submitter and submission time, newest first. You can also open a submitted change set and choose
   **Review and decide**.
2. Check the workspace, change-set name, submitted version, submitter and their comment.
   Review all proposed changes, not just the first visible record.
3. On **Records**, expand changed entries to inspect before and after values. Review created
   and deleted records as well. On **Relationships**, inspect added, changed and removed connections.

![Approver's Home with Waiting for your approval and a Review button](/docs/screens/appr-home-waiting.png)

*Above: fictional approver Rita Approver has Data owner access in Graubünden. Guide Admin's
request appears below her workspace card.*

![Review changes with a Decision panel above the proposed record change](/docs/screens/appr-decision-panel.png)

*Above: Rita sees who submitted version 2, when it was submitted and the comment about Davos
Platz's height. Expand the record below the panel to inspect the correction before deciding.*

If you open your own request while a second person is required, there is no **Decision** panel.
The review says **A second person must decide this request.** You can read the changes, but another
authorised approver must decide.

![Submitter's own review with the second-person message and no Decision panel](/docs/screens/appr-own-approval.png)

*Above: Guide Admin can inspect the Davos Platz change but cannot approve this request themselves.*

## Decide

1. Read **Decision** and confirm it names the version you reviewed. If the screen says the
   proposal changed since submission, choose **Reload** and inspect its current state. Do not
   decide an older version as though it were the current proposal.
2. To accept it, add an optional **Comment** and choose **Approve and publish**. This immediately
   attempts publication. On success, the change set is consumed, Live contains its authored
   changes and a new publication holds the result. The submitter is notified.
3. To request corrections, enter a **Comment** saying what needs attention and choose **Send back**.
   A blank comment is refused. Success returns the change set to its submitter for editing and
   another submission, without publishing it.
4. If publication reports a conflict or validation failure, read the reason and refresh the
   review. Have the proposal corrected and resubmitted where necessary. A refused decision is
   not a successful publication.

![Decision panel with a reason entered before sending the request back](/docs/screens/appr-send-back-reason.png)

*Above: Rita asks for the source of the new height. The reason is entered, but Send back has not
yet been pressed.*

If the request was withdrawn or already decided, reload to see its new state.

## Correct work that was sent back

1. Open the returned change set from your notice or the change-set list. The notice says
   **Sent back** and names the request; its detail includes the reason and approver.
2. Read the reason in the notice below the change-set band. The request is no longer waiting
   and the change set is editable again. From **Changes in this change set**, choose **See the
   data with these changes** to inspect and correct the affected records and relationships.
3. Review the whole result, then choose **Submit for publication** again. In **Comment (optional)**,
   explain what you corrected or add the context the approver requested. Choose **Submit**.
   The change set is validated again and waits for a new decision. **Cancel** leaves it editable.

![Submitter's inbox with the send-back reason and approver](/docs/screens/appr-sent-back-notice.png)

*Above: Guide Admin's newest notice carries Rita's request for a source.*

![Returned change set with the approver's reason and preparation controls](/docs/screens/appr-sent-back.png)

*Above: Guide approval example is open for correction. The banner shows Rita's reason and offers
Submit for publication again.*

![Submit for publication dialog with a new comment for resubmission](/docs/screens/appr-resubmit.png)

*Above: Guide Admin adds the source of the height in a new submission comment. The dialog explains
that the change set cannot be edited while it waits.*

## Approve the revised request and check the result

1. As the approver, open the new request from Home or the inbox. Read the current **Decision**
   details and the new submission comment. Review the records and relationships again; the earlier
   review does not approve later edits.
2. If the proposal is ready, choose **Approve and publish**. Wait for success. If it is refused,
   resolve the reported conflict or invalid data as described under [Decide](#decide).
3. Open **Publications** in the application. The new publication is **Current** and names the
   approver as the person who published it. Choose **Open publication** to inspect the snapshot.
   Check the changed records in **Live** too.
4. As the submitter, open the bell. The approval notice confirms the decision. Earlier notices
   can remain in the inbox; read the newest result rather than treating a previous send back as
   still pending.
5. To trace the work, open **Settings**, **Workspaces**, select the workspace and choose
   **Activity**. Read the actions, people and times. See [History](/docs/use/history/) for filtering.

![Approver's Decision panel showing the resubmission comment before approval](/docs/screens/appr-approve.png)

*Above: Rita reviews the new source comment before choosing Approve and publish.*

![Publications with the new current snapshot and the previous publication](/docs/screens/appr-publication.png)

*Above: Publication 2 in Graubünden is Current and was published by Rita. Publication 1 is no
longer current; it is also marked Withdrawn in this example.*

![Submitter's inbox showing the approval notice](/docs/screens/appr-approved-notice.png)

*Above: Guide Admin receives the approval result above the earlier send-back notice.*

Follow [Browse a publication](/docs/guide/use/browse-a-publication/) for inspecting the saved result.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/arrange:
---
title: Arrange records in a tree
description: Browse branches, rename a record and move it to an allowed parent.
reader: steward
---

Use a tree view to inspect where records belong and move them to an allowed place. See
[Hierarchies](/docs/use/hierarchies/) for parents, type rules and the effect on descendants.

## Browse a branch

1. Open an application in the current workspace. Choose a collection and its tree view, where
   offered. Check the heading and the banner: **Live**, a named change set or a publication.
2. Expand the arrow beside a type group or record. Its children appear below it. Continue
   down to the branch you need; collapse an arrow to hide that branch without changing data.
3. Use **Find a record** to search, checking names, types and paths before selecting a match.
   Clear the search to return to browsing. A branch loads more records as you scroll.
4. For keyboard browsing, focus the tree and use arrow keys to move through it and expand
   or collapse branches. Open the record when you need its full fields and relationships.

![A hierarchy expanded through several record types to a municipality's stops](/docs/screens/tree-geography-chur.png)

*Above: Geography in Network is expanded through Graubünden, Plessur and Chur. Stops appears
as a type group above the stop records.*

![A hierarchy with records nested under others of the same type](/docs/screens/tree-modes.png)

*Above: Modes groups Train and Tram under Rail-bound, and Bus under Road. The record type is
Mode at both levels; a tree is not limited to a chain of different types.*

If a branch reports a loading failure, retry it. A failed read does not mean the parent has
no children. If the tree is empty, check its workspace, context and search before adding data.

## Move a record

1. Choose **Live** for an immediate move, or [open a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/)
   to stage it. Check the banner and the record's current ancestors.
2. Open the record's **…** menu and choose **Move to…**. You can also open the menu with a
   right click or **Shift+F10** while the record has focus. The dialog names the record and
   shows **Now in** followed by its current path.
3. Search by name for the new parent. Check the path below each candidate to distinguish
   repeated names. Select its radio button; typing a name alone is not a selection.
4. Use **Top level** only if you intend to remove the parent and the choice is available.
   Unavailable destinations state their reason. If no destination matches, shorten the search
   and check the model's allowed placements before continuing.
5. Check the selected destination and choose **Move to** followed by its name, or
   **Move to the top level**. Before selection the button reads **Move**. Wait for completion,
   then inspect the new branch or the record's path. The descendants move with the record.
   **Cancel** leaves its placement unchanged.

![A move dialog showing the present path, candidate parents and an unavailable top level](/docs/screens/tree-move-dialog.png)

*Above: Move 85 Garage Chur shows its current place under Graubünden / Plessur / Chur and offers
other municipalities. Top level explains why it is unavailable in this tree. The dialog was cancelled.*

A choice marked **Becomes** changes the record's type in a change set. Its button opens a type
change preview instead of making an ordinary move; review the resulting fields and missing
values before applying it. Cancel if you only intended to change the parent.

Dragging a record onto a parent is another way to move it. Review the destination and any
confirmation before proceeding. On touch screens, hold the record still until it lifts, then
drag. Beginning to move your finger before it lifts scrolls the tree instead.

## Add the first top-level record

In an editable tree, choose **Add …** for the intended top-level type in the header or empty
view. Complete the new record’s name and required fields, then choose **Create**. This form
has no parent field: the record starts at the top of this tree. Add children from its menu
afterwards. The action appears only for types allowed at the top, when the view allows creation
and your permissions allow writing that type.

## Rename or add a child

1. Open the record's menu and choose its rename action, or press **F2** on the focused record.
   Enter the intended name and confirm the rename. Check the new label; the record retains
   its identity and connections.
2. To add within a parent, choose the menu's add-child action for an offered type. Complete
   the new record form, check its parent and choose **Create**. If the needed type is absent,
   ask a model administrator about the permitted children.
3. Where an availability action is offered, use it only to change whether the record is
   available under that model's rule. It does not delete the record.

If a move or rename is refused, read the reason and review the current record before retrying.
Another person's change can make your version stale. If editing controls are absent, check
[permissions](/docs/use/records/#who-may-read-and-change-records) and the configured actions;
publications and retired workspaces are read-only. For permanent removal and its impact, see
[Deleting a record](/docs/use/records/#deleting-a-record).

## Move a selection together

1. In the sidebar tree or tree view, use Cmd or Ctrl to select individual records, or Shift
   for a range. With the keyboard, use Ctrl+Space and Shift+arrows. Escape clears the selection.
2. Open the selection's menu with right click or Shift+F10 and choose **Move to…**, or drag
   the selected records together onto the new parent.
3. Read the destination and confirmation for the whole selection. Confirm only when every
   selected record belongs there. If any cannot move, none moves; correct the selection or
   destination and try again.

In a long branch opened partway down, use **Show earlier records** to read those above it.
For **Change type…**, **Insert level above…**, **Remove this level…** or
**Change type of all … in here…**, first open a change set. Review the preview's types,
values, missing values and content kept only in history before applying; see
[Restructuring](/docs/use/hierarchies/#restructure-in-a-change-set).

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0. See [The example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/)
for sources and fictional additions.*
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/ask-a-l:
---
title: Ask a list in words
description: Ask a table collection a question, review its filters and correct an incomplete answer.
reader: steward
---

Use this to find records by describing the conditions you need. You need a table collection,
an enabled AI provider, and **Browse** and **Use AI proposals** in the workspace.
See [Asking a list in words](/docs/use/ask-in-words/) for the supported questions.
Your words and the list's definitions are sent to AI; short related lists can include names.
Requests can cost money and their outcome is kept. Read [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/)
before sending sensitive information.

1. Open a table collection in the current workspace. Check whether you are reading **Live**,
   a change set or a publication: Ask searches that context.
2. Choose **Ask** beside the search box. In **Ask in words**, describe the records you want,
   using field and relationship names you recognise. For example, with the reference data:
   “Stops updated last month with no operator” asks for a Live date condition and a missing relationship.
3. Press **Enter**. **Asking…** appears with **Cancel**. Cancel stops waiting for the answer;
   do not assume it reverses a provider request already sent or its cost.
4. When the question is fully expressed, read **Your question became these filters. Change or
   remove any of them.** Check the pills and search text against your question. They replace
   the earlier search and filters. Open a pill to adjust its condition or use **×** to remove it.
   The results update as with manually chosen filters.
5. If **This list cannot answer all of that, so nothing was applied.** appears, read each
   **Not possible here:** line. Dashed pills under **What it could do:** are only a proposal.
   Choose **Use these filters** if that smaller question is useful, or rewrite the question and
   press Enter again. To disambiguate a record, use more of its name.
6. If an error appears, your words stay and the earlier list remains. Retry after the cause is
   addressed, or choose **Search** and set filters yourself. An unavailable Created or Updated
   condition needs Live; asking from a snapshot cannot supply those times.

![A table list after a question becomes ordinary editable filter pills](/docs/screens/use-ask-filters.png)

*Above: the reference Stops list after a question becomes filters. The pills, rather than the
wording of the question, determine which stops are shown.*
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/browse-:
---
title: Browse a publication
description: Open a saved snapshot, find a record and return to current data.
reader: steward
---

Use a publication to inspect records as published, even after Live changes.
See [Publications](/docs/use/publications/) for snapshot contents and status.

## Open the snapshot

1. [Open an application](/docs/guide/use/open-an-application/) in the intended workspace.
   Check **Workspace** in the sidebar.
2. Choose **Publications** above the records. The list is newest first. Read the number,
   model release, publication time and publisher; **Current** identifies the designated snapshot.
   Choose **Load older publications** if the one you need is further back.
3. Choose **Open publication** beside the intended entry. Check the purple banner for the
   publication number and model release. It says the records are read-only.

![The publication list with Open publication](/docs/screens/use-pub-list.png)

*Above: Graubünden has one publication, made after the abbreviation correction.*

## Find and inspect the record

1. Choose a collection or view in the snapshot's navigation. It uses the saved model's definitions,
   so its available views may differ from Live.
2. Search or filter as you would when [finding records](/docs/guide/use/find-records/).
   Open the record to read its fields and relationships. An empty result means no records match
   those filters in this snapshot; clear them before concluding the record was absent.
3. Use **Back to publications** to return to the list, or **Live** to inspect today's data.
   Check the banner again before making a correction in Live.

![A publication searched for a record, with its saved abbreviation visible](/docs/screens/use-pub-snapshot.png)

*Above: Thusis Süd reads THSD in Publication 1. The purple banner keeps the snapshot context visible.*

If the list says **No publications yet**, the workspace has not had a successful publication.
If loading fails, retry. If you need to prepare a correction based on a snapshot, use its menu's
**Start a change set from this publication** where permitted; opening the snapshot itself never
restores or changes live data. Follow [Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/)
for the editing and review that follows.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/change-:
---
title: Change how refiroo looks
description: Choose this browser’s theme, table density, type colours and edit hints.
reader: steward
---

Adjust the display without changing the data. See
[Appearance and devices](/docs/use/appearance-and-devices/) for keyboard and phone use.

1. Open **All settings** from your account menu, then **Appearance** under **You**.
   On a phone, open **Settings: …** to reach the settings navigation.
2. Under **Theme**, choose **Normal** or **Website purple** for the colours. Under **Light
   or dark**, choose **System**, **Light** or **Dark**. System follows the device. Both themes
   work in either mode. The page changes immediately; there is no Save button.
3. Under **Table density**, choose **Comfortable** for more space or **Compact** for more
   rows. If one table does not change, open its **Display** menu: its own density overrides
   this default. Choose Default there to use the browser preference again.
4. Under **Type colours**, choose **B: magenta and olive** or **A: plum and gold**. Read the
   record-type labels as well as colours when identifying records.
5. Under **Edit pencil**, choose **On hover and focus** or **Always, faintly**. On a touch
   screen, editable fields show their pencils regardless of this choice.

The choices stay in this browser. Repeat them on another device if needed. For individual
column visibility and widths, use the collection's **Display** menu rather than Appearance.

![Appearance showing its two colour themes separately from light or dark mode](/docs/screens/use-appearance-themes.png)

---
title: Change records with the assistant
description: Give instructions without a workbook and review the prepared changes before publication.
reader: steward
---

Use this to ask the assistant to prepare changes to records the workspace already holds.
It needs **Use AI proposals**, **Bulk and import**, **Work in change sets**, available jobs
and an enabled assistant at the values send level. Your words and the workspace model go
to Claude Code, which reads records as needed. Turns can incur costs and task files are
retained. See [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) and
[Loading with the assistant](/docs/use/loading-with-the-assistant/) for the rules.

1. Open the current workspace's **⋯** menu and choose **Ask about these records…** where it is
   offered. You can also choose **Import…** and leave **Workbook** empty in **Load a workbook**.
   Confirm **Into** names the intended workspace.
2. In **Tell the assistant about this file (optional)**, say which records should change, how to
   find them and the desired result. Words are required when there is no workbook. For example,
   with the reference data: “Set the Abbreviation of the stop ‘Thusis Süd’ to ‘THSD-REVIEW’.” Use the names of fields and relationships in your
   model. Instructions are limited to 4,000 characters.
3. Read the sending note and choose **Ask the assistant**. This starts a saved task; it is
   different from **Ask** on a table list, which only chooses filters. Until a proposal exists,
   the journey bar and trail say **Change with the assistant**. With a proposal, they say
   **Change records** if the model stays unchanged, or **Change this model** if it changes.
   The task heading gets a short title with the assistant’s first answer; any draft it makes
   is named **Assistant:** followed by that title. Your full instructions stay under **You said:**
   on the proposal. Until the title arrives, including after a stop or failure before an answer,
   the heading uses your words, shortened at a word boundary with “…” if needed.
4. Read the proposal and any counts or checks shown. Check that it affects the intended
   records and reuses existing types and records where appropriate. Answer any **Questions** with **Answer and
   design again**, or use **Tell the assistant what to change** and **Send to the assistant**.
   If the task proposes a model change, inspect **Show the model change** and involve a model
   administrator before accepting it. If the summary says **No type, attribute or relationship
   changes**, open the draft in the model editor: it may still change views or layout.
   When a task without a workbook says **No change to the model.**, there
   is no model draft, model-change detail or model editor button.
5. When the proposal and any checks match your request, choose **Accept** for words alone
   with no model change. The session prepares a new change set on the workspace’s current
   release; it installs and activates nothing. It changes no Live record.
   If the proposal also changes the model or moves records between types, follow
   [Change a model with the assistant](/docs/guide/model/change-a-model-with-the-assistant/)
   for its **Accept the model** and migration or staged-move steps. A workbook proposal showing
   **What the load does** uses **Accept and load to change set**: the engine loads the checked records and
   relationships as one batch without another assistant turn.
   If the assistant cannot do the task, read its reason and correct the instructions rather
   than assuming a partial or empty load completed the request.
6. Choose **Review the change set**. Review the actual differences, validate and follow the
   [approval and publication steps](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/).
   The workspace's normal approval rules apply, including a second person where required.

![Record-change proposal showing No change to the model, Accept and the correction box](/docs/screens/use-assistant-words.png)

*Above: the proposal changes the Abbreviation of Chur Wiesental in the reference data. Accepting prepares a change set for review; nothing is published.*

For a wrong result, [continue or correct the same task](/docs/guide/use/continue-an-assistant-task/)
while its session is available. Instructions about stored records do not create a reusable file
layout. A workbook loaded from the assistant's checked records and relationships saves no
import profile either; send the next file to the assistant again.

---
title: Change relationship values in bulk
description: Preview and apply one value across selected connections in a relationships table.
reader: steward
---

Use a [relationships table](/docs/use/relationship-tables/) when the value belongs to a connection
rather than a record. You need **Edit live** in Live, or **Work in change sets** in a change set,
with access to change the connections. A publication is read-only.

## Prepare the grid selection

1. Open an application in the current workspace and choose its relationships table. Check that
   it uses grid layout. Read the direction below the heading: rows are from records and column
   groups are to records.
2. Check **Live** or the selected change set. Open a change set first if these values need review
   before publication. The following steps then create proposed changes.
3. Use the row search and **Filter** to narrow the source records. A relationship-value filter
   matches through a connection to one of the shown column records. Check the column selection
   before interpreting how many rows match.
4. Open the menu named for the column record type. Search, filter or tick the records whose
   connections you intend to change. At most 50 column groups are shown. A count such as
   “Showing … of …” means other column records are omitted; narrow the filter if you need them.
5. Tick the intended rows. The header checkbox selects loaded rows. When all loaded rows are
   selected and more match, choose **Select all N matching** to include the whole filtered list.
   Untick individual exceptions. Read the selection count above the grid, then choose
   **Change relationship values**. Changing the search or filters starts a new selection.

## Choose and preview the value

1. In **Attribute of the relationship**, choose the field. The choices come from this view's
   relationship attributes; JSON fields are not offered for this bulk operation.
2. In **At …**, choose **All N shown …** or one named column record. “All” means the shown
   column records, not every record of that type in the workspace.
3. Choose **Set to** and enter a value using the field's own control, or choose **Clear** to
   remove the held value. No is a Yes or no value; Clear removes the value instead.
4. Wait for **The preview**. **Would change** counts linked pairs with a different value;
   **Already …** counts those holding the requested value; **Not linked to the …** counts
   selected row/column pairs without a connection. Nothing has been written yet.
5. If missing pairs should also become connections, select **Also link them, with …**. Leave
   it unticked to change existing connections only. Review the refreshed preview: new links
   must meet the same candidate, number and ownership rules as any other new connection.
6. Read the refusal notice, if shown. Each line names the row record and column record as
   **From record → To record: reason**. The same connection refused for the same reason appears
   once. The heading **N would be refused, so nothing can be changed yet** counts those lines,
   but only the first five are shown. If a record's name is unavailable, a line shows only the
   reason; this can happen with matching rows the grid has not read. Narrow the selection to
   investigate. Check the number beside **Applying changes … relationships**. **Apply**
   stays unavailable while the value is missing or invalid, the preview is loading or failed,
   nothing would change, or any pair would be refused. Correct the value or selection; do not
   assume the remaining pairs will be applied around a refusal.

![Change relationship values dialog with attribute, shown column scope, Set to or Clear and preview counts](/docs/screens/relationships-grid-change-preview.png)

*Above: 10 stops selected in Stops by operator in the Graubünden workspace. Primary contact
is ticked under Set to, at All 2 shown operators. The preview reads Would change 6, Already
Yes 4 and Not linked to the operator 10. Also link them is unticked, so Applying changes
6 relationships counts only existing connections. Apply has not been chosen.*

## Apply and check

1. Choose **Apply**. The operation checks the current data again and writes all changes together.
   Either every intended change succeeds, or none does. A preview does not reserve the data
   against another person's edits.
2. On success, the dialog closes and the grid refreshes. Check a changed cell and the counts.
   A filter on the old value may hide changed rows; clear that filter to inspect them.
3. In a change set, look for **Proposed in this change set**, then
   [review and publish](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) when ready. Applying
   this dialog alone does not publish the change set.

**Nothing was changed** means Apply was refused. Its list uses the same record names and
reasons as the preview, with up to five lines and only the reason when a name is unavailable.
Check the named connections and current values, then retry with corrected choices. Narrow the
selection if you need to investigate refusals beyond those shown. **Cancel** closes without
applying the preview.

The deployment limits how many source records can be selected and how many relationships one
atomic change can write. One source row can affect many column groups, so a selection can fit
the row limit yet exceed the write limit. If the preview reports too many, narrow the row filter,
choose fewer rows, or choose one column record. Apply smaller reviewed selections, or ask the
operator about the configured limit. Do not keep retrying the same oversized selection.

## Change ticked relationships in the rows layout

The rows layout changes connections that already exist. It does not offer the grid's choice
to add missing pairs or its preview dialog.

1. Search or filter the relationship list and tick the particular relationships to change.
   A source appearing in several rows represents separate connections; tick each intended one.
2. In the selection bar, choose **Attribute to set** and enter the value. A Yes or no field
   offers Yes and No. Leave a non-boolean value empty to clear it.
3. Read the button, **Set … to …**, which names the field and value, then choose it. The bar's
   **Clear** abandons the selection; it does not clear stored values.
4. The ticked connections are saved together using their read versions. Success clears the
   selection and refreshes the list. A refusal displays **Nothing was changed** and the affected
   connections. Review current values before trying again. Split an oversized selection.

This layout also writes proposed changes when a change set is selected, and remains read-only
in a publication.

---
title: Change relationships of many records
description: Add, remove, replace or clear one kind of relationship across selected records.
reader: steward
---

Use this when several records need the same connection changes. See
[Changing many records](/docs/use/changing-many-records/) and [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/).

1. Select records in an editable collection and choose **Change relationships**. Select the
   relationship's pill. Only relationships allowed for that record type appear; parent and
   owner connections are managed elsewhere.
2. Choose the offered action. **Add** adds the ticked records; **Remove** removes those ticked.
   **Replace with** makes the ticked records the complete set. **Set to** chooses the one record
   for a single-valued connection. **Clear** removes the set where optional. Required
   connections cannot be removed or cleared.
3. Search and tick the other records. **Remove** lists records the selection already holds and
   how many hold each. **Add** marks connections already held. Candidate rules may limit this
   list; read its explanation if an expected record is missing.
4. Read the number of changes. If it exceeds the deployment limit, reduce the selection or
   split the work. Choose **Change the rest** or, where available, **Change none**.
5. Choose **Preview**. Review additions, removals, unchanged connections and refused records.
   Use **Back** to revise, or **Apply** to proceed.
6. Read the actual result. Connections changed since preview are refused, preserving the
   newer work. Use **Preview again** after checking them, then **Done**.

The fields on each connection are not changed here. Open the record's relationship panel to
edit those fields. A replace operation removes connections you leave unticked, so review the
whole chosen set before applying.

---
title: Change values of many records
description: Set or clear fields on selected records after reviewing a preview.
reader: steward
---

Use this for the same field correction on several records. Read
[Changing many records](/docs/use/changing-many-records/) for selection, access and limits.

1. In an editable collection, tick the records or choose **Select all … matching**. Check the
   count and any exclusions in the selection bar, then choose **Change values**.
2. Choose **Change a field** and select a field. Choose **Set to** and enter its new value,
   or **Clear** for an optional field. Required fields cannot be cleared. Read-only and hidden
   fields are not offered. Repeat to change more fields together.
3. Leave a field out to keep its value. To remove a field you added, use its **Do not change …**
   button. This form does not need a Keep choice on every field.
4. Choose **Change the rest** to apply records that can change despite other refusals, or
   **Change none** to require every item to pass. If the second option is unavailable, the
   dialog explains the deployment's all-or-nothing limit.
5. Choose **Preview**. Read how many records would change, already hold the values, or would
   be refused. Open a refused record to understand its reason. Use **Back** to revise the change.
6. Choose **Apply**, then read the actual result. A record changed by someone else is refused.
   **Preview again** checks remaining work against current values. Choose **Done** when finished.

**View job** leaves a preview waiting on its job page. Closing the preview otherwise cancels
it. If the model changed, reload before making a fresh change; if the change set changed,
preview again. A successful preview never reserves a record against another editor.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/continu:
---
title: Continue a long list
description: Jump through a collection and return to the same search and position.
reader: steward
---

Find a distant row without scrolling through every earlier result. See
[Lists, search and filters](/docs/use/lists-and-filters/) for what the controls mean.

1. Open a collection and check its workspace and context. Search, filter and sort before
   choosing a position: a different condition changes which records occupy that position.
2. Scroll the rows inside the table. The footer shows your range and the full matching total.
   Scroll back up to read earlier rows; where an append-style list offers **Show earlier records**,
   choose it to read the preceding group.
3. To reach a numbered page, enter the number in **Page** and press Enter. Check the range after
   it loads. Use **Go to start** or **Go to end** for either end. With the list focused,
   Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End reach those ends too.
4. Where **Go to** is offered, enter a value for the current sort and submit it. This seeks the
   value's place in that ordering; it does not add a filter. Check nearby names and identifying
   fields if there is no exact match.
5. Open a record. Choose **←** and the list’s name above the title to return with your search, filters, sort and position.
   Save or share the address if you need to return later. Changes to the underlying data can
   change the records at that position.

If a jump fails, retry the failed read. Do not clear your search just because a page failed.
Use the list's own search rather than the browser's Find command: Find sees only drawn rows.

![A collection footer with range, total, Page, Go to and start/end controls; a noninitial position is loaded.](/docs/screens/list-position-and-seek.png)

---
title: Continue or correct an assistant task
description: Resume a stopped task, correct a proposal or reload a wrong change set without losing sight of what is discarded.
reader: steward
---

Return to the task from **Settings › Jobs**, or use the task's bar when it accompanies the model
editor or change-set review. The same assistant session can continue while the task is retained.
For a task given in words, its Jobs group and page heading use the short title the assistant
writes with its first answer; any draft it makes is named **Assistant:** followed by that title.
Your full instructions stay under **You said:** on the proposal. Until the title arrives,
including after a stop or failure before an answer, the name uses your words, shortened at
a word boundary with “…” if needed. A workbook task keeps its file name.

Further turns can incur costs and read the task's workbook and permitted records again. See
[AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) for sending and retention, and
[task states](/docs/use/loading-with-the-assistant/#stop-correct-or-end-a-task) for their rules.

## Correct a proposal

1. Read the latest notes, any **Checks**, **What the load does** or record counts, and any engine refusal. If you stopped a turn
   after it changed the draft, open the draft to inspect it: Stop does not undo those edits.
2. Under **Tell the assistant what to change**, describe the correction and choose **Send to
   the assistant**. The same session reads the current draft, if there is one, and proposes again.
3. Review the new proposal. For a workbook, inspect **What the load does**, open the type rows
   for example records and source cells, and read any repeated-name finding or refused items.
   Choose **Accept and load to change set** when those checked records and relationships match your intent.
   A draft edited after the check is checked again first; any refusal prevents the load.
   For words alone, choose **Accept** when the page says **No change to the model.**; model-only
   and record-move proposals keep **Accept the model**. If the task changed while you worked,
   inspect its latest state and try again; your old view cannot overwrite the newer work.

## Continue after a failure or Stop

1. On **The assistant stopped** or **You stopped the assistant**, read the reason in the task's
   notes. The newest three are shown; expand earlier notes if needed. If the message asks you
   to report a correlation ID, copy the ID shown with that warning for the operator.
2. Use **Tell the assistant how to go on** and **Send to the assistant** to supply corrected
   instructions. If the cause was temporary and the instructions are still right, use
   **Try again as it was** after failure or **Go on as it was** after Stop.
3. If needed, choose **Open the draft in the editor**. The draft and work so far are retained.
   If you stopped before the session had anything to resume, continuing starts it again on the
   same task with your words and any file.
4. Review the returned proposal. To end the work instead, choose **Discard this task**, which
   removes its draft and ends its session.

**Stop** while **Loading** discards the change set the load was making and returns to the
accepted proposal. Stop before any proposal leaves a stopped task that takes instructions.
Stopping a correction can return an earlier proposal whose draft already has newer edits;
read the warning before accepting anything.

![Task stopped before a proposal, with a words box, Go on as it was and Discard this task](/docs/screens/use-assistant-stopped.png)

## Correct a load before publication

1. On **Loaded into the change set**, choose **Review the change set** to understand what is
   wrong. If it can be corrected with small ordinary edits, you may make them there.
2. To ask the assistant to prepare it again, return to **Not what you wanted? Tell the assistant**.
   Describe the correction and choose **Discard and load again**.
3. Read **Discard this change set and load again?**. Confirming removes everything in that
   change set, including any edits you or others made there. Cancel to preserve it. Live data
   has not changed.
4. If you confirm a correction to a workbook load, the same session revises the proposal and
   has the engine check the records and relationships again. Review **What the load does** and
   choose **Accept and load to change set** to prepare the replacement change set. Review that change set
   before approval and publication. To abandon the work completely, use **Discard the change
   set** and confirm instead.

![A reload confirmation explaining that hand edits in the change set are removed](/docs/screens/use-assistant-reload.png)

After publication the task no longer takes corrections to that load. **Published** offers
**Change this model…** or **Ask about these records…** according to your access; use these to
prepare new work. A discarded task has ended: use **Start again** in its bar if available.

## Continue a saved layout or a model move

At a saved-layout row check, use **Back to the proposal** or the words box to have the assistant
read the file again. If **The saved layout does not fit this file** appears, choose **Read it
with the assistant**. Review its new proposal before loading.

For **The engine refused the migration** or **The engine would refuse the next step**, read
the reason on the task, then use **Tell the assistant what to change**. Review the revised
model and preview again. Whole-type migration confirmation moves records live; read the
[model-move rules](/docs/use/loading-with-the-assistant/#a-model-change-that-moves-records)
before confirming it. The assistant cannot bypass the refusal or activate a release itself.

If you lost permission for a step, the page says which permission is required. Copy the task
link for a workspace administrator. If the task expired or does not exist, choose **Go to the
workspaces**. A task whose session has ended says so: start a new task if more work is needed.

If a workbook batch is refused at acceptance, none of its records or relationships is loaded
and its change set is discarded. Read the refused records and their source cells in the task's
notes, then tell the assistant what to correct. Review and accept the revised proposal.
A model release installed before the failed load can remain installed.

For other task paths, if a failed task says it loaded changes before it stopped, choose **Review the change set**
and inspect that retained proposal before retrying. This differs from **Stop** during loading,
which discards the load's change set. Do not publish a partial proposal merely because it exists.

---
title: Continue live work while a change set is open
description: Make immediate corrections and understand which ones can conflict with proposed work.
reader: steward
---

Live remains editable while a change set is open, if you hold Edit live. See
[Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/#publishing-and-intervening-live-work).

1. Leave the change-set context and choose **Live**. Check the green band before editing.
   Opening another browser tab can help keep the contexts distinct.
2. Make and save the immediate correction. It is visible in Live now; it does not update
   the starting copy inside the existing change set.
3. Return to the change set and review its changes. An unrelated new Live record or a Live
   correction to an untouched record is kept when the change set publishes.
4. Validate and attempt publication only after reviewing current work. If Live and the change
   set changed the same record, publication refuses the conflict even if different fields
   changed. Changed mapping sets and invalid combined relationships can also stop publication.
5. Read the conflict list. Both Live and the change set remain intact, and nothing is partially
   published. Prepare a new change set from current Live and reapply the intended corrections
   after reconciling them. There is no automatic rebase or forced overwrite through retry.

Another publication between review and confirmation can also make the attempt stale. Refresh
and inspect the current result before retrying.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/copy-or:
---
title: Copy or move records to another workspace
description: Choose an approved mapping, inspect the dry run and publish the destination before source deletions.
reader: steward
---

Use a saved mapping prepared for the two workspace models. See
[Copying and moving records](/docs/use/copying-and-moving/) for access, retained identities,
omissions and the difference between Copy and Move. For mapping design, ask a model
administrator to follow [Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/).

1. Open **Settings › Workspaces and models › Copy and move**. Check **Recent copies and moves**
   for an existing operation before choosing **New copy or move…**.
2. Choose **From workspace** and **To workspace**. Check their model names and releases.
   Under **Mapping**, select the agreed saved mapping. If none fits, stop and have its owner
   prepare one; **A new mapping, proposed** is a suggestion requiring design review.
3. Choose **Open the editor**. Select **Copy** to retain the source, or **Move** to prepare
   source deletions as well. Nothing has reached Live in either workspace.
4. Beside **What to copy** or **What to move**, choose **Change…**. Choose the intended scope,
   fill its types, filters or starting record, then choose **Dry run this selection**.
   Wait for the check of all selected items.
5. Inspect creates, updates, omissions, **Values not carried** and **What cannot be copied**
   or **What cannot move**. Open the reasons and affected records. Ask the mapping owner to
   correct unexpected losses, required values or placement problems before proceeding.
6. Choose **Start the copy…** or **Start the move…**. Read the confirmation and enter
   **Name of the change set of workspace …** for the destination. Choose **Start the copy**
   or **Start the move** to load the proposal; **Cancel** keeps the work unstarted.
7. Read the actual result and refused or kept records. Choose **Review the change set** for
   the destination. Review records and relationships, correct problems, validate, and
   [publish or submit for approval](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/).
8. For Move, publish that destination first. Then choose **Review the deletions** and inspect
   the source proposal. Check which records were kept and why. Publish or obtain approval
   there separately. Publishing the copy has not itself deleted the originals.

![Finished move linking to the destination change set and source deletion proposal](/docs/screens/use-move-review-change-sets.png)
