If the mapping or workspace release changed after the dry run, inspect the current mapping
and check again. A refused start is not permission to use the older preview. If the running
operation fails, open its [job](/docs/use/jobs/) and any produced change sets before repeating
it. If no items can transfer, revise the scope or ask the mapping owner to fix the report's
reasons. Closing a running operation's page leaves it working in the background.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/correct:
---
title: Correct a record
description: Save a correction, handle a refused save, and check who changed what.
reader: steward
---

Correct one value or several fields and check the saved result. See
[Records](/docs/use/records/) for field rules, versions and editing permissions.

To change connections, follow [Relate records](/docs/guide/use/relate-records/). For a move, follow
[Arrange records in a tree](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/).


## Change one value

1. Open an application in the current workspace and [find the record](/docs/guide/use/find-records/).
   Check its heading and hierarchy path before editing.
2. Choose **Live** for a correction that should take effect immediately. Check the green
   **Live** banner. To prepare work for later publication, [open a change set
   first](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/), then check its name in the orange banner.
3. Select the value you need to correct in the heading or a details panel. An editor opens for
   that field. Enter the verified replacement using the control shown: text, number, date or
   Yes/No. Where **Set null** is offered, it stores an explicit null value. To make an optional
   field **Not set** instead, cancel this edit and use its remove-value button and confirmation.
4. Choose **Save**. On success, the editor closes and the saved value appears. Check it before
   leaving. Choose **Cancel** instead to abandon the correction.

![One numeric field open for correction with Cancel and Save](/docs/screens/stop-edit-field.png)

*Above: Stop number (UIC) is open on Chur Wiesental in Network, in the Graubünden workspace.
Its current value is 8509006; the screenshot shows the editor before a correction is saved.*

If the value cannot be selected, check whether you are viewing a read-only publication. A field
may also be read-only or your access may not allow editing it. Ask a workspace administrator if
you need access. If a save is refused, read the message and correct the reported problem before
trying again. A refused save has not applied your input.

## Change several fields together

1. Open the **…** menu in the record’s header and choose **Edit record**.
   The record’s ID and version are under **Details**.
   The **Edit object** form opens with the current values.
2. Correct the fields you need. **Name** identifies the record; the other fields describe it.
   Check each field's label rather than assuming similarly named fields change together.
3. Leave **Parent** selected as it is unless you intend to move the record. To move it, search
   for and select the intended parent, checking its path to distinguish matching names.
4. Scroll through the form and choose **Save changes**. On success, the form closes and the
   record page shows the result. If a message identifies an invalid or missing value, correct
   it and save again. Choose **Cancel** to leave without saving the form.

![The record editing form showing Parent, Name and other fields](/docs/screens/stop-edit-record.png)

*Above: Edit object for Chur Wiesental shows Chur as the selected Parent, followed by Name,
Designation, Stop number (UIC) and the other stop fields. The remaining fields and save control
are further down the form.*

## If someone else changed it first

1. If a single-field save reports **The value was not saved** and **Object version has changed**,
   leave the editor open. Your input is preserved. Read **Current saved value**, then review
   the refreshed record for the other person's changes, including changes to other fields.
2. Decide whether your correction still applies. Adjust the input if needed. Choose **Save**
   again only after reviewing the current values, or **Cancel** to abandon your correction.
3. Check the result. Another intervening edit can cause another refusal; review again rather
   than repeatedly pressing Save. If **Reload current value** appears, use it to load the
   current value before retrying.

![A refused field save with the current saved value and the user's preserved input](/docs/screens/save-conflict.png)

*Above: on Chur Depot Sand, another session changed Designation before this session tried to save
Abbreviation. The input CHSX is preserved, the current saved abbreviation DEPS is shown, and the
save is refused even though the other session edited a different field.*

For the reason a change to another field can refuse your save, see
[Versions and refused saves](/docs/use/records/#versions-and-refused-saves). If the whole-record
form reports a conflict, review the latest record and reapply only the corrections still needed;
do not assume the form's older values are current.

## Check the correction in its context

If you saved in a change set, choose **Review changes** in its orange banner. Under
**Records**, find the record and open its row to check the before and after values.
This shows the correction prepared for publication; it has not changed Live yet.
Follow [Review what a change set changes](/docs/guide/use/review-what-a-change-set-changes/)
for the full review. Record History is absent inside change sets and publications.

For a correction saved directly in **Live**, or after the change set has been published,
open the record in **Live** and check its History:

1. Scroll to **History** on the record's page. Each line identifies a change, the person who
   made it and the time. The newest changes appear first.
2. Choose **Values** for field changes, **Relationships** for connections, **Moves** for changes
   of place, or **All** to see every kind together.
3. Use **By** to narrow the history to one person. Choose **Anyone** to remove that restriction.
4. Open a history line with its arrow to inspect the change and its previous value, where
   recorded. If your correction is not visible, restore **All** and **Anyone** before looking
   again. A cancelled or refused correction is not a successful value change.

![Record history with change-kind tabs and a person filter](/docs/screens/stop-history.png)

*Above: Chur Wiesental's History shows its creation and added relationships by Guide Admin.
All, Values, Relationships, Moves and By control which events are shown; this capture does not
show a newly saved field correction.*
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/delete-:
---
title: Delete a record
description: Review dependent records and relationships before confirming a permanent removal.
reader: steward
---

Delete only when the record should be removed. To keep it for history and stop offering it,
see [Stop offering a value](/docs/guide/use/stop-offering-a-value/). Read
[Records](/docs/use/records/#deleting-a-record) for ownership rules.

1. Open the record and check its workspace and Live or change-set band. Open **⋯** and choose
   **Delete record**. You need permission for the record and dependants the deletion removes.
2. Read **Delete …?**. Choose **Delete** to request removal. If it has dependants or
   relationships, refiroo shows their impact before another confirmation.
3. Review the record count, dependent records with their types, **Relationships to remove**
   and the count of connections leading to independent records. Children and owned dependants
   go with the record, including owned records in another application. Independent records
   and their hierarchies remain.
4. Choose **Confirm deletion** only if that is the intended impact. Cancel to leave it in place.
   If there are no dependants, the first Delete can complete the removal.
5. After success, the list opens. In Live the removal is immediate; in a change set it stays
   proposed until publication. Earlier publications and history are not erased.

If someone changes the record or adds a dependant before confirmation, the stale deletion
is refused. Choose **Retry** to obtain the current record, then request deletion and review
the fresh impact. Retry does not silently confirm a larger cascade.

![Single-record deletion impact showing dependent names/types, relationships removed, independent connections retained and Confirm deletion.](/docs/screens/record-delete-impact.png)

---
title: Delete many records
description: Preview all dependent records and removed relationships before deleting a selection.
reader: steward
---

Deletion can remove more records than you selected. Read
[Changing many records](/docs/use/changing-many-records/) for permissions and
[Records](/docs/use/records/#deleting-a-record) for ownership rules.

1. Select the records in an editable collection. Check the workspace and whether you are in
   **Live** or a change set. Choose **Delete** in the selection bar.
2. Read the dialog and choose **Delete the rest** to continue with valid deletions despite
   refusals, or **Delete none** to require all items to pass, where that choice is available. Choose **Preview**.
3. Review selected records, children and owned dependants by type, relationships removed,
   and the connections reaching records that stay. A selected record may already be included
   beneath another selected record; do not count it twice.
4. Check the final total on **Delete … records**. This includes dependent records, not only
   selected rows. Use **Back** or cancel if the impact is wrong.
5. Confirm with **Delete … records**. Review the result and reasons for refusals. A new child
   or intervening edit can invalidate an item's preview. Use **Preview again** for refused or
   unprocessed items. For records refused because their version changed, the new preview
   uses their current versions. Review its updated dependent records and relationships
   before confirming again; the earlier preview no longer describes the whole impact.

Live removals take effect immediately. In a change set they remain proposals until publication.
History and earlier publications remain. A sampled preview cannot authorise deletion of items
it did not inspect. Cancellation stops remaining work and leaves already committed removals in place.

![Delete preview for two stops, showing ten relationships to surviving records and the Delete 2 records action.](/docs/screens/bulk-delete-impact.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/edit-in:
---
title: Edit in Excel and import back
description: Export a readable workbook and preview only the changes you intend to load.
reader: steward
---

Use an Excel (XLSX) workbook when you want to edit a view or a collection outside refiroo. Read
[Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/#a-workbook-for-people) before clearing cells.

If **Load a workbook** opens because the assistant is enabled, choose **Import without the
assistant…** to reach the manual import form used below. That manual path does not send the
file to an AI assistant.

1. In the collection, open **Workspace actions › Export**. Keep **What** on **This view**
   to take its search, supported filters and layout, or select the type, application or workspace.
   Choose **For editing in a spreadsheet**. For a link matrix, choose **What each cell lists**:
   **Name** or a text field identifying its records. For a table, check **Advanced: columns
   and sheets**. Choose **Start export** and download the completed file.
2. Open it in Excel. Read the second sheet, **About this export**, for the file’s source and
   load-back rules. Keep its hidden identity and version columns and saved import information.
   Edit the names or ordinary values you intend to change; leave **(not imported)** columns
   alone. Read summary cells on their referenced sheet.
3. Follow the rules for the layout you exported, below. In an ordinary table workbook,
   review relationship lists carefully: the edited list replaces the whole set.
   An empty replacement cell clears it if allowed. In a matrix workbook, clearing a cell
   changes nothing. Blank ordinary field or owned-record cells
   leave values unchanged. Removing a relationship-sheet row does not delete the connection.
4. Back in the intended Live or change-set context, choose **Workspace actions › Import** and
   select the workbook. Leave **Profile** at **None** so refiroo reads its saved layout.
5. Keep **Only if unchanged since the export** unless you have reviewed a deliberate overwrite.
   **Update them anyway** deliberately replaces values from the file even where a record
   or relationship changed since export. Review the current data first: this choice ignores
   the workbook’s saved version checks.
   Choose the refusal policy and **Preview**. The job page identifies it as **Read as exported …**.
6. Review **How the file is read**: the field each column is matched by, the values matched,
   value-sheet counts and where new records go. Change **Matched by** where needed; this runs
   the preview again without loading records. See
   [Check how the file is read](/docs/guide/use/import-a-file/#check-how-the-file-is-read).
   Review creations, updates, unchanged rows and refusals. An untouched workbook should change
   nothing. With **Only if unchanged since the export**, a record edited by another person
   since export is refused. Reconcile those rows
   with the current records before retrying, or export a fresh workbook.
7. Choose **Load the file** when the preview is right. Inspect the final results; execution
   checks current data again. Correct refused rows in the file and resend it to preview again.

In a change set this prepares proposals for review and publication; it does not change Live.
Use **Cancel import** if the preview includes unexpected changes.

## Edit a matrix workbook

The main matrix sheet loads only its cells. Row names and identifying fields help you find
the right row; editing them here does not change those records. Value sheets, where present,
load their records separately as described below.

- In a matrix showing record fields, edit the intended field under the intended column.
  Filling an empty cell creates a record only when the view permits creation. The preview
  shows where it goes, including a group that **will be created**. If no suitable place can
  be found, the refusal names the column: choose or prepare a group by creating the first
  cell in the app, then preview the file again. There is no value sheet for this layout.
- A cell holding several records is shown joined and is not loaded back in this field layout.
  Open the cell in refiroo to edit the individual records.
- In a matrix showing links, choose a record from the cell's dropdown. A non-empty list
  replaces the links within that row and column: records added are linked, records left out
  are unlinked. Other columns are unaffected. A value found neither in that column's value
  sheet nor in existing records creates a record only if the view also permits creation. It supplies the name and, when different,
  the selected text field; other required fields still need values. Otherwise choose an
  existing record. Names containing a semicolon appear with a comma instead; keep that form
  when editing.
- An empty or cleared matrix cell changes nothing. To remove every value or every link in a
  cell, use refiroo.

### Edit the value sheets of a link matrix

1. Open **Values ·** followed by the column name. Each row holds a record's name and fields,
   its group for reading, and hidden identity and version columns. Keep those hidden columns.
   Fields marked **(not imported)** are for reading.
2. Where the view permits editing or creation, edit existing records on that sheet. The hidden
   identity updates the same record, even if you change its name. Its other connections see
   those record changes too. With only Link existing and Unlink enabled, value sheets are
   for reading and their edits do not load.
3. Where the view permits creation, add a row without an identity for a new record and fill
   its required fields. The group column does not choose where it goes: check the import
   preview. A row not selected in any main-sheet cell is still created or updated.
4. In a main-sheet cell, use the chosen field's value from the value sheet. If you rename a
   record there, its old main-sheet value still identifies it unless another value-sheet row
   now uses that value. The same new value in both sheets identifies one new record. Two
   records with the same chosen value make the reference ambiguous; correct the values or
   the selected matching field in the preview.
5. Preview the workbook in refiroo. A spreadsheet cannot synchronise the main sheet's text
   and value-sheet records itself; import resolves them together. Review both value-sheet
   counts and main-sheet connections before choosing **Load the file**.

For example, a translation matrix workbook can fill missing names under language columns.
A mapping matrix workbook can link an existing code instead. Both create connections; reuse
keeps the existing record's identity. In a change set, connected systems see the accepted
changes after publication, according to what they are allowed to read.

## Edit other view workbooks

A relationships table exported as rows lets you edit connection values or add a row connecting
two named records. Removing a row does not delete its connection. In its grid layout, **Linked**
is Yes or No: Yes can add a missing connection, and No does not remove an existing one.
A table column showing a relationship that owns its records is for reading; edit the owned
records on their own sheet or in the app. Follow the file's **About this export** instructions.

A tree or a wider type selection has one sheet per type, with parents identified by name.
Keep the hidden columns where names alone would be ambiguous. A mapping grid uses a
relationship column for the target. See
[Workbook layouts](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/#workbook-layouts) for the differences.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/explain:
---
title: Explain a period in history
description: Ask for an account of changes, check its facts and open the underlying work.
reader: steward
---

Use this for a workspace's changes or one record's past. You need a configured AI provider and
**Browse** and **Use AI proposals** in the workspace. Counts and model labels go to the provider;
at values, names go too. Requests can incur costs and are recorded. Read
[AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) and
[What changed in a period](/docs/use/history/#what-changed-in-a-period) for privacy and counting rules.

1. Open a record in **Live** and its **History**, or open **Settings › Workspaces**, choose the
   workspace and open **Activity**. Opening **What changed** sends nothing to AI.
2. In **Period**, keep **Last 7 days** or **Last 30 days**, or choose **Choose dates**.
   Set **From** and **To, included**. Both dates count; the first must not be after the last.
   A workspace starts with seven days and a record with thirty.
3. Read the sending line, then choose **Explain this period**. **Writing the account** appears.
   A period without changes reports that nothing changed and nothing was sent to AI.
4. Read the statements and follow each numbered source to its fact. Expand **Show the other …**
   to inspect all the facts. The warning that AI can be wrong applies even when a source exists:
   check that the statement says what its numbers support.
5. Choose **Show it** or **Show them** beside a fact to narrow the current Activity or History.
   Use **Open the change set** or **Open the job** to inspect its preparation where offered.
   A missing job link can mean the job is no longer retained or you cannot open it.
6. Use **Show all activity** or **Show all history** to restore the full list. Change the period
   and ask again for a different interval, or use **Explain again** to refresh it. The same facts
   for exactly the same period within an hour reuse the earlier account without another provider
   call. Preset periods end at the time you ask, so **Explain again** can make a new paid call.

![A record's What changed section with date controls, statements and cited facts](/docs/screens/use-record-history-explained.png)

If **The account could not be written** appears, read the facts anyway and use **Try again**
when appropriate. If the request itself fails, its error also offers **Try again**. Neither
failure changes your records. For exact values and individual actions, use the normal
[History controls](/docs/guide/use/see-who-changed-what/); an account counts published changes,
not the record edits still waiting in an open change set.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/export-:
---
title: Export records
description: Export the view you are using, or choose a type, an application or the whole workspace.
reader: steward
---

Take a file of the data you need. Read
[Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/) for file shapes and workbook rules.

1. Open the intended view in the current workspace and **Live**, change set or publication.
   Set its search, filters, parent scope and chosen columns before opening Export.
2. Open **Workspace actions › Export**. Under **What**, the first choice is **This view**
   followed by its name. Keep it to export the view with its search and supported filters.
   Read the count line and context: a matrix reports rows × columns; a tree or mapping grid
   reports records. Counts are shown when the page knows them. This includes matching rows
   beyond those currently on screen.
3. To take a wider selection, choose **The type**, **The application** or **The whole workspace**.
   These choices select whole types rather than the current view's narrowed rows. Check
   **Record types** and **Where** where offered. You can also start an export from
   **Settings › This instance › Jobs**.
4. Choose **Kind of file**. **For editing in a spreadsheet** makes an Excel (XLSX) workbook
   shaped for the chosen view or types. **Technical** is offered for a table view, a type,
   an application or the workspace; it offers **Excel (XLSX)**, **CSV** or **JSON Lines**
   under **Format**. A matrix, tree, mapping grid or relationships table exports its view
   as a workbook for editing. In CSV, text that could start a spreadsheet formula receives
   one extra leading single quote, even when single quotes already precede the formula character.
   Keep it if you return the CSV; import reads back the original text. XLSX is unaffected.
   See [CSV text rules](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/#text-in-csv-files).
5. Read any notice about filters not carried into the file. A filter on a relationship's own
   values is not carried. The file can therefore include connections that filter hid.
   For a table workbook, **Advanced: columns and sheets** adjusts its columns and related sheets.
6. For a matrix listing linked records, check **What each cell lists**. Under **Each linked
   record is listed by its**, keep **Name** or choose a text field of those records. Choose a
   field whose values distinguish the records in each column. The file records this choice
   so import reads the cells the same way. If linked records have no value in that field,
   the export is refused; fill those values or choose another field.
   Each column also gets a value sheet with its records and fields. New records use the
   relationship's rules and existing groups when imported; there is no group choice in Export.
7. Where offered, choose **Relationships**: **Between exported records**, **All their
   relationships**, or **None**. Use **Valid on** only when you need a business-date extract.
   Check the selection and context, then choose **Start export**.
8. Open **View job** from the notification to follow progress. When completed, choose
   **Download** before retention ends. Failed or cancelled exports have no file; correct
   the stated reason and start another export.
9. In an XLSX file, read the second sheet, **About this export**. It explains the source,
   counts, relationships, what loads back and, for a creating matrix, where new records go.
   Check it before editing: a matrix workbook loads its cells, not changes to its row labels.

For a workbook to edit and return, follow
[Edit in Excel and import back](/docs/guide/use/edit-in-excel-and-import-back/).

![Export dialog showing This view, its count and What each cell lists](/docs/screens/export-for-people.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/fill-in:
---
title: Fill in a relation matrix
description: Check coverage, find missing cells, create related records and correct existing ones.
reader: steward
---

Use a relation matrix to find empty cells and maintain the records behind its cells. The rows, columns,
fields and actions come from your model. See [Relation matrices](/docs/use/relation-matrices/)
for cell states, limits and permissions.

## Read the matrix

1. Open an application in the current workspace and choose a collection with a relation matrix.
   Select its matrix view where tabs are offered. Check the heading, row type and column headings.
2. Check the banner. Choose **Live** for immediate changes, or
   [open a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) to stage them. A publication
   is read-only.
3. Read the legend above the table. **One** and **Several** count related records under the
   model's rule. **Inactive** means records exist but none counts. **None** means no related record is present and no earlier-publication record is available to show; **History
   only** has content from an earlier publication; **Conflict** needs inspection because more
   than one record counts where only one is allowed.
4. Search for a row and check its identifying fields. Open a cell under the intended column.
   The dialog heading combines the row and column, so check both before changing anything.
   You can focus the matrix and use arrow keys between cells, then Enter to open one.

![A relation matrix with operators as rows and languages as columns](/docs/screens/matrix-operator-names.png)

*Above: Operator names in Names has many None cells. French and German contain name records.
The legend explains Active is Yes as the condition for counting in this example.*

The same steps apply when columns represent something else:

![A relation matrix with municipalities as rows and systems as columns](/docs/screens/matrix-municipalities-by-system.png)

*Above: Municipalities by system in Systems compares System codes under their systems. One
means exactly one related record here, without the name matrix's Active condition.*

## Choose which columns to show

A matrix includes all records of its column type by default, even those that do not concern the
rows you are working on. Hide empty columns automatically, or choose specific columns yourself.

### Hide empty columns

1. Set the row search and scope to the rows you want to work on, then turn on **Hide empty columns**
   beside **Filter**. The matrix keeps columns with a related record in at least one of those rows,
   including rows not yet on screen. Use the column navigation to reach more columns; empty columns
   do not take up places on its pages.
2. If the switch says **No effect while columns are chosen in Filter**, open **Filter**, choose
   **Show all** followed by the column type's plural name, then **Done**. This clears the chosen
   columns and any cell-state restriction, allowing the switch to take effect.
3. When columns are hidden, read the **N empty columns hidden** line below the toolbar. Choose
   **Show all** on that line, or turn the switch off, to bring them back.

The switch is remembered for this view in this browser. Before checking for missing connections,
turn it off or choose the columns to check explicitly, so wholly empty columns are included.
See [Filters and coverage](/docs/use/relation-matrices/#filters-and-coverage) for how the setting
works with search, scope, change sets and publications.

### Choose specific columns

1. Choose **Filter**. In the section named after the column type followed by **to show**,
   search for and select the columns you need. You can select up to 20; deselect one before
   adding another if you reach the limit.
2. Leave **Cell state** on **Any state**, or choose it to remove an existing state restriction.
   Choose **Done**. The matrix shows only your selected columns.
3. To clear your selection, open **Filter** and choose **Show all** followed by the column
   type's plural name, then **Done**. Use the column navigation if they do not all fit on one page.
   This also clears any cell-state restriction. If **Hide empty columns** is on, it takes effect
   again; turn it off to bring every column back.

Your choice belongs to the page you have open; it is not saved as a setting for the view and
does not change what other people see. Bookmark or share the page's address to reopen the same
column selection. Opening the view again from the navigation clears that selection, but keeps
your **Hide empty columns** setting.

## Find empty cells across the list

1. Clear the row search if you intend to check the whole list, then choose **Filter**.
2. In the section named after the column type followed by **to show**, search for and select
   the columns to check. The chooser can show up to 20 selected columns at once.
3. Under **Cell state**, choose **None**, then **Done**. Rows remain when at least one chosen
   column has that state, across the whole list. If you choose a state without selecting
   columns first, it applies to the columns currently shown.
4. Inspect the result. **No rows match these filters** means no matches within this search
   and column selection. Check omitted columns separately before concluding coverage is complete.
5. To inspect existing records that do not count, choose **Inactive** where offered. Choose
   **Any state** or remove the state pill with **×** to remove the state restriction. Clearing
   the column selection also clears that restriction.

![The Filter panel with cell-state choices and a column search](/docs/screens/matrix-filter-panel.png)

*Above: Municipality names offers Languages to show, with English, French, German, Italian
and Romansh. The state filter tests the chosen or shown languages, not hidden languages.*

## Fill an empty cell

1. Open the intended **None** cell. Check the row and column in the heading and the message
   that no related record exists yet.
2. Choose **Create** followed by the related type's name, where offered. The form identifies
   the row and column under **For** and **under**.
3. Check **Name**, which identifies the new record. Review the proposed name rather than
   treating it as the field content. Under **Goes in**, check where it will belong. The relationship's rules can fix a group;
   otherwise refiroo selects the group already holding the most records used by this view
   in this column. A tie leaves the choice open. An unused group is never selected just
   because it is the only one. Use **Search places…** to choose another offered group.
4. Fill the type's content fields. Set any checkbox or field that determines whether it counts
   according to the legend. Fill **Attributes of the relationship**, if shown: these describe
   the new connection rather than the record itself. Choose the form's **Create** action. On success, the dialog closes
   and the cell refreshes; check its state and displayed content.
5. Use **Back** to abandon the creation form and return to the cell, then **Close** to leave
   without creating anything. If creation is refused, correct the named problem before retrying.

![A searched matrix showing one missing cell beside four filled cells](/docs/screens/matrix-missing-name.png)

*Above: Bonaduz in Municipality names has One in four languages and None in Romansh. The empty cell
was prepared for these captures and filled again afterwards; it is not the reference data's current state.*

![An empty cell dialog offering creation of the missing related record](/docs/screens/matrix-missing-name-cell.png)

*Above: Bonaduz · rm says None · no name translation yet and offers Create name translation.*

![A creation form with a proposed name, selected container, content field and current flag](/docs/screens/matrix-missing-name-add.png)

*Above: For Bonaduz under rm fixes the cell. Name is proposed as Bonaduz rm; Goes in is Romansh.
Translated name is empty and Active is selected. Back was used without saving this form.*

If **Link existing** followed by a type name is offered, use it when the desired record already
exists. Search, inspect the candidate and any refusal reason, select an eligible record, fill
**Attributes of the relationship** if offered, and choose **Link**. This adds a connection instead of creating another record.

## When a new group is proposed

If the relationship's rules identify one group and it is missing, **Goes in** says **(will be
created)**. Saving creates that group, the record and its connection together.

When neither the rules nor existing records give a place, refiroo can propose a new group
named like the groups this view uses in other columns. Review **Name of the new …** and change
it if needed. Submit the creation form once to create both group and record. Where offered,
**Use an existing group instead** opens the group choices. Only places compatible with the
relationship's rules are offered. If no proposal or suitable place is available, resolve the
missing place in the app before creating the record. No model change is needed to accept a
proposed group.

## Add another record or reuse one

1. Open a filled cell and inspect the records already connected to the row. If the cell allows
   several records and the view permits creation, **Create** appears beside **Link existing**.
2. Choose **Create** when this is a new record. Choose its **Goes in** container and fill its
   fields as for an empty cell. The record is also listed in that container; it is not stored
   only inside the matrix.
3. Choose **Link existing** when the record already exists under this column. Search the
   candidates and read any reason beside a disabled choice. An existing link or a relationship
   limit can prevent selection. Select an eligible record, fill any **Attributes of the
   relationship**, then choose **Link**.
4. Check the refreshed cell. Linking adds a relationship to the existing record. Where the
   relationship permits reuse, that record can appear under several rows. Editing its own
   fields affects that shared record; each connection keeps its own relationship values.

**Example: a mapping matrix.** A code already connected to one row can also be linked to another
where the model permits it. Reuse keeps the same record identity. Create makes a separate record
and a new connection. After publication, connected systems see the corresponding connections
where their access includes them.

A filled cell that may hold only one record does not offer **Create**. Inspect or edit the
record already there. Empty, inactive and history-only cells can still offer creation where
configured. For example, a translation matrix may permit one counting name per language:
create a missing name, and edit an existing one rather than adding another counting name.
Publishing makes the new record and its connection available to connected systems that expose them.

## Correct an existing cell record

1. Remove a missing-cell filter before searching for an existing record. Find the row and open
   the cell under the intended column.
2. The cell opens a table with one row per linked record. Use its filter box to narrow record
   names and displayed record fields. Read the record's columns first, then the tinted
   **Attributes of the relationship** columns. Choose **Open** for its full page and history.
3. Edit the intended value in place. A Yes or no checkbox saves with one click. For another
   field, open its small editor and enter the value; Enter saves an ordinary single-line field,
   and Escape cancels. Clicking outside an unchanged record-field editor closes it. Leaving
   a relationship-value editor also attempts to save. Check the refreshed value and any error.
4. Check the condition for counting before switching an availability checkbox off: the cell
   can become Inactive without removing the record. Successful inline saves leave the table
   open. If a row disappears from a state-filtered matrix, select **Any state** to find it again.
5. To remove a permitted connection, choose **Unlink** on its row. Read the confirmation there:
   **Keep** cancels, **Unlink** confirms and keeps the related record. Choose **Close** when done.

![Cell table separating record fields from relationship values, with a value editor open](/docs/screens/matrix-cell-relationship-table-editor.png)

*Above: the Schmitten (GR) cell under wikidata-municipalities in Municipalities by system in
the Graubünden workspace. One code, Q65399, has Confirmed ticked and the Note editor open
with “Merged municipality, old code kept”. These values belong to its connection to the municipality.*

![An existing cell record open for editing with a content field and Active checkbox](/docs/screens/matrix-cell-editor.png)

*Above: Chur · rm opens the Romansh name Cuira with Active selected. Open Chur (rm) leads to the
full name record. Cancel leaves its fields unchanged.*

In a one-per-column counting rule, a change set can temporarily hold two counting records
for one cell. It shows **Conflict** with the count. Open it and inspect both records. Correct
which records meet the counting condition, or **Unlink** an unintended connection where
permitted. Unlink keeps the record. Validate the change set again before publishing; resolve
any remaining refusal through the affected record's full page. Live writes refuse a second
counting record. A conflict in proposed work is not a published extra value.
See [Cell states](/docs/use/relation-matrices/#cell-states).

For an **Inactive** cell, review existing records before adding another. For **Several**,
inspect the records before deciding whether anything needs changing; several may be allowed.
For **Conflict**, resolve the extra counting records before publication. Where **Unlink** is
offered, it asks for confirmation and keeps the related record; required ownership cannot be
removed this way. To add an owned record from its owner's full page instead, follow
[Create an owned related record](/docs/guide/use/relate-records/#create-an-owned-related-record).

For **History only**, inspect the read-only content from the named earlier publication.
Where **Create from this** is offered, it opens creation with those values supplied. Review
Name, container and fields before creating a new record; it does not undo a deletion or restore
the old record's identity and history.

## When a save or read fails

A duplicate refusal can offer **Open the … already here**. Inspect that record instead of
creating another. If **Changed elsewhere** appears, review the refreshed cell and your retained
input before retrying. If the record moved out of the cell, inspect the current contents first.
A loading failure needs a retry, not a new record to fill an apparently empty cell.

If actions are missing, check that the context is editable, you have **Edit live** or **Work
in change sets** as appropriate, and the model offers the intended action. Reader can inspect
cells. A matrix is not a promise that every visible cell can be edited.

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0. See [The example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/)
for sources and fictional additions.*
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/find-re:
---
title: Find records
description: Find a record, narrow and sort the results, and inspect its fields and relationships.
reader: steward
---

Find a record and check its fields and connections. See [Records](/docs/use/records/) for
background on records, workspaces and applications.

For choosing a dataset or view, follow [Open an application](/docs/guide/use/open-an-application/).
For the connected records you inspect, see [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/).


## Open the right list

1. On Home, find the workspace you need under **Your workspaces**. Choose its name or tile
   to open its page, then choose an application. An application link on its card opens it directly.
2. Check **Workspace** in the sidebar. If it names a different workspace, select the intended
   one before searching: a record with the same name elsewhere may hold different data.
3. Choose the collection you need under **Collections**. In an application with more than
   ten sidebar entries, type part of its name in **Find a list** to narrow the entries across
   all groups. Choose a result, or press **Enter** to open the first match. **Esc** clears
   the box and restores the groups' previous folds. If **No list matches** appears, shorten
   or clear the text. This finds list names, not records; see
   [Applications](/docs/use/applications/#find-a-list-in-the-sidebar) for the sidebar's counts
   and groups. The collection's heading identifies the list. Available collections and their
   labels depend on your workspace's model.
4. Choose **Live** at the top to search current data. Check the green **Live** banner. To
   inspect proposed or previously published data, open that change set or publication instead;
   check the context before interpreting the results.

![Home showing workspace cards and their application buttons](/docs/screens/home.png)

*Above: the Graubünden workspace card offers Network, Systems and Names. Network contains the
Stops collection used in the following screenshots.*

## Search for a record

1. To search names across the workspace, use **Find any record** in the top bar or **Find a
   record** on the workspace’s page. Check the list and path beside a result; use the arrow
   keys and Enter to open one in **Live**. To stay in a change set or publication, or search
   just this collection, type all or part of the record’s name in the search box above the list. Wait for the results
   to update. Use a shorter part of the name if you are unsure of its spelling.
2. Check the result names and identifying fields before opening one. Several records may have
   similar names; a number, date or related record can distinguish them.
3. If the record is missing, check the workspace, application and context first. Clear filters
   that may exclude it. Clear the search text to see the list without that search. If the list
   reports a loading failure, use its retry control rather than treating it as an empty result.

![A record list narrowed by text in its search box](/docs/screens/stops-search-chur.png)

*Above: searching Stops for Chur in Network, in the Graubünden workspace, returns matching stops.
The number and operator columns help distinguish similar names.*

## Filter and sort the results

1. Choose **＋ Filter** beside the search box. The menu lists the fields and relationships
   available for this list. Use its search box to find an option if the menu is long.
2. To find an exact field value, select the field, choose **Is** where offered, enter the value,
   and choose **Apply**. Use a number for a numeric field or a date for a date field. A pill
   above the results shows the filter. Search text still narrows the same results; clear it
   if you are now looking by a number rather than a name.
3. To filter by a connection, select a relationship under **Relationships**. Search the offered
   records, select the one you need, and choose **Apply**. The pill identifies the chosen
   connection. If the record is not offered, check the relationship and try a shorter search.
4. Open the sort button, marked with up and down arrows beside **Display**. Choose a field.
   Open it again and choose **Ascending** or **Descending**. Ascending puts earlier dates or
   smaller numbers first; descending puts later dates or larger numbers first. The column
   heading's arrow shows the direction.
5. Check the results and the total at the bottom. Remove an unwanted filter with its pill's
   **×**. **Clear search and filters** clears both when search and filters are active. If no records match, remove
   conditions one at a time to find which one excludes the record.

If the table offers **Hide inactive (N)** beside **Filter**, turn it on to hide the records
marked **Inactive**, whose chosen Yes/No field is **No**. Check the added pill, such as
**Active: not No**. Records with no value have no mark and stay visible. To bring back the
hidden records, turn the switch off or remove the pill with **×**. Choosing **Yes** in
**＋ Filter** instead keeps only Yes records and excludes those with no value. Other field
names change the mark and switch wording. See
[Show or hide inactive records](/docs/use/lists-and-filters/#show-or-hide-inactive-records)
for the count and rules.

![The filter menu listing fields and relationships](/docs/screens/stops-filter-menu.png)

*Above: the Stops filter menu offers Stop number (UIC), date fields and the Operated by
relationship. In this example, a number filter of 8509006 identifies Chur Wiesental.*

![Filtered records sorted by a date field in descending order](/docs/screens/stops-filtered-sorted.png)

*Above: in Network in the Graubünden workspace, search Chur and Operated by Rhätische Bahn leave
eight stops. Valid from is sorted newest first; Chur Wiesental is among the results.*

## Inspect the record

1. Choose the result's name. Its page opens with a heading and identifying fields. Check the
   path above the heading to confirm its place in the hierarchy, especially if names repeat.
2. Read the fields in the heading and details panels. The labels depend on the record type.
   An unset value differs from zero or No; see [Records](/docs/use/records/#what-a-record-holds)
   if you need to interpret a field.
3. Read the relationship sections for connected records. Scroll down to find further sections.
   **No relationships yet** means that section has no connections. If a panel reports an error,
   retry that panel; the error does not mean there are no related records.
4. Choose **←** and the list’s name above the title when finished. Your search, filters, sort and position are preserved,
   so you can inspect the next result. To make a correction, follow
   [Correct a record](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/).

![A record page with its fields, hierarchy path and relationship sections](/docs/screens/stop-details.png)

*Above: Chur Wiesental in Network has its fields under Stop details. Modes shows Train and
Operator shows Rhätische Bahn. Its path places the stop under Chur.*

![Further relationship sections, including an empty section](/docs/screens/stop-relationships.png)

*Above: further down Chur Wiesental's page, System codes holds two codes from other systems.
Name translations has no relationships yet.*

## Choose the right relationship condition

1. Open **＋ Filter** and choose a relationship under **Relationships**. Select **Is any of**
   to tick one or more related records: a match to any of them keeps the row.
2. Choose **Has none** to find records without that relationship, or **Has any** to find
   records with at least one, without selecting particular records.
3. Where the related records sit under parents, **Has none under** and **Has any under**
   let you select one ancestor. They check related records at any depth beneath it.
4. Choose **Apply**, then inspect the filter pill and results. Open a pill to edit it or
   choose its **×** to remove it. On a phone, the editor opens as a sheet; its **Show …** button
   includes the number of matching records. Check that count before applying.

Other filter groups depend on the view. Text, number, date and Yes/No fields get suitable
conditions; **More** holds additional conditions. In Live, **Created** and **Updated** can narrow
by when records were made or changed. A missing optional value and a stored empty value can be
separate conditions: choose the one matching your question.

## Reach a distant row and read related columns

1. Scroll inside the list to read more records. The header and footer stay in view, including
   the range and total. Use the footer's page field to jump to a page, **Go to** to seek a
   sorted value where offered, or **Go to start** and **Go to end** for the ends of the list.
2. In a related-record column, read the chips. **+N more** counts records that do not fit on
   the line; widen the column to see more, or open the row's record to inspect the full
   relationship table. The count itself is not an expand button.
3. A column that holds only one related record can sort by that record's name, with missing
   connections last. Columns holding several related records or showing their fields do not
   sort. Use a relationship filter rather than trying to filter a chip column.
4. Use **Display** to change shown columns. A one-line value ending in an ellipsis can be read
   in full on hover, focus or long press. If columns have folded, choose **Columns · n of m**
   to show them all. Return using **←** and the list’s name above the title after inspecting a record;
   the address preserves search, filters, the single sort and your position.

The same list navigation works in Live, change sets and publications. If a jump or later page
fails to load, retry the failed read before treating the result as empty.

## Keep a search you need again

1. Copy the page address after choosing the search, filters, order and position. Opening that
   address later reads the same collection state in the named workspace and context.
2. Use the collection's search to look beyond the visible rows. The browser's Find command
   sees only rows currently drawn, so it can miss a record elsewhere in the list.
3. Without a selected sort, records normally appear by name; a view can choose a different
   initial order. Only one sort applies. Computed paths and structured values cannot sort;
   creation and update times are unavailable in contexts without those recorded timestamps.

There is no named saved-search list. **Clear all** removes filter conditions; where search
and filters are both active, **Clear search and filters** removes both together.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/follow-:
---
title: Follow a workspace
description: Receive publication notices for a workspace and stop them when no longer needed.
reader: steward
---

Follow a workspace to hear when someone else publishes a change set there. You need Browse
access. See [Notification settings](/docs/use/notifications-settings/#follow-publication-in-a-workspace).

1. Open **Home** and find the intended card under **Your workspaces**. Check the name and model
   before choosing **Follow**.
2. Check that the control reads **Following**. Your inbox now receives a notice for each
   eligible publication by another person. Your own publications do not notify you this way.
3. Open the notice from the bell or Notifications page. It opens the publication while that
   publication is active and you can browse it. A publication that is no longer active leads
   to the workspace’s **Publications** instead. The bell opens **Publications** too. Opening
   marks the notice read; if access is no longer available, it does not restore access.
   A digest link uses the Notifications page’s opening behavior.
4. For email copies, open **Settings › Notification email** and choose delivery for publication
   notices. Following itself works without mail.
5. To stop following, toggle **Following** on Home, or choose **Stop following** under
   **Workspaces I follow** in Notification email settings. Check the list after the change.

If you lose access or your account is deactivated, notices stop but the follow choice stays.
It can resume when access returns. If the toggle fails, read the error and retry rather than
assuming your preference changed.

---
title: Follow and cancel a job
description: Read a background operation’s progress and results, or stop remaining work.
reader: steward
---

Follow work after leaving its collection or import dialog. See [Jobs](/docs/use/jobs/) for
states, access and retention.

1. Open **View job** in the starting notification, or go to **Settings › This instance › Jobs**
   and open the job; a group of related jobs opens first, and its jobs under it. Check **Workspace**
   and **Requested by** before acting.
2. Read **State** and progress. A preview waiting for confirmation has not written its proposed
   changes. Review the items before choosing **Load the file** for an import or **Apply** for
   a bulk preview. A running job updates while the page stays open.
3. To stop remaining work, use **Cancel job**, **Cancel import** for a waiting import,
   or **Cancel preview** for a waiting batch preview.
   Read the confirmation, then choose **Stop the job** for running work or **Discard the
   import** / **Discard the preview** for a waiting preview. From the Jobs list, choose **Cancel
   job** in its confirmation. **Keep the job**, **Keep the preview** or **Keep the import**
   dismisses that confirmation.
4. Wait for the state to settle. **Cancel requested** is still pending. Already committed
   chunks remain applied: inspect the final counts rather than assuming cancellation undoes them.
5. For an export that completed, read **The file** and choose **Download**. For an import or
   batch, read refused and unprocessed items and their reasons. Fix the source and preview
   again before retrying work.

If the job failed, read **Why it failed**. Loss of the requester's permissions can stop a job;
a changed change set can stop its next chunk. Expired previews require a fresh preview.
Retained results and files disappear after their retention; download what you need in time.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/import-:
---
title: Import a file
description: Choose a file, review its preview and load the rows you approve.
reader: steward
---

Load into Live or a change set after checking exactly what the file means. See
[Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/) for file and profile rules.

If **Load a workbook** opens because the assistant is enabled, choose **Import without the
assistant…** to reach the manual import form used below. That manual path does not send the
file to an AI assistant.

1. Open the intended workspace and collection. Choose **Workspace actions › Import**. To
   choose another destination, open **Settings › This instance › Jobs › New import** and
   choose the workspace and **Load into** context.
2. Choose **File**. The chooser accepts Excel workbooks, CSV and supported technical export
   files. Choose the stored **Profile** for an ordinary workbook or CSV, or **None** for a
   file exported by refiroo. Read any profile problems before continuing. For an exported CSV,
   keep the protective single quotes added to formula-like text. With **None**, import removes
   exactly one such quote from names and text fields; an unchanged export changes nothing.
   XLSX is unaffected. See [CSV text rules](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/#text-in-csv-files).
3. Under **Rows that cannot load**, choose **Load the rows that can load** or **Load nothing
   unless every row loads**. Under **Records the file finds**, decide whether to update or
   refuse them. For an export, **Only if unchanged since the export** protects newer work;
   **Update them anyway** deliberately relaxes that protection.
4. If the file names another workspace's records, choose **Load them as this workspace's own**
   for separate destination records, or **Refuse them**. Check this choice before continuing.
5. Choose **Preview**. The job page opens while the file is read. Check its context, counts,
   column report, **How the file is read** where shown, and refused rows. Each failing cell identifies its column and reason.
   If only part of a large file was tried, its sample is not a promise about every row.
6. Choose **Load the file**, or **Cancel import** if the result is wrong. Loading checks
   current data and can refuse rows that passed preview. Read the final applied and refused counts.
7. Correct refused rows in the file and import it again. Resend the whole file: rows already
   loaded should be unchanged when their values and matching rules are unchanged.

## Check how the file is read

1. In the preview, open **How the file is read** where offered. Each matrix or relationship
   column shows **Matched by**, **Values matched** and **New records go into**. For a workbook
   exported by refiroo, the file records the matching field. When a file does not record it,
   refiroo compares its values with existing records and marks its choice **Guessed**. Read
   any note about an uncertain choice; do not assume a high match count proves it is right.
2. Check each column's field against what its values mean. Where a selector is offered under
   **Matched by**, choose the intended field. This starts a new preview of the same file;
   wait for it and review its counts and refusals again. Nothing is loaded by either preview.
3. For a link matrix with value sheets, check how many rows update existing records and how
   many are new. The main columns also report values found on value sheets and new values.
   An unselected value-sheet row can still create or update a record; review it too.
4. Check **New records go into**. A proposed or rule-defined missing group says
   **will create … under …**. Confirming the load creates that group with its records.
   If there is no suitable place, follow the reason and prepare the place in the app before
   previewing again. You do not need a model change to accept a proposed group.
5. When using a stored profile, choose **Save these fields in the profile** if this reading
   should apply to later files. Saving the reading does not load the file. Review all changes
   and refused rows, then choose **Load the file** only when the preview is right.

For the workbook editing rules, see
[Edit in Excel and import back](/docs/guide/use/edit-in-excel-and-import-back/#edit-the-value-sheets-of-a-link-matrix).

A malformed file or invalid profile changes nothing. Ask a model administrator about profile
rules you cannot fix. A profile deleting records absent from the file must load into a change
set. An expired preview needs a new import preview, rather than another confirmation attempt.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/load-a-: --- title: Load a workbook with the assistant description: Send a workbook, review the model and checked records, then load a change set for publication. reader: steward --- Use this when a file needs interpretation before it can load. You need the assistant enabled, permission to send values, **Use AI proposals**, **Bulk and import**, **Work in change sets** and available background jobs. A model change needs a model administrator's access too. The whole workbook, your words and the workspace model go to Claude Code; it can read records as needed. Turns can incur costs and the task and session files are retained. Read [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) and [Loading with the assistant](/docs/use/loading-with-the-assistant/) before starting. 1. Open an application in the current workspace and check that it is writable. Open the workspace's **⋯** menu and choose **Import…**. When the assistant is offered, **Load a workbook** opens first. To use a known manual import instead, choose **Import without the assistant…** and follow [Import a file](/docs/guide/use/import-a-file/). 2. In **Workbook**, choose one XLSX or CSV file. To follow the illustrated example, download the example workbook, a fictional operator’s stop list from the guide’s reference data. Check **Into** names the intended workspace. In **Tell the assistant about this file (optional)**, explain the result you need: for an update, say how rows correspond to the records already held and what must stay unchanged. Read the sending note, then choose **Read the workbook**. If the file exceeds the instance's size limit, reduce it or ask the operator about that limit; nothing has been loaded. 3. The task page shows **Working on it** and the steps actually completed. You can leave and return from **Settings › Jobs**, or choose **Stop**. A fitting saved profile can prepare the file without starting AI; the page then follows that saved layout. 4. Read **The assistant’s proposal** and **What the load does**. Check the totals for new records, existing records matched, new relationships, refused items and rows read. New relationships include the links of new records to their parents; the summary says how many of those links it includes. Open each type's row to inspect example records, their values, relationships and source cells. Read **One name twice in one type** if shown, and expand **Where each part of the file goes**. Check **Show the model change**, **Checks** and **Columns left out**. Unexpected new records instead of matches, unexplained repeated names and omitted filled cells need a correction. 5. Under **Questions**, inspect the assumed choices. Change wrong ones and choose **Answer and design again**. For other corrections, use **Tell the assistant what to change** and **Send to the assistant**. **Open in the model editor** opens the draft if you need to edit it. Close the editor to return. If the draft changed after the check, accepting checks every record and relationship again first. Ask for a revised proposal if the shown examples no longer describe what you intend. 6. When the proposal matches your intent, choose **Accept and load to change set**. The engine installs the model if it changed and loads exactly the checked records and relationships into a new change set, as one batch. No assistant turn runs and nothing is published or activated. If any item is refused, none of the batch is loaded and its change set is discarded. Read the task's reason, then tell the assistant what to correct and review its new proposal. A release already installed before a load failure can remain installed. A saved-layout task instead shows **What the load would do** and a load button: inspect the per-sheet figures, expand changed records, read refused row examples and **What confirming does, in this order** before loading. Its button explicitly says when it also activates a model; that activation is not undone if the subsequent load fails. 7. On **Loaded into the change set**, compare the actual record and relationship counts with the checked result: the same relationships, including parent links, are counted in both. A load prepared by the assistant does not save an import profile. Send the next file of the same layout to the assistant again. 8. Choose **Review the change set**. Check the actual record and relationship changes, validate, obtain any required approval and publish through [Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/). If the change set uses a different model version, review offers **Move** followed by the workspace name, the proposed version and **and publish…**. A model administrator with publication permission can use this to preview the migration and choose **Migrate and publish**. This moves the workspace to that model and publishes the change set together; a separate activation first is not required. Follow [Migrate a workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) to inspect the preview and resolve any blockers or approval requirement. Loaded records reach Live only when published. ![The workbook dialog with Workbook, Into, instructions and the sending note](/docs/screens/use-assistant-workbook.png) ![A loaded assistant task naming the change set](/docs/screens/use-assistant-loaded.png) If the proposal or load is wrong, use [Continue or correct an assistant task](/docs/guide/use/continue-an-assistant-task/). For the next file, start another assistant task and explain how it should match existing records. If you already have a separately saved import profile, use [Load the next version of a workbook](/docs/guide/use/load-the-next-version-of-a-workbook/).
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/load-th:
---
title: Load the next version of a workbook
description: Check a recurring workbook against its profile and stage its differences in a change set.
reader: steward
---

Use a saved import profile to recognise a recurring workbook. This differs from creating a
model from a new workbook; that task belongs to
[Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/).

1. Open **Settings › Workspaces and models › Import profiles**. Select the profile and read its
   **Last load**: file, destination, row counts and whether its change set was published.
2. If your permissions offer **Upload the next version…**, choose it and upload the newer
   workbook. Choose the intended comparison workspace and wait while it is checked.
   The profile is checked and saved against that workspace’s model. Nothing is loaded
   into its records by this check.
3. Review new, missing and renamed columns, new values, changed names and missing records.
   Choose **Accept** on a **Renamed** row only where the proposed column really replaces the old one.
   Choose **Ignore** on a **New** row to leave that column out. Ask the profile's model administrator to
   fix ambiguous bindings or model problems; do not guess which field a column represents.
4. Check the missing-record choice. Keeping missing records leaves them; deleting them stages
   removals and is allowed only in a change set. A missing key means reliable recurring
   matching is not available: resolve it before relying on repeated uploads.
5. When the report allows loading, choose **Load into a change set…** and review the destination
   and proposed changes in its dialog. Loading creates a new change set containing differences.
6. Choose **Open the change set review** from the completed load or **Last load**. Review
   additions, corrections and removals before publishing or submitting for approval.

If the file could not be read or the profile could not be saved, correct the displayed cause
and check again. Missing controls can reflect your access; ask the responsible model
administrator. See [Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/) for row refusals.

![Import profile after a next-version check, with Accept and Ignore beside column differences, Needs a fix and disabled Load into a change set.](/docs/screens/import-profile-next-version.png)

The pictured profile still **Needs a fix**, so **Load into a change set…** is disabled. Resolve
the reported problems before loading.

In **Load … into a change set**, check the proposed name and workspace before choosing
**Load**. The steps **Open a change set** and **Load the rows** show what is happening.
The suggested name starts with **Load**, the file name and a date. If loading fails after the
change set was opened, inspect that change set and the load's job before starting again;
do not assume the first proposal disappeared.

## Use a saved profile through the assistant dialog

A workbook loaded from the assistant’s checked records and relationships saves no import
profile. For that route, send the next file to the assistant again and explain how to match
existing records; see [Loading with the assistant](/docs/use/loading-with-the-assistant/#the-next-file-and-the-saved-profile).

If you already have a separately saved import profile, follow the steps above to reuse it.
Starting through **Import…** can also recognise that saved layout and prepare the file without
an assistant session or AI cost. You still review the proposal and row check. **The saved layout does not fit this file**
offers **Read it with the assistant**. That sends the file and instructions to Claude Code,
can incur costs and keeps task files; see [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/).
A new sheet or changed layout needs review, not an assumption that the previous mapping fits.

## Remove a file you no longer need

1. On the profile page, choose **Delete the file…** beside the upload and load actions.
2. Read **Delete <file name>?**. It removes the upload and its stored analysis, stops a check
   still reading it, and keeps the profile and already loaded records.
3. Choose **Delete the file** to continue or **Cancel** to keep it. After deletion, upload a
   file again to check it. A failed deletion leaves its reason in the dialog; resolve that
   cause before retrying.

To stop reusing the profile itself, choose **Delete the profile…** and confirm **Delete the
profile**. Read [what each deletion keeps](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/#remove-an-uploaded-file-or-an-import-profile)
before confirming; deleting a profile does not reverse its earlier loads.

![Delete an uploaded workbook while keeping its import profile and loaded records](/docs/screens/use-import-file-delete-confirm.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/map-cod:
---
title: Map codes between systems
description: Find unmapped or ambiguous rows and choose, replace or remove a mapping.
reader: steward
---

Connect each source record to the intended target using a mapping grid. Codes from another
system are one example. See [Mapping grids](/docs/use/mapping-grids/) for states, limits and
permissions.

## Find the rows that need attention

1. Open an application in the current workspace and choose a collection with a mapping grid.
   Select the mapping tab. Check the heading and the source and target types in its description.
2. Check the banner. Choose **Live** for immediate changes, or
   [open a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) to prepare them together.
3. Search for the source records you need. Read their codes and other identifying fields.
   Select **Unmapped** for rows without a connection, **Mapped** for rows with a
   target, or, on a view where a source may hold only one, **Ambiguous** for rows with several. **All** removes the state restriction.
4. Inspect each target's name and identifying fields. Select a source name or target chip to
   open that record's page for a closer look. Decide whether the current state needs changing.
   Clear search and select **All** if an expected row is absent. A read error needs
   a retry; it does not mean a row is unmapped.

## Choose or replace a target

1. Choose **Map** on an unmapped row or **Change** on a filled row. **Change mapping** opens
   with the source name in its heading and the current targets, or **Not mapped**, under
   **Currently**. Check these before searching.
2. Search for the intended target and inspect its identifying fields. Select its radio button.
   If nothing matches, shorten the search and check the model's candidate rules. Do not select
   a similar name merely to fill the row.
3. Choose **Save mapping**. This sets the row to the selected target, replacing any previous
   targets, including all targets of an ambiguous row. Check the refreshed target and state.
   If the row no longer matches the active state filter, switch to **All** and find it again.
4. Choose **Cancel** if no correction is needed. Where **Save and next** is offered, it saves
   this choice and opens the next row; check that new source before choosing again.

![A mapping dialog for an unmapped row with target radio choices and a creation action](/docs/screens/mapping-grid-map-dialog.png)

*Above: T-9999, the fictional special day pass, is deliberately unmapped. The dialog shows
Not mapped and offers stop candidates and Create new stop. It was cancelled; the screenshot
does not suggest that this pass needs a stop mapping.*

To retain several valid targets, use the record's [relationship controls](/docs/guide/use/relate-records/).
Saving one selection in this dialog resolves the row to one target.

## If the target does not exist

1. Search carefully first. If a new record is needed, choose **Create new** followed by its
   type name. The target creation form opens.
2. Check its application and parent where offered, then fill **Name** and the required fields.
   Choose **Create**, or **Cancel** to return without creating a target.
3. After creation, review the selected target in the mapping dialog and choose **Save mapping**.
   Creating a record does not itself finish the mapping. If you cancel now, the new record remains.

## Remove a mapping

1. Choose **Change** on the row and review **Currently**.
2. Choose **Remove mapping** where offered. This clears the row's mapping and keeps the source
   and target records. Check **Unmapped**, using **All** if your previous filter hides the row.
3. If the dialog says the mapping is required, choose an allowed replacement instead of clearing
   it. **Cancel** keeps the current mapping.

## Handle a refused save

If **Mapping conflict** appears, read **Current mapping** and compare it with your intended
selection. Choose **Cancel** to leave it as it now stands. Choose **Continue with my selection**
only after reviewing the other change, then save again. A further intervening change can cause
another refusal. Other **Save failed** messages name a rule to resolve before retrying.

If editing actions are missing, check your context and permissions. Reader can inspect; Contributor
works in change sets; direct Live writes need **Edit live**. Publishing proposed mappings has its
own conflict checks; see [Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/).

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0. See [The example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/)
for sources and fictional additions.*
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/move-se:
---
title: Move several records together
description: Select records in a tree and move them to one parent as a single confirmed change.
reader: steward
---

Move several records together while keeping their types. See
[Hierarchies](/docs/use/hierarchies/) for allowed placement and descendants.

1. Open an editable tree in Live or a change set. Use Cmd or Ctrl to add or remove records
   from selection, or Shift for a range. By keyboard, use Ctrl+Space and Shift+arrows.
   Selection does not itself open a different record; Escape clears it.
2. Drag the selected records to the intended parent, or right-click the selection (Shift+F10
   by keyboard) and choose **Move to…**.
3. In the move dialog, search for the parent and read disabled choices' reasons. The destination
   must allow every selected record without a type change. A place needing **Becomes …** is
   for an individual restructuring operation, not this multi-record move.
4. Review the destination and selected records, then confirm the move. They move together or
   none moves. Their descendants stay beneath them; IDs and history are kept.
5. Check their new paths. Live moves are immediate; change-set moves await publication.

On touch, hold a record still for half a second until it lifts. Moving first scrolls; a short
tap opens. Drag near an edge to scroll. In the sidebar, releasing where you lifted opens the
node menu and offers Move to. Read-only trees and publication trees do not drag.

A drop chooses a parent or level, not a manual position among siblings. The view's order
controls sibling positions. If records changed meanwhile, review the refreshed state and try
again rather than assuming the first destination is still valid.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/open-a-:
---
title: Open a retired or unavailable workspace
description: Read a retired workspace and understand why another workspace cannot be opened.
reader: steward
---

A retired workspace is readable history. An unavailable workspace cannot currently be served.
See [Workspaces](/docs/use/workspaces/) for choosing a dataset.

1. For a retired workspace, open **Settings › Workspaces** where your access offers it.
   Select the workspace and choose **Open workspace**. It may be absent from the active
   workspace selector. Check the **Retired · read only** mark and the context band’s
   **Retired: read only.** message.
2. Browse its applications, records and retained publications. Editing records, relationships,
   change sets and migrations is refused. Ask the workspace administrator about reactivation;
   do not try to work around read-only status.
3. If the destination says **Workspace … cannot be opened** or **Cannot be opened**, read its
   reason. The model's language can be too old or too new, or its release can be invalid.
   Other workspaces are not affected and nothing was changed by opening the address.
4. Send the reason to the responsible model administrator or operator. **Bring it up to date**
   and **Review the change**, when offered to an authorised administrator, belong to
   [Model language versions](/docs/model/model-language-versions/). A steward should choose
   another readable workspace while that is resolved.
5. If the page instead says **No workspace …**, check the address with its sender. If an
   application or type **is not in this workspace's model**, use **Workspaces whose model has …**
   to select a suitable destination, or **Go back**. If none exists, the page says **No other workspace's model has it.**

![Unavailable example workspace with its model-language reason, recovery review and other workspaces](/docs/screens/workspace-cannot-open.png)

An unavailable model is different from missing Browse access. Ask about the displayed reason;
repeatedly retrying a record save does not repair it.

For a missing application, collection or record type, the suggested destination button reads
**Open in …** with the workspace name. It opens that workspace; recheck its model and context
on arrival. The start-page button instead keeps you in the workspace already named.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/open-an:
---
title: Open an application
description: Choose a workspace, open an application and select a view of its records.
reader: steward
---

Open the right data before searching or editing. See
[Applications](/docs/use/applications/) and [Workspaces](/docs/use/workspaces/) for how models,
datasets and views fit together.

## Start from Home

1. Select the refiroo name in the top bar to open Home. Under **Your workspaces**, find the
   intended workspace. Check the model name and release on its card; similar workspace names
   do not guarantee the same data or structure.
2. Choose the workspace’s name or tile to open its page, then choose an application. Its
   default view opens in that workspace. The application names come from the model. An
   application link on the Home card opens that application directly.
3. Check **Workspace** in the sidebar and the context banner above the records. Choose **Live**
   for current data, or open the intended change set or publication. A publication is read-only;
   Live saves apply immediately.

![Home showing workspace names, model releases and application buttons](/docs/screens/workspaces-home.png)

*Above: Graubünden offers Network, Systems and Names. Default offers RDM Master, RDM Systems
and RDM Translations under a different model.*

If no workspace is offered, ask an administrator for **Browse** access. If Home reports a loading
failure, retry it before concluding that no workspaces exist.

## Choose a collection and view

1. Select an application in the top bar, using **More** if it does not fit. On a phone,
