   choose it in the band beneath the top bar. Read its sidebar collections; switching applications
   can change which collections are offered. If a collection group is folded, expand it.
2. Choose the collection you need. Check the page heading and description.
3. If tabs appear below the heading, choose the view that suits your task. A table helps
   [find records](/docs/guide/use/find-records/); a tree helps
   [arrange records](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/); a mapping grid helps
   [map records](/docs/guide/use/map-codes-between-systems/); a relation matrix helps
   [check coverage](/docs/guide/use/fill-in-a-relation-matrix/).
4. Check the banner again before changing anything. Opening an application or changing a view
   does not itself save a data change.

![An application with multiple views of the selected collection](/docs/screens/app-systems.png)

*Above: System codes in Systems has a table and the Codes to stops and Codes to municipalities
mapping tabs. Other collections can offer different view kinds.*

A missing view may simply not be declared by the model. Ask a model administrator about the
intended configuration. An empty collection means there are no matching records in that context;
a reported loading error needs a retry instead.

## Switch workspace

Follow [Switch workspace](/docs/guide/use/switch-workspace/) to choose another dataset and check
its model, applications and context before editing.

## If the address does not fit this workspace

After switching, read the toast if the model or release differs. An old bookmark can open
**Not in this model**: the named application, collection or type is absent here. Choose one of
the offered workspaces whose model has it, or return Home and open an application this workspace
provides. If the workspace itself cannot be served, read the displayed reason and ask the
operator for help. Other workspaces remain available. A retired workspace can be opened through
**Settings › Workspaces** where permitted, but stays read-only.

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0. See [The example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/)
for sources and fictional additions.*
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/prepare:
---
title: Prepare and publish a change set
description: Prepare related changes, review and validate them, then publish them together.
reader: steward
---

Prepare changes away from Live, review them and publish them together. See
[Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) for how starting data, live work and publications fit together.

For changes beyond fields, follow [Relate records](/docs/guide/use/relate-records/),
[Arrange records in a tree](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/),
[Map codes between systems](/docs/guide/use/map-codes-between-systems/) or
[Fill in a relation matrix](/docs/guide/use/fill-in-a-relation-matrix/).


## Start or open a change set

1. Open an application in the current workspace. Check **Workspace** in the sidebar, then
   choose **Change sets** at the top. The list identifies existing change sets by name and
   shows their versions, starting data and creators.
2. To continue existing work, find its name and choose **Open change set**. **Changes in this
   change set** opens first. Choose **See the data with these changes** to reach its lists,
   and check the name in the band before editing. Opening a change set does not publish it.
3. To start separate work, choose **Start from current live data**. Enter a **Change set name**
   that helps other people recognise the work. If **Model version** appears, keep the active
   version for ordinary data corrections; coordinate a different choice with a model administrator.
4. Choose **Create change set**. The new set opens with a copy of the current live data.
   If creation is refused, read the message and resolve the named problem before retrying.
   Choose **Cancel** if you do not intend to create it.

![The change-set list with controls to open existing work or start a new set](/docs/screens/change-sets-list.png)

*Above: Network in the Graubünden workspace lists December 2026 timetable change. Open change set
continues that work; Start from current live data begins a separate proposal.*

If creation controls are unavailable, check your access with a workspace administrator. Opening
and reading an existing set does not itself give permission to change or publish it.

## Make the changes

1. Check the orange **Change set** band. It names the intended set, its number of changes
   and state. Open **Details** for its creator, creation time, version and model. If the band
   says **Live**, open your change set
   before making staged corrections.
2. Choose a collection and find a record. [Correct its fields](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/)
   and save using the ordinary record controls. Check that the saved values appear in the
   change set, then repeat for the other records in your proposal.
3. If you switch applications or inspect **Live**, check the banner again before the next edit.
   Return to the named change set to continue preparing it. Later live corrections do not
   refresh its starting copy.
4. If a save is refused, read the message and review the current record or change-set version
   before retrying. If the band says **waits for approval**, open **Details** for the submission
   and withdraw the request before editing.

![An open change set with its name, context banner and preparation controls](/docs/screens/change-set-open.png)

*Above: December 2026 timetable change is open over Stops in Network. The orange banner offers
Review changes, Validate change set and Publish change set. The example proposal changes
Valid to (exclusive) on several stops: the first date on which each stop is no longer valid.*

## Review and validate

1. Choose **Review changes** in the banner. On **Records**, inspect every intended addition,
   change or removal. Expand a row with its arrow to compare the before and after values.
   Check names and paths to confirm that you changed the intended records.
2. Choose **Relationships** and review the connection changes too. If a long review is hard to
   inspect, use **Filter** to narrow it, then remove the restriction to check the remaining work.
   An empty filtered review does not mean the whole proposal is empty.
3. Choose **See the data with these changes** to correct anything unexpected. Save those corrections and
   review again before proceeding.
4. Choose **Validate change set**. If problems are reported, use the named records and reasons
   to correct them in the change set, then validate again. Do not proceed while problems remain.
5. Check for **Change set validation passed**. In the direct publication flow, this enables
   **Publish change set**. Validate again after any further edits.

![The record review with changed fields, record paths and a Relationships tab](/docs/screens/change-set-review.png)

*Above: the timetable change's Records tab lists stops with Changed: Valid to (exclusive).
The arrows open the differences; Relationships provides a separate connection review.*

If publication remains unavailable after validation, read the banner for a model-version or
approval requirement and check your permissions. If **Submit for publication** is offered,
follow [Approve a change set](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/#submit-your-work). Submission leaves
the proposal waiting for a decision; it does not make the changes live.

## Publish

These steps apply when **Publish change set** is offered. When approval is needed, the banner
instead offers **Submit for publication**. Follow [Approve a change set](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/)
for submission, corrections and the approver's decision. See
[Inbox and approvals](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/) for the rules and notices.

1. Choose **Publish change set**. The **Publish this change set?** confirmation opens.
2. Read the confirmation. Check the proposed version and the current publication it would
   replace. Follow **Review changes** if you need another look. Choose **Cancel** if you are
   not ready; the change set stays available for preparation.
3. To apply the reviewed changes, choose **Publish change set** in the confirmation. Wait for
   the result. Success is reported as **Published as Publication** followed by its number.
   Check the changed records in **Live** and find the resulting snapshot under **Publications**.
4. If publication is refused, read the reported reason. For conflicts, compare the named records
   with **Live** and agree which corrections are needed before changing the proposal. Review
   and validate the revised work before attempting publication again. A conflict or failed
   check publishes nothing; the proposed work remains available.

![The publication confirmation after validation has passed](/docs/screens/change-set-publish-confirm.png)

*Above: December 2026 timetable change has passed validation and its confirmation is open.
No publication has been confirmed in this screenshot; Cancel leaves it unpublished.*

An intervening live edit can still prevent publication after validation. See
[Publishing and intervening live work](/docs/use/change-sets/#publishing-and-intervening-live-work)
for what conflicts and what is preserved. A refusal needs review before another attempt.

## Discard work you no longer need

1. Open the change set and check all its proposed changes, including work by colleagues.
   If it is waiting for approval, its submitter or an approver must **Withdraw request** first.
2. Open **More change set actions** and choose **Discard change set**.
3. Read **Discard this change set?**. **Discard change set** removes all staged work in it.
   Choose **Cancel** to keep it. Live records and existing publications stay unchanged.
4. If the action fails, read its reason and refresh the change set before trying again.
   There is no undo for discarded work; a fresh change set does not recover those edits.

---
title: Prepare under the next model version
description: Coordinate a proposal’s model release with the workspace before publishing.
reader: steward
---

A change set can use an installed release while Live still uses another. Coordinate this
with a model administrator. See [Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) and
[Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/) for the reviewed conversion process.

1. When creating a change set, choose **Model version** if a choice is offered. The starting
   records must fit it. A refusal leaves Live unchanged; inspect the named incompatibilities.
2. In an editable change set, use **More change set actions › Change model version** to choose
   a **Target release** where the existing content fits without a conversion. Resolve unsaved
   input before switching. Wait for the new model to load before editing further.
3. If the releases differ, read **This change set uses a different model version**. Ordinary
   publication needs matching releases. **Move this change set to …** instead previews
   converting your proposal to the workspace's release, with no change to Live.
4. Review converted values, changed types, removals and items requiring a fix. Resolve refusals
   and explicitly accept losses before confirming **Move change set**. If the review is stale,
   choose **Preview again**. This move needs background jobs and suitable change-set rights.
5. The alternative **Move … to … and publish…** previews moving the workspace to the proposal's
   release. It needs model-release and publication rights and follows the same approval policy
   as publication. Have the responsible model administrator review it. **Migrate and publish**
   changes the workspace and publishes together, or does neither.

A submitted change set is frozen, including release changes. Its submitter or an authorised
approver must withdraw the request before editing. A changed model reload clears obsolete list
positions and can open another declared view if the old page disappeared. If the release change
succeeded but refreshing failed, reload and check the pinned release before saving; repeating
the move blindly is not recovery.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/propose:
---
title: Propose a change
description: Prepare a correction as a Contributor without changing Live.
reader: steward
---

A Contributor prepares changes in a change set for someone authorised to publish.
Read [Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) for shared work and publication.

1. In Live, open the record and choose **Propose a change**, or choose **Propose a new …**
   on a collection to add a record. These offers depend on your permission for that type.
2. If you have no open change set of your own, the **Propose a change** dialog asks for
   **Change set name**. Give the work a recognisable name, then choose **Start and edit**.
   **Cancel** leaves Live unchanged. If one already exists, refiroo continues your newest
   open change set instead of asking for another name.
3. Check the amber band for the change-set name. The Live band can also identify **Your change
   set** and its count. Make the correction with the ordinary field or record form; the save
   goes into the change set.
4. Open **Review changes** and check every proposed record and relationship. Your change set
   is shared with other authorised workers, so it can contain work beyond your latest edit.
5. Submit it for publication where offered, or ask someone holding Publish in this workspace
   to publish it. Submission freezes editing until withdrawal or send-back.

![Propose a change dialog with a change-set name and Start and edit above a record in Live](/docs/screens/contributor-propose-change.png)

*Above: a Contributor proposes a correction to Chur Wiesental in the Network application,
Graubünden workspace. Cancel closes the dialog without starting a change set.*

A Reader sees **You can read this workspace** and whom to ask, rather than proposal controls.
Narrowed permissions show actions only for the covered types. Check **Account › What you can do**
if an expected offer is absent. A publication and a retired workspace remain read-only.

---
title: Propose targets
description: Ask for mapping suggestions, review the proposed targets and publish the mappings you keep.
reader: steward
---

Use this to prepare mappings for unmapped records. You need **Use AI proposals** and **Work in
change sets**, an enabled AI provider and permission to send record values. Read
[Mapping grids](/docs/use/mapping-grids/#targets-proposed-by-ai) for candidate and confidence limits.
Names and displayed fields go to the provider; requests can incur costs and are recorded.
See [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) for details.

1. Open a mapping grid in the current workspace. Apply search or choose a parent if you want
   only those sources considered. Open **Propose targets**. The dialog counts the unmapped
   sources and states what is sent. If none remain, close it and change the scope if necessary.
2. Under **Into change set**, use the current change set or choose **New change set** and name
   it. Without an open change set, enter **Name of the new change set**. No suggestion writes Live.
3. Choose **Propose**. **Proposing targets…** shows progress. You can **Close** the dialog and
   the job continues; its end is announced. **Stop** ends further work but keeps mappings already
   proposed. If someone changed the change set before the request started, review it and propose
   again against its current state.
4. Read the result counts and warnings. **Left unmapped: no likely target** needs your own
   investigation. **Changed meanwhile, not touched** means someone changed the source while the
   answer was being prepared. A failed or unanswered batch is not a decision that no target exists.
5. When at least one target was proposed, choose **Show proposed** to open the change set's grid with **Proposed** selected. Inspect
   each target, its displayed fields, confidence and reason. On a phone, expand **Why?**.
   Use **Change** and **Save mapping** to replace a wrong target. Its AI mark disappears.
   If no target was proposed, **Show proposed** is absent. Choose **Close** and investigate
   the unmapped sources manually.
6. Review the whole change set, including any earlier work in it. Follow
   [Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) to validate,
   obtain any required approval and publish. The published history says which mappings were
   proposed by AI and who published them.

![A finished proposal job with no proposed targets, one source left unmapped and Close](/docs/screens/use-mapping-proposal-result.png)

If the provider fails, read the warning and review any proposals already saved. You can prepare
mappings manually through [Map codes between systems](/docs/guide/use/map-codes-between-systems/).
If the action disappears, ask an administrator whether the provider, send level or your access changed.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/relate-:
---
title: Relate records
description: Connect records, replace a single connection and remove an optional relationship.
reader: steward
---

Connect two records using a relationship declared by the model. See
[Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/) for candidates, ownership and required connections.

## Open the relationship section

1. Open an application in the current workspace and [find the record](/docs/guide/use/find-records/).
   Check its name, identifying fields and path.
2. Check **Live** for an immediate change, or [open a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/)
   to prepare work for publication. Check the banner before editing.
3. Scroll to the relationship section you need. Its heading describes the connected records.
   Read existing entries before adding another. **No relationships yet** means the section is
   empty; a loading error needs a retry instead.

![Relationship sections with add, change and delete controls](/docs/screens/relationships-stop.png)

*Above: Chur Wiesental in Network has Modes, Operator and System codes sections. Modes permits
several connections; Operator permits one. Further sections continue below the capture.*

## Connect an existing record

1. Choose **Add relationship**, or **Set** followed by the relationship name when the empty
   section permits just one. The connection dialog opens.
2. Check **Relationship**, including its direction. **Outgoing** reads the relationship from
   this record towards the chosen one; **incoming** reads it from the other end. If several
   choices are offered, select the intended meaning before searching.
3. Under **Object**, type part of the related record's name or a searchable field. Read any
   hint explaining which records are offered. Select a result, checking its path. Typing alone
   leaves **Nothing selected** and does not enable saving.
4. Fill any fields carried by the relationship. These describe the connection, rather than
   changing the other record's fields.
5. Choose **Create**, or **Set** in the single-connection dialog. On success the dialog closes;
   check that the connected record appears in the section. **Cancel** abandons the connection;
   if asked to discard unsaved changes, confirm only if that is what you intend.

![The Connect an object dialog with a relationship choice and candidate search](/docs/screens/relationship-picker-mode.png)

*Above: Add relationship in Chur Wiesental's Modes panel offers Served by mode (outgoing) and
candidate modes such as Boat and Bus. Nothing is selected; this dialog was cancelled.*

If a record is missing, clear or shorten the search and check the workspace, context, type and
candidate hint. A model can limit candidates by their own or their ancestors' fields. Ask a
model administrator about the rule if the expected record is still unavailable. A refused save
may report a duplicate, a number limit or changed data; resolve that reason before retrying.

## Replace a single connection

1. In a section that allows one related record, choose its **Change** action. Read **Now:**
   to confirm the connection you intend to replace.
2. Search and select the replacement under **Object**. Check its identifying fields and path.
   The currently connected record is not offered as its own replacement.
3. Choose **Change**. The replacement is saved together; check the section's new entry.
   Choose **Cancel** to keep the existing connection.
4. If the dialog says the relationship changed after the list was read, close it and review
   the refreshed section. Reopen **Change** only if replacement is still appropriate.

![A replacement dialog identifying the current record and offering other candidates](/docs/screens/relationship-picker-operator.png)

*Above: Operated by currently connects Chur Wiesental to Rhätische Bahn. The dialog offers
replacement operators. It was cancelled, leaving Rhätische Bahn connected.*

Where a relationship has its own fields, its **Edit** action opens those fields. Correct them
and choose **Save**; use **Change** when replacing the related record itself. A version refusal
requires reviewing the current saved connection before saving again.

## Remove an optional connection

1. Find the exact relationship row and choose its delete button. Check both record names
   first, especially where a section contains several connections.
2. Read **Delete relationship?**. The connected records remain; only this connection is removed.
3. Choose **Delete relationship** to proceed, or **Cancel** to keep it. Check the refreshed
   section after success. If removal is refused because the connection is required, keep it
   and review the intended correction; use a replacement where allowed.

![The Delete relationship confirmation explaining that both records remain](/docs/screens/relationship-delete-confirm.png)

*Above: deleting Chur Wiesental's Served by mode connection would leave both the stop and Train.
The confirmation was cancelled, so the connection remains.*

To change containment, [move the record](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/).
Deleting a record has a different impact; see [Records](/docs/use/records/#deleting-a-record).

## Create an owned related record

Some sections offer an add action named after the related type rather than connecting an
existing record. Use it when you need a new dependent record.

1. Choose that section's add action. Check the new record form and its already supplied
   connection to the source record.
2. Under **Parent**, search and select the intended container where requested. Check the
   selected path; search text alone does not select it.
3. Fill **Name** and the type's other fields. Set any field that determines whether the record
   counts as current according to the model's rule.
4. Choose **Create** and check the new entry in the original section. Correct any reported
   missing values or duplicate before retrying. **Cancel** leaves without creating the record.

![A new related record form with parent choices and its owner already supplied](/docs/screens/stop-add-translation.png)

*Above: Add Name translation on Chur Wiesental opens a form with Translates already set to
that stop. Parent offers languages; Name, Translated name and Active describe the new record.
The form was cancelled. This is an example of creating an owned record.*

If editing actions are absent, check your context and
[record permissions](/docs/use/records/#who-may-read-and-change-records). A publication is read-only;
a Reader can inspect connections but cannot change them.

A lock on a row explains why it cannot be deleted or changed independently. Parent connections
are maintained by moving the record. Beside a tree, **Connected** chips open related records;
open the full record page to use the relationship tables and their tooltip-labelled icons.

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0. See [The example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/)
for sources and fictional additions.*
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/replace:
---
title: Replace a record’s related records
description: Review a complete relationship set and save its additions and removals together.
reader: steward
---

Choose exactly which records should stay connected. This applies where the table offers
editing for a multi-record relationship. See [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/).

1. In an editable table, find the record's relationship column and choose its pencil, or the
   corresponding row-menu action. The dialog identifies **Related records of …** and the
   relationship. Parent, ownership, computed and read-only columns have no such editor.
2. Review the ticked records, pinned first and counted. They are the current set, not merely
   the first few chips shown in the table.
3. Search for eligible records and tick additions. Untick records to remove their connections.
   Review the whole ticked set, including choices outside the current search. Unticking removes
   the connection, not the related record.
4. Choose **Save**. Additions and removals save together as one operation; there is no partial
   replacement if a rule refuses it. Connections still selected keep their identity and fields.
5. Check the refreshed column and save notice. If **Nothing was changed** appears, read the
   cause and reopen the current set before trying again. Another person's intervening change
   must be reviewed rather than overwritten.

For a single-valued relationship, use **Set relationship** or **Change** to choose its one
record instead. To replace sets on several records, use
[Change relationships of many records](/docs/guide/use/change-relationships-of-many-records/).
The ordinary relationship panel otherwise maintains connections one at a time.

![Relationship editor with one checked record, two matching unchecked candidates, the selected count and Save disabled.](/docs/screens/replace-related-records.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/reshape:
---
title: Reshape a hierarchy
description: Preview a type change or inserted or removed level inside a change set.
reader: steward
---

Restructuring changes the meaning or levels of a hierarchy. It is available in a change set,
where the model permits it. For a parent-only move, use
[Arrange records in a tree](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/).

1. Open a change set and locate the record in its tree. Open its node menu with its actions button
   or Shift+F10. Choose the offered **Change type…**, **Insert level above…**, **Remove this
   level…** or **Change type of all … in here…**. A move to a **Becomes …** destination opens
   the same kind of reviewed restructuring.
2. Choose **New type**, or **Type of the new level** and **Name of the new level**, as the
   selected action requires. Review any records included beneath the level.
3. Read the plan's counts and open **By record** to inspect the affected records. **By type**
   compares their types and fields. Use **Show** to filter by **Needing input**, **Refused**,
   **Changing type**, **With something left without a place** or **With something restored**
   to inspect the relevant records.
4. Supply values and required connections where the new type needs them. Choose the source
   of a value where the plan offers alternatives. Values that fail the destination's rules
   need input rather than being silently carried over. Something without a place remains
   in history; it is not an editable field of the new type.
5. Resolve all refusals and missing input. **Ready to apply** means the preview can proceed.
   Choose **Apply to the change set**. If **The plan changed** appears, review its new preview
   before applying again.
6. Choose **Review the change set**. Inspect changed types, fields and paths, then validate
   and publish or submit through the usual process. Live retains the earlier structure until
   publication.

Records keep their identity and history. There is no general Undo for data edits; restructuring
can offer compatible values back from effective earlier type changes. It does not restore
intentional clears or discarded work. See [Hierarchies](/docs/use/hierarchies/).

![Insert a level above a record: one move and one new record, a required Mode code still empty, and Apply to the change set disabled.](/docs/screens/hierarchy-restructure-plan.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/review-:
---
title: Review what a change set changes
description: Inspect record and relationship differences before validation or a publication decision.
reader: steward
---

Compare proposed work with the data the change set started from. See
[Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/#review-explains-the-differences).

1. From **Change sets**, choose **Open change set** to open **Changes in this change set**.
   If you are already browsing its data, choose **Review changes** in the amber band. Confirm
   its name; open **Details** for its source. If it started from a publication, the earlier values come from that publication,
   not today's Live.
2. Under **Records**, filter by change kind or record type. Open a row to read before/after
   values and paths. A moved record names both parents. A type-change filter can match either
   its old or new type, so check the difference itself.
3. Open **Relationships** and inspect additions, changes and removals separately. A record
   review alone does not account for every changed connection.
4. Scroll or jump through the lists. The address retains the tab, filters and position so
   you can return to the same part of the review.
5. Choose **See the data with these changes** to return to editing for corrections, then
   choose **Validate change set**. Resolve its named
   problems and validate the new version again before publishing or submitting.

A record created and deleted in the same change set contributes no remaining change and is
omitted. A record edited back to its original values can still count as changed, because
publication still checks the version it claims. A successful validation is not protection
against later Live conflicts; publication checks again.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/see-who:
---
title: See who changed what
description: Trace an edit from a record, workspace activity or your own changes.
reader: steward
---

Choose the view that matches your question. See [History](/docs/use/history/) for the meaning
of authors, event kinds and publication context.

## Check one record

1. [Find the record](/docs/guide/use/find-records/) in the intended workspace and open it.
2. Scroll to **History**. Start with **All** and **By: Anyone** to avoid hiding an event.
3. Choose **Values**, **Relationships** or **Moves** to narrow the list, or select a person in **By**.
4. Read the action, author and time. Expand the entry's arrow to inspect the stored detail,
   such as the previous and new field values where recorded.
5. Check whether the action was prepared in a change set or applied by a publication before
   comparing it with the current fields.

![Record history below its relationships, with author and time on each event](/docs/screens/use-history-stop-changed.png)

*Above: Thusis Süd's history shows the correction and its later publication. The current field is THSD.*

## Check activity across records

1. Where available to your role, open **Settings**, **Workspaces** and select the workspace.
2. Choose **Activity**. It lists the newest actions first.
3. Under **What**, choose **Records**, **Relationships**, **Change sets** or **Publications**.
   Return to **Everything** to see their sequence together.
4. Read who acted and the context beside the time. Follow a linked person's name to inspect
   their changes if you need to trace their other work.

![Workspace activity with Everything selected](/docs/screens/use-history-activity.png)

*Above: Graubünden's activity connects the correction change set with the resulting publication.*

## Find your own work

1. Select the refiroo name to open Home. Read **Your recent changes** for recent actions.
2. Choose **See all your changes**. The **Your changes** page opens.
3. Choose **Workspace**, **What** and **Period**. Read each result's action and context.
   Widen those filters if the expected action is missing.

![Your changes with workspace, kind and period filters](/docs/screens/use-history-changes.png)

*Above: the list is narrowed to Guide Admin's work in Graubünden.*

A failed read needs a retry; an empty filtered result needs broader filters. If workspace
management is unavailable, use the record's History or Your changes, or ask someone with the
necessary access to inspect workspace Activity. History cannot restore a value by itself:
follow [Correct a record](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/) to make a new correction.

Under each day heading, read the newest entries first. On the record's History, use **Load older history**
to read 20 more after the initial ten and **Show fewer** to shorten the list. Check a job or
publication named as the cause; **client** marks a system's work, and **Before sign-in** marks an
older entry with no recorded author. Your changes has no value details or export: return to the
record's History for the saved values.

## Read an AI account or assistant origin

For a short explanation with links to the counted changes, follow
[Explain a period in history](/docs/guide/use/explain-a-period-in-history/). Opening History
sends nothing; asking for the account sends counts and, at values, names to the provider.
Calls can incur costs and are recorded; [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) explains
sending and retention.

On a record history entry, read **Proposed by the AI assistant** or **Prepared by an assistant**
alongside who asked, who edited and who published. These are different responsibilities.
An external assistant’s displayed name is its own claim. The personal Changes page has no
assistant filter; use [the record’s History](/docs/use/history/#work-prepared-by-an-assistant)
for the mark.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/set-up-:
---
title: Set up email notices
description: Turn on email, choose notice kinds and check your digest schedule.
reader: steward
---

Choose email copies without changing your inbox. See
[Notification settings](/docs/use/notifications-settings/) for eligibility and limits.

1. Open **Settings › Notification email**, or choose **Notification email settings** from
   the Notifications page. Check the address under **Email**.
2. Turn on **Email me when something arrives in my inbox**. If no switch is offered, read the
   reason: mail may not be set up or your account may have no address. Ask an administrator
   to resolve it; following workspaces can still work without mail.
3. Under **How each kind reaches me**, choose **At once**, **Digest** or **Off** for each kind.
   Changes save immediately. If an error appears, correct the cause and try again.
4. For a digest, choose **Every morning at 07:00** or **Mondays at 07:00** under **The digest**.
   Read the displayed time zone and **Next digest**. The browser supplies the zone; the hour
   is fixed. The first kind put into Digest starts a daily schedule automatically.
5. Return to **Notifications** for the full inbox. Reading a notice before its digest is sent
   leaves it out. Nothing eligible means no digest; older unread notices are not excluded
   merely because they are more than a day old.

To stop all email, turn the master switch off. To stop just one kind, choose **Off** beside
it. Inbox notices remain either way. Immediate mail does not backfill notices from before
you enabled email and only sends unread notices less than a day old.

![Notification email enabled with one kind assigned to a daily digest and its next time visible](/docs/screens/use-notification-email-digest-settings.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/start-f:
---
title: Start from an earlier publication
description: Use a retained snapshot as a proposal’s starting point without restoring it over Live.
reader: steward
---

Start a proposal from known published data. This is not a rollback. Read
[Publications](/docs/use/publications/) and [Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/).

1. Open **Publications** in the intended workspace. Find the snapshot by its number, date
   and model version; open it first if you need to verify its content.
2. On its row, open **More actions** and choose **Start a change set from this publication**.
   You need Work in change sets; Browse alone cannot create it.
3. Give the change set a name and confirm the creation form. Open it and check that its
   source names the intended publication and its model release.
4. Make the changes you intend. **Review changes** compares them with this source snapshot.
   It does not describe all differences between that old snapshot and today's Live.
5. Validate and publish or submit as usual. Only changes made in this change set are merged
   into current Live. Newer untouched Live work survives; conflicts prevent publication.

If the proposal's release differs from the workspace's, coordinate with a model administrator
and follow [Prepare under the next model version](/docs/guide/use/prepare-under-the-next-model-version/).
Withdrawing a publication or starting from it never restores its records over Live.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/stop-of:
---
title: Stop offering a value
description: Keep a record and its history while marking it unavailable or ending its validity.
reader: steward
---

Keep the record when it must remain identifiable for older references. The model must provide
an availability field or validity dates; these controls do not exist on every type.
Read [Records](/docs/use/records/#validity-periods).

1. Find and open the record. Check its workspace and whether the change should be immediate
   in **Live** or proposed in a change set.
2. If the model provides an availability field, edit it to **No** and save. In an editable
   tree, the availability switch or **Mark not …** menu action can change the same field.
   The label comes from the model. The record remains, even if a view filters it out.
3. If the type has validity dates, set its end to the first day on which it must no longer be
   valid. The end is exclusive: an end of 13 December means the last valid day is 12 December.
   If both dates are present, the end must be later than the start. Save the field.
4. Check the saved value and history, or review and publish the change set when ready.
   If the record disappears from a filtered view, clear its availability filter to inspect it.

Setting an end date does not schedule publication or remove the record. The browser has no
business-date selector for browsing an earlier state; a validity field filter is not a
whole-workspace date view. Ask the model administrator if the type offers neither mechanism.
Do not delete a record simply because its availability control is absent.

An availability flag does not automatically hide the value from every consuming system.
Each system's agreed reading rules decide whether unavailable records are included. If the
record still appears elsewhere, check that agreement with the integration owner rather than
deleting the record to make it disappear.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/switch-:
---
title: Switch workspace
description: Open another workspace and check its model, applications and data context.
reader: steward
---

Switch workspaces to work with another dataset. It does not copy or move records.
See [Workspaces](/docs/use/workspaces/) for models, access and retired workspaces.

## Choose from the sidebar

1. Check the current **Workspace** and the model and release beneath it.
2. Open the workspace selector. Search for the workspace if necessary. Check its model before
   selecting it: **Other model** means a different structure, and **Other release** means another
   release of the same model.
3. Choose the destination. Check the workspace name after it opens. If the previous application
   or view is unavailable there, choose one of the destination's applications and collections.
4. Read the context banner before editing. **Live** saves apply immediately; a change set holds
   proposed work; a publication is read-only. Open the intended context in the new workspace.

![The workspace selector with an Other model marker](/docs/screens/workspace-switcher.png)

*Above: Default is marked Other model while Network is open in Graubünden.*

![The destination workspace showing its different applications and an empty collection](/docs/screens/use-workspace-default.png)

*Above: choosing Default opens RDM Master and its Domains collection. The toast explains that
Default runs a different model from Graubünden. No records were copied.*

## Choose from Home

1. Select the refiroo name in the top bar.
2. Under **Your workspaces**, check the destination card's model and release.
3. Choose the workspace’s name or tile to open its page, then choose an application.
   Check the sidebar and banner in the application that opens.
   Continue with [Open an application](/docs/guide/use/open-an-application/).

If the selector is absent, only one workspace is available. If the intended workspace is missing,
ask an administrator about Browse access or retirement. Where permitted, **Manage workspaces**
opens the full management list; a retired workspace opened there is read-only.
If switching reports an error, retry and confirm which workspace is open before changing data.

## If the address does not fit this workspace

After switching, read the toast if the model or release differs. An old bookmark can open
**Not in this model**: the named application, collection or type is absent here. Choose one of
the offered workspaces whose model has it, or return Home and open an application this workspace
provides. If the workspace itself cannot be served, read the displayed reason and ask the
operator for help. Other workspaces remain available. A retired workspace can be opened through
**Settings › Workspaces** where permitted, but stays read-only.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/withdra:
---
title: Withdraw a publication
description: Remove the current designation while retaining the snapshot and Live data.
reader: steward
---

Withdraw when a publication should no longer be designated current. You need Publish in the
workspace. See [Publications](/docs/use/publications/) for what the designation means.

1. Open **Publications** and locate the row marked **Current**. Check its number and workspace.
2. Open the row's **More actions** and choose **Withdraw publication**.
3. Read **Withdraw Publication …?**. Confirm with **Withdraw publication**, or cancel to keep
   the current designation.
4. Check that the snapshot is **Withdrawn** and no publication is current. Live data, earlier
   publications and history remain. An earlier snapshot is not made current automatically.

If another publication became current meanwhile, the stale withdrawal can be refused. Reload
and review the current row before deciding again. This action does not retire the workspace,
delete the snapshot or undo its data changes. To prepare work from it, use
[Start from an earlier publication](/docs/guide/use/start-from-an-earlier-publication/).
guide/src/content/docs/integrate/api-ref:
---
title: The API reference
description: Find operation contracts and try requests against your instance.
reader: integrator
---

Open the [API reference](/docs/api/) to find the operations, request schemas and responses your integration uses. The pages at `/docs` explain capabilities and sequences; `/docs/api` renders the OpenAPI documents as an interactive reference using Scalar.

## Choose the right source

The reference opens with **Management API** and lists the consumer APIs declared by the selected workspace's model, each with its contract version. Retained earlier versions also have their own OpenAPI documents; their operations are marked deprecated and their introduction names the replacement and any announced sunset day. Select the version your client actually calls. Without an explicit workspace, it uses the default workspace. Reload the reference after changing a workspace's model release so its sources reflect that release. A consumer API missing from this list may belong to another workspace's model; check the workspace before changing your client.

In the browser, **Settings › Connections › API reference** lists the sources, versions and OpenAPI document links. Select a source name to open its reference. You can also open the [management source](/docs/api/?api=management), or discover consumer sources through the [API index](/docs/api/?api=management). See [Discovering the model](/docs/integrate/discovering-the-model/) for selecting a contract programmatically.

The management document describes the engine's management interface. Each consumer API has a separate document describing the contract declared in the model. Use those documents for generated clients and validation; the guide does not duplicate their schemas.

## Try an operation

The console sends real requests to the instance that serves it. When you are signed in in that browser, it starts with your identity and permissions and renews its console token while needed. A successful request can change data, start a job or publish a change when your permissions allow that operation.

To exercise an integration's access, supply its client token instead. A token you paste replaces the console's automatic token and is not renewed for you. Without a browser session, supply a token before trying protected operations. Consumer data requires a client token with the consumer audience and an API grant in the workspace; the browser identity alone cannot read it. Follow [Get a token](/docs/guide/integrate/get-a-token/) and [Read through a consumer API](/docs/guide/integrate/read-through-a-consumer-api/).

If the reference opens but the request is refused, inspect the operation's error and your [permissions](/docs/integrate/security-model-for-integrators/). If only management appears, the workspace's model may be unavailable or declare no consumer APIs. Check its [model context](/docs/integrate/workspaces-contexts-and-models/).

## Use it without internet access

The reference script is bundled with the engine by default. It does not need an external font, hosted client or telemetry service. An operator can instead select the pinned CDN script; that mode needs internet access from the browser. See [Configuration](/docs/run/configure/) for deployment settings.

The bundled reference uses Scalar 1.72.2. The operator can set `RDM_API_REFERENCE_SCRIPT=cdn` to use the pinned jsDelivr copy, checked by its integrity hash; `bundled` is the default. A pasted token is used as supplied, so use a consumer client token when trying consumer data operations. Consumer source links use `api=consumer-<name>-v<version>` and can include the intended workspace.

The [consumer index](/docs/api/?api=management) marks retained entries with `deprecated: true` and an optional `sunset`. These entries remain callable until a model release explicitly stops them. See [Earlier contract versions](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/#earlier-contract-versions) for response headers and stopped-version errors.
guide/src/content/docs/integrate/assista:
---
title: Assistant tasks
description: Submit a workbook or instructions, review the checked proposal and hand changes to a person for publication.
reader: integrator
---

Use an assistant task when a client needs to submit a workbook or instructions and let a person review the proposed model and data changes. The built-in assistant runs a Claude Code session through refiroo's API. It can prepare a model draft, check the file and load a change set. A person takes the final activation, migration or publication steps.

This is separate from [external assistants over MCP](/docs/integrate/assistants-and-agents/). The task API needs `AI_AGENT_COMMAND`, not `AI_PROVIDER` or `MCP_ENABLED`. Use the [AI task operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/ai) for request schemas and individual actions. The sequence below explains how to build a client around them.

## Before submitting

The deployment must allow integration jobs. The requester needs **Use AI proposals** and **Bulk and import** in the workspace. Loading a change set also needs **Work in change sets**. Model work requires the corresponding model permissions; permission to ask for AI does not supply them. Tasks are visible to their requester and workspace administrators. Other callers receive `AI_TASK_NOT_FOUND`.

Tasks require send level `values`. The session receives the instructions, workbook if supplied, workspace model and OpenAPI document, and can read records as needed. It uses Claude Code's configured credentials and incurs that service's charges. Each turn records tokens and any reported cost in refiroo; a missing cost is not a free turn. Tasks and workbooks normally remain for 90 days, and session files and transcripts remain while work can continue. Call-content logging is separate. Read [About AI](/docs/run/ai/) for the full data, cost and retention policy, and ask the operator to [set up the assistant](/docs/run/set-up-ai/) if it is unavailable.

The session's dedicated client has no more access than the requester and cannot approve, publish or activate a release. It is a client of kind `session`, not an agent client. It has no reusable secret and is omitted from ordinary client lists unless `kind=session` is requested. Narrowed type and application permissions remain in force.

## 1. Submit and follow the task

Send `POST /api/v1/ai/tasks` as multipart form data. Include the workspace and instructions in the JSON `request` part, and optionally an XLSX or CSV `file`. Words alone can request work on stored records; neither a file nor nonblank words gives `AI_TASK_NEEDS_WORDS`. The [create operation](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/ai) defines the fields and upload refusals.

Keep the returned task ID, version and job ID. A `202` means work was accepted, not reviewed or published. Follow the [job](/docs/integrate/jobs/) and reread the task for the proposal. The job kind is `aiTask`; task state and job state are separate. A worker restart ends an earlier still-running session before resuming, so two sessions do not work in the same task folder.

The [task response](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/ai) returns the original `words` uncut
and, beside them, `title`: a short title the assistant writes with its first answer. It is
`null` until then and for a task that ends before an answer. Name a words-only task by
`title` when present; otherwise use `words`, shortened at a word boundary with “…” if needed.
Keep the full request visible with the proposal. A workbook task keeps its file name, and
the assistant’s draft is named `Assistant: <title>` once the title arrives.

| Task state | Client behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `reading` | The file is being read or the session is starting. |
| `checking` | A session turn or dry run is working. While `ahead` is a number the task's job still waits for the assistant's worker: show how many tasks are ahead, not the work. |
| `checked` | Present the proposal for a person's review. |
| `loading` | Follow the engine loading checked items or a saved layout into a change set. |
| `loaded` | Inspect the result and show the next human action. This does not mean live data changed. |
| `failed` or `stopped` | Show the task's notes and offer continuation or discard. |
| `cancelled` | The task was discarded. Start a new task for new work. |

Do not use the legacy `read` state as a step: the response schema includes it, but current tasks do not enter it. Use `phase` for progress while a job runs. Reread before every action and claim the current `expectedVersion`; on `AI_TASK_VERSION_CONFLICT`, present the new task rather than replaying a stale decision.

## 2. Show what the proposal actually changes

At `checked`, present the summary, the outline per type, the questions and assumed answers, and the engine's checks. Link the `draftId` to the model editor. A person can edit that draft, and the next session turn rereads it.

For a workbook the assistant reads the file, model and workspace records itself, changes the
model draft where needed, and turns the file into batch items. It submits those items to the
[draft dry-run operation](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/model%20administration). The engine checks every
item against the draft's model in a transaction it rolls back. No record changes are saved by
that check and the assistant writes no import profile. The set must fit both the background
and atomic batch limits; see [Writing in bulk](/docs/integrate/writing-in-bulk/) and the
[API reference](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/model%20administration) for the limits and refusals.

Present `design.load` as **What the load does**: new records, existing records matched, new
relationships, refused items and rows read. Show its type table with changed counts and linked
types, expandable example records with typed values, relationships and source-cell references,
and the engine's findings of repeated names within a type, including their parents. Offer the
file-part ranges as secondary detail. These examples help review the proposal; they are not
the complete load. Questions concern only choices the file and the person's words leave open.

For these tasks, `design.itemsLoad` is true, `check.mode` is `items` and `check.sheets` is empty.
Use `design.load` for examples and source cells; do not request sheet changes when no sheet
sources exist. Tasks recorded with a profile and saved-layout checks keep per-sheet figures.
For those checks only, page the [checked-change operation](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/ai)
using a source number from `check.sheets`. An unknown source returns `AI_TASK_TABLE_UNKNOWN`;
before any check the operation returns `AI_TASK_STATE`.

`check.draftChanged` means the check predates an edit and does not describe the current draft.
For an items proposal, acceptance checks every item again first. If any is refused, the task
fails before installation or loading. A person can also ask for a revised proposal and check
before accepting. Saved-layout checks retain their stale-check refusal.

The person can answer the questions or give a correction in words. A correction starts another turn and another check; answers that all keep the assumed choices start nothing and leave the task `checked`, and any other answer starts a turn. Neither accepts the proposal. A draft held by another assistant task cannot be written by this session (`AI_TASK_DRAFT_HELD`). Use a draft of this task's own instead of trying to share it.

## 3. Accept, then hand over the result

Send the [acceptance action](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/ai) only after the person reviews the
proposal. For an items proposal, label it **Accept and load to change set**. The engine installs a release if
the model changed, opens a change set over current live data, and loads exactly the stored,
checked items as one atomic batch. No assistant turn runs. Without a model change, the change
set uses the workspace's current release. The engine neither activates nor publishes.

If the data changed and the batch refuses an item, none of the batch is written: its change set
is discarded and the task becomes `failed`, with notes naming refused records and their source
cells. A release installed before the refusal can remain installed. A correction or retry
returns to the assistant for a revised proposal and items check, followed by a new acceptance.
A successful items result includes the change set, counts, and `importJobId` naming the `batch`
job, whose `parameters.taskId` associates it with the task. An items load saves no import profile.

A proposal's `design.removals` lists what the person's words explicitly ask to remove: `kind` (`objectType`, `application`, `attribute` or `relationType`), `key`, `words`, the engine's counts `records`, `values` and `relationships`, and a plain `text` sentence to show before acceptance. A migration that would lose anything outside those removals is never offered: the task fails with a warning note naming the loss per type, and no data is changed.

Words-only tasks without a model change keep their **Accept** step: the session prepares a
nonempty change set on the current release. Model-only and record-move tasks keep **Accept the
model** and their migration or staged-move endings. Show the result according to what it contains:

| Result | Person's next action |
| --- | --- |
| `changeSetId` | Review the records and relationships, then publish under the workspace's approval policy. |
| `migration` | Preview and confirm the migration using its release and its mappings: `typeMappings` (with `toApplicationKey` for a type that moves to another application), `relationTypeMappings`, `splits` and `listConversions`, as the draft's migration states them joined with the assistant's moves. Whole-type moves change live data; a model-only change has no type moves and changes only the running model. No change set is created. |
| `changeSetId` with a distinct `thenReleaseId` | Activate the release holding both shapes, review and publish the change set, then activate the final release. |

When `thenReleaseId` equals `changeSetReleaseId`, the model keeps the old types alongside the new ones. There is no final removal step. Do not show an activation with nothing to do. A whole-type migration is confirmed by someone holding Model release; it does not use the change-set approval policy. A partial move uses that policy when its change set is published.

Link to [Model and release operations](/docs/integrate/model-and-release-operations/), [Move records between models](/docs/guide/integrate/move-records-between-models/) and [Changes, approvals and publication](/docs/integrate/changes-approvals-and-publication/) for these human-controlled boundaries. Never infer publication from `loaded` or assume every loaded task has `changeSetId`.

Proposed rows carry AI origin, the task and who requested them. Later edits record who edited them; publication preserves origin in history while the publishing person is the actor. This survives task expiry. MCP's `channel: mcp` identifies the other interface and is not the task's provenance marker.

## Repeated layouts can avoid a session

If a stored import profile fits the workbook as well as the engine's reading, refiroo prepares its proposal without starting Claude Code. This path has no assistant-session cost. Review its questions and check as usual, then use the saved-layout load action. That action can install and activate a changed draft when the requester holds Model release; the session path above never activates. Use the [task operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/ai) to distinguish these paths.

A workbook loaded from the assistant's checked items returns no reusable profile. Submit the
next file of the same layout to the assistant again. Reuse without a session requires an
import profile saved separately; an earlier assistant load is not enough. See
[Files, imports and exports](/docs/integrate/files-imports-and-exports/) for profile-based loading.

## Stop, correct or discard

Use the [task continuation and cancellation actions](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/ai), not a second create request, to continue the same task.

- A stopped or failed task can take correction words or retry from where the session was. The task's `canTell` tells the client when it can accept words.
- Stopping an active turn does not discard the task. It returns to the last proposal, or becomes `stopped` when none exists. A stopped load discards the change set it was creating and returns to the accepted proposal. Inspect warnings if the stopped turn already edited the draft.
- Correcting a loaded task before publication discards its change set, including people's edits. For an items load, the assistant then revises the proposal and checks the items again; present that proposal for another acceptance before loading. Obtain the person's decision with the discard consequence visible before sending the correction.
- Discarding a loaded, unpublished task also discards its change set. A published or discarded set cannot be corrected through that old session; start new work.
- A saved-layout proposal can return from its load stage to the proposal. It can also be read with the assistant if the saved design no longer fits.

A loaded, failed or stopped task can keep its session files while it can continue. Publication, change-set discard, confirmed migration, task discard or expiry ends the session; the next task read or expiry sweep cleans its folder, logs and transcript and deactivates the client. Installed releases that nothing uses are retired rather than deleted; pre-existing releases are left alone. See [retention](/docs/run/ai/#what-is-kept) for operational details.

## Recover from a refusal

| Refusal | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `AI_NOT_CONFIGURED` | Ask the operator to configure `AI_AGENT_COMMAND`; a provider alone cannot run tasks. |
| `AI_SEND_LEVEL_TOO_LOW` | The task requires `values`; lowering a request cannot override the instance ceiling. Use a manual import if sending values is not allowed. |
| `AI_TASK_NOT_FOUND` | Check task ID, retention and requester or workspace-administrator access. |
| `AI_TASK_STATE` | Reread state and result; use only an action allowed now. |
| `AI_TASK_VERSION_CONFLICT` | Reread and review the current proposal before sending its version. |
| `AI_TASK_CHECK_STALE` | The saved-layout draft changed after its check; obtain a new checked proposal. |
| `AI_TASK_NOTHING_TO_LOAD` | Correct the design so the saved-layout load has something to import. |
| `AI_TASK_DRAFT_HELD` | Have the session use its own draft. |
| `AI_ASSISTANT_ROLE_CHANGED` | Ask a security administrator to restore the assistant role's required groups as the message explains. |

The task's notes explain a session failure; the call record can provide a diagnostic reference. A turn over the session limit (`AI_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, 30 minutes) is stopped as a person's Stop is: the task returns to its last point with a note, and the person can continue or try again. Provider-call timeouts are separate from this session limit. Fix credentials or reachability with the operator, then continue the task rather than treating a failed turn as a successful load.

Use the proposal and acceptance actions for assistant tasks. A `/plan` action and a task `plan` are not available; the changes read selects by `source`, not `table`. Use ordinary import profiles for deterministic loading without a session.

---
title: Assistants and agents
description: Connect an assistant through MCP, read within grants and prepare changes for a person to review.
reader: integrator
---

An external assistant can read refiroo and prepare changes through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Connect it to the instance's `/mcp` address. A person signs in on refiroo's own page; an unattended system uses an agent client. Follow [Connect an assistant](/docs/guide/integrate/connect-an-assistant/) for the sequence.

This connection is separate from the [built-in assistant task API](/docs/integrate/assistant-tasks/). MCP does not need refiroo's AI provider or assistant command. The operator enables it with `MCP_ENABLED=true`; while disabled, the endpoint, discovery metadata and registration answer `404`, and no agent token is issued.

## Identity and permission

MCP uses Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`, with protocol version `2025-11-25` and JSON answers. It accepts only tokens for the `agent` audience. Such a token cannot call management or consumer API routes. An API client cannot request an agent token; create a client of kind `agent` instead. See the [client operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/security) and [OAuth operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/oauth).

The connection acts as its person or client. Its management permissions are restricted to **Browse** and **Work in change sets**, even if that identity also holds Approve or Publish. Consumer API grants remain available. Tools outside its access are absent from the tool list and refused if called directly. Application and record-type restrictions still apply to writes.

A client with only a consumer API grant sees that API's lookup tool, without general workspace browsing. A missing workspace and one the caller cannot read give the same refusal. Read [Security for integrators](/docs/integrate/security-model-for-integrators/) when choosing grants.

## Read through tools and resources

Start by discovering the connection's tools rather than assuming that every tool exists.

| Tool | Use and result |
| --- | --- |
| `describe_access` | Read who the connection acts as, its grants and consumer APIs before choosing a task. No workspace argument is needed. |
| `list_workspaces` | Page through active workspaces the identity can browse; optionally search their names. |
| `describe_model` | Read one workspace's applications, views, record types, relation types and consumer APIs by key and name. |
| `describe_type` | Inspect a type's attributes, value types, filters, parents, relationships and views. Supply `changeSetId` to inspect an owned change set's pinned definition. |
| `find_records` | Query one type using fields, ancestors and one relationship hop. It reads live data unless an owned `changeSetId` selects proposed data. Continue with cursors. |
| `read_record` | Read one record's values and path, with a page of relationships. Continue to read all relationships; an owned `changeSetId` selects proposed data. |
| `mapping_coverage` | Read a mapping view's source records and their targets. Use `state=unmapped`, `mapped` or `ambiguous`, with optional search and parent scope. |
| `record_history` | Page through one record's history, newest first; optionally filter by kind or actor. |
| `history_facts` | Read counted facts for a workspace or record over a period. Supply `since` and `until`; dates use UTC unless an IANA `timeZone` is given. This is a nonpaged answer; narrow the period if it exceeds the answer limit. |
| `list_changes` | Page through workspace changes, newest first; optionally narrow by kinds, actor and period. |
| Generated `lookup_<key>` | Read one granted consumer contract using the operations and inputs described below. Discover its actual name from the connection. |

These tools return the corresponding API shapes. Use the [record and query operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/objects), [mapping operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/mapping), [changes operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/changes) and [agent-access reference](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/agent-access) for the contracts.

`mapping_coverage` takes the application and view; refiroo reads the relationship binding from that view. `history_facts` reads a workspace or a record over a period whose start is included and end excluded, with an optional IANA time zone. `HISTORY_PERIOD_INVALID` means the dates or time zone need correcting. The assistant receives the facts and can word them itself; it cannot request a provider-written history account through this connection.

A workspace's model is also a listed resource at `refiroo://workspaces/{key}/model`. Resource templates expose its applications at `…/applications/{key}`, types at `…/object-types/{key}` and views at `…/views/{application}/{key}`. These resources require Browse. Use the MCP resource-read operation with the listed URI. The server records that operation internally as `read_resource`; it is not a callable tool in the tool list. `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` means the requested resource URI does not identify an available resource; rediscover the listed resources and templates.

### Consumer API tools

Each tool comes from a consumer API declaration in the model. It offers only the operations that declaration provides: `xref`, `lists` and `objects`. It accepts the definition's parameters, `to.` targets and `asOf` where supported. It reads live data, without publication pinning, event feeds or batch resolve. Use the [consumer API routes](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/) for those integration tasks.

Equal definitions in several workspaces share a tool; choose the workspace on each call. Differing definitions under one key have separate tools. Names that would collide or exceed 48 characters have a short hash suffix, so discover the name rather than constructing it. In the guide's reference model, the `stops` definition produces a lookup tool for the same contract described in [Reading business objects](/docs/integrate/reading-business-objects/).

`OBJECT_ID_REQUIRED` asks for the record ID needed by an `objects` read. `LIST_REQUIRED` asks for the declared list needed by a `lists` read. Discover those from the tool schema and the model rather than guessing them.

### Read every page

Pass a returned `nextCursor` as `cursor` to continue. The normal API paging limits apply. `MCP_ANSWER_BYTES`, default 40,000, can make a page smaller: refiroo reduces its size and returns a continuation cursor. It does not silently truncate a collection. An individual item or nonpaged answer that cannot fit is refused; model resources are returned whole. Writes run once and are not repeated to fit an answer-size limit.

The per-person or per-client rate limit is `MCP_RATE_PER_MINUTE`, default 120 calls. A limited call is an error tool result with a wait interval; wait before retrying. Several connections acting as the same identity share that limit.

## Prepare a change for review

With Work in change sets, an assistant can use the following tools:

| Tool | Use and result |
| --- | --- |
| `my_change_sets` | Page through this identity's open change sets, newest change first, with versions and submission states. Optionally narrow to one workspace. |
| `read_change_set` | Read an owned set's version, model release and submission state, including the last decision and comment. |
| `change_set_changes` | Page through records or relationships added, changed or removed compared with live data. |
| `create_change_set` | Start a named set from the workspace's live data. Keep the returned ID and version for subsequent calls. |
| `add_record` | Add a named record with its application, type, optional parent and typed values. It returns the proposed record's ID and versions. |
| `change_record` | Change an existing record's name, parent or selected values. Attributes omitted from the call are kept. |
| `set_field` | Add or replace one typed attribute value on a proposed record. It does not clear a value. |
| `add_relation` | Connect two records using a declared relation type and optional relationship attributes. |
| `change_relation` | Replace a relationship's attribute values, using its current version. This is a replacement, so read and retain every value you intend to keep. |
| `validate_change_set` | Check the owned set's data against model rules. Read all diagnostic parts using the returned `nextCursor`. Validation does not publish. |
| `submit_change_set` | Validate and freeze the set for a person's decision, with an optional comment. Submission does not make its rows live. |

It may work only in change sets created by its own person or client. A person's own browser-created change set counts. A colleague's change set answers `CHANGE_SET_NOT_FOUND`, even when the management API would allow collaboration. `find_records`, `read_record` and `describe_type` accept `changeSetId` for those unpublished rows and their pinned model release; without it they read live data.

The sequence is to read the model, create or read an owned change set, add or change data, validate, fix refusals, and submit. Keep the returned IDs and versions. Writes to a change set claim `expectedChangeSetVersion`; changes to existing rows also claim their version. The [change-set operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/change-sets) explain validation and submission, and [Versions and conflicts](/docs/integrate/versions-and-conflicts/) explains rereading after a stale claim.

A refused tool result has `isError` and gives `CODE: message`, followed by the engine's details as JSON. A stale claim includes the current version; an invalid change set includes diagnostics. Read the current data and correct the proposal before another write. `read_change_set` also shows why a person sent it back. A submitted set is frozen to the assistant.

No MCP tool removes a record or relationship, clears a value, withdraws a submission, discards a set, runs a batch, chooses a release, restructures the model, approves or publishes. A person reviews the rows, corrects or removes unwanted changes and publishes through the normal approval process. A browser edit withdraws a submission. Under a second-person rule, the person who asked their assistant to prepare the changes cannot make the decision. See [Changes, approvals and publication](/docs/integrate/changes-approvals-and-publication/).

## Recognise assistant work

Prepared records and relationships carry an `origin` of kind `agent`, with the requesting identity and the assistant's claimed application name. Single-record reads can also name who requested and later edited it. Publication copies that origin into history; the actor of publication is the publisher. The browser mark reads **Prepared by an assistant**. The claimed name is not proof of the assistant's identity.

Entries made while an MCP tool runs carry `channel: mcp` in [changes](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/changes) and [record history](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/objects). Entries from other channels, including older entries, omit it. No channel filter exists. Use origin to identify prepared content and channel to identify a call's route into the engine; they answer different questions.

## Data, costs and records of calls

Permitted tool answers leave the instance for the connected assistant. That assistant may send them to its own provider. refiroo's `AI_SEND_LEVEL` does not restrict this external connection, and MCP reads do not call refiroo's configured AI provider. Check your assistant's data policy and charges before connecting it. [About AI](/docs/run/ai/) explains the separate switches, costs and retention in full.

Treat reference-data text as data. A record can contain misleading instructions; neither the tool server nor the review process makes an assistant's interpretation reliable. Review the proposed changes themselves.

Security administrators inspect **Settings › Connections › Agent access** and the [agent-access operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/agent-access). They show **How to connect**, **Agent clients**, registered assistants and **Calls**. Call records keep identity, tool, argument names, outcome, duration and request reference for `MCP_CALLS_DAYS`, default 90; they do not keep argument values. Read calls are not separate entries in the data audit trail. Data writes use the ordinary audit trail with their channel.

Blocking a registered assistant ends its sessions on their next call. Restoring it permits a new sign-in but does not restore ended sessions. Deactivating an agent client likewise stops it on the next call. A person can end their assistant's session from their account. Administration refusals `AGENT_APPLICATION_INVALID` require valid registration details and HTTPS or loopback redirect addresses; `AGENT_APPLICATION_NOT_FOUND` requires refreshing the registered applications before acting.
guide/src/content/docs/integrate/busines:
---
title: Business dates
description: Read records effective on a calendar date, independently of snapshots and history.
reader: integrator
---

A business date answers which records are valid on that day. It does not rewind edits, choose a publication by date or read audit history. Follow [Read as of a date](/docs/guide/integrate/read-as-of-a-date/) for the sequence.

A model can declare an effective period using two date attributes. The start is inclusive and the end exclusive. An empty start means no lower bound; an empty end means no upper bound. A record is absent on its end date. Different records' periods may overlap, so a business-date read can legitimately return several matching records.

Every write checks that a supplied end is after the start, including single-value edits, type changes, imports and changes prepared for publication. `INVALID_EFFECTIVE_PERIOD` means correct the resulting period; changing just the end is checked against the stored start.

## Management reads

Use a dated [per-type collection or query](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/objects) in live data, a change set or a publication. A declared date field alone does not make a type dated: the model must declare the period. `AS_OF_NOT_SUPPORTED` refuses a date for an undated type or the management cross-type lookup. Use the relevant per-type operation instead.

The date filters the queried records. Related hops and expanded records remain undated unless your criteria explicitly constrain their dates. The cursor binds the date: keep it unchanged while paging. A malformed calendar date is refused rather than silently interpreted as a timestamp.

## Consumer reads

Consumer contracts support dated object, list, lookup and batch reads where their exposed types declare periods. See the selected contract's [operations in the API reference](/docs/api/) and [consumer reading sequence](/docs/guide/integrate/read-through-a-consumer-api/).

An existing object or list of an undated type refuses a date. A mixed lookup retains undated types and filters the dated ones. Check the answer's indication of which public types were dated. Ancestors, related items, parameter matching and score sources remain undated: a returned object's period does not imply that everything represented with it was valid that day. Invalid consumer dates produce `INVALID_AS_OF`.

Adding or moving a period in a model can require data repair before activation. Removing a period used by a consumer contract requires a higher contract version. The built-in browser shows ordinary date fields; it has no business-date filter.

Consumer pages and batch answers name the sorted public types dated in `asOfApplied`; every dated object or page read also carries `RDM-As-Of-Applied`. Both are absent without `asOf`. If none of the types an XREF can return has a declared period, it answers `400 AS_OF_NOT_SUPPORTED`. An otherwise known dated object outside its period answers `404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`. Batch items use these same rules individually. Supply exactly one `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar day; timestamps, zones, impossible dates and repeated dates produce `400 INVALID_AS_OF`.
guide/src/content/docs/integrate/changes:
---
title: Changes, approvals and publication
description: Prepare and validate shared changes, request approval and publish without overwriting live work.
reader: integrator
---

Use a change set when changes should be prepared and reviewed together. Publishing merges its changes into live data and records an immutable publication. Use the [change-set operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/change-sets) for creation, validation, submission, decisions and publication; the same record and relationship operations write within its context.

## Start from the intended base

Choose current live data or an existing publication explicitly. The source options must agree (`CHANGE_SET_SOURCE_INVALID` otherwise). Current-live capture makes a private immutable base; it does not create a publication.
