```json
        "fsoNumber": null,
        "latitude": "46.65674442039232",
        "longitude": "8.709084193690385",
        "height": "1701.3",
        "sboid": null,
        "parent": {
          "objectType": "Municipality",
          "id": "06073bf3-cb29-475e-a87a-8fc6dbb8b8cc",
          "code": null,
          "name": "Tujetsch"
        },
        "path": "Graubünden/Surselva/Tujetsch",
        "operator": {
          "id": "f94ef862-2a95-4675-9e31-6b1d0a03317f",
          "code": "MGB-fo",
          "name": "Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn (fo)",
          "localName": null,
          "isPrimary": null
        },
        "modes": [
          {
            "id": "0f61601d-ec0c-4944-bab9-cf0d1d8665a9",
            "code": "TRAIN",
            "name": "Train"
          }
        ],
        "systemCodes": [
          {
            "system": "Wikidata: stations",
            "systemKey": "wikidata-stations",
            "code": "Q33467326",
            "name": "Q33467326 Tschamut-Selva"
          }
        ],
        "translations": [],
        "matchScore": 900
      }
    },
    {
      "index": 1,
      "ref": "row-2",
      "status": "not_found",
      "error": {
        "code": "NO_MATCH",
        "message": "No object matches the query"
      }
    }
  ],
  "workspace": "graubuenden",
  "publication": null,
  "counts": {
    "found": 1,
    "notFound": 1,
    "ambiguous": 0,
    "rejected": 0
  }
}
```

`T-9999` is the reference data's deliberately unmapped **fictional** Regional ticketing code. The HTTP request succeeded, but the second source row has no answer. Keep its `not_found` outcome rather than replacing it with the first result. A malformed item is `rejected`; a tied best match is `ambiguous`. The response keeps input order and echoes each `ref`.

An item using `id` reads the known UUID directly and does not add a query score. Use one of `query` and `id` per item. For a whole file, follow [Resolve a file of codes](/docs/guide/integrate/resolve-a-file-of-codes/). The instance's [Resolve reference](/docs/api/?api=consumer-stops-v1#consumer-stops-v1/POST/api/consumer/stops/v1/resolve) remains the generated contract pointer.

These response bodies were read from the reference instance. The anchor is the complete opaque value from that lookup. Obtain an anchor from your own response and keep it with the same workspace, query and parameters.

*Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0. Regional ticketing and its codes are fictional.*

An ambiguous lookup’s details include the tied count and up to ten candidates with ID, public type, name and score. Paging parameters are unsupported with `expect=one`. XREF pages support cursor traversal, position and end selection, but neither seek nor `includeTotal`: totals are always returned. Empty query terms are ignored.

Resolve’s optional `ref` is 1–200 characters. Outcome errors preserve the single-read code and add a JSON pointer into the item or defaults. Over-limit errors name the setting, maximum and submitted item count. Put `workspace`, `publication` and `asOf` on the request URL, never in `defaults` or items; definition filters and crosswalk choices belong in the body.
guide/src/content/docs/integrate/model-a:
---
title: Model and release operations
description: Author models, activate releases and review migrations or moves through the API.
reader: integrator
---

Use model operations to shape what a workspace can hold. Installing a release and activating it are separate steps. Data changes in a change set are another lifecycle. Read the [model authoring operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/model%20administration), [release operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/model) and [workspace model operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/workspaces) for their contracts.

## Author, validate and install

A model draft changes through typed operations naming elements by key. One request's operations apply in order, all or none, and form one history step. A draft can be temporarily invalid while being assembled; inspect its diagnostics and validate before installation. Installation refuses an invalid model. Whole-model editing is also recorded as a step.

Read the outline, expanded model and operation history as needed. Undo applies inverse operations; later steps depending on a removed element must be undone first or together. `OPERATION_HAS_DEPENDANTS` identifies those steps. `NOTHING_TO_UNDO`, `NOTHING_TO_REDO` and `NOTHING_TO_APPLY` mean refresh the history rather than inventing another change. `INVALID_OPERATION` and `OPERATION_BATCH_TOO_LARGE` require a valid bounded operation request.

A change to a released element applies as a draft step even when stored data depends on it.
Its history entry carries `migration` marks with the affected elements and impact counts; a
released key change is marked even with no data. `OPERATION_REQUIRES_MIGRATION` is no longer raised.
Read the [draft migration operation](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/model%20administration)
before installing changes that need data migration.

Attached source files can be profiled, bound and dry-run without writing data. A draft's dry run without a `profile` reads the file with the profile the draft holds, and the profile the draft's profile read answered can be sent back unchanged. Deterministic inference can propose bindings for review; its job is separate from applying proposals. `INFERENCE_NOT_FOUND`, `INFERENCE_NOT_READY` and `INFERENCE_STALE` require a current completed inference. `PROPOSAL_NOT_FOUND`, `PROPOSAL_ALREADY_APPLIED` and `PROPOSAL_REQUIREMENT_MISSING` require reviewing the proposal and its prerequisites. `INVALID_INFERENCE_REQUEST`, `DRY_RUN_NOT_FOUND` and `IMPACT_SUMMARY_DRAFT_INVALID` require correcting or rerunning the relevant model check. See [Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/).

Compilation checks the draft against its base release, or its model's latest installed release when it has no base. It reports contract changes and workspace compatibility. Installing saves an immutable release but does not activate it. If activation subsequently fails, that installed release remains. `MODEL_DRAFT_NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_MODEL`, `MODEL_HASH_CHANGED` and `RELEASE_IDENTITY_CONFLICT` require the intended validated draft and release identity, not a forced overwrite. `RELEASE_IDENTITY_CONFLICT` means another release of the same key already has that version, for example one an assistant task installed. Its `details.freeVersion` names a free version: send `setRelease` with it and install again. The draft's outline proposes a free version before you install, as `suggestedReleaseVersion`.

## Activate in one workspace

Read the workspace's current assignment and claim its version and release when activating. Other workspaces keep their assignments. Read placements in the target context to discover allowed root types, children and replacement types; parent candidates can be narrowed without losing truthful totals.

`ACTIVATION_CONFLICT` requires a fresh assignment read. `MODEL_MIGRATION_REQUIRED` means data needs reviewed conversion. `CONSUMER_CONTRACT_VERSION_REQUIRED` and `CONSUMER_CONTRACT_VERSION_DECREASED` refuse incompatible version choices. `CONSUMER_API_REMOVED` is a warning: removing the whole API is allowed and ends its address after activation. `CONSUMER_KEPT_VERSION_CHANGED` refuses a retained contract that would read differently; restore its definition and model sources, or stop serving it. Raising the current version again does not fix that retained contract. `CONSUMER_VERSION_STOPPED` warns that a retained version is removed and its consumers receive `404 CONTRACT_VERSION_NOT_FOUND` after activation. Review [earlier contracts](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/#earlier-contract-versions) before confirming. A release change can leave open change sets on their old pin and pause incompatible subscriptions. Subscriptions on a still-served earlier contract keep their accepted version. Inspect both consequences.

`MODEL_RELEASE_NOT_FOUND`, `MODEL_RELEASE_RETIRED`, `MODEL_RELEASE_IN_USE` and `MODEL_RELEASE_IS_DEFAULT` require choosing or retaining an eligible release and resolving its assignments before removal. `MODEL_RELEASE_VERSION_CONFLICT` needs its current version. `UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION`, `UNSUPPORTED_PINNED_MODEL_SCHEMA`, `PINNED_MODEL_INVALID` and `PINNED_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` require a supported valid release. Stored-release raising is a maintenance operation with its own refusals (`RELEASE_NOT_RAISABLE`, `RELEASE_RAISE_REFUSED`); see [Model language versions](/docs/model/model-language-versions/).

`MODEL_REGISTRY_REFRESH_FAILED` after activation means the change committed but the serving process could not load it. Have the operator recover the registry before resuming; do not assume the activation rolled back. `MODEL_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE` means the named workspace's model cannot currently be served.

## Migrate reviewed data

Start a [workspace migration](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/workspaces) as a job using the
draft's proposed mappings when available. Keep its relationship renames, splits, list conversions,
named destination applications and draft reference with the type mappings; a type mapping alone
does not express all of these changes. Inspect converted, reclassified, created, lost and refused
items, then confirm the exact reviewed assignment and feed position. Type mappings explain which old types and attributes become which new ones; unmapped content can be lost. Accept loss explicitly only after reviewing it. Execution converts and changes the workspace's release in one transaction.

`INVALID_MIGRATION_MAPPING`, `INVALID_TYPE_MAPPING` and `INVALID_CLEAR_ATTRIBUTES` require a valid mapping and clearing instruction. `MIGRATION_HAS_REFUSALS` requires correcting data and previewing again; `MIGRATION_LOSS_NOT_ACCEPTED` needs a deliberate loss decision. `MIGRATION_REVIEW_STALE` requires a new preview after intervening data or model changes. `MIGRATION_TARGET_IS_CURRENT` needs no migration. `MIGRATION_FAILED` changes nothing from that execution and supplies the failure reference.

A change set pinned elsewhere has two explicit options. If its content already fits, change its pin after validation. Otherwise migrate the change set onto the workspace's release, or migrate the workspace to the change set's release and publish it together. The target restrictions are `MIGRATION_TARGET_NOT_WORKSPACE_RELEASE` and `MIGRATION_TARGET_NOT_CHANGE_SET_RELEASE`. Moving a change set changes its prepared content and base, not live data; migrating the workspace and publishing does both atomically. See [Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/).

## Transfer between models

A model mapping maps source types, attributes, relationships, parent placement, value conversions, defaults and target matching. Its [operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/model%20mappings) have versions, history, undo and redo. Read its problems and coverage against the releases involved. `INVALID_MODEL_MAPPING`, `MODEL_MAPPING_EXISTS`, `MODEL_MAPPING_NOT_FOUND`, `MODEL_MAPPING_MODEL_MISMATCH` and `MAPPING_VERSION_CONFLICT` require the correct current mapping.

Start a [move or copy](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/moves) with a source context and explicit selection. Selection does not automatically pull every related record into scope. The dry run reports created or updated records, refused items, items not moved, uncarried values and possible duplicates. It matches origins, counterparts and then the declared match before creating a target record. Values convert under the target model's rules.

Confirmation loads the source as previewed into a new target change set, reevaluating target rules. It does not make data live. A move can also prepare source deletions, retaining source records changed meanwhile or needed by records left behind. Publish the target copy first; `MOVE_COPY_NOT_PUBLISHED` blocks source deletion before that. Consumers see each side only after publication.

`MOVE_SAME_WORKSPACE` needs two workspaces; `MOVE_MAPPING_CHANGED` needs another dry run; `MOVE_MAPPING_HAS_PROBLEMS` needs a corrected mapping; `MOVE_NOTHING_TO_MOVE` means no proposed target changes can load. Follow [Move records between models](/docs/guide/integrate/move-records-between-models/) and [Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/) for the task and design choices.

## Review release status separately from content

A release’s content is immutable; its active or retired status has a separate version claim. Retirement stops new selections but leaves workspaces and change sets already using it operational. The default workspace’s release cannot be retired. Reinstalling the exact content of a retired release restores it. Ask for usable releases when choosing a new assignment: that excludes retired releases and unsupported schema versions.

Deletion requires no remaining references. The release reports whether deletion is allowed and the first blocker: a running workspace, history, an import profile or a model mapping. Inspect those references rather than assuming retirement makes deletion possible. Release activation history records selections, oldest first; installation order and bootstrap do not prove an activation occurred.

A structural diff can use a selected installed baseline while activation compatibility still checks the target workspace’s current data and release. Additions omit the before side; removals omit the after side. An omitted side differs from a present null value. Compilation reports compatible, migration-required or invalid; diagnostics have severity and a JSON Pointer, and compatibility findings can also give the affected count. Identical installation can return the existing release; it still does not activate it.

## Draft steps and generated documents

Draft operation requests are bounded by `MODEL_OPERATION_MAX_ITEMS` (default 500). A key omitted for a new element is generated from its name, using lowercase hyphenated ASCII and a numeric suffix on collision. An explicit key change rewrites references in the draft, including consumer definitions.
For a released key, coordinate integrations naming the old key before migration; the draft's
migration identifies the consumer APIs of the base release that name it. Removing a referenced element can leave issues to repair in those definitions. Inspect diagnostics after every step.

Changes to released structures apply to the draft; they do not convert stored data. Read
`GET /model-drafts/{id}/migration` through the
[model-authoring reference](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/model%20administration) to obtain the
migration derived from the effective steps and the two models. Undo removes a step's contribution;
redo restores it. The proposal is computed on every read, rather than stored separately.
Request a workspace-specific check to inspect expected moves, creations, losses and refusals.
A whole-model replacement can hide element identity changes; review the returned notes and mappings.

Installation makes the installed release the draft's base. To read the intended migration afterwards,
use `againstReleaseId` for the workspace's current release and `toReleaseId` for the installed target.
Start the [workspace migration](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/workspaces) with that proposal and
retain the draft reference so a client can show its proposed rows. Follow the operation's request
contract for the mapping options. Review first, confirm second; installation alone activates nothing.
Activation still refuses `MODEL_MIGRATION_REQUIRED` when the data needs a migration that has not run.

A stale draft-version refusal can include up to 100 intervening operations and a continuation to history. Undo respects dependencies and reverses an entire step. A new request or whole-model edit after undo clears redo; installing does not. Installation makes the installed content the draft’s base without changing its content version.

The outline remains useful while a draft is invalid: it shows what structure can be read and attaches diagnostics to elements. A compiled draft model supplies placements but no records; reads of real records still use a running workspace model. A new type therefore has no live sample merely because its draft can be previewed.

For a consumer declaration, the draft offers its authored and expanded definitions, compatibility findings, a JSON Schema 2020-12, a type-based message example and an OpenAPI document. Generating these is read-only. Examples do not read records. Invalid drafts refuse the three document downloads with `INVALID_MODEL` and diagnostics. Use the [model-authoring reference](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/model%20administration) for operations and downloads.

## Review conversions and loss

Migration previews distinguish conversion, reclassification, creation, loss and refusal.
Splits create related records holding the moved values; a many-to-one split shares records with
identical moved values. List conversions create one record per distinct value and relationships
from the source records. The carried values leave the source records. Moving an attribute
attachment between types instead lists its source values as loss; it cannot transfer values
between different records. Top-level moves remove the old parent and containment relationship;
other parent changes can produce refusals. Relation-key mappings carry existing relationships. A target lacking a source type can lose its records; a type moving to an application must have an unambiguous destination or an explicit type mapping. Mapping named attribute sources takes precedence over same-key fallback. Records that survive retain their public identity and history; publications retain their original release.

Supported value conversions include text and long text, integer to decimal, integral decimal to integer, values to their stored text form and parseable text back to the target type. A date converts to midnight UTC; an instant converts to a date only at midnight UTC. Values can convert to JSON, and text to JSON only when parseable. Review individual losses and refusals instead of assuming a declared conversion succeeds for every value. A migration preview can hold writes to the records being converted until it ends.

Confirmation claims the reviewed assignment and feed position and explicitly accepts any loss. A stale review writes nothing. Migrating a workspace and publishing a change set can be one atomic execution: publication failure leaves the migration unapplied. Moving a change set onto its workspace’s model instead converts that prepared content, replaces its base with current live data and advances its version once; it does not write live records, feed positions or publications. Conflicts with newer live work must still be resolved.

A model mapping names its source and target releases. One source type maps to one target type; several source types may share a target. Defaults fill missing source values, not values already supplied. Inspect coverage for unmapped source content and required target content left unfilled. Deterministic inference proposes mappings from keys, names, compatible attributes, relationships and stored records; review the evidence and apply only the proposals you intend.

A move’s selection combines its type criteria, subtree and explicit IDs; it does not pull every parent or related record along. The default is a complete preview in copy mode. Source values are fixed when previewed; target writes are decided again during loading into a new change set. A source record changed since the preview is retained when preparing source deletion, as is a record still needed by content left behind. Refused or unselected records are not silently deleted.

## Ask for an account of a model change

Before activating a release or applying a draft, the [impact-summary operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/ai) can explain its effects in a workspace. They require Activate model releases and Use AI proposals there, with a configured provider. The engine computes model differences, data-rule failures and counts, consumer-contract effects, activation blockers and records per touched type. The provider words those facts; it does not decide whether a change is safe or approve it.

The model changes and counts go to the provider, without record values. This is available at every send level and can incur provider charges. Facts and wording are cached for an hour for the same request; a cache hit makes no second call. [About AI](/docs/run/ai/) explains what is sent, call records, costs and retention. Do not send a request until the person asks for the explanation; the browser action is **Explain this change**.

Present every returned fact alongside the statements and their citations. Statements without valid fact references are removed and counted. A failing provider can still return HTTP `200` with all facts, no statements and a `failure`; show the facts and the failure instead of an empty success. No explanation activates anything. Continue through the ordinary preview, review and activation operations only after the person's decision.

`IMPACT_SUMMARY_DRAFT_INVALID` requires correcting and validating the draft. A stale draft version requires rereading it. Missing draft or release refusals require an existing accessible resource. A summary is not attached permanently to a release and is not a substitute for migration preview.

For changes proposed from words or a workbook, use [Assistant tasks](/docs/integrate/assistant-tasks/). A result can lead to migration, a change set or staged release activations; those remain explicit actions by a person.

## Give automation the right access

Model operations have separate permission boundaries. **Model authoring** allows draft work and release reads. **Install a model** allows installing a release without changing a workspace; **Model release** also allows installation and permits activation or migration in its workspace. **Copy and move** covers model mappings and transfers, with Browse on the source and additional source change-set rights for a move. Check the [security catalogue](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/security) and each operation's declared action before assigning a role. A consumer grant provides none of these permissions.

For a release rollout, save the draft ID/version, compiled content identity and intended target workspace. Install, retain the returned release ID, reread the workspace assignment and check activation compatibility. If migration is needed, read the draft's proposal against the source and installed target releases, preview with its mappings, then review and confirm. Otherwise activate with the current assignment claim. Verify the workspace now names the intended release and rediscover its model and consumer contracts. If only installation succeeded, the release is available but no workspace changed. If serving refresh failed after activation committed, ask the operator to restore serving rather than reinstalling as if nothing happened.

Keep exported model definitions and mapping definitions under your organisation's change control. These are useful design artefacts, but they are not a restore of release IDs, draft history, publication pins or runtime records. [Operator backup and restore](/docs/run/backup-and-restore/) covers the instance state. To stop a rollout, leave an installed release unactivated or retire an unused release with its status claim. Changing back to an older release is another checked activation or migration; it is not an unconditional data rollback.
guide/src/content/docs/integrate/overvie:
---
title: Integrating with refiroo
description: Choose the interface and sequence your integration needs.
reader: integrator
---

Use refiroo's APIs to read reference data, supply changes or keep another system in step. Choose an interface by the contract your system needs, then give that system its own [client identity](/docs/administer/clients/).

| Your task | Start with |
| --- | --- |
| Work with records, relationships, models or change sets | The management API in the [API reference, objects and model tags](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/objects) |
| Read a stable business contract without knowing the underlying model | [Consumer APIs](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/) |
| Load many changes or exchange a file | [Bulk writes](/docs/integrate/writing-in-bulk/) and [files](/docs/integrate/files-imports-and-exports/) |
| Maintain a local copy | [Load, then follow changes](/docs/guide/integrate/load-then-follow-changes/) |
| Receive notifications at your endpoint | [Consumer events and webhooks](/docs/integrate/consumer-events-and-webhooks/) |

The management API exposes the model and its runtime capabilities, including operations the browser does not use. Its names come from the model; applications and record types are configuration. Consumer APIs present selected business objects under names and versions declared by a model administrator. They are read-only.

Bulk writes, imports and exports produce [jobs](/docs/integrate/jobs/). A successful HTTP request can still contain refused items: inspect the job result. The raw change feed identifies changes without carrying values; consumer events identify affected business objects and can include their current representation.

Start by [getting a token](/docs/guide/integrate/get-a-token/), [discovering the model](/docs/integrate/discovering-the-model/) and learning [paging and errors](/docs/integrate/identifiers-paging-and-errors/). For reviewed changes, use [change sets and publication](/docs/integrate/changes-approvals-and-publication/).

The documentation is at `/docs`. Operation details, request schemas and examples are in the [API reference](/docs/api/). These pages explain which operations to combine and how to recover when a sequence cannot finish.

## Integrate with assistants

Use [Assistants and agents](/docs/integrate/assistants-and-agents/) for an external MCP connection, or [Assistant tasks](/docs/integrate/assistant-tasks/) to submit a workbook or instructions to the built-in assistant. Both prepare work for human review and cannot approve or publish. Provider features can propose [mapping targets](/docs/integrate/writing-in-bulk/#propose-mapping-targets-into-a-change-set), turn [questions into filters](/docs/integrate/reading-records/#turn-a-question-into-filters), or explain model changes and activity. Each needs its own permissions and configuration. Read [About AI](/docs/run/ai/) for what leaves the instance, charges and retained records before offering these actions in a client.
guide/src/content/docs/integrate/reading:
---
title: Reading business objects
description: Read one declared object or a complete list in the correct workspace and publication.
reader: integrator
---

Read through a [consumer API](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/) when another system needs the model's declared business representation. Use an object ID already held, or page a list declared by the contract. Follow [Read through a consumer API](/docs/guide/integrate/read-through-a-consumer-api/) for a complete sequence.

Values carried by a connection can appear inside a declared related block, with their own types
and nulls. When the block is served, they use the same object shape in single reads, lists, XREF and Resolve; see
[Publish values of the connection](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/#publish-values-of-the-connection).
To read or maintain the underlying connections through the management API, use
[Relationships and their values](/docs/integrate/relationships-and-their-values/).

## Read one or many

The get-by-ID operation reads a public record ID. A code from another system belongs in [lookup](/docs/integrate/looking-up-and-resolving/). A list returns its declared type in its configured order; an optional parent scope selects descendants at any depth, not just immediate children. Several parent IDs are alternatives.

**Example:** in the reference contract, use [Get by ID](/docs/api/?api=consumer-stops-v1#consumer-stops-v1/GET/api/consumer/stops/v1/objects/{id}) for a known stop identity, or [List all-stops](/docs/api/?api=consumer-stops-v1#consumer-stops-v1/GET/api/consumer/stops/v1/lists/all-stops) for all exposed stops. The contract also declares narrower lists; inspect its document rather than inventing one.

Parameters are declared by the contract. Values within one parameter are alternatives; different parameters combine to narrow the result. They may select a public type, an ancestor, a related record or records inside a projected block. Some projection parameters remove objects left with no matching related records; others only trim that block. On a single read, filtering the object out is `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`, not an empty object.

## Ask for a related block

The contract can serve related blocks always or only on request. This applies both to the
object's blocks and to blocks nested inside its parent. Get by ID and lists accept `include`;
XREF uses the same choice. The generated contract lists the valid names. Name only blocks
served on request; always-served blocks are already present.

**Illustrative catalogue example:** these requests use the
[catalogue declaration](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/#parent-values-and-blocks-served-on-request),
not the reference instance. An item has a category with an approval flag. Both the item's
codes and its category's codes are served on request. Start without include:

```http
GET /api/consumer/catalog/v1/objects/11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111?workspace=catalogue HTTP/1.1
Host: <instance>
Authorization: Bearer <consumer-token>
Accept: application/json
```

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
RDM-Workspace: catalogue
```

```json
{
  "objectType": "Item",
  "id": "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111",
  "name": "Notebook",
  "parent": {
    "objectType": "Category",
    "id": "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222",
    "name": "Stationery",
    "isApproved": true
  }
}
```

The parent's `isApproved` output reads the `approved` attribute as a boolean; its name comes
from the declaration, not the attribute key. Its extra attributes keep their declared types; a missing
value or an attribute not bound by this parent's type is null. The two codes blocks are absent,
not empty. To read both, repeat include:

```http
GET /api/consumer/catalog/v1/objects/11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111?workspace=catalogue&include=codes&include=parent.codes HTTP/1.1
Host: <instance>
Authorization: Bearer <consumer-token>
Accept: application/json
```

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
RDM-Workspace: catalogue
```

```json
{
  "objectType": "Item",
  "id": "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111",
  "name": "Notebook",
  "parent": {
    "objectType": "Category",
    "id": "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222",
    "name": "Stationery",
    "isApproved": true,
    "codes": [{"code": "CAT-01"}]
  },
  "codes": [{"code": "ITEM-01"}]
}
```

`include=codes,parent.codes` is equivalent. The parent prefix is used in the request, not
as a key inside the returned parent. It stays `parent.` even if the parent output is renamed.
An included many-valued block with no related records is `[]`; a single-valued block is null.
If the record has no parent, the entire parent output remains null even with an include.

A list can select children by a parent's code and ask to see the matching codes:

```http
GET /api/consumer/catalog/v1/lists/items?workspace=catalogue&categoryCode=CAT-01&include=parent.codes HTTP/1.1
Host: <instance>
Authorization: Bearer <consumer-token>
Accept: application/json
```

Here `categoryCode` is the declared filter name; `parent.codes` is the block name. The
filter keeps items whose parent has a matching code and trims that parent's codes to
matches. With no matching parent item, a child is removed because the filter declares
`keepOnlyMatching`. Omitting include still selects the same children, but their parent
codes are absent. A filter without keep-only-matching trims the block without removing
children. On Get by ID, a child removed by a filter gives `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`.

An include name outside the on-request list gives `400 UNKNOWN_INCLUDE`, even if it names
an always-served block. Read `error.details.valid`, correct the name against the contract,
and retry the intended request. Adding a parent field or serving a new block always does
not make it a valid include name. Events and webhook deliveries do not accept includes and
leave on-request blocks out of their full objects.

## Page and cache

Consumer list pages hold 1–100 objects, default 20. Follow opaque cursors for traversal, or use supported position, end and seek navigation for a jump. Do not combine selectors. Totals are opt-in for lists; XREF lookup always provides them. Keep workspace, filters, requested includes and selected publication with the checkpoint.

For a fixed extract, choose a publication. Selecting the current one resolves a concrete snapshot that its cursors keep using. A conditional GET lets the server return `304 Not Modified` while the cached answer remains valid. Keep the opaque ETag with the exact request, and retain the cached body on an unchanged response.

## Recover without changing the question

`CONSUMER_API_NOT_FOUND`, `CONTRACT_VERSION_NOT_FOUND`, `LIST_NOT_FOUND` and `OPERATION_NOT_OFFERED` require rediscovering the workspace's contract. `UNKNOWN_PARAMETER` and `PARAMETER_NOT_SUPPORTED` mean correct the request rather than dropping a requested restriction. `INVALID_PAGE_SIZE`, `INVALID_PAGE_PARAMETER` and `CONFLICTING_PAGE_PARAMETERS` require supported paging. `INVALID_CURSOR` requires restarting the intended query.

`WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` requires the intended workspace; `FORBIDDEN` requires its consumer grant. A missing or contract-mismatched publication needs an explicit baseline choice. Do not silently retry against live data and present it as a snapshot. Business dates remain a separate filter; see [Business dates](/docs/integrate/business-dates/).

## A complete object read

**Reference-data example:** the requests below use the `stops` declaration explained in [Consumer APIs](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/#from-a-declaration-to-a-running-api). Replace the host and token with your instance's values. The response bodies below were read from the reference instance using the 2 November 2026 dataset. Cursors and ETags are the complete values from that read. Obtain fresh values from your own responses; these strings depend on the instance and read context.

The declaration's `operations.objects` exposes this request. Notice that the path uses the record UUID, while the returned `code` is a separate business identifier:

```http
GET /api/consumer/stops/v1/objects/8d90eede-23cf-47c1-8dac-cb37956f5fd5?workspace=graubuenden HTTP/1.1
Host: <instance>
Authorization: Bearer <consumer-token>
Accept: application/json
```

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
RDM-Workspace: graubuenden
ETag: W/"aa0a706f7657c2adb5a7:1"
```

```json
{
  "objectType": "Stop",
  "id": "8d90eede-23cf-47c1-8dac-cb37956f5fd5",
  "code": "ch:1:sloid:5173",
  "name": "Tschamut-Selva",

    "code": null,
```

This is the whole body, not an envelope containing a record. `objectType` uses the declaration's public name. `stopNumber` is an integer; decimal coordinates and height use the API's decimal string encoding, preserving their precision. Nulls mean this object has no applicable value for that output. The declared operator is an object; modes, system codes and translations are arrays. An empty array is a real empty projection, not an omitted part of this example.

## A list page with navigation

`all-stops` declares `of: stop` and `sortBy: stop-number`. This request asks for its first record and an exact total:

```http
GET /api/consumer/stops/v1/lists/all-stops?workspace=graubuenden&pageSize=1&includeTotal=true HTTP/1.1
Host: <instance>
Authorization: Bearer <consumer-token>
Accept: application/json
```

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
RDM-Workspace: graubuenden
```

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "objectType": "Stop",
      "id": "6583e8c9-582c-4bc5-b113-dbdbcc31a44a",

      },
      "path": "Graubünden/Surselva/Tujetsch",
      "operator": {
        "id": "69907d18-f444-400a-b8a2-359bfbd405fc",
        "code": "MGB/Autofo",

        "isPrimary": null
      },
      "modes": [
        {
          "id": "ef9e4eea-74a4-4380-a426-b9faae4a298f",
          "code": "BUS",
          "name": "Bus"

      ],

  ],

  "publication": null,

  "nextCursor": ".Xq2rRTwSbhFk87_MbE_pH5rw0C6dLWShygnYcAxwlxs",

```

Follow `nextCursor` with the same list, workspace and filters. URL-encode the opaque cursor as one query value; keep `includeTotal=true` if you still need counts. `prevCursor` goes back; `anchor` reopens this page. At the last page `nextCursor` is null. The 2,443 total describes the reference snapshot, not a fixed product limit. Without totals requested, `totalCount` and `startIndex` are null.

Position navigation is a jump to a numbered row; `from=end` starts at the end; `seek` jumps by a supported sort value. Choose only one navigation method in a request. Use a publication when the extract must stay fixed while pages are read.

## The same list narrowed by a declared parameter

The declaration's `operator` filter reads the `operator` projection, matches its code or name, and requires a match. It does not add a new route. Add it to the list request:

```http
GET /api/consumer/stops/v1/lists/all-stops?workspace=graubuenden&operator=MGB-fo&pageSize=1&includeTotal=true HTTP/1.1
Host: <instance>
Authorization: Bearer <consumer-token>
Accept: application/json
```

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
RDM-Workspace: graubuenden
```

```json
    {

      "sboid": null,
```

The reference snapshot has 13 stops for this operator. Reusing the unfiltered cursor here is invalid: the filter changes the collection. A `municipality` ancestor filter can instead match its declared fields, while the scoped `/lists/stops` route's municipality parent parameter takes municipality IDs. Do not assume a parent parameter accepts every field that an ordinary filter accepts.

## Reuse an unchanged answer

Save the body from the earlier object GET and read its `ETag` response header. In the captured response it is `W/"aa0a706f7657c2adb5a7:1"`. Copy the whole header value into `If-None-Match`, including `W/` and both quotes; use the value from your own response rather than a placeholder:

```http
GET /api/consumer/stops/v1/objects/8d90eede-23cf-47c1-8dac-cb37956f5fd5?workspace=graubuenden HTTP/1.1
Host: <instance>
Authorization: Bearer <consumer-token>
Accept: application/json
If-None-Match: W/"aa0a706f7657c2adb5a7:1"
```

If the saved tag still matches, the conditional response is:


```http
HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
RDM-Workspace: graubuenden
ETag: "aa0a706f7657c2adb5a7:1"
```

A matching-tag 304 has **no response body**. Keep using the cached body. If the server instead returns 200, replace the cached body and tag together. A live write elsewhere in the workspace can change the tag; it is not a per-object change counter. Adding `publication=<publication-id>` pins the read, and the answer identifies it in `RDM-Publication` and collection `publication` fields.

## A request that the declaration cannot answer

The model offers a list named `all-stops`; it does not offer `no-such-list`:

```http
GET /api/consumer/stops/v1/lists/no-such-list?workspace=graubuenden HTTP/1.1
Host: <instance>
Authorization: Bearer <consumer-token>
Accept: application/json
```

```http
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "LIST_NOT_FOUND",
    "message": "List 'no-such-list' not found"
  }
}
```

Correct the list name using the declaration or rediscover the intended workspace's contract. Do not turn a request error into an empty dataset. Inspect the [reference operations](/docs/api/?api=consumer-stops-v1#consumer-stops-v1/GET/api/consumer/stops/v1/lists/all-stops) for the instance's complete generated schema.

*Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0.*

## Parameter values and response metadata

In query strings, repeat a parameter or separate its values with commas for alternatives. A literal comma inside a value must be percent-encoded as `%2C`. Comparisons are case-insensitive. For a list's special parent parameter, supply public record UUIDs, not names or codes; use a declared ancestor filter on another list to match those values instead. Without that parent parameter the list covers the whole type.

Successful data responses identify the workspace in `RDM-Workspace`. The missing-list error above does not include that header; retain the request context when handling an error. Publication reads also supply `RDM-Publication` and collection `publication`. Lists return `items`, `workspace`, `publication`, `pageSize`, `nextCursor`, `prevCursor`, `anchor`, `totalCount` and `startIndex`; totals and start index are null unless requested with `includeTotal=true`. A get-by-ID response is the bare business object. Unknown, deleted, unexposed or other-workspace records all answer `404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`.

The contract's Publications operation lists snapshots newest first, with `id`, `publishedAt`, `status` and `eventSequence`. It supports ordinary paging but no seek. `eventSequence` can be null for an older snapshot; do not assume that is zero. Use a snapshot with a usable sequence when preparing a load-and-follow baseline. `publication=latest` selects the active publication, and fails with `PUBLICATION_NOT_FOUND` if none exists.

ETags have an opaque digest and contract version. Keep the whole value, including quotes, and send it as `If-None-Match` for the same GET. The server compares after validating the read; a cached tag does not bypass access or request validation. Resolve is POST and has no conditional GET behavior.

A parent UUID that is missing or has the wrong parent type gives `404 PARENT_NOT_FOUND`. An unknown public type filter gives `400 UNKNOWN_OBJECT_TYPE`. A value that cannot parse as a typed match field simply does not match that field. A shared-related route does not by itself include the matching record: that needs `itself` in the declaration.

Conditional reads accept `If-None-Match: *`, a list of tags and weak comparison. A 304 has no body and retains the ETag and read-context headers. A live cursor combined with publication selection, a pinned cursor without publication selection, or a different explicit publication ID gives `INVALID_CURSOR`. Keep `publication=latest` on continuation requests to follow the publication first resolved by that cursor.

## Select a publication before a baseline

**Reference-data example:** ask for the workspace's publications through the [Publications operation](/docs/api/?api=consumer-stops-v1#consumer-stops-v1/GET/api/consumer/stops/v1/publications):

```http
GET /api/consumer/stops/v1/publications?workspace=graubuenden&pageSize=20&includeTotal=true HTTP/1.1
Host: <instance>
Authorization: Bearer <consumer-token>
Accept: application/json
```

Before that workspace has any publications, the complete successful body has this shape. This is an illustration of the empty state, not a captured answer from the reference instance:

```json
{
  "items": [],
  "workspace": "graubuenden",
  "pageSize": 20,
  "nextCursor": null,
  "prevCursor": null,
  "anchor": null,
  "totalCount": 0,
  "startIndex": 0
}
```

A nonempty answer includes each publication's `id`, `publishedAt`, `eventSequence` and `status`. `active` identifies the snapshot selected by `publication=latest`; `withdrawn` includes superseded or withdrawn snapshots, still readable by explicit ID. The collection has no `publication` field of its own. Without `includeTotal=true`, its total fields are omitted; this operation uses the ordinary collection envelope rather than a data list's nullable totals.

For a baseline, select an ID with a usable sequence, then add `publication=<id>` to the declared list or object request. A publication can still fail the contract-compatibility check on that read; its presence in the catalogue does not establish compatibility. If the catalogue is empty, use live reads for current answers or arrange a publication for a fixed extract. Do not invent a publication ID or treat null `eventSequence` as zero. Follow [Load, then follow changes](/docs/guide/integrate/load-then-follow-changes/#use-a-consumer-contract-instead) when continuing from its sequence.

## Reading through an earlier contract

A retained earlier contract reads current data using that version’s fields, names and
related blocks. Keep its version in object, list and lookup addresses, and keep checkpoints
with that version and workspace. It is not a snapshot of the data from when the contract
was superseded. Use a compatible publication for fixed values.

The workspace must currently serve the requested version, even for a publication read.
The publication must also contain that version’s definition; keeping v1 live does not
make a publication containing only v2 compatible with v1. If the administrator stops v1,
its reads return `404 CONTRACT_VERSION_NOT_FOUND`; `details.servedContractVersions` lists
available numbers. Rediscover and inspect the intended replacement rather than changing
the URL and reusing an unreviewed parser. See [Earlier contract versions](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/#earlier-contract-versions)
for deprecation headers, discovery and an example response.

---
title: Reading records
description: Choose precise record, query and relationship reads without walking an entire workspace.
reader: integrator
---

Choose a read by what you already know. The [object operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/objects) offer individual records, per-type collections and a cross-type lookup. The [query operation](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/queries) selects one type using the model's fields and relationships. All use the selected [workspace and context](/docs/integrate/workspaces-contexts-and-models/).

## Find records

Use the cross-type lookup when the type is unknown: search names and built-in fields, narrow to types, an application, a parent or the top level. A parent scope and a top-level scope cannot be combined (`MUTUALLY_EXCLUSIVE_SCOPE`). Model-declared attributes belong to per-type reads: asking for one on the cross-type lookup is refused with guidance to that route.

Use a per-type list for searchable or filterable attributes declared on that type. Keep filter values typed. A boolean stays a boolean; dates and date-times follow their declared types. Date-times keep their UTC instant and explicit offset; a missing zone means UTC. Equivalent decimals read in a canonical form without trailing zeros. Do not turn all values into text to make handling easier.

Use the model-aware query to combine typed field criteria, an ancestor at any depth, or one relationship hop or its absence. You can select fields, choose a sort and include related records. Ancestor field output chooses the matching ancestor nearest the root. A related criterion does not mean an unbounded recursive graph traversal.

Expansions return at most 20 related records per item. Follow their continuation through the [relationship collection](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/relations) when you need the rest. A query's main cursor continues that query only. For date-sensitive questions, read [Business dates](/docs/integrate/business-dates/): dating the root records does not date their expansions.

## Read relationships and values

The [workspace edge list](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/relations) reads all or selected relationship types in one workspace, including snapshot contexts. A selected mapping view changes the projected fields; without it the ends expose identity and name. Without a direction restriction the mapping list can show both orientations of an edge. Keep physical relationship identity if deduplicating.

Relationships of one record can be searched and sorted by the related records' fields. Read an individual attribute through the [attribute operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/attributes), in the same context as its record. Their add, change and remove operations claim the owning record version. Adding an existing value is `ATTRIBUTE_ALREADY_EXISTS`; changing or removing an absent one is `ATTRIBUTE_NOT_FOUND`; a required value cannot be removed (`CANNOT_DELETE_REQUIRED_ATTRIBUTE`). Fields not bound to the type cannot be written.

## Correct an invalid read

`INVALID_FILTER`, `INVALID_SORT`, `INVALID_QUERY`, `INVALID_EXPAND`, `INVALID_RANGE` or `INVALID_DATE` require correcting the request against the current model and operation. `INVALID_OBJECT_TYPE_FOR_APPLICATION` means the selected type is outside that application. `OBJECT_TYPE_CHANGED` means reread the record before using the old type route. `UNKNOWN_ATTRIBUTE_TYPE` requires checking the definition key, while `VIEW_NOT_FOUND` requires selecting a view in the current context.

For [relation matrix operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/relation-matrix), `CONFLICTING_COLUMN_PARAMETERS`, `DUPLICATE_COLUMN_IDS` and `TOO_MANY_COLUMNS` require a valid bounded column selection. `RELATION_MATRIX_STATE_REQUIRES_COLUMNS` needs a column scope before filtering by state. `RELATION_MATRIX_VIEW_NOT_FOUND`, `RELATION_MATRIX_PARENT_NOT_FOUND`, `RELATION_MATRIX_ROW_NOT_FOUND` and `RELATION_MATRIX_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` require selecting the declared view and records of its expected types in the same context. `RELATION_MATRIX_PARENT_SCOPE_MISMATCH` requires a parent type that can contain its rows. `RELATION_MATRIX_ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` means the model does not permit the requested cell change. At most 20 columns can be chosen together; without a selection the columns page separately. A cell preview holds at most five records while reporting its full count; open the cell collection to read the rest. Incoming views cannot show inactive or uniqueness-conflict states from rules declared on the binding's target end. Matrix state remains maintained when writers race; the client must still respect version conflicts.

Use [paged traversal](/docs/guide/integrate/read-a-collection-completely-and-resume/) for a complete result, and [bulk writes](/docs/integrate/writing-in-bulk/) for changes, including typed relationship values and initial relationships.

## Read and replace a mapping set

The [mapping operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/mapping) expose a declared mapping view's coverage, candidate records and target membership. Keep the application and view together with the workspace and context. Target details give the exact count and at most 20 preview targets; follow their continuation for the rest. That continuation is bound to the set version. If membership changes, reread the set rather than joining pages from different versions.

Read the existing set before replacing it and retain its set version. Submit all intended targets together, including existing targets you want to keep. On a single-target mapping save, omitting relationship attributes retains their values. Sending an explicit attribute object replaces those values; an empty object clears them only where valid. Clearing the target accepts no non-empty relationship values. Replacement preserves suitable existing relationships and refuses a stale set, so a concurrent edit cannot disappear behind your save. See [Versions and conflicts](/docs/integrate/versions-and-conflicts/) and [Bulk relationship sets](/docs/integrate/writing-in-bulk/#relationships-and-sets).

| Refusal | Recovery |
| --- | --- |
| `INCOMPLETE_VIEW_IDENTITY` or `MAPPING_VIEW_REQUIRED` | Supply both parts of the selected view identity. |
| `MAPPING_BINDING_NOT_FOUND` | Discover an allowed relationship binding in the context's model. |
| `MAPPING_VIEW_BINDING_MISMATCH` | Use the binding and direction declared by the selected view. |
| `MAPPING_PARENT_SCOPE_MISMATCH` | Select a parent whose type can contain the view's sources. |
| `MAPPING_CANDIDATE_TYPE_MISMATCH` | Ask for candidates on the view's target side. |
| `MAPPING_SOURCE_NOT_FOUND` or `MAPPING_ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND` | Reread the source and targets in the selected workspace and context. |
| `MAPPING_ENDPOINT_TYPE_MISMATCH` | Use endpoints of the binding's declared types. |

## Keep query and edge continuations separate

The workspace Relations and Mappings reads expose the same edge-list contract. The anchored relationship read is a different collection; a cursor from one route does not continue another. Use either a change-set or publication context, never both (`MUTUALLY_EXCLUSIVE_CONTEXT`).

Model-aware queries combine criteria with AND, support one relationship hop or its absence, and one sort field with a stable tie breaker. They do not support OR groups or nested relationship hops. Field criteria follow the type’s filterable declarations. A criterion for an ancestor tests containment, rather than following an arbitrary relation. An expansion limit is 1–20; the expansion reports its full count and a continuation through the relationship collection.

Selected query items always retain public ID, type and version; selected values are under `fields`. Omitting selection uses the list’s usual item shape. The main cursor binds the query body, so preserve criteria, selection, expansions, context and business date when continuing. A malformed body uses `REQUEST_VALIDATION_ERROR`; model-dependent mistakes use `INVALID_QUERY` with a pointer. Consult the [query operation](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/queries) for its full grammar.

Attribute values preserve their declared JSON form. Decimal responses use precision-preserving strings, while requests can supply a decimal number. Integers and booleans remain numbers and booleans. Dates use ISO 8601 days, and date-times return their UTC instant with an explicit offset. Treat missing and empty text as no value.

Unique attributes are unique across all records carrying that attribute type within a workspace, including different object types. Scalar types support uniqueness; JSON does not. `DUPLICATE_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE` identifies the attribute and conflicting record. Any number of records can leave a unique text value empty. Do not use a non-unique name as a substitute for a batch key.

## Turn a question into filters

The [query-translation operation](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/ai) turns words about a table list into that list's filters and name search. It needs Browse and Use AI proposals in the workspace, with a configured provider. It answers directly, without a job, for live data, a change set or a publication. Other view types are refused as `QUERY_TRANSLATION_VIEW_UNSUPPORTED`.

The question, today's date, field labels and types, conditions and relationships go to the provider. At `samples` or `values`, it also receives record names for relationship types whose lists in that context contain at most 50 records; at `structure` it receives no record names. The question itself can contain names you type. The request can incur provider charges and leaves a call record; [About AI](/docs/run/ai/) explains send levels, costs and retention. The requester may lower the send level but cannot raise the instance ceiling.

Show the proposed filters and search to the person. When `applied` is true, every part was expressed and the client can use the returned ordinary filters for the requested list. When `applied` is false, apply nothing: show each `notExpressed` part and its reason, and let the person explicitly choose whether to use the partial filters. The built-in browser presents these as dashed pills with **Use these filters**. Never treat a partly understood question as a complete query.

refiroo resolves a named record in the requested context: first an exact name ignoring case, otherwise a single partial match. Missing or ambiguous names remain unexpressed. A requested sort, who changed a record, or something the list cannot filter is also unexpressed. Created and updated time filters are available only on live lists. Once accepted, the result uses the same filters for reading, selection and export.

`QUERY_TRANSLATION_FAILED` means no usable translation came back, including an answer with invalid fields, conditions or values. Keep the person's question and existing list unchanged; the response's call reference helps an operator inspect the failure. `AI_NOT_CONFIGURED`, `AI_SEND_LEVEL_TOO_LOW` and `FORBIDDEN` mean the feature is unavailable under the current settings or permissions; ordinary filters remain available.
guide/src/content/docs/integrate/relatio:
---
title: Relationships and their values
description: Read connections and change their typed attributes through the management API.
reader: integrator
---

Use management relationship operations when an integration maintains connections or values
belonging to those connections. A relationship joins two public record IDs and holds only the
attributes declared for its directed type pair. Those values retain their declared types and
numeric bounds. They are separate from both endpoint records' attributes.

All management paths below begin with `/api/v1`. Use a management token with Browse for reads
and Edit live or Work in change sets for writes in the selected context, subject to scoped
grants. Consumer grants do not grant these writes. The [relationship operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/relations)
define the requests and responses. For read-only business projections, see
[Consumer APIs](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/#publish-values-of-the-connection).

## Records reused or created through a matrix

A relation matrix is a view over records and relationships. Creating in a cell adds a record
in a container and a relationship to the row. Placement follows the binding's candidate
rules, then existing use of groups by the view; a missing rule-defined group or a group
proposed from other columns can be created with the record in one atomic change. The browser
allows review of the place and editing a proposed group's name. See
[View exports and placement](/docs/integrate/files-imports-and-exports/#export-a-declared-view). Linking in a cell adds a relationship to
an existing record. Where the binding permits reuse, that record can be connected to several
rows: it has the same public record ID under every row, with a separate relationship ID and
attribute set for each connection. Do not create one local copy per cell.

Unlink removes the relationship, not the record. A required owner connection cannot be removed
alone. In the [workspace change feed](/docs/integrate/following-changes/), an unlink is a deleted
relationship entry retaining its endpoint IDs; remove the local edge without deleting the
shared record. Consumer events instead follow their declared watches: do not assume every
unlink produces a particular consumer event.

For example, a translation matrix can create a missing name for one language, with one
counting record allowed per row and language. A mapping matrix can reuse a code already
connected to another row or create a separate code. Both are configurations of the same
record and relationship operations. A one-per-column counting rule can leave a proposed cell
showing **Conflict** when two records count in a change set; resolve and validate it before
publication. A relationship's cardinality can also prevent adding another record without
producing that counting-conflict state.

After publication, the consumer API can expose the new record and its relationship according
to its declaration and grants. Unpublished change-set edits are invisible to consumers.
Direct live writes are already visible to live consumer reads; a read pinned to an earlier
publication keeps that publication's state. A shared record's own fields are shared wherever
it is exposed; values on each relationship remain specific to that connection. See
[Consumer APIs](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/#live-and-publication-reads) for read contexts and
[Fill in a relation matrix](/docs/guide/use/fill-in-a-relation-matrix/) for the browser actions.

## Read connections before writing

Use the [workspace edge list](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/relations/GET/api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_key}/relations)
when the integration needs relationships across records. `fromObjectId` and `toObjectId` narrow
the list to particular endpoints. Page until no continuation remains; do not infer that one
page contains every connection.

To read the rows of a declared relationships table, supply its `applicationKey` and `viewKey`.
The view fixes its relation and endpoint types. Do not also supply `relationTypeKey`,
`fromObjectTypeKey`, `toObjectTypeKey` or `direction`: that gives `422 RELATION_TABLE_BINDING_FIXED`.
A row has `source` and `target` with the endpoint fields chosen by the view, `attributes`,
`relationId` and `relationVersion`. Keep that relationship version for a value edit.
`mappingVersion` instead versions the source record's relationship set; it is used when
changing membership, not as the version of one connection's values.

The view's `sortFields` and `filterFields` determine sorting and filtering. An equality filter
uses `filter.<ref>.eq`, where the reference begins with `from:`, `to:` or `relation:`. Repeated
equalities on one field are alternatives; different fields must all match. Values are parsed
in the field's type. `search` finds either endpoint's name without letter case. Use `sort` or
a leading minus for descending order. Missing sort values come last.

Cursor, position, end and seek navigation follow the [paging rules](/docs/integrate/identifiers-paging-and-errors/).
With a grouped view, `seek` targets the group record's name; otherwise it targets the first
sort value. `groupCounts` reports matching relationships for each group record on the page,
across the filtered list rather than just that page. An undeclared filter or operator gives
`422 INVALID_FILTER`; an undeclared sort gives `422 INVALID_SORT`. Sort or field filters
without a relationships-table view give `422 RELATION_TABLE_VIEW_REQUIRED`.

The same read works in Live, a change set (`changeSetId`) or a publication (`publicationId`).
Select one context deliberately and keep it with paging checkpoints. A publication is read-only.

## Read a grid without losing missing connections

Use the [relationship grid read](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/relations/GET/api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_key}/relation-grid)
with `applicationKey` and `viewKey`. It accepts any relationships-table view, whichever layout
the browser uses. A different view gives `404 RELATION_TABLE_NOT_FOUND`.

Each matching from record appears once, including records with no connection. The page's
`columns` contains up to 50 matching to records in name order, each with `linkedCount` across
all filtered source rows. `columnTotal` reports all matching column records and `rowTotal`
reports matching rows. Narrow the column selection when the total exceeds what is returned.
Repeat `toObjectId` to select column records and use `toSearch` to search them.

Each source row has `mappingVersion` and a `relations` map keyed by column record ID. An entry
holds `relationId`, `version`, `attributes` and `proposed`. A missing entry means not linked;
an empty or missing attribute on an existing entry means no held value, not no connection.
`proposed` marks a staged connection in a change set and is false in Live and publications.

Filters use `filter.<ref>.<operator>`. The grid offers its declared filters and the filter fields
of each endpoint type's main table view. `from:` narrows rows, `to:` narrows column records,
and `relation:` keeps rows with a matching connection to a shown column record. Conditions on
relationship attributes must hold on the same connection. Operators follow the field's type,
including equality, text comparisons, ranges and empty/unset tests where supported. The
endpoint fields also support their collection's related-record filters. Invalid fields or
operators are refused rather than ignored. Row sorting uses a declared `from:` field; a
declared sort for another part falls back to the source record's name.

Repeat `attribute` to request particular relationship attributes among the view's attribute
columns. An invalid choice gives `422 INVALID_ATTRIBUTE`. Without this parameter the read returns
all stored relationship values, including values not displayed by the view. Preserve those
values when constructing a replacement write.

Grid paging, search and context selection follow the row read. See the
[grid's browser explanation](/docs/use/relationship-tables/#grid-each-from-record-once) for the
meaning of linked counts and gaps.

## Change one connection or a known set

Use [Update relationship](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/relations/PATCH/api/v1/relations/{relation_id})
with `attributes` and `expectedVersion` from the read. **PATCH replaces the relationship's
attribute set.** Merge a single changed value into the complete stored set before sending it,
otherwise omitted values are removed. A stale claim gives `409 VERSION_CONFLICT`; reread and
reconcile instead of silently retrying against a new version. This edit does not replace its
endpoint records or change their own fields.

For several known connection IDs, use [Batch relationship values](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/relations/POST/api/v1/relations/batch).
Each item's attributes are merged over its stored values, and null clears a named value.
Omitted attributes remain. This differs from PATCH. Keep each item's relationship version.
All items are validated and saved together: a refusal leaves every connection unchanged.

`RELATION_BATCH_REFUSED` returns 409 when a version was stale, otherwise 422. Its
`details.items` identifies each failure by index, relationship ID, error code, message and
further details. Read these item codes before deciding whether to reread, correct a value or
change the intended links. Repeating a relationship ID gives `422 DUPLICATE_BATCH_ITEMS`;
exceeding `BATCH_MAX_ITEMS` gives `413 BATCH_TOO_LARGE`.

For Live batch writes, pass `workspaceKey` explicitly. For change-set writes, pass `changeSetId`
and the current `expectedChangeSetVersion` as well as each connection's version. Keep the
returned `changeSetVersion` for the next write. None of these operations changes a publication.

## Change a filtered grid selection

[Grid change](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/relations/POST/api/v1/relations/grid-change) changes one
scalar relationship attribute across selected source rows and column records. Unlike a list
of known relationship IDs, it can also link missing pairs. Start with `dryRun: true`, inspect
all counts and refusals, then submit the reviewed selection with `dryRun: false`. The server
checks current data again; the preview does not reserve it.

Follow [Submit a bulk change](/docs/guide/integrate/submit-a-bulk-change/#change-relationship-values-from-a-grid-selection)
for a request and preview. This is a synchronous atomic operation, distinct from a background
job. It does not inherit job confirmation or idempotency behavior just because it affects many
connections. After a lost response, reread current data before deciding what to send next.
guide/src/content/docs/integrate/securit:
---
title: Security for integrators
description: Understand permissions, narrowed writes and the identity recorded for API work.
reader: integrator
---

Give each system its own [client](/docs/administer/clients/) and grant only the work it needs. Authentication establishes the caller; the audience selects an interface; grants decide what that caller can do. A valid token alone is not permission to read or write data.

## Management roles and workspace scope

A management role contains action groups, such as Browse, Bulk and import, Work in change sets, Publish or Feed. Use the [security catalogue and grant operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/security) to discover and administer them. A grant can apply at the instance or to one workspace. An instance grant applies to present and future workspaces.

Use these predefined role keys in the [grant operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/security);
the names are those shown in Settings. The role catalogue also lists custom roles and their keys.

| Name in Settings | Key for commands and API grants |
| --- | --- |
| Reader | `reader` |
| Contributor | `contributor` |
| Data steward | `steward` |
| Data owner | `owner` |
| Model administrator | `model-admin` |
| Workspace administrator | `workspace-admin` |
| Integration administrator | `integration-admin` |
| Operator | `operator` |
| Security administrator | `security-admin` |
| Agent | `agent` |

Browse permits reading throughout its workspace. Application and record-type narrowing limits writes, not reads; data that must be hidden from some readers needs a separate workspace. Collections show only resources the caller may access. A direct request for a named resource outside that access is refused.

A narrowed write grant applies to the action group used by the operation. A Bulk and import allowance does not imply permission to edit live individually or publish. Several grants for the same action can add their allowed types together. A relationship write is allowed when either endpoint's type is allowed. Cascading deletion must also be allowed for the records and relationships it removes; publishing must be allowed for the types the change set affects, including the live records it replaces or deletes.

A single write or publication is refused as a whole. A batch or import reports refusals per item according to its failure policy. Previews show the same permission refusals as execution. See [Bulk writes](/docs/integrate/writing-in-bulk/) and [Changes, approvals and publication](/docs/integrate/changes-approvals-and-publication/).

`FORBIDDEN` identifies the missing action and workspace, and names refused record types where applicable. Ask the administrator to review that grant; renewing the same token does not add permissions. A grant that refers to applications or types removed by a model release is stale and allows nothing until corrected. Deployment capabilities also apply: a role cannot enable an operation the deployment has disabled.

## Consumer API access

Consumer data routes accept clients only. Each client needs a grant for the named API in each workspace it reads. A management role, including Security administrator, does not replace this grant. Use a token with the consumer audience; the wrong audience is refused as `TOKEN_INVALID`. The API index accepts a consumer token and lists the APIs granted in that workspace, or a management token with Browse and lists all its APIs. Each definition’s OpenAPI document is public and needs no token. See [Consumer APIs](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/), [Get a token](/docs/guide/integrate/get-a-token/) and [Roles and grants](/docs/administer/roles-and-grants/).

## Jobs and changing access

Permissions and active state are checked on requests and at each job step. A job runs as its original requester, even when someone else can inspect or confirm it. Revoking that requester's permission or deactivating them can stop a running job at its next step. Confirmation checks the requester again; refusal leaves the job waiting. Inspect committed chunks before deciding how to recover a partially applied job.

The requester can read, follow, cancel and confirm their own job. Other callers need the action group for that job kind in its workspace. See [Jobs](/docs/integrate/jobs/) for state and recovery. A write without an identified requester fails closed with `WRITER_UNKNOWN`; report it with its request reference as an engine problem.

## Trace who did the work

Read [record history](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/objects) for changes to one record and the [changes operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/changes) for visible changes across workspaces. The actor identifies the person or client. The cause identifies work applied by a job or publication. A recorded channel identifies how work reached the engine where supplied; it does not confer permission. Job changes name their requester; applied publication changes name the publisher. Names reflect the identity's current name. Engine work is distinguished from older entries with no recorded actor.

The history of a record can include changed values. The raw change feed identifies changed fields without their values, and consumer record events omit actor identity. Choose the appropriate interface for an audit export rather than inferring authorship from a consumer event.

Security administrators can read [security events](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/security) for sign-in outcomes and changes to people, groups, roles, grants, clients and signing keys. They contain no passwords, secrets or keys. Security administration does not grant Browse over every workspace's data history. See [Who changed what](/docs/administer/audit/) for the browser views.

## Correct access-administration refusals

| Refusal | Recovery |
| --- | --- |
| `GRANT_NOT_FOUND` or `ROLE_NOT_FOUND` | Read the current grants or roles and use the intended existing identity. |
| `GRANT_SCOPE_INVALID` | Correct the combination of role or consumer API and scope using the grant operation's schema. |
| `GRANT_SCOPE_UNKNOWN` | Choose applications, types or an API present in that workspace's model. |
| `ROLE_NAME_TAKEN` | Choose a distinct name. |
| `ROLE_PREDEFINED` | Copy the predefined role into a custom role before editing. |
| `ROLE_IN_USE` | Reassign or remove its grants before deleting the custom role. |
| `LAST_SECURITY_ADMINISTRATOR` | Retain an active person with instance Security administration. A client does not satisfy this safeguard. |

Model-draft history refusals such as `INVALID_OPERATION`, `NOTHING_TO_APPLY`, `NOTHING_TO_UNDO`, `NOTHING_TO_REDO` and `OPERATION_HAS_DEPENDANTS` belong to [Model and release operations](/docs/integrate/model-and-release-operations/).

For leaked credentials, coordinate [client-secret rotation](/docs/administer/clients/#secrets-and-rotation) with the administrator. Webhook signing keys have a separate lifecycle and can be rotated with zero overlap for immediate replacement; see [Consumer events and webhooks](/docs/integrate/consumer-events-and-webhooks/#verify-before-accepting).

## Automate access administration

A client holding Security administration can manage people, groups and roles through the [security operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/security). Discover the current resources and versions, make the intended change, then reread access where needed. Keep administrative credentials separate from the client that loads or consumes data. For the corresponding browser tasks, see [People and groups](/docs/administer/people-and-groups/), [Roles and grants](/docs/administer/roles-and-grants/) and [Sign-in](/docs/administer/sign-in/).

| Refusal | Recovery |
| --- | --- |
| `ACTION_GROUP_UNKNOWN` | Read the action catalogue and choose a known group. |
| `USER_NOT_FOUND`, `GROUP_NOT_FOUND` or `GROUP_MEMBER_NOT_FOUND` | Refresh the people, groups or membership before changing it. |
| `EMAIL_TAKEN` or `GROUP_NAME_TAKEN` | Choose an unused e-mail address or group name. |
| `GROUP_FROM_PROVIDER` | Change membership in the sign-in provider; it is synchronized at sign-in. |
| `GROUP_CLAIM_TAKEN` | Use the existing group for that provider claim or choose a different claim. |
| `SIGN_IN_PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND` or `SIGN_IN_PROVIDER_KEY_TAKEN` | Select an existing provider or give the new one a distinct key. |
| `SIGN_IN_PROVIDER_IN_USE` | Add another provider instead of changing the issuer people already use. |
| `SIGN_IN_PROVIDER_SECRET_REQUIRED` | Supply the new provider's client secret when changing issuer. |
| `SIGN_IN_PROVIDER_UNREACHABLE` | Check the provider address and reported connection or metadata failure. |
| `NO_WORKING_PROVIDER` | Complete a successful sign-in through an enabled provider before disabling local sign-in. |
| `LAST_LOCAL_ADMINISTRATOR` | Retain another permitted local administrator or restore local sign-in before removing this one. |
| `LOCAL_SIGN_IN_OFF` | Use the configured provider; local passwords are restricted to administrators retained for recovery. |

Linking identities moves a provider sign-in between people; it is not a way to merge arbitrary access. `IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND` or `NO_IDENTITY_TO_LINK` requires the source's existing provider identity. `IDENTITY_PROVIDER_TAKEN` means the target already has that provider. `LINK_SAME_PERSON` requires two different people. `LINK_TARGET_DEACTIVATED` requires activating the intended target first. `PERSON_HAS_ACCESS` requires reviewing and removing the source's own access or choosing the opposite linking direction, as the refusal explains.

## Keep person-only flows separate

Client credentials do not create a person's password, second factor or browser session. Person-only operations refuse a client as `NOT_A_PERSON`. A browser integration acting for a person uses the [sign-in operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/oauth) and the person's [security operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/security); see [Signing in and tokens](/docs/integrate/signing-in-and-tokens/#browser-sessions).

| Refusal | Recovery |
| --- | --- |
| `PASSWORD_INCORRECT` | Ask the person for their current password again. |
| `PASSWORD_REJECTED` | Choose a password satisfying the reason returned. |
| `SIGN_IN_SLOWED` | Respect the returned wait interval; repeated attempts do not speed recovery. |
| `PROOF_REQUIRED` | Obtain the person's required password or authenticator proof. |
| `CODE_INCORRECT` | Obtain a fresh valid code; used codes cannot be replayed. |
| `SECOND_FACTOR_EXISTS` | Read the existing enrollment instead of starting another. |
| `SECOND_FACTOR_NOT_FOUND` | Start or refresh the enrollment appropriate to the operation. |
| `SECOND_FACTOR_REQUIRED` | Set up another permitted factor before removing the last required one. |
| `PASSWORD_REQUIRED` | Passkeys require a local password account; a provider-only account cannot enroll one. |
| `PASSKEY_NOT_FOUND` or `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` | Refresh the person's current keys or open sessions. |
| `TOO_MANY_PASSKEYS` | Remove an unused key before adding another. |

## Mail administration failures

Use the [mail operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/mail) with the required administrative permission; [Sign-in and mail setup](/docs/run/sign-in-and-mail-setup/) explains deployment preparation. `MAIL_PASSWORD_REQUIRED` means resend the password after a host or port change. `MAIL_SEND_FAILED` requires correcting the reported test-delivery failure. `NO_EMAIL` needs an address on the person, or a securely passed link where that operation offers one. `MESSAGE_BEING_SENT` needs a short wait; `MESSAGE_NOT_WAITING` means a message is no longer queued to stop. `NOT_FOUND` on a message requires refreshing the queue and selecting an existing message. Message text is not available through the administration API.

`ROUTE_NOT_DECLARED` means an operation lacks an engine permission declaration. Like `WRITER_UNKNOWN`, it fails closed and needs investigation using the request reference; adding a broader grant cannot repair it.

## Distinguish a role from the action it grants

Use the [action catalogue](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/security) and caller permissions to discover effective rights. Browse includes exports and model-aware queries, but Feed is separate.
