Bulk and import permits batches and file loads; Copy and move additionally needs Browse at the source and, for a move, Work in change sets there. Model authoring and release permissions are separate from workspace data writes. Operations permits configuration, detailed health and metrics; a metrics scraper uses its own client with that permission.

Application and record-type narrowing combine as alternatives within a grant. Grants for the same action add together, and any unnarrowed grant allows all types for that action in its scope. A type change needs permission for both the type left and the type taken. Migrations and publication withdrawals are not type-narrowed. Shared open change sets can be edited by authorised collaborators; creation does not make them private.

Jobs continue to act for the original requester. A refusal after that requester loses access includes their identity in `requestedBy`; another administrator confirming the job does not replace that identity. A source file is available to its uploader and the appropriate Bulk and import holders, rather than every signed-in client. Check the operation’s declared action instead of inferring access from ownership.

## Restrict assistant connections

[External MCP assistants](/docs/integrate/assistants-and-agents/) use a separate `agent` token. Their management grants are restricted to Browse and Work in change sets; consumer API grants remain. They cannot approve or publish, and can prepare data only in change sets their own identity created. A built-in [assistant task](/docs/integrate/assistant-tasks/) uses a separate session client drawn from its requester's permissions and also cannot approve, publish or activate.

Security administrators manage registered assistants, agent clients and call records through the [agent-access operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/agent-access). Operations holders inspect AI calls through the [AI operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/ai). Deployment switches and secrets, including `MCP_ENABLED`, `AI_AGENT_COMMAND`, `AI_PROVIDER` and send levels, are environment settings read at startup; the Deployment screen does not edit them. [About AI](/docs/run/ai/) covers what leaves the instance, costs and retention. These controls do not change an external assistant's own provider policy.
guide/src/content/docs/integrate/signing:
---
title: Signing in and tokens
description: Authenticate a client and keep its access working during token and secret rotation.
reader: integrator
---

Give an unattended integration a client identity. An administrator [creates the client and grants access](/docs/administer/clients/); your integration exchanges its credentials for a bearer token through the [OAuth token operation](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/oauth). Follow [Get a token](/docs/guide/integrate/get-a-token/) for the sequence.

## Choose the audience

Request the management audience for management operations or the consumer audience for consumer data. The audience selects which interface accepts the token; it does not grant permissions. Management access comes from roles. Consumer access requires a separate grant for the API in the workspace, and is available to clients only. A person's browser role does not make their token a consumer credential.

The default access-token lifetime is one hour. Use the lifetime returned when the token is issued; the operator can change it. Clients have no refresh token. Obtain another access token using the client credentials before the current token expires. Send tokens in the authorization header, never in URLs.

Tokens identify the caller. Permissions and whether the caller is active are checked on requests, so removing access or deactivating a client takes effect on the next request. Do not store a permission decision for the lifetime of a token.

## Rotate without interrupting work

The administrator can rotate a client secret with an overlap. Store the new secret securely, switch the integration to it and obtain a token to check it works before the old secret ends. The administrator can see last-use times and end the overlap early. See [Client secrets](/docs/administer/clients/#secrets-and-rotation) and the [security operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/security). A missing client or secret is reported as `CLIENT_NOT_FOUND` or `CLIENT_SECRET_NOT_FOUND`; `CLIENT_HAS_NO_SECRETS` requires an administrator to supply a usable secret.

Token signing keys rotate independently of client secrets. A token refused after a signing-key change needs a new token, not a new client secret.

## When sign-in or a request fails

OAuth failures use the OAuth error format. `invalid_client` means the credentials cannot authenticate the client; check the ID, secret, expiry and active state. Repeated failures are slowed, including failures with an unknown client ID. Respect the retry interval. `invalid_scope` needs a supported audience; `invalid_request` needs a corrected token request.

Protected API calls use the engine's error format. `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` means no token was supplied. `TOKEN_INVALID` identifies an expired, revoked, wrong-audience or unverifiable token: obtain the correct token, and investigate revocation rather than retrying indefinitely. `CONSUMER_API_CLIENTS_ONLY` requires a client identity. `FORBIDDEN` requires a suitable grant; its explanation names the action and workspace. See [Security for integrators](/docs/integrate/security-model-for-integrators/).

Health probes, public OpenAPI documents, the API reference and sign-in endpoints have open routes. Data routes require authentication; there is no setting to turn it off.

## Browser sessions

People sign in through the authorization-code flow with PKCE. Their refresh tokens rotate and belong to sessions; clients do not reuse this mechanism. Browser sessions default to 12 idle hours and 14 days overall. A used refresh token has a 30-second recovery grace only while its successor is unused. Older reuse or reuse after that successor was consumed ends the session. A transient server failure during renewal does not itself sign the browser out. Browser applications should preserve that distinction between a refused session and a temporarily unavailable server.

## Use OAuth metadata and standard client credentials

The engine is its own OAuth 2.0 authorization server. Its RFC 8414 metadata at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` names the issuer, token endpoint, grants and supported PKCE method. Public verification keys are at `/oauth/jwks`. Access tokens are JWTs signed with ES256 and identify a signing key with `kid`. The issuer and token audience must be those of your instance; a sign-in provider’s token is not a substitute for the engine’s access token.

The [token operation](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/oauth) supports `client_secret_basic` or `client_secret_post`; choose one, not both. `scope=management` is the default and `scope=consumer` selects consumer access. A successful answer includes the bearer token, `expires_in` and scope, with `Cache-Control: no-store`. Use the returned lifetime. A 401 `invalid_client` with Basic authentication includes `WWW-Authenticate: Basic`; repeated failures can return 429 with `Retry-After`, even when the next credentials are correct. Wait before retrying.

JWT claims include issuer, subject, audience, expiry, issue time, token ID and principal kind. A person’s token also identifies their session. They contain no permission grant. Verify JWTs against the issuer’s current public keys if your system validates them locally, while recognising that only the engine can decide current access on each API call.

Token signing keys normally rotate every 30 days (`TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY_DAYS`); the previous key remains usable until its last token expires. An administrator’s immediate rotation retires the current key at once. Client secrets and browser refresh tokens do not use that signing key, so replacing either is a separate operation. Obtain a fresh access token after an unknown-key refusal.

## Assistant connections

External MCP assistants use the `agent` audience, accepted only at `/mcp`. A system uses a client of kind `agent` and requests `scope=agent` (or leaves scope empty for that client); other scopes are refused as `invalid_scope`. An API client cannot request it. A person's assistant uses discovery, public-client registration and authorization code with PKCE; its session and rotated refresh tokens issue only agent tokens. A browser session never issues them. An optional OAuth `resource` must name this instance's `/mcp`, or the request fails as `invalid_target`.

Follow [Connect an assistant](/docs/guide/integrate/connect-an-assistant/) and the [OAuth operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/oauth). This connection gives the external assistant the data it may read and uses its own provider and charges. refiroo keeps tool-call records; [About AI](/docs/run/ai/) explains the data and retention boundaries. The [built-in task assistant](/docs/integrate/assistant-tasks/) instead uses a secretless session client managed by the engine.
guide/src/content/docs/integrate/version:
---
title: Versions and conflicts
description: Keep concurrent changes safe and recover from stale data or models.
reader: integrator
---

Keep the version you read with the change you intend to make. Updating against that version lets refiroo refuse a stale change instead of silently replacing somebody else's work. The [object](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/objects), [relationship](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/relations), [model administration](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/model%20administration) and [change-set operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/change-sets) document their claims.

## Claim what you are changing

Records and relationships have versions. A mapping replacement claims the relationship set, since the membership can change without changing the anchor record. A model draft, change set, release retirement and workspace model activation each have their own concurrency claim. A write inside a change set can need both the record's version and the change set's version.

On `VERSION_CONFLICT`, read the current resource, compare it with your source and decide whether to rebuild or abandon the change. The refusal identifies the current version. Do not simply replace your saved claim with the latest number and send the old change again. More specific failures include `CHANGE_SET_VERSION_CONFLICT`, `MODEL_RELEASE_VERSION_CONFLICT` and `ACTIVATION_CONFLICT`.

A batch update or upsert that would change nothing is reported as unchanged before its version claim. It advances no record version and produces no data-change event. Mapping replacement has a deliberate distinction: a mapping save still checks a stale set token when unchanged, while a bulk set-replacement item can report unchanged before checking it.

## Claim the model as well

Read the model release identity with the model, then use the expected-model-release request header on requests built from it. A `MODEL_RELEASE_CHANGED` refusal means the workspace or context now resolves another release, or it changed during execution. Read the model again and rebuild the request. A live write refused by the commit guard saves nothing. A background job can already have committed earlier chunks: inspect its outcomes before resubmitting.

## Publishing is another comparison

Publishing checks the change set, the workspace's current publication, its model release and the records and mutable relationship sets touched by the changes. Unrelated newer live records are preserved. Record divergences appear as conflicts; a changed relationship set can report `MAPPING_SET_CHANGED`. Review current live data and reapply the intended changes in a new current-live change set when necessary. Revalidating an unchanged conflicting change set cannot resolve its stale base.

`CHANGE_SET_MODEL_RELEASE_CONFLICT` needs an explicit model decision. [Move the change set onto the workspace's release, or migrate the workspace](/docs/integrate/model-and-release-operations/); no implicit rebase happens. Unique-value, cycle and relationship-cardinality checks still apply to racing writers. Retrying must not bypass the rule that refused one writer.

## Use the exact context’s release and version

Model reads identify their release in `X-Model-Release-Id`. Return it as `X-Expected-Model-Release-Id` on management requests built from those definitions. Live requests compare the workspace’s release; change-set and publication requests compare their pinned release. A mismatch is `409 MODEL_RELEASE_CHANGED` before the requested read or write. Details identify the workspace, expected and current release, and the change set where applicable. Without that header, the server still checks the release under which an in-flight write was validated at commit.

A concurrent model switch can also refuse a read with `MODEL_RELEASE_CHANGED`; retry after rediscovery. Read the change-set resource for its current aggregate version: record GET responses do not consistently supply it. Do not infer that claim from a nullable field on another response.
guide/src/content/docs/integrate/workspa:
---
title: Workspaces, contexts and models
description: Select the data and model that each request reads or changes.
reader: integrator
---

A workspace owns its records and runs one installed model release. Two workspaces can run different models or different releases of the same model. Choose the workspace before discovering its types or constructing a request.

The caller's own-workspace collection lists browsable active workspaces, default first, with their applications and relevant open-change-set counts. Use the [workspace operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/workspaces) to discover workspaces you can read. An omitted workspace on a read generally selects the default workspace. An unknown workspace never falls back to that default. A live record create must name its workspace explicitly; `WORKSPACE_KEY_REQUIRED` means the write lacks that scope.

## Choose a context

| Context | What you read | What you can write |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Live | Current committed data under the workspace's release | Direct changes with the appropriate live permission |
| Change set | Its base plus its prepared changes under its pinned release | Prepared changes, claiming the change-set version |
| Publication | An immutable graph under the release recorded with it | Nothing; derive a change set to prepare changes |

Use the same canonical [record](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/objects) and [relationship operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/relations) in these contexts. Do not construct separate change-set CRUD routes. A publication remains unchanged by later live writes, and a publication is not automatically filtered by business date.

Select one context. `MUTUALLY_EXCLUSIVE_CONTEXT` means incompatible selections; `WORKSPACE_CONTEXT_MISMATCH` means the selected change set or publication belongs elsewhere. `WORKSPACE_RETIRED` prevents changes to a retired workspace. Records and relationships in snapshots have no recorded creation or update timestamps, so those fields cannot be used there for filtering or sorting.

## Read across workspaces

The management [cross-type object lookup](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/objects) can combine several named workspaces' live data. Each result identifies its workspace and model release. It cannot combine multiple workspaces with a change set or publication.

A filter naming an application or type must make sense in every selected model. `MODEL_ELEMENT_NOT_IN_EVERY_MODEL` means narrow the workspace selection or choose a common field. Do not interpret a missing type as an empty dataset. If a selected model is unavailable, the entire read fails rather than silently omitting that workspace.

Workspace catalogue changes have their own safeguards: `WORKSPACE_ALREADY_EXISTS` includes retired keys; `WORKSPACE_IS_DEFAULT` and `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_CANNOT_BE_RETIRED` require choosing another default; `WORKSPACE_NOT_EMPTY` and `WORKSPACE_HAS_PUBLICATIONS` require reviewing the retained content instead of forcing deletion. See [Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/).

## Keep assignments explicit

A new workspace can name an installed usable release; otherwise it starts on the default workspace’s release. After creation its assignment is its own. Changing the default workspace does not switch any existing workspace’s model. Model discovery identifies the selected workspace with `RDM-Workspace`, and its release with `X-Model-Release-Id` and the model ETag.

One unavailable workspace does not justify reading another workspace as a fallback. Across-workspace record lookup fails as a whole if any selected workspace cannot load its release. Its cursor binds the selected workspace set, and each result carries `workspaceKey` and `modelReleaseId`. Feeds, relationship collections and exports remain within one workspace.

An administration list filtered by a consumer API name can include subscriptions from several workspaces where that name denotes different contracts. Keep both API name and workspace in integration configuration. Import profiles and model mappings identify their models; a shared instance catalogue does not mean their definitions apply to every workspace model.

## Deletion and reusing a workspace key

Deletion is restricted to a non-default, empty workspace that has never been published and
has no change sets or webhook subscriptions. `WORKSPACE_HAS_SUBSCRIPTIONS` requires removing
those subscriptions first; deletion does not silently discard them.

Deleting an eligible workspace removes its feed positions and idempotency keys. Audit history
is retained without that workspace or its feed positions. Creating a new workspace under the
same key starts a separate feed at position 1; a retried job request does not replay the deleted
workspace's job. Rediscover the new workspace rather than reusing saved positions or assuming
that an old idempotency key still protects a request. See the [workspace operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/workspaces).
guide/src/content/docs/integrate/writing:
---
title: Writing in bulk
description: Apply bounded changes with explicit failure policy, safe retries and per-item outcomes.
reader: integrator
---

Use a batch to create, update, upsert or delete records and relationships together. A batch is a job even when it runs inline. The [batch operation under jobs](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/jobs) defines the available operations. Follow [Submit a bulk change](/docs/guide/integrate/submit-a-bulk-change/) for the sequence.

## Choose policy and execution

Choose the policy explicitly. **Atomic** applies all items or none. **Independent** lets valid items apply when another is refused. Items run in order and see earlier applied items; this is not deferred validation of a final graph. For example, swapping two unique values cannot rely on an intermediate duplicate being tolerated. Use a change set for changes needing whole-graph preparation.

Choose inline or background explicitly; refiroo does not silently switch the response when a request grows. Default limits are 1,000 items and 5 MB inline, 1,000,000 items and 50 MB for a background JSON batch, and 10,000 items for an atomic job. Read the current [capabilities](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/model); operators can change these limits. `BATCH_TOO_LARGE` means split the request or choose the supported larger mode. A larger file can be loaded through [imports](/docs/integrate/files-imports-and-exports/).

A processed inline request can succeed at HTTP level while some or all items are refused. Read the job result and every item's outcome:

| Outcome | Meaning for your source system |
| --- | --- |
| Applied | The item committed, including unchanged items that needed no write. |
| Rejected | Correct the item using its machine-readable refusal. |
| Unprocessed | The item has no committed change from this execution. Inspect whether rollback, cancellation, a model change or a job failure stopped it. |

An atomic refusal rolls back earlier items and marks other items unprocessed. Independent work commits in chunks, so later failure leaves earlier committed changes intact.

## Address records and protect changes

Address an existing record by public ID or an attribute declared unique for its type. References can find a record applied earlier in the same batch. `INVALID_RECORD_KEY` requires a genuinely unique attribute; `REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND` requires loading the target first; `REFERENCE_TYPE_MISMATCH` requires the right type. A create using an occupied ID is `OBJECT_ALREADY_EXISTS`, including IDs held in another workspace.

Updates claim the version read. A changing upsert without a version is `VERSION_REQUIRED` unless the request explicitly permits overwrite. Use overwrite only when the supplying system is authoritative; it is recorded in history. An unchanged item needs no version change or event. Initial relationships on an upsert are used only when the record is created.

A batch targets either live data or a change set, not a context per item. `INVALID_BATCH_CONTEXT` needs a corrected selection. In a change set, claim its version for the job as well as applicable item versions. If the model changes during an inline batch, the request and job save nothing. A background job reports what its earlier chunks already saved.

## Relationships and sets

A batch can create, ensure, update or delete a relationship, ensure that two records are not related, or replace a whole set. Both ends must exist in the context and belong to the same workspace. Typed relationship values obey their declarations. A set replacement keeps existing relationships when possible and claims the set version read; relationship creation and deletion can also claim that set. `RELATION_SET_VERSION_CONFLICT` requires rereading the membership; `RELATION_SET_CLAIM_INCOMPLETE` requires a complete claim.

Ensure operations are useful for repeated loads. Ensuring absence removes an existing mutable relationship or returns unchanged if none exists. It cannot remove containment or a required relationship. A previewed set replacement carries the set version it showed into execution. A mapping save checks a stale set token even on an unchanged save; the bulk replacement can answer unchanged first.

The same model rules apply to single and bulk writes. `CARDINALITY_VIOLATION` means the binding allows fewer relationships; many-to-one permits at most one on its constrained side. `INVALID_RELATION_PAIR`, `RELATION_CANDIDATE_REFUSED` and `RELATION_ANCESTOR_REQUIRED` require allowed endpoint types and candidates. `RELATION_WRONG_SCOPE` or `PARENT_WRONG_SCOPE` requires one workspace. `DUPLICATE_RELATION`, `RELATION_ALREADY_EXISTS` and `DUPLICATE_INITIAL_RELATION` require removing duplicates or using an ensure operation. `IMMUTABLE_RELATION`, `REQUIRED_RELATION` and `REQUIRED_OWNERSHIP_BINDING` require the permitted containment or ownership operation rather than deleting an essential edge.

## Preview and delete safely

A background preview writes no data changes. Inspect the proposed counts and refused items, and whether the preview covered every item or only a sample. Confirm through the [job operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/jobs) or cancel. Execution evaluates current data: preview success is not a reservation.

Cascading deletion needs confirmation of each record's impact. Without cascade, `OBJECT_HAS_DEPENDANTS` asks you to inspect that impact. `DELETION_PREVIEW_REQUIRED` needs a preview token; `DELETION_PREVIEW_CHANGED` needs a fresh preview. Confirming a batch preview carries its per-item deletion tokens. Unpreviewed deletes in a sample remain unconfirmed. If an earlier delete in the same job already removed a selected child, its later item is unchanged and identifies that earlier item.

## Retry without duplicating a job

Give a job-creating request an idempotency key and retain the exact request with it. Retrying the same request returns the original job. `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS` means follow that job or wait for the retry interval. `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` means the same key names a different request: correct the error instead of treating it as a replay. Keys expire with job retention, so they are not permanent deduplication identifiers. An unkeyed create without a supplied ID can create a duplicate after a lost response.

## Correct refused data

Missing required values or relationships, unknown or read-only attributes, invalid types, duplicates and numeric bounds need source correction. These include `MISSING_REQUIRED_ATTRIBUTES`, `MISSING_REQUIRED_RELATIONS`, `OBJECT_ATTRIBUTE_RULE_VIOLATION`, `DUPLICATE_ATTRIBUTE`, `DUPLICATE_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE`, `READ_ONLY_ATTRIBUTES`, `UNKNOWN_ATTRIBUTES`, `UNKNOWN_RELATION_ATTRIBUTES`, `INVALID_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE`, `ATTRIBUTE_BELOW_MINIMUM` and `ATTRIBUTE_ABOVE_MAXIMUM`.

For parent changes, `PARENT_REQUIRED`, `PARENT_NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_PARENT_TYPE`, `CHILD_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED` and `PARENT_CYCLE` require an allowed hierarchy. Racing moves cannot create a cycle. `TYPE_CHANGES_NEED_CHANGE_SET` or `CHANGE_SET_REQUIRED` requires preparing the change in a change set; `REQUIRED_RELATION_WITHOUT_PLACE` means the new type cannot preserve required content. `OBJECT_TYPE_UNCHANGED` needs no type change. For [restructuring operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/objects), `RESTRUCTURING_NOT_READY` or `RESTRUCTURING_PLAN_CHANGED` needs a new valid plan; `RESTRUCTURING_TOO_LARGE` and `TOO_MANY_RECORDS` need a supported smaller scope.

## Interpret outcomes and retries

An item reference is 1–200 characters and is echoed with the item’s index. Rejections use the same machine-readable codes as single writes, with a pointer to the failing input. Unprocessed reasons distinguish `BATCH_ROLLED_BACK`, `JOB_CANCELLED`, `MODEL_RELEASE_CHANGED` and `JOB_FAILED`. Treat unknown action or reason values according to their enclosing status. A completed job’s result is `applied`, `partial` or `rejected`; HTTP 200 means the batch was processed, even when none of its items applied. Request-level refusals create no job.

A genuinely unchanged update or upsert takes no version, history entry or feed position, even if its supplied version is stale. For a changing upsert, the default `onExisting` policy rejects an unclaimed overwrite; opt in to overwrite only deliberately. An overwrite outcome reports the previous version and history records that no version was claimed.

Idempotency keys contain 1–200 printable characters and are scoped by route and workspace. Keep the same request with each key: reordering or changing its content can change its fingerprint. A completed replay carries `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; work still running answers `409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS` with job ID and `Retry-After`. A changed request under that key gives `422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. Background replay returns 202 with the job’s current state. Once retention removes a key, submitting it can start new work.

## Resolve references before depending on them

Batch attribute-key references require a unique attribute on the named type, scoped to the workspace. They do not match by display name. Import profiles can match non-unique fields, but must resolve them unambiguously to IDs before the write. Order a parent or relationship endpoint before an item that refers to it. Under independent policy, a failed parent does not skip its child: the child is evaluated and gets its own missing-reference refusal.

An upsert does not change an existing record’s type or application. A key finding the wrong type or application is `REFERENCE_TYPE_MISMATCH`; prepare an intentional type change through the supported change-set workflow instead. Omitting a parent on an upsert keeps the found record where it is.

A retained relationship keeps its ID during set replacement. Omitting its attribute values keeps them; supplying an explicit values object replaces them. An empty target set requests removal of all removable members. A set claim is evaluated after the earlier items in the same batch, so it must describe the state at that point. Containment changes use the record’s parent operation; direct containment relationship items are refused as `IMMUTABLE_RELATION`.

Applied outcomes identify the changed record or relationship and its version. A live deletion has no new entity version. Set replacement reports the set version and created, kept and removed relation IDs; these describe the committed membership, not the item’s source-row identity. Page outcomes through the [job operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/jobs) when the inline response is incomplete.

Batch previews require background execution. They try items independently even for an atomic policy, then roll the preview back as a whole. The job waits for confirmation; execution starts again at the first stored item. Check whether `JOB_PREVIEW_MAX_ITEMS` (default 10,000) made it a sample. Confirmation carries previewed cascade-deletion tokens and relationship-set versions into execution, so changed impacts or memberships are refused rather than silently adopted.

An unpreviewed relationship-set replacement in a sample has no captured set claim and is refused with `VERSION_REQUIRED` unless execution has a valid explicit claim. Do not treat sample counts as confirmation of every destructive item. A versioned ensure-absence checks the relationship found; without a version claim, it removes that mutable relationship as it stands.

## Propose mapping targets into a change set

The [mapping-proposal operation](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/ai) can prepare targets for the unmapped sources of a declared mapping-grid view. This requires a configured provider, Use AI proposals, Work in change sets with permission to write the mapping, and send level `values`. A proposal never writes live data or publishes. Source and target names and displayed fields go to the provider and can incur charges; [About AI](/docs/run/ai/) explains data handling, costs and retained call records.

Select the application and view, optionally narrowed by search and parent, and choose a new change set or an existing open one with its current version. Follow the returned `aiProposal` job. The provider chooses only among eligible targets: all when there are at most 100, otherwise each source's 20 closest by name and fields. A source with no candidate is not sent. Calls normally contain up to 25 sources; `AI_CONTEXT_TOKENS` reduces them to fit half the configured context window. Fields that repeat the name or contain a generated identifier are omitted.

Read the separate result counts. `proposed` counts prepared targets. `unmatched` includes no eligible or sufficiently confident choice; `changed` means the source's mapping set changed meanwhile and was left alone. `refused` counts targets refused by a rule, and `notAnswered` counts missing answers or failed calls. A provider warning does not turn ordinary mapping work into a failure. Cancelling the job keeps proposals already written.

Review the change set before publication. In the browser, **Proposed** lists the marked targets; each **Proposed by the AI** entry gives the confidence and reason. Correct or remove unwanted targets and publish through the normal approval process. Changing a target makes a new relationship without AI origin. Published history preserves the original proposal's origin, with the publisher as actor.

The [mapping-coverage operation](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/mapping) supports `proposed=true` only with `changeSetId`; without it the refusal is `MAPPING_PROPOSED_NEEDS_CHANGE_SET`. `MAPPING_VIEW_NOT_FOUND` needs an available mapping-grid view in the selected model, and `MAPPING_PARENT_NOT_FOUND` needs a parent in the selected context. `CHANGE_SET_VERSION_CONFLICT` requires rereading the open set. `AI_NOT_CONFIGURED` or `AI_SEND_LEVEL_TOO_LOW` requires operator configuration or ordinary manual mapping; an API request cannot override the send ceiling.
guide/src/content/docs/journeys/change-w:
---
title: Change with approval
description: Prepare coordinated changes, review differences, obtain approval and publish safely.
reader: steward
---

Use these journeys when related changes must reach Live together, need review, or depend on a
model release. A change set holds the proposal; a publication preserves the result. Read
[Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) for their states and permissions. Work in change sets,
Publish and Approve publications are separate permissions; a reviewer does not automatically
have permission to decide or publish.

## Prepare and publish a coordinated design

A person preparing changes, or an integrator, starts a change set from current Live data or a
retained publication. Follow [Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/)
to name the proposal, make the ordinary record and relationship changes, review them, and validate
the whole result. Publish when validation, access and approval policy permit it. Then inspect the
new [publication](/docs/use/publications/) and its source.

Staged edits remain invisible to Live readers until publication. Publication applies all proposed
changes together, or none. A failed validation or conflict keeps the proposal for correction.
Installing a model or saving a record inside the proposal does not publish it.

**Example:** a coordinated change can update the validity dates of several stops for a timetable
change. The dates are data; publication is the act that makes the prepared changes live.

## Continue live work while a change set is open

A steward keeps routine corrections moving while colleagues prepare a larger proposal. Read
[how a change set works apart from Live](/docs/use/change-sets/#working-apart-from-live), then
[continue live work](/docs/guide/use/continue-live-work-while-a-change-set-is-open/) in the Live
context. Later publication applies only the proposal's changes: live additions and corrections to
untouched records survive.

If both sides changed the same record, publication stops and names it, even when different fields
were edited. Inspect the live record and the proposal before deciding how to revise the work.
Successful earlier validation does not reserve the live data.

## Withdraw a publication and start reviewed changes from history

A person responsible for publication, or an integrator, begins by
[browsing a publication](/docs/guide/use/browse-a-publication/) as it was saved. If the current
publication should no longer be designated current,
[withdraw it](/docs/guide/use/withdraw-a-publication/). Its snapshot and history remain readable;
Live is unchanged and no older publication becomes current automatically.

Next, [start from an earlier publication](/docs/guide/use/start-from-an-earlier-publication/),
prepare explicit corrections and return to review, validation and publication. Choosing an older
source does not roll back Live. Newer live records that the proposal leaves untouched are kept.
See [Publications](/docs/use/publications/) for the difference between Current, earlier and Withdrawn.

## Review what a change set changes

A reviewer or integrator opens the proposal to understand its effects before deciding.
[Review what a change set changes](/docs/guide/use/review-what-a-change-set-changes/)
connects record changes and relationship changes, their filters and the before-and-after details.
Inspect additions, removals, moves, changed types and fields across the complete lists.

“Before” is the proposal's starting data, including an older publication when that was its source.
The review explains the authored differences; validation and publication also check their combined
effect against current Live. If nothing matches a filter, clear it before assuming the proposal
is empty. Continue to [approval](#propose-and-approve-a-change) or direct publication as permitted.

## Prepare under the next model version while live keeps the current one

A person preparing a proposal works with a model administrator to use a candidate release before
Live switches to it. First [install the release](/docs/model/releases/) without activating it.
Then [prepare under the next model version](/docs/guide/use/prepare-under-the-next-model-version/).
The change set's forms and rules follow that release; Live and other proposals keep theirs.
Starting data must fit the chosen release.

Normal publication needs matching releases. Coordinate activation with the administrator.
If records require conversion, read [Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/): either move the proposal
to the workspace's current release, or review a workspace migration combined with publication.
Each preview changes nothing, lists any losses and blockers, and must be refreshed if stale.
Moving a proposal alone changes no live data. A submitted proposal must leave its waiting state
before editing or changing its release; discarding remains an option for abandoned work.

## Propose and approve a change

A contributor prepares a change set, then submits it to someone allowed to approve publications.
Start with [Propose a change](/docs/guide/use/propose-a-change/), read
[Inbox and approvals](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/), and follow
[Approve a change set](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/) from submission to decision.
Submission validates and freezes the proposed version without changing Live. The approver opens
the notified request, reviews its differences and either approves and publishes or sends it back
with a required comment. The submitter receives the decision and can correct and resubmit returned work.

A workspace's [approval policy](/docs/administer/approval-policies/) determines whether approval
and a second person are required. With a second-person rule, the submitter cannot decide their own
request. To resume editing while waiting, the submitter or an authorised approver withdraws the
request; that keeps the proposed changes. Approval rechecks current data and can still refuse a
conflict. Reload and review the current request before another decision.

## Resume or abandon unfinished work

An open change set remains until published or discarded; job retention does not expire it.
Reopen it, check its context and review its current differences before continuing. Live or model
changes since the last visit can require fresh validation or a migration. See
[Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/).

If the proposal is no longer needed, withdraw a waiting submission before discarding it.
Discarding removes proposed work, while sending it back keeps it available for correction.
Neither undoes Live or removes a publication. After a lost publication response, inspect
publications and history before repeating the request: a consumed change set can mean that
publication succeeded. [Changes, approvals and publication](/docs/integrate/changes-approvals-and-publication/)
explains the corresponding integration recovery.
guide/src/content/docs/journeys/index.md:
---
title: All user journeys
slug: journeys/index
description: Find a complete path through refiroo for data work, model design, access, integration and operations.
reader: evaluator
---

Choose the outcome you want, then follow its journey to the explanations and task guides in the
order you need them. A journey connects the whole task; the linked guides give the detailed steps.

The journeys cover people looking after data, model and access administrators, operators and
systems using the API. Permission and deployment settings determine which actions are available.
Applications and record types come from each workspace's model. Public transport stops, names and
codes from Graubünden are marked examples, rather than fixed applications everyone must use.

## Look after data

Find, maintain and connect records in the workspace you are working in. See [look after data](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/) for the complete paths.

- [Start from home](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#start-from-home).
- [Find and inspect a record](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#find-and-inspect-a-record).
- [Correct a record](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#correct-a-record).
- [Add a record where it belongs](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#add-a-record-where-it-belongs).
- [Delete a record and what depends on it](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#delete-a-record-and-what-depends-on-it).

- [Review and replace a record's related records](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#review-and-replace-a-records-related-records).
- [See and fill relationship coverage across ancestors](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#see-and-fill-relationship-coverage-across-ancestors).
- [Change many records of a collection at once](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#change-many-records-of-a-collection-at-once).

- [Copy or move records to another workspace](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#copy-or-move-records-to-another-workspace).
- [Continue in a retired or unavailable workspace](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#continue-in-a-retired-or-unavailable-workspace).
- [Adjust the display and work with a keyboard](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#adjust-the-display-and-work-with-a-keyboard).

## Change with approval

Prepare coordinated proposals, review them and bring them into Live safely. See [change with approval](/docs/journeys/change-with-approval/) for the complete paths.

- [Prepare and publish a coordinated design](/docs/journeys/change-with-approval/#prepare-and-publish-a-coordinated-design).
- [Continue live work while a change set is open](/docs/journeys/change-with-approval/#continue-live-work-while-a-change-set-is-open).
- [Withdraw a publication and start reviewed changes from history](/docs/journeys/change-with-approval/#withdraw-a-publication-and-start-reviewed-changes-from-history).
- [Review what a change set changes](/docs/journeys/change-with-approval/#review-what-a-change-set-changes).
- [Prepare under the next model version while live keeps the current one](/docs/journeys/change-with-approval/#prepare-under-the-next-model-version-while-live-keeps-the-current-one).
- [Propose and approve a change](/docs/journeys/change-with-approval/#propose-and-approve-a-change).
- [Resume or abandon unfinished work](/docs/journeys/change-with-approval/#resume-or-abandon-unfinished-work).

## Work with an assistant

Review machine-made proposals and keep control of what changes. See [work with an assistant](/docs/journeys/work-with-an-assistant/) for access, disclosure, costs, retention and review.

- [Use AI proposals](/docs/journeys/work-with-an-assistant/#use-ai-proposals).

- [What changed in a period](/docs/journeys/work-with-an-assistant/#what-changed-in-a-period).

## Shape a model

Define applications and data rules, load workbooks and manage workspace releases. See [shape a model](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/) for the complete paths.

- [Load the next version of a workbook](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#load-the-next-version-of-a-workbook).

- [Move data between workspaces whose models differ](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#move-data-between-workspaces-whose-models-differ).
- [An account of a model change](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#an-account-of-a-model-change).

- [Recheck a workbook design or a saved mapping](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#recheck-a-workbook-design-or-a-saved-mapping).
- [Maintain released contracts and definitions](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#maintain-released-contracts-and-definitions).

## Integrate a system

Connect another system through complete reads, controlled writes and reliable change delivery. See [integrate a system](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/) for the complete paths.

- [Discover the model and the API](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#discover-the-model-and-the-api).
- [Read a collection completely and resume](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#read-a-collection-completely-and-resume).
- [Request the precise dataset an integration needs](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#request-the-precise-dataset-an-integration-needs).
- [Answer a business-date question](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#answer-a-business-date-question).
- [Submit a bounded bulk change](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#submit-a-bounded-bulk-change).

- [Follow changes reliably](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#follow-changes-reliably).
- [Exchange a supplier file](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#exchange-a-supplier-file).
- [Read a business object through a consumer API](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#read-a-business-object-through-a-consumer-api).
- [Resolve a business object through a consumer API](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#resolve-a-business-object-through-a-consumer-api).
- [Follow a consumer API's changes](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#follow-a-consumer-apis-changes).
- [Automate a reviewed change and its approval handover](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#automate-a-reviewed-change-and-its-approval-handover).
- [Administer models and transfer records through the API](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#administer-models-and-transfer-records-through-the-api).
- [Submit an assistant task from an integration](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#submit-an-assistant-task-from-an-integration).

## Manage access

Sign in, grant people and systems access, and review its security. See [manage access](/docs/journeys/manage-access/) for the complete paths.

- [Sign in and work](/docs/journeys/manage-access/#sign-in-and-work).
- [Manage who can do what](/docs/journeys/manage-access/#manage-who-can-do-what).
- [A system calls with a client](/docs/journeys/manage-access/#a-system-calls-with-a-client).
- [Rotate a key](/docs/journeys/manage-access/#rotate-a-key).
- [Check the security model](/docs/journeys/manage-access/#check-the-security-model).
- [Move people to the organisation's sign-in provider](/docs/journeys/manage-access/#move-people-to-the-organisations-sign-in-provider).
- [Tailor a responsibility and remove access when it ends](/docs/journeys/manage-access/#tailor-a-responsibility-and-remove-access-when-it-ends).
- [Configure publication review and system delivery](/docs/journeys/manage-access/#configure-publication-review-and-system-delivery).
- [Control assistant access and inspect AI use](/docs/journeys/manage-access/#control-assistant-access-and-inspect-ai-use).

## Run the service

Start, inspect and recover the deployment. See [run the service](/docs/journeys/run-the-service/) for the complete paths.

- [Run the service, and recover from an expected refusal](/docs/journeys/run-the-service/#run-the-service-and-recover-from-an-expected-refusal).
- [Check what a deployment runs and how it is configured](/docs/journeys/run-the-service/#check-what-a-deployment-runs-and-how-it-is-configured).
- [Open a production installation over HTTPS](/docs/journeys/run-the-service/#open-a-production-installation-over-https).
- [Upgrade and recover a failed cutover](/docs/journeys/run-the-service/#upgrade-and-recover-a-failed-cutover).
- [Back up, rehearse and move to another host](/docs/journeys/run-the-service/#back-up-rehearse-and-move-to-another-host).
- [Replace secrets and watch growing storage](/docs/journeys/run-the-service/#replace-secrets-and-watch-growing-storage).
- [Enable optional AI or prepare a developer instance](/docs/journeys/run-the-service/#enable-optional-ai-or-prepare-a-developer-instance).

## Receive notices

Set up mail and choose how to hear about work and publications. See [receive notices](/docs/journeys/receive-notices/) for the complete paths.

- [Send mail](/docs/journeys/receive-notices/#send-mail).
- [Notification digests and following a workspace](/docs/journeys/receive-notices/#notification-digests-and-following-a-workspace).

If you are new to refiroo, start with [What is refiroo?](/docs/about/what-is-refiroo/) and
[How it works](/docs/about/how-it-works/), then choose a journey above.
guide/src/content/docs/journeys/integrat:
---
title: Integrate a system
description: Discover contracts, read complete datasets, submit changes and follow events reliably.
reader: integrator
---

These journeys connect an integration's first contract read to ongoing synchronisation and
recovery. Use the management API to work with the model and records, or a model-declared consumer
API to read business objects. Start with [the integration overview](/docs/integrate/overview/)
and [signing in and tokens](/docs/integrate/signing-in-and-tokens/). Roles and consumer API grants
are separate; a token must also be intended for the API it calls.

The linked documentation explains sequences. Use the [API reference](/docs/api) for management
operations and their exact inputs and responses. Consumer API shapes depend on the model and are
explained with examples in [Consumer APIs](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/).

## Discover the model and the API

An integrator first checks what the deployment enables, its limits, and the workspace and model
release to use. [Discovering the model](/docs/integrate/discovering-the-model/) connects these
reads to types, attributes, relationships and permitted placements. Choose the data context before
reading metadata: a change set or publication can use a different release from Live.

Next open the [API reference documentation](/docs/integrate/api-reference/) and the
[management operations](/docs/api). Discover consumer APIs and their own generated contracts
rather than assuming all models expose the same paths. Stable public keys and record IDs identify
resources. If a model cannot be served, resolve the named workspace's problem instead of substituting
another workspace's definitions.

## Read a collection completely and resume

An integrator reads a bounded first page, processes it and follows the returned cursor until the
end. [Identifiers, paging and errors](/docs/integrate/identifiers-paging-and-errors/) explains
page positions, totals, reverse traversal and seeking where supported.
[Read a collection completely and resume](/docs/guide/integrate/read-a-collection-completely-and-resume/)
connects processing to saving a continuation point and restarting the same query.

Keep the query, workspace and context with that continuation. Reusing a cursor for a different
read is refused; do not construct or edit one. A page maximum is a page limit, not a limit on the
whole collection. A live traversal is not a frozen extract: choose a retained publication when the
integration needs a fixed snapshot. Browser readers can
[continue a long list](/docs/guide/use/continue-a-long-list/) through scrolling and position controls.

## Request the precise dataset an integration needs

An integrator selects types and a data context, combines typed field filters with hierarchy and
relationship criteria, chooses returned fields and related data, then pages the result.
[Reading records](/docs/integrate/reading-records/) explains the choices and links to the
[query operations](/docs/api). Use type-specific reads for model-declared fields; the cross-type
lookup serves the common fields it supports. A workspace relationship list answers questions
about connections rather than just records.

An invalid filter or sort is a refusal, rather than permission to return a broader dataset.
Correct the named criterion and restart with cursors for that query.

**Example:** read stops below chosen municipalities and include connected operators. Those types
and fields belong to the example model; the querying capability works over the selected model.

## Answer a business-date question

An integrator asks which records apply on a calendar date using a model-declared validity period.
[Business dates](/docs/integrate/business-dates/) explains inclusive starts, exclusive ends and
open boundaries. [Read as of a date](/docs/guide/integrate/read-as-of-a-date/) carries the date
through every page in the chosen live or published data.

A business date does not reconstruct an old database state or date every related record in a
projection. Check which types the answer actually dates. A type without a configured period cannot
answer a dated object or list read; mixed supported consumer lookups identify which types were
dated. Use a publication when you need a saved snapshot rather than validity on a date.

## Submit a bounded bulk change

An integrator sends a bounded group of record and relationship changes as one batch.
[Writing in bulk](/docs/integrate/writing-in-bulk/) leads to
[Submit a bulk change](/docs/guide/integrate/submit-a-bulk-change/) and the
[batch operations](/docs/api). Choose atomic execution for everything or nothing, or independent
execution when other items may succeed despite a refused item. Reference existing records by
ID or unique key and inspect each item's result before retrying.

Reuse the same idempotency key only for the same request: replay returns its original outcome;
changing the request under that key is refused. The ordinary model and version rules apply to
every item. Previewing a batch requires a background job; use the
[large-job journey](#run-a-large-background-job-and-recover) for work beyond inline limits.

## Run a large background job and recover

An integrator or exchange operator submits background work, keeps the returned job identity,
follows progress and reads item outcomes as execution advances.
[Jobs](/docs/integrate/jobs/) connects submission to completion, cancellation and recovery;
[Follow and cancel a job](/docs/guide/use/follow-and-cancel-a-job/) gives the browser view.
A preview can wait for explicit confirmation without having written the proposed changes.

After interruption, a worker resumes at the first unfinished item. Cancellation or failure of
independent work can leave committed chunks; atomic work rolls back together. A model, workspace,
permission or change-set change can stop work before the next chunk. Read the reason and applied
outcomes before resubmitting. Retention can remove detailed item results while keeping a summary,
so collect outcomes while they are available. Operators use
[Background jobs](/docs/run/background-jobs/) for worker recovery.

## Follow changes reliably

An integrator keeps another system current by processing a workspace's ordered change feed and
saving the last safely processed position. Read [Following changes](/docs/integrate/following-changes/),
then [load, then follow changes](/docs/guide/integrate/load-then-follow-changes/) to connect an
initial publication or consistent export with later changes. Feed entries identify changes and
their causes; they do not contain field values. Read records when the integration needs values.

Recognise replay by position and save progress only after processing succeeds. Keep following
continuation even through an empty filtered page until caught up. Unpublished edits and refused
writes do not appear. An expired position needs a fresh baseline and continuation from its stated
position; an ahead-of-head position needs investigation, including whether the wrong workspace
or a restored database was used. Do not silently skip to the current head.

## Exchange a supplier file

An exchange operator, steward or integrator identifies the destination, file layout and mapping,
then previews additions, updates and refused cells without changing data.
[Files, imports and exports](/docs/integrate/files-imports-and-exports/) leads to
[Exchange a supplier file](/docs/guide/integrate/exchange-a-supplier-file/) and its
[import and export operations](/docs/api). Browser workers can instead
[import a file](/docs/guide/use/import-a-file/) or
[export records](/docs/guide/use/export-records/). Choose the failure policy and inspect whether
the preview covered all execution items or only a sample before confirmation.

Read each applied or refused outcome, correct rejected rows and retry without duplicating applied
work. A changed profile, model or change set can require another preview. For a workbook intended
for people to edit, [edit in Excel and import back](/docs/guide/use/edit-in-excel-and-import-back/)
uses the carried mapping and versions; stale records are refused. A failed, cancelled or expired
export does not provide a partial download. Check a successful export's scope and position before
using it as a synchronisation baseline.

**Example:** exchange a workbook of stops and codes from other systems. The file's destination and
mapping determine what it changes; a similar column label does not establish identity.

## Read a business object through a consumer API

A consuming system discovers a declared contract and reads an object by its stable ID, or pages
a declared list. Start with [Consumer APIs](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/) and
[Reading business objects](/docs/integrate/reading-business-objects/), then
[read through a consumer API](/docs/guide/integrate/read-through-a-consumer-api/).
Declared parameters can narrow objects or their related blocks. The same object shape is used
across the contract's reads.

Live reads include saved live corrections, never unpublished proposals. Choose a publication for
a repeatable extract; its continuation stays with the starting snapshot even if a newer one
becomes current. An unsupported operation, wrong contract version or another workspace's record
is refused. Use the model's current contract documentation rather than guessing another path.

**Example:** the reference stops API combines a stop's fields with its names and external codes.
Those outputs are a declaration, not a fixed feature every model must expose.

## Resolve a business object through a consumer API

A consuming system starts with a code, name, ID or related value instead of a known record ID.
[Looking up and resolving](/docs/integrate/looking-up-and-resolving/) explains matching, scores,
ambiguity and translating into a target representation. [Resolve a file of codes](/docs/guide/integrate/resolve-a-file-of-codes/)
connects lookup to batch resolution and per-item found, missing, ambiguous or rejected outcomes.

Narrow ambiguous results using the definition's parameters; never pick an arbitrary tied match.
A unique best object can still have a missing or ambiguous target representation. Review those
separate outcomes before accepting a crosswalk. Use a publication to resolve the whole file
against a fixed dataset. The consumer documentation gives the contract-specific requests and
responses, including limits; broad or oversized lookups must be narrowed or divided.

## Follow a consumer API's changes

An integrator loads a publication, then follows the declared consumer events from its position.
[Consumer events and webhooks](/docs/integrate/consumer-events-and-webhooks/) connects full or
identity-only events, cursors, duplicate recognition and recovery after expiry. Process every
event at a position and keep its continuation; several events can share one raw change position.
Recognise repeated events by their event identity.

For pushed delivery, an authorised administrator [creates a webhook](/docs/guide/administer/create-a-webhook/)
and the integration [subscribes and verifies it](/docs/guide/integrate/subscribe-a-webhook-and-verify-it/).
Verify the signed request, process it safely and acknowledge successful receipt. Failures are
retried before later deliveries; inspect [webhook deliveries](/docs/administer/webhooks/) when
recovery is needed. Changed models, expired events or prolonged failures can suspend a subscription.
A reset skips missed events, so restore a baseline before treating the receiver as current.

Filters can hide the change by which an object leaves their scope. If your copy must remove such
objects, follow the necessary type-wide events and apply narrower criteria locally. This matters
for pull reads and webhook subscriptions alike.

## Automate a reviewed change and its approval handover

[Changes, approvals and publication](/docs/integrate/changes-approvals-and-publication/)
connects capture of an explicit base, versioned writes, complete validation and submission.
Present the differences and diagnostics to a person who may decide under the current policy.
Submission changes no Live data; approval publishes the reviewed version and can still refuse
competing live changes. Keep publication identity and feed position after success.

An open set is not a job that expires under item-result retention. To abandon it, withdraw a
submission where necessary and discard its prepared work. After losing a publication response,
read publication and change-set state before retrying. A consumed proposal can mean success.
Use approval events or inbox operations for review notifications; these are separate from the
data feed used for synchronisation. The page links to each [management operation](/docs/api).

## Administer models and transfer records through the API

[Model and release operations](/docs/integrate/model-and-release-operations/) connects draft
steps, validation, generated documents, installation and activation. Keep the model release
and record versions explicit. A data conversion needs a fresh migration preview with blockers
and losses presented for a person's confirmation; installing alone does not activate.

[Move records between models](/docs/guide/integrate/move-records-between-models/) follows a
saved mapping through selection, complete dry run and loading into change sets. Review omitted
values and dropped relationships as well as successful records. A move needs publication of
the target before source deletions. Changed releases or mappings invalidate an old review.
Use the linked [model operations](/docs/api) rather than editing stored definitions directly.

## Submit an assistant task from an integration

[Assistant tasks](/docs/integrate/assistant-tasks/) explains submitting instructions or a file,
following work, displaying checked changes and accepting a reviewed proposal. The requester
needs **Use AI proposals**, **Bulk and import**, and the permissions for model or change-set
work. This needs the built-in assistant and permission to send values, separately from an
external MCP connection.

Keep the task and job identities. Read current state before every action; distinguish a checked
proposal, a loaded change set and a migration requiring human confirmation. Session work cannot
approve, publish or activate. A matching saved-layout path can activate a draft with the right
permission, so show the actual path and result. Stopping, correcting or discarding can remove
an unpublished result and people's subsequent edits; show that consequence before acting.
Read its data, cost and retention rules, and link users to
[Work with an assistant](/docs/journeys/work-with-an-assistant/) for review and recovery.
guide/src/content/docs/journeys/look-aft:
---
title: Look after data
description: Find, correct and connect records, maintain hierarchies and review data history.
reader: steward
---

These journeys connect everyday data work, from opening a workspace to checking the history of a
saved change. Start with the task you need. The linked pages explain the rules and the guides give
the screen-by-screen steps. Your workspace's model determines the applications, record types and
views available.

Reading needs Browse access. Live changes need Edit live; proposed changes need Work in change
sets. Publications are read-only, and retired workspaces refuse changes. See
[record permissions](/docs/use/records/#who-may-read-and-change-records) before starting.

## Start from home

Anyone returning to refiroo can use [Home](/docs/use/home/) to find accessible workspaces,
continue a recent visit, open a proposal or review a request awaiting approval. Choose the
workspace and then [open an application](/docs/guide/use/open-an-application/). Check the workspace
and data context on arrival before changing anything. If there are no workspaces to open, ask an
administrator for Browse access; signing in alone does not grant it.

## Find and inspect a record

A steward or integrator starts by choosing the workspace and the data to read: Live, a change set
or a publication. [Workspaces](/docs/use/workspaces/) and [applications](/docs/use/applications/)
explain that choice. [Find records](/docs/guide/use/find-records/) then connects search, filters
and sorting to the record's fields, hierarchy path, related records and history. Returning to the
list keeps its search and position. An empty relationship list means there are no matching
connections; a failed read needs a retry before drawing that conclusion.

An integrator can follow [reading records](/docs/integrate/reading-records/) for the corresponding
reads, including typed filters and related fields. Zero and No remain values in both channels.

## Correct a record

A steward or integrator corrects a name or field while keeping the record's identity, place and
relationships. Read [Records](/docs/use/records/), then [correct a record](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/)
in the intended context and check its saved values and history. A routine Live correction needs
no change set; a correction made within an open change set stays there until publication.

If another person saves first, review the current record and your attempted value before retrying.
Required, read-only, unique and range rules still apply. Integrators use
[versions and conflicts](/docs/integrate/versions-and-conflicts/) to protect the same save.

## Add a record where it belongs

A steward or integrator starts from a collection, a parent, or the record that must own the new
record. [Add a record](/docs/guide/use/add-a-record/) brings together its name, typed fields,
allowed parent and required relationships in one save. [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/)
explains ownership, including an owner in another application. If a required choice is missing
or a value is already taken, correct it before saving again: no incomplete record is created.
A record created in a change set is not visible in Live until publication.

## Delete a record and what depends on it

A steward or integrator who needs permanent removal first reads the
[deletion rules](/docs/use/records/#deleting-a-record), then
[deletes a record](/docs/guide/use/delete-a-record/) after reviewing its impact. Descendants and
owned dependants go with it, including dependants in other applications; independent records
survive the removal of their connections. Cancelling changes nothing. If the impact changes,
obtain a fresh preview and review it again. Existing publications keep their snapshots.

## Relate records and maintain their relationships

A steward or integrator uses [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/) to understand the connection
and its meaning in each direction, then [relates records](/docs/guide/use/relate-records/).
Choose an eligible candidate, save the connection and, where allowed, edit its fields or remove
it later. Connections can cross applications within the workspace. The model controls candidates,
required connections and how many are allowed. Move a record through its parent to change
containment; do not try to remove its parent relationship here.

## Build and change a hierarchy

A steward or integrator finds a branch, adds children and moves records to permitted parents.
[Hierarchies](/docs/use/hierarchies/) explains placement; [arrange records in a tree](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/)
and [move several records together](/docs/guide/use/move-several-records-together/) take the work
through confirmation to the new paths. Descendants and relationships travel with the moved record.
A move into its own subtree, or one breaking a relationship rule, is refused. A refused multi-record
move moves none of the selection. Review the named record and choose a permitted destination.

## Reshape a hierarchy across types, and change a record back

A steward or integrator makes structural changes in a change set when a move also changes record
types, inserts a level or removes one. [Reshape a hierarchy](/docs/guide/use/reshape-a-hierarchy/)
connects choosing the operation to reviewing the proposed types, values, relationships and missing
information. Apply only after resolving the plan's questions, then
[review and publish](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/). IDs and history survive.
Content without a place in the new type is retained in history and can be offered when changing
back. If the data changes after preview, preview again before applying.

## Review and replace a record's related records

A steward or integrator reviews which sources have no, one or several connections, then chooses
the set they should have. Start with [mapping grids](/docs/use/mapping-grids/), then
[replace a record's related records](/docs/guide/use/replace-a-records-related-records/).
A replacement saves together; retained connections keep their identity and values. Clearing is
available only where the rules permit it. If the set changed meanwhile, review the current
connections alongside your preserved choice before trying again. Publications allow inspection only.

**Example:** codes from another system can be connected to the stops they identify. The codes,
stops and connection rules come from the example model; the same journey works with other types.

## See and fill relationship coverage across ancestors

A steward or integrator uses a model-declared [relation matrix](/docs/use/relation-matrices/)
to compare row records with columns above their related records in a hierarchy. Start by
[filtering and filling the matrix](/docs/guide/use/fill-in-a-relation-matrix/): inspect missing,
filled, inactive or conflicting cells, then create a related record or link an eligible existing
one where offered. The state filter covers every matching row, beyond those currently visible.
An inactive cell may already contain a record that needs correction. Removing a connection cannot
leave an owned record without its required owner. Review staged work before publication.

**Example:** a matrix can compare stops with languages, showing each stop's names under a language.
The model supplies the row types, columns and rules for which names count.

## Change many records of a collection at once

A steward uses [changing many records](/docs/use/changing-many-records/) to select explicit rows or
all records matching a search and its filters. Continue with the guide for
[values](/docs/guide/use/change-values-of-many-records/),
[relationships](/docs/guide/use/change-relationships-of-many-records/) or
[deletion](/docs/guide/use/delete-many-records/), then inspect the preview and each job outcome.
Choose whether the change must succeed together or may apply to records that can change.
A deletion's total can include descendants and owned records beyond the selection.

A new search, filter, scope or context clears the selection; scrolling and sorting keep it.
Publications do not offer selection for writes, and bulk work requires jobs to be enabled.
If a preview is stale or exceeds a deployment limit, refresh it or narrow the selection.
[Follow the job](/docs/guide/use/follow-and-cancel-a-job/) to distinguish refused items from saved ones.

## See who changed what

A steward, model administrator, access administrator or integrator starts with the question:
one record, activity across a workspace, or a person's actions. [History](/docs/use/history/)
and [See who changed what](/docs/guide/use/see-who-changed-what/) connect the question to filters
and recorded before-and-after values. These reads respect access and do not undo changes.
For sign-in, access or administration events, continue to [Audit](/docs/administer/audit/)
and [find who changed something](/docs/guide/administer/find-who-changed-something/).
An empty filtered result calls for widening the filters, rather than assuming nothing changed.

## Stop offering a value without deleting it

Read [Records](/docs/use/records/#validity-periods), then
[stop offering a value](/docs/guide/use/stop-offering-a-value/) through the model's availability
field or validity dates. Keep its identity for older references and check the saved value and
history. A validity end is the first day excluded. Neither choice deletes the record, schedules
publication or guarantees every consuming system filters it out. If the type declares neither
mechanism, ask the model administrator rather than deleting it to hide it.

## Exchange a workbook and repeat the load

A steward with **Bulk and import** starts with [Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/).
[Export records](/docs/guide/use/export-records/) for an extract, or
[edit in Excel and import back](/docs/guide/use/edit-in-excel-and-import-back/) when people need
to return corrections with their record identities and versions. To add related owned records
as columns, follow [Add a language with a workbook](/docs/guide/use/add-a-language-with-a-workbook/);
its ownership and parent choices apply beyond languages.

For a supplier layout, [import a file](/docs/guide/use/import-a-file/) through the agreed profile,
inspect its preview and choose whether the work must succeed together. Read saved and refused
outcomes; a cancelled independent job can already have saved work. Use
[Load the next version of a workbook](/docs/guide/use/load-the-next-version-of-a-workbook/) to
review layout changes and reuse the profile. Missing rows stay unless deletion is explicitly
configured. Review the resulting change set before publishing. Ask a model administrator about
an invalid profile binding instead of bypassing the check.

## Copy or move records to another workspace

A steward begins with [Copying and moving](/docs/use/copying-and-moving/) and an agreed model
mapping, then [copies or moves records](/docs/guide/use/copy-or-move-records/). Read access to
the source and **Copy and move** for the destination are required; a move also needs
**Work in change sets** in the source. Check scope, omissions, losses and the complete dry run
before starting. Review actual results even when the preview passed.

Publish the target proposal first, then review and separately publish source deletions for a
move. Records changed meanwhile or needed by records staying behind can be kept with reasons.
A failure needs inspection of the job and retained proposals before repeating it. Discard an
unwanted proposal before publication; deleting the mapping does not undo a published transfer.

## Continue in a retired or unavailable workspace

[Switch workspace](/docs/guide/use/switch-workspace/) when the data or model you need lives
elsewhere. [Open a retired or unavailable workspace](/docs/guide/use/open-a-retired-or-unavailable-workspace/)
distinguishes readable retired data from a model that cannot be served. Read the displayed
reason and give it to the model administrator or operator. Missing Browse access requires a
grant; an unsupported model needs model recovery. Choosing another workspace never moves data.

## Adjust the display and work with a keyboard

Follow [Change how refiroo looks](/docs/guide/use/change-how-refiroo-looks/) for this browser's
colour, light or dark, density and edit-hint choices. [Appearance and devices](/docs/use/appearance-and-devices/)
explains keyboard operation, resizable panels and phone navigation. Changes are immediate and
do not affect colleagues' settings or records. For a long collection,
[continue a long list](/docs/guide/use/continue-a-long-list/) with scrolling or a position jump;
use its search rather than the browser's Find to reach records not currently drawn.
guide/src/content/docs/journeys/manage-a:
---
title: Manage access
description: Connect sign-in, people, roles, system clients, key rotation and security review.
reader: access-admin
---

These journeys connect getting into refiroo with granting and reviewing access. People and
systems need permission for the work they do, in the workspace where they do it. An administrative
role does not automatically grant access to reference data. Start with
[People and access](/docs/about/people-and-access/) for the distinction between roles and grants.

## Sign in and work

A person opens refiroo, signs in by an offered method and returns to the page they wanted.
[Sign-in](/docs/administer/sign-in/) explains local passwords, an organisation's provider, passkeys
and second factors. [Account](/docs/use/account/) connects personal security settings, password
changes and sessions. Use the account menu to sign out when finished, or end other sessions from
your account when needed.

Repeated failed sign-ins are slowed. If a required second factor is unavailable, use a saved
recovery code or ask an administrator to
[help after a lost device](/docs/guide/administer/help-someone-who-lost-a-device/).
Where mail is configured, a forgotten-password request can provide a fresh one-use link; a reset
does not remove the second factor. If sign-in succeeds but no workspace opens, ask for Browse
access rather than resetting the password again.

## Manage who can do what

A security administrator [adds a person](/docs/guide/administer/add-a-person/), who sets their
password through the one-use link, or arranges the organisation's provider sign-in.
Next read [Roles and grants](/docs/administer/roles-and-grants/) and
[grant a role](/docs/guide/administer/grant-a-role/) directly or through a
[group](/docs/guide/administer/manage-a-group/). Choose the workspace and, when appropriate,
[narrow writes to record types](/docs/guide/administer/narrow-a-grant-to-record-types/).
Browse covers the workspace; narrowing writes does not hide other records there.

Review effective access, including grants inherited through groups and from the installation.
A Reader reads but cannot write; a Contributor proposes changes in change sets. Grants and
activation state take effect on the next request, and jobs recheck their requester's permissions.
The last security administrator cannot be removed. Use [Audit](/docs/administer/audit/) to check
who changed access and investigate a refusal against the action and workspace it names.

## A system calls with a client

An integration team asks a security administrator to create a separate identity for its system.
Read [Clients](/docs/administer/clients/), then
[create a client](/docs/guide/administer/create-a-client/) and save its secret when it is shown
once. Give it management roles for the work it must perform, or
[grant a consumer API](/docs/guide/administer/grant-a-consumer-api-to-a-client/) in the intended
workspace. One kind of grant does not imply the other.

The integrator then follows [system sign-in](/docs/integrate/signing-in-and-tokens/) and
[obtain system access](/docs/guide/integrate/get-a-token/) to connect the system under those grants.
Check allowed work and refused work before relying on it. Later,
[rotate the client secret](/docs/guide/administer/rotate-a-client-secret/) with an overlap when
needed, or deactivate the client to end its access. A deactivated client cannot keep working
with previously issued access. Keep a client separate from a person's browser account so its
activity and grants remain identifiable.

## Rotate a key

A security or integration administrator first identifies which credential needs replacement.
[Signing keys](/docs/administer/signing-keys/) explains ordinary replacement and emergency
retirement; [Rotate signing keys](/docs/guide/administer/rotate-signing-keys/) carries the chosen
action through verification. Normal replacement preserves existing access until expiry.
Emergency retirement ends access signed with the retired key immediately; browser sessions renew
and integrations must obtain fresh access.

For a delivery-signing key, [rotate a webhook key](/docs/guide/administer/rotate-a-webhook-key/)
