guide/src/content/docs/model/model-mappi:
---
title: Model mappings
description: Map records between different workspace models, inspect losses and review the resulting change sets.
reader: model-admin
---

Use **Settings**, **Copy and move** when records need to go into a workspace whose model differs.
A model mapping says what each source type, field, parent and relationship becomes in the target.
It does not change either model. Follow
[Move records to another model](/docs/guide/model/move-records-to-another-model/).

This is different from a mapping grid: a grid relates records within a model; a model mapping
translates records between models. The source and target must be different workspaces.

## Proposals need your decision

Choose an existing mapping for the two models or ask for **A new mapping, proposed**. The engine
uses the models and shared record values to suggest matches. The editor shows source types on the
left, mapping choices in the centre and target types on the right. A saved mapping can be reused;
opening it does not copy records.

![Mapping editor with proposed type and field choices and a dry run summary](/docs/screens/model-mapping-proposed.png)

*Above: Guide mapping proposes Operators to Domains and Modes to Codelists between Graubünden and
Default. Those are suggestions to review, not a recommendation to use this mapping.*

**Proposed** means the choice is still the engine's suggestion. Select a row for **Why this step**
and read the supporting evidence. Alternatives offer other choices. A similarity
in fields or values does not prove the types mean the same thing.

![Selected mapping row with the proposal reason and alternative target types](/docs/screens/model-mapping-why.png)

*Above: Operator code is selected; alternatives change what Operator becomes in the target.*

![Proposal evidence expanded beside the selected mapping row](/docs/screens/model-mapping-evidence.png)

*Above: the evidence reports one of two fields shared, with values that convert. This observation
alone does not establish that an operator should become a domain.*

Edit a row's choice to make it yours. Review fields that are not carried, parent placement,
relationships and **Records already in the target**, not just the type names. Matching by a unique
field can find an existing target record; matching only records moved before is narrower. Records
found again are updated rather than duplicated. **Undo** and **Redo** revisit saved mapping steps.

## Choose records and inspect losses

**What to copy** or **What to move** offers every mapped type, the whole workspace, chosen types
with optional filters, or one record and everything under it. Unmapped types in a whole-workspace
selection are reported as left out. A subtree includes its contained descendants.

The dry run checks the selection without writing records. Review creates, updates, refused
records, carried relationships and dropped relationships. Open **What cannot be copied** or
**What cannot move** for each reason and its items. An unmapped field may lose its value even
when its record can be copied. A relationship can be carried only when its ends can be resolved
in the target; otherwise it is reported as dropped.

Correct a required value through a suitable mapping or default, place children under an allowed
parent, and map relationships you intend to keep. Do not add arbitrary defaults solely to make
a rejection disappear. A partial result needs a deliberate decision about what stays behind.
[Issues and dry runs](/docs/model/issues-and-dry-run/) explains the figures.

## Copy and move reach live data through review

**Copy** prepares a new change set in the target. Source records remain in place.
**Move** also prepares a deletion change set in the source. Review and publish the target copy
first, then review and publish the source deletions separately. The source deletion cannot be
published before its target copy. Records changed since the dry run, or needed by records staying
behind, are kept rather than silently deleted.

Starting the operation does not publish either change set. Review the actual job result as well
as the earlier prediction. A newer mapping version or changed model can invalidate confirmation;
refresh and review a new dry run before retrying. A selection with nothing eligible cannot start.

The **Mappings** list keeps reusable mappings. **Recent copies and moves** lists operations and
dry runs waiting to start; a dry run replaced by a later editor step is not listed.

## Access and availability

Copying and moving needs **Copy and move** access in the relevant workspaces. Reading records,
preparing change sets and publishing them require the corresponding workspace permissions too;
being a model author alone does not grant data publication rights. Ask an access administrator
when a step is refused. This flow also needs background jobs and model administration enabled
on the instance. When unavailable, the page explains why.

## Editor tabs and the running job

**Settings › Workspaces and models › Copy and move** lists saved Mappings with their source and target
models, version and updated time. **Recent copies and moves** lists workspace pairs, Copy or Move,
state, change sets and creation time. **Load more mappings** reads older mappings.

The editor uses **Mapping**, **Source**, **Target** and **Not copied** or **Not moved** tabs,
particularly on a phone. **Why this step** explains a proposed row with evidence and alternatives;
it shows no match score. If **The mapping names other releases than the workspaces run** appears,
choose **Use the releases the workspaces run**, inspect the affected rows and run the dry run
again before starting. Read **Copying and moving are read-only here** or **This editor reads
only** as a deployment restriction; ask the operator about model administration and jobs.

After starting, inspect the job's actual creates, updates, omissions and refusals and the links
to the produced change sets. Its result counts can differ from the dry run after intervening
changes. A completed job is not publication: review and publish the target proposal first and,
for a move, the source deletion proposal afterwards.

## Focused tasks and results

[Edit a mapping row](/docs/guide/model/edit-a-mapping-row/) covers targets, defaults and evidence.
[Choose what moves](/docs/guide/model/choose-what-moves/) covers selection and the loss report.

After completion, **Review the change set** opens the target changes and **Review the deletions**
opens the source deletion proposal for a move. Inspect deleted and kept counts and each reason.
**The copy did not complete** or **The move did not complete** means no publication happened;
inspect the job and any produced change sets before starting again. **Nothing to copy** or
**Nothing to move** needs a broader eligible mapping or selection, not repeated confirmation.
A running operation continues when you leave its page.

The job's result lists actual created, updated, refused or kept items and lost values or
relationships. **Items that cannot …** groups reasons; **No item has this reason any more**
means the current report no longer contains that group. **Values not carried** lists the type,
field, record count and reason. A report counts records, relationships and values separately.

Previously copied or moved records retain their correspondence between workspaces. Moving them
back can update their original counterparts rather than inventing duplicates; inspect the target
matching rule and dry run. This is different from splitting a model definition in a draft.
The browser mapping editor offers the rows described here; specialist mapping transformations
beyond those controls need an integrator. Release comparisons show relationships and views,
not changes to these separately saved model mappings.

## Delete a saved mapping

In **Mappings**, **Delete…** is shown to people with **Copy and move** access. The confirmation
is **Delete the mapping …?**. **Delete the mapping** removes the mapping together with its
history and proposals. **Cancel** keeps it. Copies and moves already made stay as they are;
a new operation needs another mapping. This is separate from deleting records or discarding
a change set. Deletion has no Undo in this list.

The delete uses the version you viewed. If someone changes the mapping first, deletion is
refused; refresh the list, inspect the new mapping and decide again. A failed deletion leaves
its error in the confirmation. Do not assume a mapping disappeared until the list removes it.
Follow [Delete a model mapping](/docs/guide/model/delete-a-model-mapping/) for the steps.
guide/src/content/docs/model/models.md:
---
title: Models
description: Shape applications, record types, fields, relationships and views through drafts and releases.
reader: model-admin
---

Use a model to decide what people can keep in a workspace and how they work with it.
A model defines applications, record types, fields, relationships, hierarchies and views.
Changing a model changes those definitions; editing a record changes the data held under them.
Start with [Create a model draft](/docs/guide/model/create-a-model-draft/).

## What a model contains

| Part | What it decides |
| --- | --- |
| Applications | Named work areas and the types and views available in each. |
| Object types | The kinds of record people can create. The editor calls a record type an **Object type**. |
| Attribute types | Reusable field definitions, such as a date or a whole number. A type attaches an attribute and decides whether it is required or read-only there. |
| Relation types | The meaning of a relationship, with names for its forward and reverse directions. Allowed pairs decide which record types it may connect. |
| Hierarchies | Which types may stand at the top level or under another type, connected by a containment relation. |
| Views and record pages | How records appear: tables, trees, mapping grids, relation matrices and the panels on a record page. |

The same type can be listed in several applications. It keeps the same field and relationship
rules wherever it appears. An attribute type can also be shared: changing its definition affects
every type that attaches it, while **Required** and **Read-only** belong to each attachment.

Every application can use the same kinds of view. Its name or subject does not determine its
features; the declared structure determines which views fit. The applications shipped in the
starter model are examples you may replace, reshape or remove.

## Draft, release, activation

These are three separate stages:

1. A **draft** is saved, editable work. You can leave it unfinished, close it and return later.
   Its version increases as you edit it; that number is not a release version.
2. **Installing** makes an immutable release: a fixed set of definitions with a release version.
   Later draft edits never rewrite that release.
3. **Activating** selects the installed release for one workspace. refiroo checks that workspace's
   data before switching. Other workspaces keep the releases they already run.

The editor combines the last two stages in **Install and activate…**, with a confirmation that
names the target workspace. An installed release may remain inactive if activation fails.
See [Releases](/docs/model/releases/) for compatibility and open change sets.

## Find a model and its workspaces

Open **Settings**, then **Model**. Search by model name. The list separates the model run by the
default workspace, other models in use and drafts without an installed model. It shows release
counts, the latest release, drafts and schema. The schema identifies the model language refiroo
reads; it is separate from the release version you choose for your model.

![Model list with releases, latest versions, draft counts and workspace use](/docs/screens/model-list.png)

*Above: Public transport stops of Graubünden runs the default workspace. RDM Starter Model runs
another workspace; a further draft has no installed model yet.*

Open a model for **Overview**, **Releases**, **Drafts** and **Structure**. Overview identifies the
workspaces using it; Structure initially shows the newest release read only, with a picker for other releases. Use a draft to change it.

![Model overview showing its newest release and the workspace running it](/docs/screens/model-overview.png)

*Above: the Graubünden model's overview names its running workspace and offers Change model….*

**Settings**, **Workspaces** shows the model and release beside each workspace. Open a workspace
and choose **Edit model** to work in its context. The editor says **Applies to** that workspace
and offers **Apply to this workspace…**. Check that name before applying.

![Workspaces listed with the model and release each runs](/docs/screens/model-workspaces-list.png)

*Above: Graubünden and Default run different models. Default is a workspace name here; the green
Default mark identifies Graubünden as the default workspace.*

## Who may do what

The supplied **Model administrator** role brings together model authoring and release permissions.
Administrators can also grant these separately, so the permissions and their scope matter more
than a role's name.

| Permission | What it allows |
| --- | --- |
| Model authoring | Create and edit drafts, use their editor, issues and history, and read releases. |
| Install a model | Install a draft as a release without choosing it for a workspace. |
| Model release | Install and activate releases, and migrate the workspace where the permission is granted. |
| Workspace administration | Create and manage workspaces, including creating a new target workspace. |

Authoring a draft does not itself grant permission to activate it. A workspace's **Edit model**
route needs authoring and release access there. Record editing and change-set publication need
their own data permissions. If a control is missing or unavailable, ask an access administrator
to check your grants and whether model administration is enabled on the instance.

Continue with [The model editor](/docs/model/the-model-editor/) or
[Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/) if your starting point is a spreadsheet.

The model list orders the default workspace's model first, then other models in use, then the
rest and **Drafts without an installed model**. Pills identify **Runs the default workspace**,
**Retired** and **Draft**. A model with every release retired and no running workspace appears
under **Retired**. Open **Change model…** on Overview beside a workspace to choose its release
and check that workspace's stored data before any switch.

On **Structure**, choose **Release** to inspect that release's attributes and rules and its
relationships, other types and reverse names. This tab is read-only. Open the release to compare
or export it; open a draft to edit.

If **Model mutations are disabled** appears, installed releases remain available for inspection
and export. Ask the operator about the deployment setting before expecting draft or activation
actions. [Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/) covers workspace administration.

## Continue by task

Use [Create a model draft](/docs/guide/model/create-a-model-draft/) or
[Start from a workbook](/docs/guide/model/start-a-draft-from-a-workbook/), then the
[model editor](/docs/model/the-model-editor/). [Consumer APIs](/docs/model/consumer-apis/) shapes
what consuming systems read. [Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/) covers conversions and reviewed
loss; [Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/) covers data between two workspaces.

The model's name, applications and record layouts come from its definitions. The top bar uses
the default workspace model's product name; a job describes types from its own workspace's model.
A different workspace can therefore show different applications without being a different edition
of refiroo. Model drafts and activation history identify the author of changes.

A draft accepts at most 500 operations in one grouped save. Ordinary visual actions group their
related operations for you. A specialist exceeding that bound must split the work into smaller
reviewable saves, rather than repeating the refused oversized save.

When a draft is no longer needed, follow [Delete a draft](/docs/guide/model/delete-a-draft/).
Export any design you need to keep first; deleting a draft removes its saved editing work and attached workbook.

## Keep and reuse a model elsewhere

[Export an installed release](/docs/guide/model/export-a-release/) to keep its exact definitions.
On another instance, a specialist can use **New draft**, **Import JSON** to import that document,
then validate, install and choose a workspace separately. The destination must support its
model language. Importing definitions does not bring records, grants, subscriptions, workbook
files or editing history with them. For recovery of a whole installation, use the operator’s
[backup and restore procedure](/docs/run/backup-and-restore/).

guide/src/content/docs/model/record-page:
---
title: Record pages and tables
description: How a type gets its record page, and how panels and table columns show related records.
reader: model-admin
---

A record page brings one record's fields, place in a hierarchy and related records together.
A table compares records in rows. As a model administrator, you choose their arrangement in
a draft before activating it for a workspace. You need **Model authoring** to edit the layout.

A type shared by several applications can have a different page in each one. Each application
can declare one record page for that type and can offer table views with different columns.
These are model choices available to every application.

## The page a type gets

refiroo uses one rule for a new type's page, **Declare its page**, and the page shown when an
application has no declared page for the type. Adding a newly allowed relationship uses the
same rule to build its panel. The starting layout therefore does not depend on how the page
was created.

| Region | Starting content |
| --- | --- |
| **Side** | **Details**, with the type's fields in their defined order. **Hierarchy** follows when the type can have a parent. |
| **Main** | One panel for contained types, if there are any, followed by a separate panel for each relationship in each direction the type can read. |

The contained-record panel takes the first contained type's plural name as its title when
several types are listed. Relationship panels follow the model's relationship order. Their
titles read from the open record's side: the forward name for relationships it holds outwards,
the reverse name for relationships pointing towards it. A relationship with no reverse
direction is shown only from its forward side. Containment does not get another
relationship panel; its context is already shown by the hierarchy and contained records.

Each generated relationship panel starts with these columns, in this order:

- **Name** of the related record.
- A containing type's name, if all related types have the same single direct parent type.
  This column shows each related record's parent name. A hierarchy within the same type
  does not add this column.
- Up to four fields of the related types, in their defined order, without repeated fields.
- **Type**, when the panel lists more than one type.

The relationship label is omitted because the panel's title already says it. When the panel
lists one related type and has a parent column, that column is its initial sort. Otherwise,
the initial order is by name. The four-field starting limit is not a limit on the columns you
can select afterwards.

![Stop record page with separate panels for its relationships](/docs/screens/model-stop-page-relationship-panels.png)

Above: a Stop page in the guide's Graubünden model. **Details** and **Hierarchy** are at the
side. **Main** has **Served by mode**, **Operated by**, **Is represented by system code** and
**Has name translation**. System codes have a **System** column and translations a **Language**
column. These are relationships and parent types declared by this model.

## Declared pages and later changes

Without a declared page, refiroo draws the starting layout from the type's current fields,
containment and relationships. **Declare its page** saves that layout in the draft so you
can arrange it. It does not replace a page already declared.

Existing pages keep their arrangement. Adding a newly allowed relationship adds its panel
on the declared pages at both ends, where that direction is readable and no panel already
lists it. It also adds a relationship column and filter to the types' declared tables.
Removing that allowed relationship, or undoing its addition, removes the dependent layout
items that no longer have an available relationship. A panel covering other relationships
can remain with those relationships.

This does not rebuild older pages to match a new starting layout. Use **Add panel…** to
add a missing relationship panel to an existing page. It offers **Related records**,
**Contained records** where this application lists eligible contained types, and **Fields**.
The title follows the related or contained choice until you change it. Choose **Main** or
**Side** for its region. A relationship already listed is marked **(on the page)** and may
be used again. The server builds related-record and contained-record panels consistently
for every client. Applying the dialog is one draft step, with **Undo**.

Follow [Edit a record page](/docs/guide/model/edit-a-record-page/) for adding panels, moving
fields and choosing columns.

## What panels can show

| Panel | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Fields | Selected fields of the open record. Separate field groups give them different headings. |
| Contained records | One or more types that the open record can contain. |
| Related records | Records reached through selected relationships, in the outward, inward or both directions. |
| Table | Records of a type listed in the application, optionally limited to direct children of the open record. |
| Hierarchy | The parent, ancestors, or both. |

**Add panel…** creates related-record panels, contained-record panels or field groups; it
is not a form for every panel kind and setting. A specialist author maintains settings
that have no visual form. See [Applications and views](/docs/model/applications-and-views/).

Panels have a title, region, order and visibility. Ordering is separate within **Main** and
**Side**. Hiding a panel keeps its definition; removing it takes it off the page. Neither
deletes records or values. Grouping fields moves them from their current groups. **Add fields…**
adds fields omitted from the page, not new field definitions. Menus provide keyboard alternatives
to dragging panels and fields.

A list panel's **Columns…** offers the listed records' name and fields. Under **Where it sits**,
a column for a containing type shows that ancestor record's name, including ancestors beyond
the direct parent. **Type** is offered when several types are listed. These choices do not
include fields of the ancestors themselves; those are available as related-field columns
in a table view.

Related-record panels can sort by their supported column headers. Their **Sort…** layout
menu appears when the panel declares allowed sort fields. These can include name, type,
relationship, non-JSON fields of related records, and a containing type when the panel reaches
one related type. Records missing the chosen field sort last. Live timestamps are not
related-record panel sort choices. A declared initial order can be descending.

List panels can read 1–100 rows per page. A reading size limits a page of results, not the
whole collection. The record header normally shows the name and type; a declared title or
subtitle field can supply other context. The line above the title holds the list link, when
opened from a list, and the ancestors the model shows; it has no application entry. In **Record
page**, choose **Header and breadcrumbs…** to set the title, optional line under it, type label
and whether ancestors appear. Either type-name choice places the type in the header. This page-specific header does not change
the type’s shared Display attribute.

## Table columns, filters and sort

The **Table** layout tab arranges an existing table view. Columns, available filters and
initial sort are defaults for everyone using that view, rather than one person's saved search.
The view needs at least one column, filter field and sort field, with no repeats within each
list. Its initial sort must be one of its allowed sort fields. Ordinary non-JSON field columns
can sort from their headers; additional allowed fields supply further sort choices.

A relationship column shows related record names as chips in name order, with **+N more**
when they do not fit. It combines the allowed related types for that relationship at the
listed record's end. There is no fixed number of relationship columns. People can hide
columns through **Display**; a hidden relationship column is no longer read for the table.
A names column can sort only when it represents one allowed type pair and each row can have
at most one related record through it.

In **Columns…**, **Fields of** beneath a relationship unfolds the related records' fields.
**Where they sit ·** headings offer the names and fields of their containing types. Each
checked field is a column of its own; selecting it does not require selecting the relationship's
names column. Its heading combines the relationship and field labels. Each related record
contributes its value, with **—** for a missing value. A field holding JSON is not offered.
These related-field columns never sort.

For example, in the guide's Graubünden model, the Stops table can show
**Has name translation · Language code**. The value comes from the language containing each
translation, rather than from the Stop or the relationship itself.

**Filters…** offers the relationship itself, without unfolding its fields. A relationship
filter can find records linked to any selected records, linked to any record, or linked to
none. Choosing a related-field column does not provide a filter on that field. Ordinary field
filters require a filterable, non-JSON field. Fields stored on a relationship itself cannot
be columns.

Relationship columns can be declared in table views and contained-record or table panels;
they do not add columns to trees, mapping grids, relation matrices, related-record panels
or headers. The table view's **Columns…** offers the related fields directly. A panel's
**Columns…** offers its listed records' fields and **Where it sits** instead.

Follow [Choose table columns, filters and sort](/docs/guide/model/choose-table-columns-filters-and-sort/).
**The draft declares no table view** means there is no table to arrange here. Add one through
the application’s **Add a view…**; see [Add a view](/docs/guide/model/add-a-view/).

## Mark inactive records in a table

In the **Table** layout, **Inactive records…** sits beside **Filters…** and
**Sort menu and page size…**. It lets this view use one of its record type's Yes/No fields
to mark records whose value is **No**. The choice **A record is inactive when this is No**
offers **None** and the type's Yes/No fields. **None** leaves the table without an inactive
mark or switch. A field of another type, or one that is not Yes/No, is invalid for this
setting; the editor offers only eligible fields.

With a field selected, a record with **No** keeps its row and order. Its name is quieter,
with a grey **Inactive** pill when the field is called Active, or **Not** followed by the
field's name in lower case for another name. A missing value is not marked. The setting
neither changes stored values nor grants editing rights; a read-only field may be used.
It applies to this table view, rather than every table or panel listing the type.

Readers see inactive records by default and can use **Hide inactive (N)** beside **Filter**.
The switch hides exactly the marked records through a filter pill, such as **Active: not No**,
that stays in the page address. Records with no value stay visible. It works even when the
chosen field is not offered in **Filters…**. Its count is the number with **No** after the
list's search and other filters, including **0** when none match. Choosing **Yes** in the
ordinary **＋ Filter** menu instead excludes records with no value; the switch does not use
that condition. The mark and switch use the values of the current Live, change-set or
publication context; publication data remains read-only.

Follow [Choose table columns, filters and sort](/docs/guide/model/choose-table-columns-filters-and-sort/#choose-how-the-table-marks-inactive-records)
to set the field. See [Lists, search and filters](/docs/use/lists-and-filters/#show-or-hide-inactive-records)
for the reader's controls.

## Preview and validation

**Preview** draws draft definitions over live records from a chosen workspace, without changing
those records. Data-changing controls are disabled. Choose **Workspace** and **Record**, or
**Show an empty record** for a type with no records yet. Follow
[Preview a type](/docs/guide/model/preview-a-type/).

![Draft preview showing workspace and record choices](/docs/screens/model-type-preview.png)

An invalid draft cannot be previewed or laid out. **Show issues** names the definitions to
repair. Validation checks distinct panels, available fields and relationships, containment,
application membership and reading sizes. Hiding an invalid panel does not repair its
references. This model check does not prove compatibility with every stored record.

Every saved layout change is a draft history step. A refused action shows **Not applied**
and changes nothing. Review populated and empty records, check **Issues**, then follow
[Install and activate a release](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/).

## Panel settings and reading sizes

Open a panel’s **Settings…** in the record-page layout. The choices depend on its kind:

| Panel | Settings you can change |
| --- | --- |
| Related records | **Relationships listed**, **Listed from**, the relationship label column and allowed sort fields. Leaving the sort choices empty lists by name. |
| Hierarchy | **Show the parent** and **Show the records above the parent**, independently. |
| Contained records | **Rows on a page**. The contained types were selected when the panel was added. |
| Table | **List only the records under this one** and **Rows on a page**. The table’s record type itself needs a specialist to change. |
| Fields | No additional Settings dialog; use the field and group controls. |

**Listed from** can read **This record to the others**, **The others to this record**, or
**Both ways**. Changing direction changes which connections appear, without reversing any
stored relationship. **Show which relationship joins each record** is useful when combining
several relationships in one panel. Changing panel contents can make existing columns invalid;
check Issues and revise the columns as needed.

In **Table**, **Sort menu and page size…** chooses the fields people can sort by and the
number of **Rows on a page**. The form offers Name, current choices and fields marked Sortable.
If you remove the initial sort field, the first remaining field becomes the default. Leaving
all choices unchecked keeps the current table sort list. This differs from a related-record
panel, where no sort choices returns to name order.

Reading sizes in these forms are 10, 20, 25, 50 or 100; an existing different valid size is
also preserved as an option. The model permits 1–100. Table and contained-record panels default to 20 when no size is specified; generated table
views start at 50. A reading size does not cap a collection: people continue scrolling to read more.
Some supported declarations still need the [JSON view](/docs/model/json-view/): changing the
record type of a table panel, changing a contained panel’s type list after creation.

---
title: Releases
description: Understand immutable model releases, workspace activation and compatibility checks.
reader: model-admin
---

Install a draft to keep a fixed model release. Activate that release to make one workspace use
its definitions. These stages are separate even when the editor offers them in one confirmation.
Follow [Install and activate a release](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/).

## An installed release never changes

A release records its model name, stable release key, version and schema. The version distinguishes
releases of your model; the schema identifies the model language. Neither is a draft's edit count.
To change definitions, make a draft and install another release. You cannot overwrite a release's
content by reusing its identity for different definitions.

Open **Settings**, **Model**, choose a model and select **Releases**. The list shows its installed
versions, schema, installation date and workspace use. **Drafts** lists editable work separately,
with each draft's base release.

![Installed versions on a model's Releases tab](/docs/screens/model-releases.png)

*Above: the Graubünden model has one installed release, 1.0.0, used by Graubünden.*

![Drafts listed separately with their base release and date](/docs/screens/model-drafts.png)

*Above: Guide draft and another draft both start from the Graubünden model's release 1.0.0.*

Open a release to inspect its counts and workspace use, **Create draft from release**, or
**Activate in a workspace…**. **Structure** on the model’s page is read-only and initially selects the newest release;
its Release picker can show another version.

![Read-only model structure with application and type counts](/docs/screens/model-structure.png)

*Above: the newest Graubünden release lists Network's types and the other applications.*

The release's **Changes in this release** section lets you choose **Compare with**. It shows
added, changed and removed definitions relative to that choice. Check the before and after
release names: a chosen comparison may be another model rather than this release's predecessor.
With no earlier release, there may be nothing to compare until you choose a baseline.

## Activation belongs to one workspace

Each workspace runs its own release. Different workspaces may run different versions or entirely
different models. Making a release available does not switch every workspace. The default workspace
is simply the default destination; it does not impose its model on the rest.

![Workspace overview identifying its model and applications](/docs/screens/model-workspace-model.png)

*Above: Graubünden runs Public transport stops of Graubünden 1.0.0 and offers Edit model.*

![A second workspace overview with a different model and applications](/docs/screens/model-workspace-other-model.png)

*Above: Default runs RDM Starter Model 0.10.0 alongside Graubünden, with its own applications.*

Activation checks the target workspace's records, values and relationships. It is refused when
those data do not fit unchanged, or when consumer API compatibility requires another contract
version. A release that fitted yesterday can fail today if data changed. Selecting an older release
is subject to the same checks; it is not a way to undo record edits.

When you open **Edit model** from a workspace, the editor identifies it with **Applies to** and
**Apply to this workspace…**. The confirmation lists the model differences, data compatibility,
consumer API compatibility, other workspaces left unchanged and open change sets left behind.
If data needs migration, it offers **Preview what happens to the records…** for a separate review
and confirmation. Opening that preview alone changes nothing.

## Change sets keep their release

Activating a new release does not rewrite open change sets. They remain pinned to their old
release and cannot be published while the workspace runs a different one. The confirmation lists
them so you can plan the change. Move each to the new release and validate it, or discard it
through the change-set workflow. Publications remain fixed snapshots.

See [Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) before applying a model change beside work in progress.

## Retiring a release

A release can be **Retired** to stop it being chosen for new work. Workspaces and change sets
already on it keep working. On the release page, **Retire…** asks for confirmation; **Bring back**
makes a retired release available again. The default workspace's release cannot be retired.
These controls need installation permission.

Deletion is more restrictive: a release must have no remaining references. A running workspace,
history, an import profile or a mapping can prevent deletion, and the refusal explains why.
Deleting a release does not delete its drafts. Read the confirmation before using **Delete release**.

## Read the result of both stages

**Installed, not active** means installation succeeded but the workspace did not switch. The
installed release remains available. Resolve the reported reason and activate that release from
its page; do not assume a second installation is needed. A concurrency refusal means the workspace
or draft changed after your check: refresh, review the current state and check again.

If the mutation controls are unavailable, check your permissions in
[Models](/docs/model/models/#who-may-do-what) and whether model administration is enabled.

## Availability, details and checks

The page marks **Runs this release** for a workspace using it and **Run by no workspace** when
none does. Under **Technical details**, **Release ID** and **Content hash** each have **Copy**;
these identify a release and its exact content, rather than its displayed version alone.
**Export JSON** downloads the immutable model document for a specialist model author.

**Activation check** checks each workspace running this model separately. Read the workspace name
and result; a successful check for one workspace says nothing about another's data. A failed
check is not compatibility. The confirmation checks again when you activate.

**Retire…** removes a release from new choices without changing workspaces already running it.
**Bring back** makes it available again. A release never run and with no records, change sets or
publications made under it can offer **Delete…** with confirmation. Retirement preserves the
release; deletion removes an unused one. A model with all releases retired and no running
workspace appears under Retired.

Release pickers offer usable releases supported by this refiroo version. A new workspace starts
with the newest release of each model offered, with older versions available on request.
A change set offers every usable version and its own workspace's release even if that release
is retired. Older unsupported releases remain inspectable and exportable; ask the operator
about updating their model-language version before using them again.

## Tasks and checks

[Compare releases](/docs/guide/model/compare-releases/),
[Retire or delete a release](/docs/guide/model/retire-or-delete-a-release/) and
[Export a release](/docs/guide/model/export-a-release/) cover the release page's actions.
[Change a workspace's model](/docs/guide/model/change-a-workspaces-model/) explains the activation
results; [Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/) explains conversion and explicit acceptance of loss.
[Model language versions](/docs/model/model-language-versions/) explains a historical release that
cannot be used by this deployment.

The release page's **Activation check** covers workspaces running this model. A workspace running
another model is checked separately when selected as a destination. **Historical release** means
this deployment cannot interpret its model language for the usual comparison and activation checks;
its metadata and raw export remain readable.

Installation makes the installed release the draft's base without resetting its editing
version. A second different definition under the same release key and version is refused; the
install dialog proposes an editable next version. Exact reinstallation of the same content can
restore a retired release. After a switch, an older open data form may be refused because it
was based on the old model; reload and review the new definitions before editing again.

Open change sets can use **Change model version** only when their content already fits the
chosen release. If conversion is needed, use the migration review. Starting a change set from
current live data likewise checks that its selected model can hold that data; choosing a model
version does not waive its rules. Publication requires a successful validation of the current
change-set version and agreement with the workspace's active release. See
[Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) for the ordinary creation and publication steps.

## Ask what activation changes

With a configured AI provider and the required workspace permissions, the activation dialog
offers **What this change does**. [Accounts of model changes](/docs/model/model-change-accounts/)
explains the facts, sent data, costs and limits. Follow
[Explain a model change](/docs/guide/model/explain-a-model-change/) to ask; opening the dialog
alone makes no provider request.

guide/src/content/docs/model/the-model-e:
---
title: The model editor
description: Find definitions, edit their structure, preview layouts and review the draft history.
reader: model-admin
---

Use the model editor to change a draft through named actions. Each saved action becomes a step
in its history. You need **Model authoring**; applying the result also needs release access.
See [Models](/docs/model/models/) for the stages and permissions.

## Find your way around

The header identifies the draft, its base release, draft version and validation state. **Undo**
and **Redo** act on saved steps. **Close** keeps the draft and its proposals. The main confirmation
is **Install and activate…**, or **Apply to this workspace…** when you came from a workspace.

The model pane lists applications and their types in a hierarchy, followed by **Relation types**,
**Attribute types** and **Relationship matrix**. A type listed in several applications still has
one definition. Select an element to see its details in the centre. Use the plus button to add
an element, or the selected element's menu for its operations.

![Draft editor with its header, model pane and Issues and history bar](/docs/screens/model-editor-overview.png)

*Above: Guide draft starts from the Graubünden release. The model pane lists Network, Systems and
Names; no element is selected in the centre.*

An application shows its types, where they stand, field and relationship counts, views and
navigation groups. A type shows **Attributes** and **Relations**. Select an editable cell to
change it with **Save**, or leave it with **Cancel**. Menus offer operations such as **Rename…**,
**Move to…**, adding fields and allowing relationships.

| Mark | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Released | The element is unchanged from the draft's base release. |
| New | The draft adds the element. |
| Changed | The element, or something within it, differs from the base release. |
| Proposed | The element still reflects the engine's suggestion from a source. Review it before relying on it. |

Renaming a label does not change its key. A released key can also change, but integrations
that name it must change with it. The element panel says **Released: a key change needs a migration**.

Removing, moving, splitting or merging a released type, converting a field to a list type,
or tightening a rule saves a draft step even when stored data uses the element. Menus warn
**Needs a migration when installed** where an action can need one. **Move to…** explains what
happens to the records or values when the migration runs. Changing the draft does not move
live records; review the migration before activating the release.

## Work with a navigation group

Select a group in the model pane, or choose its name in the application's **Navigation groups**
table. Its panel shows the application it belongs to, whether it starts open or folded, and how
many entries it holds. **Entries** lists **Entry**, **Kind**, **Opens on** and **State**.
Collections and relation matrices share this table and its order.

**Add to group…** opens a searchable list where you can tick several collections and matrices.
Location notes show what is at the top of the sidebar, inside a row collection or in another
group; choosing an entry in another group moves it. One addition, even with several entries,
is one saved step and one **Undo**. **Rename…** and **Start folded** / **Start unfolded** adjust
the group itself.

In an entry's menu, **Move up** and **Move down** change its position. **Move to another group…**
is offered when another group exists. **Take out of the group** returns a collection to the
sidebar's top level, or leaves a matrix available through its row collection without a separate
entry. These actions arrange navigation; they do not move records.

For a collection with several views, edit **Opens on** in place and **Save** the choice.
It decides which view opens from that collection's sidebar entry or the group page. Without a
separate choice, the application default is used when it belongs to the collection, then its
table, then its first view. Other view tabs stay available. A matrix entry shows **Itself**:
it always opens that matrix, using its view name and a matrix symbol in its row type's colour.
The row collection stays in navigation and still offers the matrix among its tabs.

The application panel's **Entries** column lists the collections and matrices in each group.
Its **In no group:** line offers **Add to a group…** with ungrouped collections ticked.
A relation matrix's menu in **Views** offers **Move to group…** when a group exists.
Follow [Group collections in navigation](/docs/guide/model/group-collections-in-navigation/)
for the steps. Navigation changes reach a workspace when the model release is activated.

## When there is a workbook

A workbook adds a **Source** pane with sheets, columns, mapping states and statistics. Select a
column to see what it feeds; select a type to see the columns that feed it. **Map to…** in the
column menu provides an alternative to dragging it onto the model. A proposal's **Proposed because**
explains the suggestion; **Evidence** opens the supporting observations. You can change or undo
proposals. The original workbook is not rewritten.

While profiling is running, wait for the sheets and columns. If profiling fails, read the reason
and upload the workbook again from the draft menu. Once columns are mapped, the **Dry run** tab
checks their rows after edits. Narrow screens present the panes as tabs.

For source selection, mapping and loading, follow
[Load a workbook](/docs/guide/model/start-a-draft-from-a-workbook/). The source pane is absent from a draft with
no attached workbook.

## Preview and layout

**Preview** on a type shows the draft's layout over records read live from a workspace running
its model. Its data controls are disabled: previewing writes nothing. Check the workspace and
record selectors; an empty preview for a new model does not mean the draft failed.

![Type preview with a workspace selector and disabled record controls](/docs/screens/model-type-preview.png)

*Above: Stop's draft layout is shown over a live Graubünden record. Step-free access is still a
draft addition, with no live value.*

**Edit layout** opens the layout editor. **Record page** arranges panels and fields in the main
and side regions. **Table** chooses columns, filters and the default sort. Layout changes are
saved draft steps too; they reach the workspace's record screens after activation.

Follow [Add a record type and fields](/docs/guide/model/add-a-record-type-and-fields/),
[Add a relationship](/docs/guide/model/add-a-relationship/) and
[Arrange applications and views](/docs/guide/model/arrange-applications-and-views/) for the actions.

## History, undo and other editors

Expand **Issues and history** and choose **History**. Steps appear newest first, with the action,
author, time and whether they are applied or undone. A single step may contain related actions,
such as creating an attribute and attaching it to a type.

A step that changes a released element used by stored data is marked **Needs a migration**,
with the counts of records, values and relationships using it. A released key change has the
mark even when no stored data uses it. Other changes to unused released elements have no mark.

![History showing two applied steps and their Undo actions](/docs/screens/model-history.png)

*Above: Guide draft records adding Step-free access and allowing Inspected by as two saved steps.*

**Undo** reverses a step in the draft; **Redo** restores an undone step. A new edit clears what
can be redone. If later steps depend on the step you undo, refiroo names them and offers to undo
them together. Read that list before confirming. Undoing a draft step never rewrites an installed
release or reverses already published record changes. Undo also takes the step's part out of
the draft's proposed migration; redo puts it back. The proposal follows the steps that are
currently applied.

If another administrator edits the draft first, your older edit can be refused. The **Another change came first** notice lists the steps applied since you opened it, and the
model below shows the newer version. Read those steps, then choose **Apply mine again** if your
change still belongs, or **Discard mine** to leave it out. A further intervening edit can refuse
the retry too.

## Compare before releasing

The install confirmation summarises changed applications, types, fields and relationships against
the draft's base release. A draft without a base is compared with the newest release of its own
model, if one exists; a wholly new model has no earlier definitions to compare.

Read those differences together with validation, stored-data compatibility and **Consumer APIs**.
A comparison of definitions does not prove that the workspace's existing records fit. The separate
checks are explained in [Issues and dry runs](/docs/model/issues-and-dry-run/).

When the selected workspace needs a migration, **Install and activate…** and **Apply to this
workspace…** show **Activation needs a migration**. Read the steps and the proposed changes:
which types records become, where they move, and whether they leave their parents. The figures
show records moving, records and relationships created where applicable, and refused items.
For each key change, the dialog warns that integrations naming the old key must change and
lists the consumer APIs of the base release that name it.

Choose **Install … and preview the migration…**, or **Preview what happens to the records…**
from **Apply to this workspace…**. This installs the release and opens the migration preview;
it does not activate the release in the workspace yet.

On the migration page, **What the draft proposes** is already filled in. Each type's row shows
**Records of**, **Become**, **In**, **Under** and **Records**, with a **Proposed** mark for the
draft's choice. Change **Become** to preview another choice without editing the draft.
Splits and list conversions can create records and relationships; inspect them under **Created**.
Fix refused items before confirming, and review and explicitly accept any removals.
The workspace keeps its current release until the migration is confirmed and succeeds.
See [Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/) for what each kind of change carries or removes,
and follow [Migrate a workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) to complete the review.

## Header, keyboard and phone controls

Open **About this draft** for its base release (or **A new model**), edit version and validity.
The version increases with each saved step. Change the editable draft title to rename the draft;
this does not rename a release. **Saved as you go** means closing keeps the draft and proposals.

The **Add** menu offers **Application…**, **Object type…**, **Attribute type…**,
**Relation type…** and **Navigation group…**. In an empty draft, add an application first.
An operation opens a dialog; **Not applied** means the attempted step did not save. Correct its
reported cause, or cancel. **Delete draft…** in **More actions** asks for confirmation and removes
only the editable draft, its steps and attached source, leaving installed releases unchanged.

In the model pane, Up/Down and Home/End move focus; Enter or Space selects. Right and Left unfold
and fold sections. Shift+F10 or the context-menu key opens the selected row's operations.
On a phone, tabs replace the panes. Use the menus: model-editor drags are off on phones.
**Earlier steps** in History reads more than the initial saved-step list.

**Relationship matrix** shows every type as a row and column, with rows as the from end.
Cells list permitted relationships and their number limits; containment reads **contains**.
Move with arrow keys and select a pair with Enter. The selected pair's panel offers its existing
relations' menus and an action to allow another. It can be resized.

## Consumer contracts and the structured-document view

The **Consumer APIs** tab holds the contracts other systems read. Add a consumer API with its
name and the types to expose, then inspect **Types and related**, **Fields**, **Operations**,
**Filters**, **Schema** and **Message example**. Fields and related lists shape the public data;
operations choose what consumers can read. The compatibility status says whether a higher
contract version is needed. Raising that version is separate from numbering the model release.
Review breaking changes with the consuming teams before activation.

The header also offers **Open as JSON** for specialist model authors who maintain the complete
structured model document. Normal screen-based editing does not need it. Both routes edit the
same draft and record saved steps; document edits appear as **JSON edit** in History. Use
**Export JSON** there, or on an installed release, to download its document. If that view reports
a newer saved draft, preserve your local work with **Copy local JSON** before
**Reload saved version**. Reloading does not merge the two versions.

## Next tasks

Use [Find your way around](/docs/guide/model/find-your-way-around-the-editor/) for keyboard and phone
navigation, [Undo and review history](/docs/guide/model/undo-and-review-the-draft-history/) for saved
steps, and [Work on a draft with others](/docs/guide/model/work-on-a-draft-with-others/) for version
conflicts. [Delete a draft](/docs/guide/model/delete-a-draft/) removes only editable work.

[Types, attributes and relations](/docs/model/types-attributes-relations/),
[Applications and views](/docs/model/applications-and-views/),
[Record pages and tables](/docs/model/record-pages-and-tables/) and
[Consumer APIs](/docs/model/consumer-apis/) explain each part of the editor.
The specialist [JSON view](/docs/model/json-view/) exposes the complete model document.

Draft comparison uses the base release where there is one, otherwise the latest installed
release of that model, otherwise an empty model. There is no automatic rebase or merge of a
draft onto a newer release. To start from different definitions, create a new draft from the
intended release and review the changes you carry across. A refused grouped operation applies
none of that step. Intermediate invalid drafts may be saved; Issues identifies what still needs work.

A navigation group's initial folded state is a model default; each browser can remember a
different state. A group page gathers its collection and matrix entries with search over their names. During a drag in the model
pane, moving near its upper or lower edge scrolls the pane. Keyboard and phone users use
**Move to…** and the ordering menus instead.

## Describe a change in words

You can also [ask the assistant to propose a model change](/docs/model/ai-model-changes/)
and open its draft in this editor. Review the proposal before accepting; direct edits here
are read again when the assistant continues.

guide/src/content/docs/model/types-attri:
---
title: Types, attributes and relations
description: Define kinds of record, shared fields, allowed connections and containment.
reader: model-admin
---

Define a type for each kind of record people maintain. Its attributes hold values; its
relationships connect records. You need **Model authoring** to change these definitions in a draft.
[Models](/docs/model/models/) explains when changes reach a workspace.

## Types and where records stand

The editor calls a record type an **Object type**. **Name** is singular; **Plural name** labels
its collection. **Stands** places it at the top level or under another type. A child is joined
to its parent by a containment relation, with names in both directions. Containment is not an
extra label on an ordinary relationship: it defines the record hierarchy too.

A type may be listed in several applications while keeping one definition and one set of rules.
Removing a listing differs from removing the type. Follow
[Add a record type and fields](/docs/guide/model/add-a-record-type-and-fields/) or
[Split, merge and move types](/docs/guide/model/split-merge-and-move-types/).

## Attributes and shared definitions

An attribute type defines a reusable field, including its name, value type and features.
The value types offered are **Text**, **Long text**, **Whole number**, **Decimal number**, **Yes or no**, **Date**,
**Date and time** and **JSON**.
Choose the type for the value people hold, rather than storing every value as text.

An attachment to a record type determines **Required** and **Read-only** there. **Unique** belongs
to the shared attribute definition. Changing a shared name, value type or feature affects every
attached type; **Shared with** identifies them. A required field needs a value; a read-only field
cannot be changed through the ordinary record form. **Searchable** includes the field in search and **Filterable** permits filtering. Views choose
which filter controls they offer. **Sortable** is shown, but ordinary non-JSON fields can sort
from list headers regardless of that checkbox. These features do not select table columns.
JSON fields cannot be made unique, sorted or filtered. They can be displayed in a table or
record field; they are not eligible as candidate criteria or scalar labels for trees and matrix
column headings.

![Released Stop type with its attribute rules and key-change migration notice](/docs/screens/model-type-fields.png)

*Above: Stop has nine attributes with their value types and local rules. Its facts say Released: a key change needs a migration.*

[Reuse and change attributes](/docs/guide/model/reuse-and-change-attributes/) explains the controls.
The visual editor sets numeric bounds and effective periods. Attribute defaults need a specialist in the [JSON view](/docs/model/json-view/).
The editor does not offer text-format or length rules.
A list of reference choices is modelled as related records, rather than as another value type:
[Turn an attribute into a list](/docs/guide/model/turn-an-attribute-into-a-list/).

## Relationships and permitted pairs

A relation type supplies the forward and reverse meanings. Permitted pairs separately say which
types it may join. Their **Cardinality** limits the number of connections at each end;
**Required** declares dependent ownership: the target is created with its owner connection.
It is supported for one-to-one or one-to-many relationships; **Many to one** cannot be required. **Which records** can narrow candidates by name,
attached attributes or ancestor. Criteria can apply to the records chosen and the records choosing.
Do not confuse a candidate rule with a filter that hides rows in one view.

**Relationship matrix** shows all permitted type pairs. Rows are the from end. Each cell lists
the relation types and number limits, with **contains** for containment. Select a pair to inspect
or change its permissions. This design grid differs from a relation matrix that people use for data.

![Relationship matrix with a selected from and to pair](/docs/screens/model-matrix-pair.png)

Follow [Add a relationship](/docs/guide/model/add-a-relationship/).

The attributes carried by a permitted pair belong to each connection, not to either record.
**Reference-data example:** Operated by, from Stop to Operator, carries Local name (Text),
Primary contact (Yes or no) and Inspected on (Date). Maps to, from System code to Municipality,
carries Confirmed (Yes or no) and Note (Text). These fields describe each connection, so
connections to the same operator or municipality can hold different values. The model chooses
which fields each permitted pair carries.

Choose the shared definitions in the pair's **Carries** cell. All eight attribute value types
listed above are available. The pair is directed: the selected from type, relation and to type
determine which attributes it carries. Opening the same connection from its other end reads
the same stored values; it does not create a second set. Another permitted pair using the same
relation type can carry different attributes.

People see these values in the record's Relationships panel and a relation matrix's cell table.
A [relationships table](/docs/use/relationship-tables/) can put them beside both records or
under column groups in a grid. Follow [Add a relationships table](/docs/guide/model/add-a-relationships-table/)
to choose its layout. Declaring carried attributes does not add a view by itself.
A [consumer API](/docs/model/consumer-apis/) can explicitly expose these values within a related
block; carrying a field does not automatically publish it to other systems.

## Released elements and migrations

You can rename, re-key, remove or reshape a released element in the editor. Labels change
without changing identity. A released key can also change, but needs a migration even when
there are no records: integrations naming the old key must change with it.

A structural step that affects stored data applies to the draft and is marked **Needs a migration**
in **History**, with the records, values and relationships that hold the element. The counts cover
Live and open change sets in every workspace running the draft’s model; workspaces running
other models and immutable publications are not counted. A structural step with nothing holding
the element has no mark, except for a released key change. Activation checks the data again.

Menus warn **Needs a migration when installed**. Saving the step does not change live data.
Installing the draft shows the migration to review before activating it. See
[Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/) for what is carried, created, removed or refused.

See [Rename or re-key an element](/docs/guide/model/rename-or-re-key-an-element/) and
[Remove an element](/docs/guide/model/remove-an-element/).

## Rules beyond the visual forms

The type’s **Settings** chooses a **Display attribute**, an **Effective period**, **At least one of**
and **Parent relationships**. A display
field must be attached to its type. An effective period uses appropriately typed fields and
requires a valid date order. Relationship attributes retain their types just as record fields do.

A relationship’s uniqueness rule can also be limited by a declared ancestor scope or condition. Those references
must resolve to the appropriate type and field. Such rules apply to writes through all clients;
a hidden field or filtered view does not bypass them. The visual candidate editor offers
**Which records may be chosen** and **Which records may choose**, with names, fields and ancestor
fields. Candidate criteria govern new choices; a later value change does not automatically remove
an existing relationship.

A mapping grid's relation cannot be containment or required ownership. Resolve the named model
issue by selecting a suitable relationship, rather than treating an application name as a special
permission to use the view. For the visual relation controls, select a **Relation type** to edit
**Names** and **Reverse name** and inspect **Allowed between**. **Allow between two types…**
chooses the From and To pair; **Change keys…** changes the identifying keys. Released key changes
need a migration, and integrations naming those keys must change too.

## Lists are types too

Give each independently maintained list its own record type. Its relationships then offer the
right kind of record without filtering by a parent's spelling. A list can have its own fields,
related names and external codes. Do not tie a model definition to one existing record as a way
to select a list: record values change independently of model releases. Use separate types and
[group their collections](/docs/guide/model/group-collections-in-navigation/) when there are many.

## Value rules

A declared default supplies a missing field on creation. It does not refill a cleared value on
an existing record. Required fields cannot be empty; empty text counts as missing. For an ordinary
unique field, a non-empty value can be held by only one record in the workspace, across all types
that use that shared definition. Empty values do not reserve a value. A change set checks its own
effective data, and publication checks again against changes made elsewhere.

Whole-number and decimal fields may have a minimum, a maximum or both. Bounds must be finite
numbers, and the minimum cannot exceed the maximum. The same bounds apply wherever the shared
field is used, including declared relationship fields. A value outside a bound is refused; change
the value or review the intended definition. Other value types cannot declare numeric bounds.

A type can also require at least one of a declared group of fields. This differs from making
each field required. The rule checks the complete result of an edit, including clearing a field:
people cannot clear the last populated field in that group. All named fields must be attached
to the type. Choose **At least one of…** in the type’s Settings to select the group. Clear every selection
to remove the grouped requirement. Set numeric bounds through an attribute type’s
**Minimum and maximum…**; leave either end empty for no bound. Attribute defaults still need
a specialist in the JSON view.

## Number limits and ownership

| Cardinality | Limit at each end |
| --- | --- |
| One to one | A source has at most one target and a target at most one source. |
| One to many | A source may have many targets; each target has at most one source. |
| Many to one | A source has at most one target; a target may serve many sources. |
| Many to many | Neither end is limited to one by this rule. |

These limits are counted for the relation type at the limited end, including its other allowed
type pairs. Adding another permitted pair does not give a record another single-choice slot.

For required one-to-one or one-to-many ownership, the source owns the dependent target. The target
is created with that relationship; people cannot remove the connection alone and leave an invalid
dependent. Confirmed cascade deletion of the owner also deletes its dependants. For an optional
association, removing the source's connections preserves the independent records at the other end.
Containment cascade deletes descendants. In a change set these deletions remain proposed until
publication; an existing publication stays unchanged.

A relationship stores only the fields declared for its allowed type pair. With no declared
relationship fields, it cannot hold arbitrary extra values. Supplied values keep the shared
field's type and numeric bounds. Relationship fields are separate from either endpoint's fields.

A type may contain more records of its own type, allowing several levels without creating a
new type for each level. Declaring that structure does not itself add a tree view: choose its
presentation separately. Move a record through its parent controls; a containment connection
cannot be edited independently of the parent. refiroo keeps the parent and its typed connection
together when records are created or moved.

A specialist can limit a relationship to one target per source and named ancestor of the target.
For example, a record may have one current related name under each language record. A condition
on a target field can restrict which relationships reserve that slot. The rule checks live data
and a change set's effective data, then checks the merged result at publication. Older publications
do not reserve slots in current data. This is a relationship uniqueness rule, separate from a
field's workspace-wide uniqueness.

A relation's discovery hint does not expand ordinary record search through its connections.
Search uses record names and searchable fields. Creation controls and hierarchy presentation
come from the declared panels and views, rather than from a relation's descriptive hints alone.

## Candidate criteria

The two ends can have different criteria. With none, any record of the allowed type is eligible.
Criteria can name the record's name, any attached non-JSON field, or a name or field of an ancestor.
The field need not be filterable in collection views.

| Field | Conditions offered |
| --- | --- |
| Text or long text | **is**, **contains**, **starts with**; the last two ignore case. |
| Numbers, dates and times | **is**, **is less than**, **is at most**, **is more than**, **is at least**. |
| Yes or no | **is**, with yes or no. |
| Any offered field | **is empty**, with yes or no. |
| Attached attribute | Also **has no value**, with yes or no, to test whether a value is held at all. |

Criteria use “and”, except that several **is** values on one field are alternatives. When
several criteria name one ancestor type, one ancestor must satisfy them together. In a recursive
hierarchy any ancestor of that type can qualify, at any depth. Unknown fields, an impossible
ancestor type, JSON fields, unsuitable conditions and wrongly typed values prevent a valid model.

The same eligibility governs relationship pickers, bulk relationship changes, mapping grids
and relation matrices. It also governs loads and writes from other clients. A grid normally
omits an ineligible source, but keeps it visible when it already has the relationship. Removal
still lists existing connections.

Changing values or criteria never automatically removes an existing connection, flags it as
invalid or blocks publication just because it no longer qualifies. The rules apply to new choices.
Use a purpose-made Yes/No field where possible: a condition on a name follows that name when
someone renames the record. Follow [Add a relationship](/docs/guide/model/add-a-relationship/)
to edit **Which records may be chosen** and **Which records may choose**.

## Effective periods

A type can declare one period of business validity using two different attached **Date** fields.
**Date and time** fields cannot define this period. The starting date is included; the ending date
is excluded. An empty start means no beginning limit; an empty end means no ending limit. Different
records' periods may overlap.

When both dates are present, the end must be later than the start. Equal dates are invalid.
The rule applies to live edits, change-set edits, validation and publication. Activating a release
that adds a period or changes its fields also checks existing records and refuses invalid periods.
Correct the affected dates under the current model or revise the declaration before retrying.

This period is independent of record versions, history and publications. Other systems can read
records valid on a chosen business date when the type declares a period. Removing the declaration
keeps the date values but removes that date-based reading capability; for an exposed type this
can require a higher consumer contract version. To set the period, open the type’s **Settings**, edit **Effective period**, and choose
**Starts on** and **Ends on**. The control is offered when two Date attributes are attached,
or a period already exists. Choose **None: records have no effective period** in Starts on
to remove it. Check existing dates before applying the release.

## Visibility, help and relationship settings

A type’s **Attributes** table has editable **Hidden** and **Help text** cells. Hidden leaves a
field off record screens and forms; it does not remove its values or its validation rules.
Do not hide a required field unless records can obtain its value another way. At **Attribute
types**, the shared definition’s **Settings** applies Hidden and Help text wherever it is used.
A locally hidden field stays hidden; a local No does not reveal a field hidden by its shared
definition. Local help text takes precedence over shared help text; clearing it uses the shared text.
Neither setting grants or removes access to stored data.

Select a **Relation type** and edit **Oriented** in **Settings**. It defaults to Yes.
This affects cascade deletion: an oriented required one-to-one or one-to-many relationship
can take the owned target records with its source. Optional relationships lose the connection
while keeping the other record. Containment descendants are included independently.
It does not rename the two directions or change their number limits.

On a type’s **Relations** table, **Carries** shows the shared attributes attached to that
allowed pair. Choose **Attributes of the relationship…** to select them. This is available
for non-containment pairs with attribute definitions to choose from; changing a released pair
that stored data uses can need a migration. **Cardinality and required…** edits the pair’s number and ownership
rules together. Saving definitions creates no relationships or values between actual records.

**Parent relationships…** selects incoming relationships that supply parent context for this
type in trees and matrices. It is a draft-only structural choice. It differs from moving an
existing record or choosing its containment parent. Review the eligible choices and Issues;
do not use it to bypass the type’s placement rules.
