turns. The engine resets the selected user's processes, home and temporary files around each turn.
Keep Compose's `init: true`; when running the image directly, supply `docker run --init`.
See [Set up AI](/docs/run/set-up-ai/#if-startup-or-a-request-fails) for reset and pool failures,
and [the assistant's session](/docs/run/ai/#the-assistants-session) for the remaining limits.

## Maintain build versions

Release source files fix the versions used to build the images. Preserve them with the deployment
record. When maintaining your own build, move each pin deliberately:

- **Base images:** the Dockerfiles and Compose files name a tag and a SHA-256 digest. Pull the
  chosen tag and read its digest with `docker buildx imagetools inspect <image:tag>` (the
  `Digest:` line). Replace the digest in `backend/Dockerfile`, `frontend/Dockerfile`,
  `compose.yml` or `compose.acme.yml`, as applicable, then rebuild. If maintaining CI too,
  update its PostgreSQL digest in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
- **Claude Code:** `CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION` in `backend/Dockerfile` names the installed version (default `2.1.295`).
  Change that default, or run `docker compose build --build-arg CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=<version> engine`.
  `npm view @anthropic-ai/claude-code version` reports the newest published version; it does not
  choose one for your build. Check the built version with
  `docker compose run --rm --no-deps --entrypoint claude engine --version`, then recreate the
  engine and check an assistant turn as described in [Set up AI](/docs/run/set-up-ai/).
- **Python dependencies:** the engine image installs with `backend/constraints.txt`. After changing
  `backend/pyproject.toml`, or to take newer dependencies, regenerate it from `backend/`:

  ```bash
  uv pip compile pyproject.toml --extra dev --universal --python-version 3.14 \
    --no-header --annotation-style line -o constraints.txt
  ```

  Keep the file's comment header, review the version changes and run the relevant tests before
  building. The ranges in `pyproject.toml` describe compatible versions; the constraints select
  the installed versions.
- **Browser application and guide:** `npm ci` installs the versions in each directory's
  `package-lock.json`. Keep the matching lock file with any package change and rebuild the image.

These changes need rebuilt images, not a container restart. Preserve the earlier source, build
configuration and matching backup until the new build has passed your cutover checks.
guide/src/content/docs/run/webhook-deliv:
---
title: Webhook delivery
description: Enable event delivery, diagnose retries, and retain enough history for recovery.
reader: operator
---

Enable `CONSUMER_SUBSCRIPTIONS_ENABLED=true` in the engine environment and recreate the container
to serve subscription routes and run delivery. The default is `false`. Subscriptions are deployment
state, separate from model releases. Switching delivery off removes all subscription routes, including reads, and stops the dispatcher.
It preserves stored subscriptions, but their undelivered events can expire while it is off.
Turning it back on resumes delivery subject to subscription validation and event retention;
expired positions suspend delivery as `EVENTS_EXPIRED`. Repeated requests to an absent route do
not turn it on. Check Deployment, enable the setting on the intended instance and recreate it.

An administrator or integration owner manages subscriptions on **Settings › Connections › Webhooks**.
Use [Subscribe a webhook and verify it](/docs/guide/integrate/subscribe-a-webhook-and-verify-it/) for the integration sequence and the
[API reference](/docs/api) for operations. Receivers need a consumer API that declares events.

## Find the subscription's state

Subscription management requires Integration administration for its workspace; an Operator role
alone does not grant it. On **Settings › Connections › Webhooks**, open the subscription by name.
Check the address, consumer API, workspace, selected events, filter tags and request format against
the receiver's configuration. The **Configuration** tab shows its state, suspension reason and
recovery advice. Authorised owners can edit, suspend, resume, rotate its key or delete it there.
Read current state before an edit: a version conflict requires reloading and reviewing the other
administrator's change.

A workspace with subscriptions cannot be deleted. Its refusal identifies the subscriptions to
review; delete unneeded subscriptions or keep the workspace. Retiring a workspace suspends its
subscriptions instead. Before resuming, correct the recorded cause: resume checks the model,
contract, filter and retained position again.

## Network and receiver requirements

Allow direct outbound HTTPS from the engine to receivers. A redirect is not followed: configure
the final URL. By default, a destination is refused if its address, or any address its host name
resolves to, is loopback, private, IPv6 unique-local, shared `100.64.0.0/10` or otherwise non-public.
The check runs when a subscription is created or changed and again at every delivery attempt.
Each attempt resolves DNS again and connects to the checked address. There is no host allowlist.

For a receiver inside your network, set `WEBHOOK_PRIVATE_ADDRESSES_ALLOWED=true` and recreate
the engine. It is off by default. Plain HTTP is accepted only for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or
`::1`, and also needs this setting on. Link-local addresses are always refused, even with the
setting on. A refused delivery records an `address` attempt with its reason in the delivery log.
After upgrading, existing subscriptions on private addresses stop delivering until the setting
is on; check their attempts and resume any that became suspended after correcting the cause.

Certificates must verify against the system trust store. For an internal CA, supply a bundle with
`SSL_CERT_FILE`. Delivery does not use an outbound proxy.

A receiver must durably accept the POST and return 2xx within ten seconds. Allow bodies up to 1 MiB
and larger for an unusually large single object. Verify the timestamp and `RDM-Signature`, and
deduplicate events by `eventId`: delivery is at least once. During key rotation, accept any valid
signature in the comma-separated header. Signing secrets must never be committed or logged.
[Consumer events and webhooks](/docs/integrate/consumer-events-and-webhooks/) explains the protocol.

## Retries and suspensions

Requests to one subscription stay ordered. A failed batch blocks later batches and keeps its events
and delivery ID while retrying after 10 seconds, 30 seconds, 1, 2, 5, 10 and 30 minutes, then hourly,
with 20% jitter. After 24 hours from its first failure, the subscription is suspended.
Inspect its pending attempt, last error and next-attempt time before restarting anything.

| Suspension | Recovery |
| --- | --- |
| `DELIVERY_FAILED` | Fix the receiver or URL, then resume from the first unacknowledged event. Editing the URL retries immediately. |
| `FILTER_MATCHES_NOTHING` | Fix the filter and resume. |
| `EVENTS_EXPIRED` | Resume with reset first (it starts after the feed head named in the message), then reload the receiver from current data taken after the reset. The publication named in the details may be older than the head. |
| `MODEL_CHANGED` | Review what the activated model removed; correct the subscription before resuming. |
| `CONTRACT_VERSION_CHANGED` | Update the receiver for the selected consumer contract, then resume. |
| `WORKSPACE_RETIRED` | Resolve the workspace's retired state before resuming delivery. |

Events derive from the change feed in the background, normally checked once per second. They expire
with `FEED_RETENTION_DAYS`, default 30, and are cleaned hourly. A consumer's `headPosition` is the
derived event head, which can lag the workspace feed. Several processes divide derivation by
workspace and delivery by a 60-second subscription lease.

## Retain delivery evidence

`CONSUMER_WEBHOOK_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` defaults to 7. The delivery log keeps request bodies up to
1 MiB and response excerpts up to 4 KiB, with attempts and durations. Retried or awaiting-resume
batches can remain longer. Expiry runs at most hourly. Inspect **Deliveries** on the webhook's page. Choose **Status**: **All**, **Queued**, **Sending**,
**Retrying**, **Succeeded**, **Failed** or **Dropped**, and use **Refresh** to read again.
The table shows **Event ID**, **Event**, **Object ID**, **Status**, **Attempts**, **Response** and
**Sent**. Open an event ID for the request as sent, each attempt and its response excerpt.
**No delivery has this status** can mean the filter is too narrow; **Nothing delivered yet** means
there are no retained deliveries to show, not proof the receiver never received data.

**Resend** sends the selected event again; an already delivered event asks **Resend a delivered
event?** before **Resend event**. A failed event can be resent directly. An event never sent has
nothing to resend and the control is disabled. A manual resend is marked with `RDM-Redelivery`;
the receiver must still deduplicate by event ID. It does not repair the subscription's normal
position or replace resolving its suspension. Operations summarizes failing and suspended subscriptions. Budget database space for these payloads
and restrict access to logs containing reference data. Your delivery capacity is **not measured**.

Rotate a subscription key when it leaks or policy requires it. The default overlap is 24 hours,
up to seven days; **Stop it now** selects zero, which ends the old key at the next delivery. Give the receiver the new key before
the overlap ends. This is separate from [resealing the installation's secrets](/docs/run/secrets-and-keys/).

Filters use a record's state at delivery time. A record leaving a filtered scope is not delivered
as a removal; deletions are always delivered. A receiver needing exact scope membership should
subscribe by type and narrow locally, or periodically reconcile its list.

The subscription defaults to one event per request. For a bulk workload, choose a larger batch
(up to 1,000 events); requests stop at 1 MiB except that a single larger event is sent alone.
A slow receiver adds its response time to each sequential request. Increase batching before
assuming another engine process speeds up one subscription; several processes share its lease
and preserve its order.

## Enable and check delivery without creating duplicate loads

Before enabling delivery, have an Integration administrator for the workspace, a consumer API with
events, a working HTTPS receiver, its signing-secret storage and enough retained feed history for
the expected outage window. The operator needs Docker and Operations access. CPU, database sizing
and delivery throughput for that receiver are **not measured** by this guide.

1. Set the capability in the private environment and recreate the engine:

   ```dotenv
   CONSUMER_SUBSCRIPTIONS_ENABLED=true
   ```

   ```bash
   docker compose up -d engine
   curl -i https://refiroo.example.org/health
   docker compose logs --tail=100 engine
   ```

   Expect readiness 200 and `webhookDispatcher` Running on Operations once a model is servable.
   No subscription means there is nothing to deliver; a running dispatcher alone is not a test
   of the receiver.
2. Ask the Integration administrator to review the subscription's URL, workspace, contract version,
   filter and retained position. Coordinate a harmless reviewed change with the data owner, then
   check the event and successful attempt in Deliveries and the receiver's durable event log.
3. Compare delivery ID, event ID and response status across both sides. Confirm that a retry of an
   already stored event is acknowledged without applying it again. Verification/deduplication is
   the receiver's responsibility; a successful HTTP answer does not prove its downstream update.
4. If delivery is failing, inspect the same pending batch and fix its cause. Do not delete and
   recreate the subscription merely to clear its state: that can abandon its recorded position.

These delivery-related environment settings are non-secret and need engine recreation:
`CONSUMER_SUBSCRIPTIONS_ENABLED`, `WEBHOOK_PRIVATE_ADDRESSES_ALLOWED`,
`CONSUMER_WEBHOOK_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` and `FEED_RETENTION_DAYS`.
The subscription's signing secret is secret database state sealed with the installation key.

## Recover a suspension in order

For `DELIVERY_FAILED`, repair the receiver's certificate, body limit, authentication or response
time, then resume the existing subscription. Inspect the first resumed delivery and the receiver
before declaring the backlog recovered. Later events wait behind the failed batch by design.
For `FILTER_MATCHES_NOTHING`, correct the saved filter, then resume and check its scope.

For `EVENTS_EXPIRED`, coordinate a full receiver re-sync with the integrator. Reset the subscription
first, then load the publication/list named by the refusal and reconcile the receiver. Reset starts
after the current head; it does not replay expired events. A receiver loaded before reset could
miss the interval between loading and reset. Preserve the old receiver state or a rollback copy
until reconciliation and later deliveries have been checked.

After `MODEL_CHANGED` or `CONTRACT_VERSION_CHANGED`, involve the model administrator and receiver
owner before resuming. After `WORKSPACE_RETIRED`, resolve the workspace's retirement intentionally;
repeated engine restarts do not change that state. Manual **Resend** is for a retained event and
does not move the normal subscription position or repair a suspension.

To pause the entire capability, restore `CONSUMER_SUBSCRIPTIONS_ENABLED=false` and recreate.
Subscriptions stay stored, while their events continue to age. To undo that pause, enable it again,
then inspect each subscription for expiry and validation failures. This is not an indefinite queue
retention switch. For a single receiver pause, use the subscription's suspend operation through
its administrator, retaining its identity and position.

The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over the timestamp, a literal dot and the exact request body:
`{RDM-Timestamp}.{body}`, using the subscription's signing secret. Receivers must check timestamp
freshness as well as the signature. An nginx receiver with its default 1 MiB body limit may refuse
an unusually large single event; arrange an adequate receiving limit before enabling delivery.

A dispatcher handles four subscriptions concurrently, while requests for each subscription stay
sequential. Each failed attempt writes one INFO line and each suspension one WARNING line. Check
these alongside the saved attempt history; adding processes does not parallelise one subscription.
guide/src/content/docs/use/account.md:
---
title: Your account
description: Check your sign-in, manage your own browsers and see what your roles allow.
reader: steward
---

Open the avatar at the top right and choose **Account** to see who you are signed in as,
manage your sign-in methods and inspect your permissions.

## The account menu

The avatar menu shows your name and the roles you hold in the workspace currently open. **Account**, **Notifications** and **All settings**
open those pages. **Theme** offers **System**, **Light** and **Dark**. System follows your device;
the choice is saved in this browser. **Sign out** ends your current sign-in.

![The avatar menu with account links, theme choices and Sign out](/docs/screens/use-account-menu.png)

*Above: Guide Admin's menu shows their roles in Graubünden. Other people can have fewer roles.*

## Your identity and sign-in

The account card shows your name, e-mail address, how you signed in and when.
These details help you check that you are using the intended account. **Sign out** on the card
ends the current browser's sign-in.

![Account with identity, password, passkeys and authenticator setup](/docs/screens/use-account.png)

*Above: Guide Admin signed in with a password and has not set up an authenticator app.*

### When an administrator manages your sign-in

If Account says **An administrator manages the sign-in of this account.**, the password,
passkeys, authenticator app and **Where you’re signed in** sections are not shown. Your
profile and **Sign out** remain. You can sign out of this browser, but you cannot sign out
other browsers or sign out everywhere.

You cannot change your own password, set up, confirm or remove an authenticator app, make
new recovery codes, or add, rename or remove passkeys. Ask a security administrator for a
password-setting link or help with a lost device. **Forgotten your password?** gives the
usual response but sends no mail for this account. See
[Help someone who lost a device](/docs/guide/administer/help-someone-who-lost-a-device/).

### When you manage your own sign-in

The controls depend on how you signed in. If your organisation provides sign-in, its password
is managed there. The local Password control appears when you signed in with your refiroo password.

To change that password:

1. Choose **Change password**. Enter **Current password** and **New password**.
2. Choose **Save new password**. A successful save keeps this browser signed in and signs out
   your other browsers. **Cancel** closes the form without changing the password.
3. If a password is refused, read the reason beside the field and correct it. A failed save
   does not change your password.

Under **Passkeys**, choose **Add a passkey** and follow your browser or device's instructions.
A WebAuthn passkey uses your fingerprint, face or device PIN to sign in, or to provide the second step.
Registered passkeys can be renamed so you can tell them apart, or removed. Removal asks for your
password or a code from your authenticator app. If the device prompt is cancelled, no passkey is added.

An authenticator app supplies time-based one-time passwords (TOTP). Under **Authenticator app**, choose **Set up an authenticator app**. Scan the displayed code with
your app, or enter its key, then enter **Code from the app** to confirm setup. Keep the recovery
codes shown afterwards somewhere safe: each works once if you lose access to your phone.
They are shown once. **New recovery codes…** replaces the old codes after you prove your sign-in;
the old ones then stop working. If the instance requires a second factor with a password, removal is offered only when a
passkey provides another way to meet that requirement. Otherwise, ask a security administrator.

## Where you’re signed in

Each row names a signed-in browser or other sign-in session and shows when it last acted and
when it signed in. **This browser** marks the one you are using. Several rows can have the same
browser name; use their times to distinguish them.

![Signed-in sessions with last activity, sign-in times and individual Sign out buttons](/docs/screens/use-account-sessions.png)

*Above: the reference account has many sessions from browser work and automated captures.
A row labelled Python-urllib is not another person's browser.*

Choose a row's **Sign out** to end that session. Choosing it for This browser signs you out here.
For a lost device or an unfamiliar session, **Sign out everywhere** asks for confirmation and
ends all your sessions, including this one, at their next request. It does not delete your work.
If ending a session fails, retry after reading the error; do not assume it has ended.

## What you can do

The bottom of Account lists your roles by workspace and what they allow: reading, proposing
changes, changing Live, publishing and approving. Restrictions may name particular applications
or record types. Instance-wide roles appear separately under **Across the instance**.

![Account permissions grouped by workspace and instance-wide responsibilities](/docs/screens/use-account-permissions.png)

*Above: Guide Admin holds Data owner for every workspace and five instance-wide administrative roles.*

This is a view of your access, not a form for granting yourself roles. Ask an access administrator
if something you need is missing. To act on a proposal, follow
[Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) or
[Approve a change set](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/). For notices and their email options,
see [Inbox and approvals](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/).

Each role is listed once, with the groups through which you hold it. A limited permission is
shown as a count: open it to see the applications and record types covered, and the roles that
allow each. On a phone, the workspace sections stack vertically.

Use **Settings › Notification email** for email choices: switch on **Email me when something arrives
in my inbox**, then choose **At once**, **Digest** or **Off** for each kind. Digests run every
morning or on Mondays at 07:00 in your browser's time zone; the page shows the next one. No unread
notices means no digest. The email switch is absent if mail is not configured or you have no
email address; the page explains why. **Settings › Appearance** holds display preferences.
For administrator-managed sign-in and help with lost devices, see
[Sign-in and second factors](/docs/administer/sign-in/).

## Sign-in and password help

Opening a saved application address without a session shows the sign-in page, in this browser's
theme. Use your e-mail address and password, a passkey, or the offered organisation's provider.
After signing in you return to the requested page. An ended session sends you there again.
A wrong e-mail address or password does not reveal which was wrong. Repeated failures slow attempts;
they do not permanently lock your account. Wait before retrying rather than repeatedly submitting.

Sessions renew while you work, but still have idle and overall expiry limits set by the operator.
If sign-in keeps ending unexpectedly, sign in again and ask an administrator to inspect the
session rather than changing unrelated record data. Under **General › Account**, **Loading your
account** is a loading state, not missing identity; retry a failed read.
The identity card can say **Signed in with your password**, **Signed in with a passkey** or
**Signed in with …**, with **Since …** for this session's start. **Where you’re signed in**
counts browsers and shows **Active now** or last activity with sign-in time.

The normal password rule is 15–128 characters. Common passwords and your e-mail address are refused;
use a longer distinct password, not repeated guesses. A development instance can have a lower
minimum, so the displayed refusal is authoritative. The current password is needed to change
it. Use the reveal buttons to check the current or new password privately. If you forgot it,
use **Forgotten your password?** when offered, or ask an administrator for a password-setting
link. The response does not reveal whether an account exists. Your organisation manages its
provider password separately.

**Add a passkey** opens a separate refiroo page. Give the passkey a recognisable name and provide
**Your password, or a code from your app** before the browser's device prompt. This proof prevents
an unattended signed-in browser adding a lasting sign-in method. Cancellation adds nothing.
Passkeys belong to the host where they were made; moving refiroo to another host affects them.
Renaming changes their display name only. Removing the last second factor can be refused where
one is required: add another passkey or set up an authenticator app first.

For display steps, see [Appearance and devices](/docs/use/appearance-and-devices/).
For the next digest time and delivery choices, see
[Notification settings](/docs/use/notifications-settings/).

An account using only an organisation's provider cannot add refiroo passkeys or an
authenticator app to bypass that provider. Manage those sign-in protections with your
organisation. If proof for adding or removing a passkey is refused, correct the password or
use a current authenticator or unused recovery code; a slowed sign-in needs time before retrying.

**Rename …** opens the passkey's **Name** field. Choose **Save** after changing it. **Remove …**
opens a separate confirmation with **Remove passkey**; it does not remove the device's other
passkeys. **New recovery codes…** asks for **Code from the app, or a recovery code**, then
**Make new codes**. Save the replacements: the old recovery codes stop working. Removing the
authenticator app uses **Remove the second factor** and **Remove it**; your recovery codes then
stop working too.

## Session limits and organisation sign-in

By default a session ends after 12 hours without use or 14 days in total, even if it has
continued renewing while you work. The operator can change these limits. Repeated failed
password attempts can delay another attempt by up to fifteen minutes; the account is not
locked permanently.

Your organisation can offer **Continue with** its OpenID Connect sign-in provider, such as
Microsoft Entra ID, Google or Keycloak. The provider handles its own second factors. On your
first sign-in, refiroo takes your name and email from the provider and updates membership of
its groups at sign-in. The roles granted to those groups determine what you can do here.

If you already had a local account, first provider sign-in can create a separate person.
Ask a security administrator to link the accounts so your existing roles and history stay
with the original person. Signing out of refiroo signs out of the provider too only when
that provider is configured to do so. If you can immediately sign in again without a password,
check whether the provider still has an open session.

**Forgotten your password?** asks for your e-mail address. It gives the same
response whether or not that account exists. A reset message is sent only for an account
with a local password and an email address whose sign-in is not managed by an administrator. For a provider account, reset your password with
the organisation instead. An administrator can supply a one-time password-setting link
when email recovery is unavailable.

## Sessions for an assistant

An external assistant you signed in for appears in **Where you’re signed in** as its name
followed by **(assistant)**. **Sign out** on that row ends its session, stopping it on its next
request. A blocked assistant also loses access; restoring it does not restore the ended session.
You must sign in for it again. Its sign-in page shows the name it claims and where it returns.
Check those details before allowing it. See [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/)
for what it may read, what it may prepare and why its provider privacy settings matter.

## Complete a second sign-in step

After your password, refiroo can ask for another proof of identity:

1. If **Use a passkey** is offered, choose it and complete the device prompt. Cancelling the
   prompt leaves you at sign-in; it does not remove your passkey.
2. To use an authenticator app, enter its current six-digit **Code** or **Code from the app**.
   Choose **Sign in** or **Sign in with the code**, as shown. A refused code needs a new
   current code; repeated failed attempts can require a wait.
3. If you cannot use the app, choose **Use a recovery code instead**, enter one unused
   **Recovery code** and choose **Sign in**. That code cannot be used again. **Use the app's
   code** returns to the ordinary code entry. **Start again** returns to the first sign-in step.
4. If setup is required before you can continue, scan the displayed code with your app or
   copy the displayed key into it. Enter **Code from the app** and choose **Confirm and
   continue**. Save the recovery codes when they are shown.

If you have lost all usable proofs, ask a security administrator to help restore access.
After removing a passkey in refiroo, also remove its saved entry from your device or password
manager; the entry there is not deleted automatically.

![Second sign-in step offering a passkey, an authenticator code and recovery-code sign-in](/docs/screens/use-sign-in-second-step.png)
guide/src/content/docs/use/ai-and-your-d:
---
title: AI and your data
description: Understand who can use AI help, what is sent, the costs and what is kept.
reader: steward
---

Before asking AI for help, check that the task and the data suit your organisation's rules.
AI can misunderstand a question or propose the wrong change. You review its work before
publishing it. Asking a list changes its filters, not its records.

## Which help is available

refiroo offers three separate kinds of help. Your operator chooses which are enabled.

- An AI provider turns a question into list filters, proposes mapping targets and explains changes.
  The provider can use the Claude API or a compatible service, including a model run inside your organisation.
- The built-in assistant uses Claude Code to read a workbook or your instructions and prepare
  a model and records for review. It can be enabled without the provider.
- An external assistant can connect through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), if your organisation
  enables agent access. It acts within your access, limited to reading and preparing change sets.

The **Use AI proposals** permission is needed for built-in AI actions. The predefined
**Data steward**, **Data owner**, **Model administrator**, **Workspace administrator** and
**Integration administrator** roles include it. Your grant determines which workspaces it covers.
Other permissions still apply: AI access alone does not let you import, change a model or publish.
An absent action can mean the feature is disabled, the data allowed to be sent is insufficient,
or you do not have the required access.

## What leaves the instance

An operator sets a ceiling on what refiroo's AI features may send. These are the send levels
named by the screens:

| Send level | What it allows |
| --- | --- |
| structure | Names of types and fields, headers, their rules and counts; no stored record values. Your question or instructions are still sent. |
| samples | Also sample values, normally up to a limit chosen by the operator. Questions in words have the short-list exception below. |
| values | The record values the feature needs. The sample limit does not cap this level. |

[Asking a list](/docs/use/ask-in-words/) sends your question, today's date and the fields and
relationships the list can filter. At samples or values, it also sends related-record names when
that type's list has at most 50 records in the current context. Ancestor names can be included too.
Those short lists are sent whole, regardless of the ordinary sample limit. At structure, no
stored record names are included. Anything you type into the question is sent at every level.

[Proposed mapping targets](/docs/use/mapping-grids/#targets-proposed-by-ai) need values. The
provider receives source and candidate target names and the fields shown by the grid.
[The assistant](/docs/use/loading-with-the-assistant/) also needs values: it receives your words,
the workspace's model and the whole workbook, if supplied, and reads the records its task needs.

[Explaining a period](/docs/use/history/#what-changed-in-a-period) sends counts and model labels.
Names of records, people, change sets and files are included only at values. Explaining a model
change sends the model's differences and counts, without record values. See
[Explain a model change](/docs/guide/model/explain-a-model-change/) for that model-administrator task.

Read the line beside an action before sending. An external provider receives the information
under your organisation's agreement with it. A local provider can keep it inside the organisation.
These send levels do not control what an external MCP assistant sends on after reading permitted data;
check that assistant's settings too.

## Costs and saved information

AI requests and assistant turns can incur charges or consume your organisation's subscription
allowance, even if they fail or you later discard the work. Your operator can see call records
under **Settings › Administration › AI**, including who asked, what for, the outcome, tokens and
reported cost. A missing cost means none was reported; it does not mean free usage. Provider
billing and Claude Code billing are separate. A saved workbook layout that fits the next file
can prepare it without another assistant session and without AI cost.

Call metadata is kept. Request and answer text is not kept in the call log by default; an operator
can enable it, normally for seven days. Assistant tasks keep instructions, proposals, checks and
the workbook for the configured retention period, normally 90 days after completion or the last
change. The session's working files and Claude Code transcript remain while the task can continue,
including after a failure, stop or load awaiting publication. They are removed when the completed
work is next checked, or on expiry. Turning off call-text logging does not remove those files.
Published records and their history remain when a task expires. The provider's own retention is
separate. See [AI operation and retention](/docs/run/ai/) for the full settings and limits.

## Your review stays necessary

Proposed mappings and loaded records wait in a change set. You correct them and follow the
workspace's normal approval and publication rules. The assistant cannot approve, publish or
activate a model. A whole-type model migration is different: a person's explicit migration
confirmation moves the records live. Read that preview before confirming it.

An external assistant cannot approve or publish either. If you sign in for one, refiroo's sign-in
page names the assistant and where it returns. That name is supplied by the assistant itself.
Check both before allowing it. Find its session in [your account](/docs/use/account/) to sign it out.
guide/src/content/docs/use/appearance-an:
---
title: Appearance and devices
description: Adjust the display and use refiroo with a keyboard, touch screen or phone.
reader: steward
---

Make refiroo comfortable to read in this browser. Open **Settings › Appearance**; changes
apply immediately and need no Save button. Other browsers and devices keep their own choices.
Follow [Change how refiroo looks](/docs/guide/use/change-how-refiroo-looks/) for the steps.

## Display choices

| Setting | Choices and effect |
|---|---|
| Theme | **Normal** or **Website purple** changes the application colours. Either works in light or dark mode. |
| Light or dark | **System**, **Light**, **Dark**. System follows your device's light or dark setting. |
| Table density | **Comfortable** or **Compact** sets the default; a table's own Display choice overrides it. |
| Type colours | **B: magenta and olive** or **A: plum and gold**. The palettes differ in their third and fourth colours. |
| Edit pencil | **On hover and focus** or **Always, faintly**. Touch screens always show edit hints. |

A table's **Display** menu controls visible columns, density, rows per page and column widths.
The identity column stays visible. These choices are remembered on this device for that view;
page size also travels in the address. **Reset display** restores its display defaults.
There is no column-reordering control in this menu.

Drag a panel's resize separator to change its width. Focus the separator and use Left/Right
for small changes, or Shift with those arrows for larger changes. Home chooses its minimum;
End chooses its maximum. Where reset is offered, Enter or double-click resets it.
**Resize record inspector** adjusts the inspection pane; **Resize record properties** adjusts
the record's properties. Availability and widths depend on the current layout.

## Keyboard operation

Opening a record collection or view puts focus on its page title; after deleting a record,
focus returns to the list heading. Tab then moves through controls with a visible focus indicator; Shift+Tab moves back. Use the skip
link at the beginning to reach the main content. Enter or Space activates a focused button.
Menus offer keyboard choices; Escape closes a menu or dialog. Enter saves a single-line inline
edit and Escape cancels it. Escape also clears the tree search or Notifications search. Dialogs keep Tab within them and
return focus when closed. Resolve an unsaved-input prompt before leaving an editor.

In a tree, Up/Down moves between visible records, Right expands or moves into children and
Left collapses or returns to the parent. Home/End reaches the first/last visible entry.
Shift+F10 opens the focused record's menu where available, as does right-click.
Use **Move to…** when dragging is inconvenient.

In tables, Up/Down moves row focus. Space toggles a focused selection checkbox; Shift extends
a range. Cmd/Ctrl+A inside a selectable table selects all matching records. Ctrl+Home and
Ctrl+End jump through long lists. These keys apply in their local controls; there is no global
command palette, search shortcut or shortcut-reference screen. Use each list's search: the
browser's Find sees only drawn rows of long lists.

## On a phone or touch screen

The band beneath the top bar keeps workspace, application and Live/change-set/publication
choices within reach. Open the navigation drawer for collections. In Settings, use the
**Settings: …** toggle for the navigation and the Back link to return. Panels can stack or
use tabs rather than staying side by side. On narrow tables, **Show all … columns** reveals
extra columns and **Show fewer columns** hides them again.

Tap a record to open it. In an editable tree, hold a record still for about half a second to
start a drag; moving sooner scrolls instead. Drag near an edge to scroll. A stationary release
in the sidebar opens its node menu. Read-only and publication trees do not drag. See
[Hierarchies](/docs/use/hierarchies/) for permitted destinations.

Long text can be read on hover, focus or touch; Escape closes its full-text box. Record and
relationship labels accompany colours, and controls have accessible names. These facilities
describe how to operate the interface, rather than a guarantee for every browser or assistive
device combination.

![Appearance settings with Normal and Website purple themes, light or dark mode, density and edit hints](/docs/screens/use-appearance-themes.png)

Settings groups its pages under **General**, **Administration**, **Data operations**,
**Security** and **Integration**. Your permissions determine which pages and groups appear.
**Jobs** lets you inspect background work; **Import profiles** needs Bulk and import, and
**Copy and move** needs the corresponding permission. A missing navigation entry does not
grant access through a copied address. Ask an administrator about missing permissions.

![Phone application navigation drawer with collections and record search](/docs/screens/phone-navigation-drawer.png)

## Help beside your work

Choose **?** in the top bar, to the left of the bell, to open the documentation in a new tab.
The documentation and API reference share a header: the logo returns to the application,
**Documentation** and **API reference** switch between them, and the documentation has search.
The **System**, **Light** and **Dark** theme choice is shared with the application, including
other open tabs in this browser.

The initial choices are **Normal**, **System**, **Comfortable**, **B: magenta and olive**
and **On hover and focus**. To return to those defaults, select them again. Clearing this
site's browser storage also loses display preferences, so keep any collection addresses you
need separately. Display preferences do not change your roles or the workspace model.
---
title: Applications
description: Understand the collections and the kinds of view an application can offer.
reader: steward
---

Open an application to reach the records and views you need in the current workspace.
Choose a workspace’s name or tile on Home to open its page: it offers record search, applications,
your waiting change sets and the five latest changes. **Edit model** and the workspace’s **⋯**
menu offer the actions and Settings pages your access allows.
Follow [Open an application](/docs/guide/use/open-an-application/) for the steps.

An **application** groups record types and views. Its name, collections and starting view come
from the workspace's model. Applications are not fixed modules of refiroo: a model can rename,
replace or remove them. Any application can offer any of the view kinds when the model
declares the structure that view needs.

## Collections and views

Choose an application in the top bar, then a collection in the sidebar. A collection can have
several views, shown as tabs under the list’s title. Changing tabs changes how you inspect the records; it does not
copy them. The model can choose which view opens when you select a collection in the
sidebar or on a group page. That choice may differ from the application's starting view;
use the tabs to switch to another view when needed. **Browse records** offers another route to individual records through their hierarchy. Open it to browse; it starts folded and remembers your choice in this browser.

![An application with collections, record browsing and a table of records](/docs/screens/app-network.png)

*Above: Network in Graubünden shows the Stops table and the collections declared by its model.*

| View | What you can do |
| --- | --- |
| Table | Search, filter and sort records, then open one. See [Records](/docs/use/records/) and [Find records](/docs/guide/use/find-records/). |
| Tree | Browse parents and children and move records to an allowed place. See [Hierarchies](/docs/use/hierarchies/) and [Arrange records in a tree](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/). |
| Mapping grid | Inspect connections, missing connections and multiple targets. See [Mapping grids](/docs/use/mapping-grids/) and [Map codes between systems](/docs/guide/use/map-codes-between-systems/). |
| Relationships table | List one relationship's records and its own values (a weight, a flag) as rows. Declared by the model; in the model contract (`relationTable`). |
| Relation matrix | Compare related records across columns and find missing connections. See [Relation matrices](/docs/use/relation-matrices/) and [Fill in a relation matrix](/docs/guide/use/fill-in-a-relation-matrix/). |

![A collection with a table and two mapping views](/docs/screens/app-systems.png)

*Above: System codes in Systems offers a table and mapping views. These are choices in the
example model, not features reserved for this application.*

A missing tab may mean the model does not declare that view. Ask a model administrator if you
need a different presentation. An empty table means no records match the current context and
filters; a loading error needs a retry before you can draw that conclusion.

## Shared workspace, different ways in

Applications in one [workspace](/docs/use/workspaces/) use that workspace's data. Relationships
may connect records across applications where the model allows it. The same record can appear
in a table, a hierarchy, a mapping grid and a relation matrix without becoming separate records.

The banner identifies **Live**, a **Change set**, or a publication. Live edits apply immediately;
a change set holds proposed changes; a publication is read-only. On a computer the band shows
only this data context, its explanation or change-set summary and the **Live · Change sets ·
Publications** switch. On a phone it also shows the workspace and application. Check the context before editing.
Your roles determine which actions are offered. A declared view does not grant permission to
change its records. See [Record permissions](/docs/use/records/#who-may-read-and-change-records).

For configurations of these capabilities, see [The example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/)
and [The starter model](/docs/examples/the-starter-model/).

## Collection groups and record pages

Ungrouped collections appear first. Expand or fold a labelled group with its arrow; your choice
is remembered in this browser. The model sets whether a group starts folded on your first visit. A folded group is marked when it contains the open collection.
Choose the group's name to open its page, search entries by name and open one in the same
Live, change-set or publication context.

A relation matrix the model places in a group has its own entry, named after the matrix's
view. Its matrix symbol uses the row collection's colour. Choose it to open the matrix
directly, from either the sidebar or the group page. The row collection stays in the sidebar
and still offers the matrix among its view tabs. A matrix without its own group entry is
available through that collection. Groups have one level and show no record counts.

![Application sidebar with a relation matrix listed alongside a collection in a group](/docs/screens/app-navigation-matrix-entry.png)

*Above: the Graubünden example model places Municipalities by system in a navigation group.
The matrix opens directly; its row collection is still available.*

A record page combines panels for fields, children, relationships, tables, hierarchy and history.
The model chooses their arrangement. If it declares no detail layout, refiroo provides a default.
The collection views above are the supported kinds; dedicated form and dashboard views are
not available.

The group page's **Find a collection or matrix** searches collection and matrix names. **This group has no collections or relation matrices.**
describes an empty group, rather than no records in its collections. For the shared table
controls, see [Lists, search and filters](/docs/use/lists-and-filters/).

On a wide screen, each application has a coloured tile in the top bar. The open application
is underlined; hovering over its tab shows the model's description. The product mark returns
to **Home**, and the gear opens **Settings**. Applications that do not fit are under **More**.
Settings opens an index grouped by task. Inside Settings, **← Back to** followed by the workspace’s
name returns to its page. On a phone, choose the application from the band
beneath the top bar instead. See [Appearance and devices](/docs/use/appearance-and-devices/).

If a group says **No collection or relation matrix in this group matches “…”**, clear **Find a collection or matrix**
or press Escape in that search field. This search covers collection and matrix names, not records.
Opening a collection result uses its chosen starting view; opening a matrix result goes straight
to that matrix. Both keep the current data context.

### Find a list in the sidebar

When an application has more than ten sidebar entries, **Find a list** appears under
**Collections**. Collections and relation matrices with their own sidebar entry count together,
including entries in folded groups. With ten entries or fewer, this search is not shown.

Type part of a list's name. The search ignores upper and lower case and matches your words
as one phrase within a name, in the order you type them. Reversing the words does not match
the same phrase. Matching letters appear in bold. It searches entries in every group and
those in no group, rather than the names of groups or records. The count beside **Collections**
shows the total, such as **25 lists**, then the matching count, such as **3 of 25**, while you
search. Screen readers announce count changes without interrupting you.

Groups with matches open and show only those entries; groups without matches disappear.
Their fold buttons are unavailable during the search. Choose a result, or press **Enter** in
the box to open the first match. The hint **Enter opens the first match · Esc clears** reminds
you of these keys. If **No list matches** appears, shorten or clear the text. Press **Esc** in
the box to clear it and restore each group's previous fold choice.

**Find any record** in the top bar searches record names across the workspace instead. Results
are grouped by record type and show each record’s place. Use the arrow keys to choose a result and
Enter to open it. Workspace search opens the record in **Live**; use a collection’s own search
to stay in a change set or publication. **Browse records** has no search box of its own. The group page's
**Find a collection or matrix** searches only that group's entries.
---
title: Asking a list in words
description: Turn a question into ordinary list filters and understand what the list can express.
reader: steward
---

Use **Ask** when you know which records you want but are unsure how to set their filters.
The answer becomes search text and ordinary filter pills. It changes which records you see;
it does not change any record. Follow [Ask a list in words](/docs/guide/use/ask-a-list-in-words/).

## Where Ask is offered

A table collection offers **Search** and **Ask** beside its search box when an AI provider is
enabled and you have **Browse** and **Use AI proposals** in the workspace. Ask works in Live,
a change set and a publication. It is absent from mapping grids, trees and the Changes page.
You can always use the list's ordinary [search and filters](/docs/use/lists-and-filters/).

## What a question can become

Ask can use the view's filter fields and every relationship of the listed record type,
including relationships absent from **＋ Filter**. In Live it also offers **Created** and
**Updated**. Those two times are unavailable in change sets and publications.

You can ask for field values, missing relationships, or records with a relationship below a
named ancestor at any depth. The result uses the list's existing conditions. Ask cannot
choose a sort order or find who changed a record. Use the sort controls or record History
for those tasks. Questions are limited to 500 characters.

When you name a related record, refiroo looks for an exact name, ignoring letter case, then
for a single name containing your words. No match or several matches means that part is not
expressed; it does not pick a record for you. Use a more complete name and ask again.
Choosing records by the meaning of their names needs the short-list names described below.
For larger lists, give an exact or unambiguous partial name.

## Read the result before relying on it

A complete answer applies its search and filters to the list, replacing the previous search
and filters. The line **Your question became these filters. Change or remove any of them.**
appears. Check each pill: the provider can misunderstand your intent. Open a pill to edit it,
remove it with **×**, or return to Search. The current sort stays as it was.

If any part cannot be expressed, the list stays as it was. A warning names the missing part
and shows **What it could do:** as dashed pills. **Use these filters** applies only that
partial answer. Review what was left out before choosing it. A failed request applies
nothing and keeps your question, so you can correct it, retry or use Search instead.

![Ask showing a part it cannot express and the filters available for review](/docs/screens/use-ask-partial.png)

## What is sent and kept

Your question, today's date, field names and relationship definitions go to the configured
provider when you press Enter, not as you type. At structure, no stored record names are
included. At samples or values, related-record and ancestor names are also included when
their type's list contains at most 50 records in this context. That short list is sent whole.
Your own words are sent at every level, so include only information you are allowed to send.

Requests can incur provider costs and are recorded with their outcome. Request and answer
text is kept in the call log only if the operator enables it. Read
[AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) for permissions, retention and provider privacy.
guide/src/content/docs/use/change-sets.m:
---
title: Change sets
description: Understand coordinated changes, review, validation, publication, approvals and model versions.
reader: steward
---

A change set is a place to prepare related changes away from live data, review their combined
effect and publish them together. It belongs to a workspace. It can contain changes across that
workspace's applications, including new records, corrections, moves, relationships and deletions.

Use one when a group of changes needs to go live together or needs review before publication.
For an everyday correction that should be visible immediately, you can
[correct the record in Live](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/). Having an open change set does not
prevent direct live work, and changing many records does not by itself require a change set.

For the working sequence, see
[Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/).

For preparing specific kinds of change, see [Relate records](/docs/guide/use/relate-records/),
[Arrange records in a tree](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/),
[Map codes between systems](/docs/guide/use/map-codes-between-systems/) and
[Fill in a relation matrix](/docs/guide/use/fill-in-a-relation-matrix/).


## Where a change set starts

A change set starts from a copy of data at a particular moment. Its source is shown alongside
its name, version and model release in the change-set list; inside it, open **Details** in the
band to read its source, creator, creation time, version and model.

| Source | What the change set initially contains |
| --- | --- |
| Current live data | Live records and relationships at creation, including direct corrections made since the last publication. |
| A publication | The records and relationships in that retained snapshot, using the model release it was published under. |

**Start from current live data** creates the first kind. A publication's menu offers
**Start a change set from this publication** for the second. Neither action changes live data or
creates a publication. See the
[starting instructions](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/#start-or-open-a-change-set).

Starting from an older publication does not restore it over current data. Only changes deliberately
made in the change set are applied when it publishes. Newer live records and corrections that
the change set leaves untouched remain in place.

![The change-set list with its source, version and creation details](/docs/screens/change-sets-list.png)

*Above: the Network application in the Graubünden workspace lists December 2026 timetable change.
It started from current live data. The button offers a separate new change set.*

## Working apart from Live

Inside a change set, lists and record pages show the starting copy with your proposed changes
applied. Later live edits do not refresh that copy. People reading Live continue to see live
data, and other people can keep correcting it while the change set is open.

The orange **Change set** band shows its name, number of changes and state in one row on a
computer. Edits stay in this change set until it is published. The green **Live** banner says that edits apply immediately in the
workspace. Check this context before saving. The ordinary record controls work in either context;
their destination is different. See
[Make the changes](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/#make-the-changes) and
[Correct a record](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/).

![An open change set above a collection of records](/docs/screens/change-set-open.png)

*Above: December 2026 timetable change is open over the Stops list. The orange banner identifies
the proposed data and offers Review changes, Validate change set and Publish change set.*

A change set can be shared by people with access to the workspace. It has its own version,
so a save based on an older change-set version can be refused after another person changes it.
Refresh and review their work before retrying. This protection is separate from the record
version described in [Records](/docs/use/records/#versions-and-refused-saves).

## Review explains the differences

Opening a change set from the list opens **Changes in this change set**, which compares it
with its starting data. Choose **See the data with these changes** to browse or edit its lists.
A newly created change set, or your own open change set from Home’s **Continue where you left off**,
opens on the data. From there, **Review changes** in the band opens the comparison. **Records** shows additions,
changes and removals, including moves and type changes where applicable. A row identifies the
record and its path; expanding it shows the before and after details. **Relationships** shows
changes to connections. Filters help narrow the review to a kind of change or a type.

For a change set started from a publication, “before” means that publication. It does not mean
today's live data. Review describes what the change set proposes; validation and publishing also
check whether those proposals can be applied safely now.

Follow [Review and validate](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/#review-and-validate)
for the controls and the route back to editing.

![The Records tab of Review changes with changed fields and record paths](/docs/screens/change-set-review.png)

*Above: the timetable change proposes changes to Valid to (exclusive) on several stops.
The Records tab lists them; Relationships is a separate tab for connection changes.*

## Validation checks the whole proposal

**Validate change set** checks the complete proposed data against its model, including required
values and relationships, allowed structure and uniqueness rules. Some problems can only be
judged across the whole set of records. Individual successful saves do not replace this check.

Validation changes no live data and creates no publication. Problems identify what needs
attention. A successful check displays **Change set validation passed**. In the direct publication
flow, that check enables **Publish change set** for the validated version. Editing afterwards
requires validation again.

A passed check is not a reservation of live data. Someone can still make a live edit or publish
another change set before you publish. Publishing checks the current situation again. For the
sequence, see [Review and validate](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/#review-and-validate).

## Publishing and intervening live work

Publishing applies the change set's changes over current live data and records the result as
the next publication. The whole operation succeeds together or changes nothing. There is no
partially published change set.

Unrelated live work survives. A new live record is kept if the change set has not changed it;
a live correction to a record left untouched by the change set is kept too. Publication is not
a replacement of Live with the older copy you have been editing.

If both Live and the change set changed the same record, publishing is refused and names the
conflict. This can happen even when different fields were changed. The combined result must
also satisfy the model: changes that are valid separately can conflict when brought together.
An invalid combined result publishes nothing.

The confirmation is also tied to the current publication and the change-set version that were
reviewed. If these have changed meanwhile, the stale attempt is refused. Live data and the change
set are kept. Review the reported conflicts and the latest live data before preparing another
attempt; retrying does not authorise overwriting another person's work.

The [Publish instructions](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/#publish) explain the
confirmation. Success is reported as **Published as Publication** followed by its number. The
change set's work is then live and represented by that publication.

![Successful validation behind a publication confirmation](/docs/screens/change-set-publish-confirm.png)

*Above: the timetable change has passed validation and the Publish this change set? confirmation
is open. The screenshot shows a proposal awaiting confirmation; nothing has been published.*

## When approval is required

A workspace can require approval and a second person to decide. The banner then offers
**Submit for publication** where appropriate; submission validates and waits for a decision,
without making changes live. These policies do not remove separately granted Live editing rights.
Administrators configure them under [Approval policies](/docs/administer/approval-policies/).

For waiting, withdrawal, sending back and resubmitting, see
[Inbox and approvals](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/#from-submission-to-decision).
Follow [Approve a change set](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/) for the working steps.

## Publications keep the result

A **publication** is a read-only snapshot of a workspace created by a successful publish. It
keeps the model release it was published under, rather than showing its records through today's
definitions. Later live corrections and model changes do not rewrite it.

Publications have numbers within the workspace. A new publication becomes **Current**, replacing
the previous one's current designation. Older snapshots remain available. Current means the
designated publication; it does not mean the snapshot includes live corrections made after it.

The **Publications** list offers **Open publication**, its model version, when and by whom it was
published, and its source and predecessor. Opening one is read-only. For the relationship between
publishing and the resulting snapshot, see
[Publish](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/#publish).

For snapshot rules, see [Publications](/docs/use/publications/). To open and inspect one, follow
[Browse a publication](/docs/guide/use/browse-a-publication/).

## Withdraw a request, discard a change set, or withdraw a publication

These actions have different effects:

| Action | What happens to the proposed work | What happens to Live and publications |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Withdraw request | Ends a pending submission; keeps the change set for further editing. | Nothing changes. |
| Discard change set | Removes the change set and its staged work after confirmation. | Live records and existing publications stay unchanged. |
| Withdraw publication | Keeps the snapshot, marking it Withdrawn and no longer Current. | Live records and history stay unchanged; no publication is current. |

**Discard change set** is on the change-set menu when the set is editable. A pending request
must first leave its submitted state. Discarding is still possible when the change set's model
release differs from the workspace's release. See the
[change-set guide](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) for the editing context.

**Withdraw publication** is offered for the current publication, with confirmation. It does not
restore older data, select an older publication as current, delete records or retire the workspace.
A retained publication can still be the source of a new change set, as described under
[Where a change set starts](#where-a-change-set-starts).

## Preparing for another model release

A change set uses a particular model release. With the necessary access, a new change set can
use an installed newer release while Live keeps using the workspace's current release. Its
forms, fields, rules and views then come from the selected release. Incompatible starting data
can prevent creation; refiroo reports the records that do not fit.

The change set cannot publish normally until its release matches the workspace's active release.
The banner explains a mismatch. A model administrator can activate the intended release when
the data is compatible. Where migration is available, the banner also offers a reviewed move of
the change set to the workspace's release, or a move of the workspace to the change set's release
with publication. These options depend on permissions and the deployment's available features.

**Change model version** can select another release when the existing content fits it. It does
not silently convert incompatible records. A refused change leaves the original release and
content in place. Discarding remains an alternative for work that is no longer needed.

For ordinary data changes, keep the current **Model version** in the
[creation form](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/#start-or-open-a-change-set).
Coordinate a different release with a model administrator before preparing work under it.

## Who may do what

Roles granted directly or through a group determine access in a workspace. Custom roles can
combine permissions differently from the predefined roles below.

| Permission | What it allows | Predefined roles that include it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browse | Open change sets, read their records, review differences and browse publications. | Reader, Contributor, Data steward, Data owner |
| Work in change sets | Create, edit, validate and discard change sets; submit for publication. | Contributor, Data steward, Data owner |
| Publish | Publish a change set directly, subject to approval policy; withdraw the current publication. | Data steward, Data owner |
| Approve publications | Decide a submitted change set: approve and publish, or send back. | Data owner |

Creating a new change set and opening an existing one need different permissions: opening and
reviewing are reads. A reviewer with **Browse** does not thereby gain approval rights. A person
with **Publish** alone does not gain **Approve publications**. In the browser, preparing a direct
publication also needs **Work in change sets** to run validation.

Write grants can be narrowed to applications or record types. This includes edits and publication;
permission for one type does not authorise publishing changes to other types. Reading is available
across the workspace where **Browse** is granted. Model administration and workspace administration
roles do not by themselves give the data permissions above. A retired workspace permits reads
but refuses change-set work and publication.

See [Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) for the
working flow and [Records](/docs/use/records/#who-may-read-and-change-records) for direct editing
permissions.

## Model-version actions on the banner

The amber strip's **More change set actions** menu holds model-version changes and discarding.
When the releases differ, **Move this change set to …** previews converting the proposal onto
the workspace's release. Review converted values, type changes, accepted removals and items
that must be fixed, then confirm **Move change set**. This changes no Live data or workspace
release. Unchanged records then read as they are live.

The alternative **Move … to … and publish…** moves the workspace to the change set's release.
It requires model-release access, model administration and background jobs. Review the migration,
explicitly accept any removals and resolve all items to fix, including live conflicts. Confirm
**Migrate and publish** only when ready: migration and publication happen together or neither
does. Opening either preview changes nothing. A stale review needs **Preview again**.

Policy configuration belongs to
[Approval policies](/docs/administer/approval-policies/). A pending request may be withdrawn by
its submitter or an authorised approver before editing resumes.

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0.*

## Special review cases and recovery

The list shows each change set's version, source, model and creator. **Untitled change set**
is the fallback name. Use **Load more change sets** for older entries. **Empty bootstrap**
identifies a change set with no starting records; its initial changes are additions only.
The ordinary browser creation button starts from current Live, not an empty root.

A created record deleted again in the same proposal is omitted from review. A record saved
back to its original fields can still appear as **Saved unchanged**: publishing claims its
version and must still check for Live changes. In **Relationships**, **Show parent links**
reveals containment connections otherwise hidden because moves already appear as Parent changes.
**Clear filters** restores the complete review; **No changes yet** and **Nothing matches** have
different meanings. Follow [Review what a change set changes](/docs/guide/use/review-what-a-change-set-changes/).

Unique field values are checked immediately, including in a change set. A direct swap of two
held unique values is refused; plan an intermediate valid value where permitted. Some
ancestor-scoped relationship conflicts can be staged but fail validation or publication.
A profile deleting records absent from a file can load only into a change set.

Publishing coordinates with Live writes in the same workspace; unrelated change sets remain
available for work. If a colleague changes this change set between background-job chunks,
the job can stop at its next chunk and retain earlier applied chunks. Read its results on
[Jobs](/docs/use/jobs/) before retrying.

A submitted change set cannot be edited or moved to another release until its request is
withdrawn by the submitter or an approver. Open work is shared with authorised workers, not
reserved for its creator. **More change set actions** holds discard and version actions;
there is no rename form here.

A release switch protects unsaved input and reloads the pinned model before enabling edits.
Old list positions are cleared; a disappeared page can lead to another model-declared view.
If **Model version changed, but the interface could not refresh…** appears, the release change
already succeeded. Reload and check the pinned release before editing. Other action failures
say **Change set action could not be completed** and keep the diagnostic reason.
See [Prepare under the next model version](/docs/guide/use/prepare-under-the-next-model-version/).

Other useful tasks are [Continue live work](/docs/guide/use/continue-live-work-while-a-change-set-is-open/),
[Start from an earlier publication](/docs/guide/use/start-from-an-earlier-publication/) and
[Propose a change](/docs/guide/use/propose-a-change/).
guide/src/content/docs/use/changing-many:
---
title: Changing many records
description: Select records, preview a bulk change and understand refusals before applying it.
reader: steward
---

Change fields or relationships across a collection, or delete selected records, after reviewing
a preview. These actions need **Bulk and import**, permission to write the selected types in the
current context, and a deployment that allows jobs. Publications and retired workspaces are
read-only. A Contributor works in a change set rather than Live.

## Choose exactly which records

Tick individual row checkboxes, use Shift for a range, or select the rows shown. The selection
bar counts them. **Select all … matching**, or Cmd+A when the collection selection handles the
shortcut, selects every record matching the search and filters, including rows not yet drawn.
Untick individual records to leave them out. **Clear selection** removes the selection.
Check whether the bar says a count or **All … matching except …** before starting an action.

The deployment limits how much one change can hold. An oversized selection reports its count,
the limit and what to do: narrow the list or select fewer records. A relationship change may
make several changes per selected record, so its limit can be reached sooner.

## Preview, then apply

- [Change values](/docs/guide/use/change-values-of-many-records/) sets or clears selected fields.
  Fields not added to the change keep their values.
- [Change relationships](/docs/guide/use/change-relationships-of-many-records/) adds, removes or
  replaces one kind of connection. It does not edit fields on the connections themselves.
- [Delete many records](/docs/guide/use/delete-many-records/) includes children and owned dependants.
  Independent connected records stay.

Choose whether a refusal should **Change the rest** or **Change none**. The all-or-nothing
choice has its own deployment limit and disappears when this change exceeds it. Deletion uses
the corresponding delete choices. Nothing is written by **Preview**. Read the counts of changes,
unchanged records and refusals, and open refused records to inspect their reasons.

**Apply** checks the records again. Someone else's saved changes are refused instead of
overwritten. A relationship change also checks that the connections have not changed since
preview. A deletion checks the exact impact, including children added in the meantime.
For a sampled deletion preview, only items whose impact was actually previewed are authorised;
other items need a new preview and may be refused during execution.

## Finish or leave the dialog

The result reports what actually changed, what did not need changing and what was refused.
**Preview again** retries against the data as it is now. The selection remains for another
change; deleted records leave it. Do not assume a finished job means every item succeeded.

Before applying, **Back**, closing the dialog or clicking outside cancels its waiting preview.
**View job** keeps the preview waiting on its [job page](/docs/use/jobs/), where you can apply
or cancel it. Once applying, **Keep running in the background** leaves the job working.
Stopping a job does not undo chunks it has already committed. If a colleague changes a shared
change set between chunks, the next chunk can fail while earlier chunks remain applied.

![Selected rows and selection bar, followed by a Change values preview with changed, unchanged and refused counts and Apply.](/docs/screens/bulk-selection-preview.png)

## Default limits

Normally one background change can hold up to 1,000,000 items, a preview tries at most
10,000 items, and **Change none** or **Delete none** can hold at most 10,000 items.
The operator can change these limits; use the count and limit shown by your dialog.
An item is a requested change, so one selected record can contribute several items to a
relationship change. A sampled preview is not a promise that all remaining items can succeed.

For **Delete**, the refusal choices are **Delete the rest** and **Delete none**. The first
allows valid deletions to continue when another item is refused. The second applies none
unless the whole operation can succeed within its limit.
guide/src/content/docs/use/copying-and-m:
---
title: Copying and moving records
description: Use a saved model mapping to prepare records in another workspace and review what stays behind.
reader: steward
---

Copy records when another workspace needs its own data. Move them when the source records
should also be removed after the destination is ready. Both operations prepare change sets;
neither publishes automatically. Follow [Copy or move records to another workspace](/docs/guide/use/copy-or-move-records/).

A **model mapping** describes what source types, fields, parents and relationships become
in the destination. It can also identify existing destination records to update. Have a model
administrator prepare and check it; see [Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/).
This differs from a [mapping grid](/docs/use/mapping-grids/), which connects records inside
one workspace. Switching workspaces alone never copies records.

## Access and starting data

Open **Settings › Data operations › Copy and move**. You need access to read the source and
**Copy and move** for the destination; a move also needs **Work in change sets** for the
source deletion proposal. Review and
publication need their own workspace permissions. This page does not give you publication
rights. Background jobs and model administration must be enabled; otherwise the page explains
why copying and moving are read-only. Ask an administrator about absent workspaces or actions.

**Mappings** lists saved instructions. **Recent copies and moves** shows operations and waiting
dry runs. Check it before starting the same transfer again. The source and destination must
be different workspaces. Their model releases must match the releases used by the mapping.

## What is checked before starting

Choose **Copy** or **Move**, then the records to include: **Every mapped type**, **The whole
workspace**, **Chosen types** with optional filters, or **One record and everything under it**.
A subtree includes its descendants. A whole-workspace choice can leave out unmapped types;
read the report rather than assuming everything will transfer.

The dry run checks every selected record and relationship without writing them. Review records
created or updated, records that cannot transfer, relationships carried or dropped, and
**Values not carried**. A record can transfer while losing an unmapped field. Missing required
values, unsuitable parents, incompatible values and unresolved relationship ends need attention.
Ask the mapping owner to correct its choices; do not invent data just to pass a check.

![Copy dry run showing the two workspaces, selected scope, record counts and omissions](/docs/screens/use-copy-dry-run.png)

Changing the mapping or selection checks again. If **The mapping names other releases than
the workspaces run** appears, coordinate **Use the releases the workspaces run** with the
mapping owner, inspect the changes and obtain a fresh dry run. **Nothing to copy** or
**Nothing to move** means no selected record would be created or updated; confirmation cannot
make that empty selection useful.

## What happens after confirmation

**Copy** prepares a target change set and keeps the source. **Move** also prepares a source
deletion change set. A source record changed since the dry run, or required by records staying
behind, is kept with a reason. Publication of the source deletions is refused until the target
copy has been published. Review each proposal and its workspace's approval requirements separately.

The running job continues when you leave the page. Its actual result can differ from the dry
run after another person's changes. **Review the change set** opens the target proposal;
**Review the deletions** opens the source removal proposal where one was made. **The copy did
not complete** or **The move did not complete** needs inspection of the job and any retained
change sets before retrying. Read [Jobs](/docs/use/jobs/) for cancellation and retention;
stopping a job is not an undo of proposed chunks already written.

Copies keep their correspondence to the source. A later transfer can update the earlier copy;
a move back can update the original or recreate its original identity. Review matching decisions
and current values before repeating a transfer. This is a separate dataset, not a continuously
synchronised mirror.

## Change your mind

Before starting, cancel the confirmation to keep the dry run without loading records. After
loading, use the ordinary change-set controls to discard an unwanted proposal, after checking
for colleagues' edits. Do not publish its source deletions if you intend to retain the originals.
Once published, correcting data requires new reviewed changes; removing a saved mapping does
not reverse a transfer. Mapping changes and deletion belong to its administrator and affect
future operations, not already published copies.
guide/src/content/docs/use/hierarchies.m:
---
title: Hierarchies
description: Understand trees, parents and children, allowed placements and moves.
reader: steward
---

A hierarchy places records under parents so you can browse and maintain their structure. Use
[Arrange records in a tree](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/) to expand branches,
rename records and move them.

## Parents, children and branches
