A record has at most one parent. Records directly inside it are its children; all the records
below it are its descendants. The path on a record's page shows its ancestors. A branch can
contain several record types, or repeat the same type through several levels.

The model defines which types may contain which others and which types may stand at the top
without a parent. A type label grouping records in a tree is navigation, not another record.
A tree view shows the roots and types chosen by the model; it need not show every record in the
workspace. The sidebar’s **Browse records** tree is another route to records. Open its folded
heading to browse; your choice is remembered in this browser. Use **Find any record** in the
top bar to search names across the workspace.

![A tree expanded from a canton through a district and municipality to stops](/docs/screens/tree-geography-chur.png)

*Above: Geography in Network follows Graubünden through Plessur and Chur to Chur's stops.
Cantons, Districts, Municipalities and Stops are type groups between record levels.*

![A tree in which parent and child records have the same type](/docs/screens/tree-modes.png)

*Above: Modes in the same application has Mode records below other Mode records. Rail-bound
contains Funicular, Metro, Rack railway, Train and Tram. This is another model-defined hierarchy.*

## What a move changes

Moving changes a record's parent. Its descendants move with it, keeping their places relative
to that record. The record keeps its identity and history. refiroo changes the parent and the
containment relationship together; ordinary relationship editing cannot change only one of them.

A move is refused if the destination has a disallowed type or would create a cycle, such as
moving a record into itself or one of its descendants. The **Move to…** dialog lists destinations
with a reason beside unavailable choices. **Top level** means no parent; it is available only
where the model and the view permit that placement. A record allowed at the top of the workspace
may still be outside the roots shown by this particular tree.

In Live, a move preserves the record's type. In a change set, a destination marked **Becomes**
can offer a type change. That opens a preview of the resulting types and fields before applying
it to the change set. Review what needs values and what is retained only in history. Live data
changes only when the change set is published. Do not use this route for an ordinary move unless
you intend to change the type too.

## Other tree actions

Where configured, a record's menu offers adding a child, renaming and changing availability.
The model chooses the allowed child types and whether an availability field exists. Renaming
keeps the record's identity. Availability is a field value; it does not remove the record.

Change sets can also offer restructuring actions such as **Change type…**, **Insert level above…**
and **Remove this level…** where allowed. These require reviewing their preview and the proposal
before publication. They are different from merely folding a branch or moving it.

Deleting a parent can delete its descendants. Review [record deletion](/docs/use/records/#deleting-a-record)
and the impact shown before confirming; collapsing a branch never deletes it.

## Access and recovery

**Browse** allows reading a tree. Editing needs **Edit live** or **Work in change sets** for the
records affected, and the view must offer the action. See
[Record permissions](/docs/use/records/#who-may-read-and-change-records). A publication or retired
workspace is read-only. A change set awaiting approval may need to be withdrawn before editing.

A move based on an older record version can be refused. Review the latest parent and values
before trying again. A loading error is not evidence that a branch has no children: retry it.
For related records that do not determine placement, see [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/).

## Browse and move several records

The sidebar tree handles hierarchies of any size and depth. Its search lists matching records
of every type with their paths. Type groups fold like records; a single top-level group starts
open. Expanding can also open its only child one level further. Long groups load as you scroll;
**Show earlier records** reads the part above a group opened midway through. Your sidebar place
is kept within the application and workspace.

Use Cmd or Ctrl to add or remove a record from selection, Shift for a range, Ctrl+Space to
select by keyboard and Shift+arrows to extend it. Escape clears selection. Drag the selected
records together or open **Move to…** with right click or Shift+F10. One confirmation moves
all selected records or none. On touch screens, hold still for half a second until the record
lifts; moving earlier scrolls. Rest near an edge while dragging to scroll to the destination.

Type groups normally start folded; the sole top-level group is the exception and starts open.
Expanding a group or record opens its only child one level further without repeatedly
expanding an entire branch. Loading more records keeps the sidebar's scroll position.
On touch screens, the drag preview stays above your finger. Letting go at the starting place
does not open the record; in the sidebar it opens the record's menu instead.

## Restructure in a change set

Besides **Becomes** destinations, the node menu can offer **Change type…**,
**Insert level above…**, **Remove this level…** and **Change type of all … in here…**.
Only model-permitted changes appear. A preview lists each resulting type, values and origin,
values still needed and anything with no place in the new structure. Content with no place is
kept in history. Records retain their IDs and history; the new structure reaches Live only
when the change set publishes. Cancel the preview if the result does not match your intent;
resolve missing values before proceeding.

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0. See [The example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/)
for sources and fictional additions.*

## Ordering, limits and changing back

A parent must be in the same application and workspace. Its type must be allowed to contain
the child. A self-hierarchy can continue to any depth, but a record cannot become its own
ancestor. Moving beneath a new ancestor also rechecks uniqueness in that scope.
A tree drop chooses a parent or level, not a position among siblings; the model's order decides
that position. Moving several selected records together requires their types to stay unchanged.
Follow [Move several records together](/docs/guide/use/move-several-records-together/).

Restructuring carries fields between equal value types, and can widen text to long text or
whole numbers to decimal numbers without losing information. A value failing the destination's
rules becomes a required answer in the preview. Values and connections with no place remain
in history. A later type change can offer them back from effective earlier reclassifications
in the current or published change sets, keeping restored connections' identities. Deliberately
cleared values and discarded work are not restoration sources.

An operation can restructure at most 500 records. A larger subtree is refused with its limit;
choose a smaller operation and inspect its impact. The preview also becomes stale if the
change set changes before applying. Follow [Reshape a hierarchy](/docs/guide/use/reshape-a-hierarchy/).
Opening an old address for a retyped record follows its current type in the selected context;
review filters can match either the old or new type.

A tree view opens a record beside the list, with **Expand to full page** for its full page.
An explorer-tree record opens without a collection behind it. A table record instead offers
**←** and the list’s name in the line above its title, followed by its parents where shown. **Resize navigation rail** changes the rail width; see
[Appearance and devices](/docs/use/appearance-and-devices/) for keyboard resizing.

The rail is named **Browse application**, or **Application navigation** in its phone drawer.
A **Move to…** dialog for several selected records is headed **Move … records**. Search
**Search new locations**, or choose **Top level — No parent** where allowed. **Not every record
can move there** means the destination does not fit the whole selection; revise the selection
or choose another parent. **Could not save the change** leaves a failure to resolve; **Dismiss**
closes the message, without applying the refused change.
guide/src/content/docs/use/history.md:
---
title: History
description: Find what changed on a record, across a workspace or in one person’s work.
reader: steward
---

Use history to find who changed data and when. Start from a record for one item's past,
a workspace for activity across records, or Home for your own work.
Follow [See who changed what](/docs/guide/use/see-who-changed-what/) for the steps.

## A record's History

In **Live**, a record page’s **History** shows the newest entries first.
The record History panel is absent inside a change set or publication. Use
[Review changes](/docs/guide/use/review-what-a-change-set-changes/) for a change set’s
prepared differences, or return to Live for the record’s history. **All**, **Values**,
**Relationships** and **Moves** select kinds of event. **By** narrows the entries to one person;
**Anyone** removes that restriction. Expand an entry with its arrow to see recorded details,
including previous values where available.

![A record's History with event kinds, author and time](/docs/screens/use-history-stop-changed.png)

*Above: Thusis Süd records the Abbreviation change and the later update applied by publication.
The details panel shows the current abbreviation, THSD.*

Creation, field changes, relationship changes and moves are different events. A successful Live
save appears in history; a refused save is not a saved correction. Work prepared in a change set
and work applied by publication have different contexts. Read the cause alongside the person
and time rather than assuming two lines mean two direct live edits.

History names the person or client responsible, using their current name. Earlier events recorded
before sign-in was recorded read **Before sign-in**. Renaming a person does not mean another person performed
the old action. Read access is limited to workspaces you may browse.

## Activity across a workspace

The workspace’s page shows its five **Latest changes**. For more activity, where your access
opens workspace management, choose **Settings**, **Workspaces**, the workspace,
then **Activity**. Its **What** choices are **Everything**, **Records**, **Relationships**,
**Change sets** and **Publications**. Entries identify the action, person and time, and can also
name its change set or publication context.

![Workspace Activity with kind filters and changes across records](/docs/screens/use-history-activity.png)

*Above: Graubünden's Activity shows the creation and validation of the correction change set,
the record update and Publication 1, newest first.*

## A person's changes

On [Home](/docs/use/home/), **Your recent changes** gives a short list. **See all your changes**
opens **Your changes**. Choose **Workspace**, **What** and **Period** to narrow it. A person's
linked name can also lead to their changes, within the workspaces you may read.

![Your changes filtered by workspace with What and Period choices](/docs/screens/use-history-changes.png)

*Above: Guide Admin's changes in Graubünden include the published correction and earlier work.*

These lists help locate an action; they do not undo it. To correct current data, follow
[Correct a record](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/). To read the saved result of a publish,
[browse a publication](/docs/guide/use/browse-a-publication/).

If a history read fails, retry it. If no entries match, remove the person, kind or
period filters. A filtered empty list does not prove that the record has never changed.

## Reading more and the limits of the list

History groups entries under day headings. It starts with the ten newest; **Load older history** reads
20 more and **Show fewer** shortens it again. Jobs are named as the cause of their changes;
changes applied by publication name that publication. A system's author name is marked **client**.
Where an earlier value was not recorded, the expanded entry says so rather than reconstructing it.

The person's **Changes** page helps find actions across workspaces. It shows no field values
and cannot be exported; open a record's History for values. It leaves out model-to-model mapping
operations. Older changes without a workspace are visible only to someone who reads every
workspace. Entries recorded before named sign-in say **Before sign-in**. Model-administration
entries also require Model authoring access.

## Empty results and continuing the list

**No history recorded yet.** means there are no retained record events. **No change matches.**
means the filters found none: remove **By** or the event-kind filter before concluding the
record never changed. **Show all history** clears a narrowed history. **Loading history…**
is still a pending read.

The person's Changes list groups actions by day and reads across workspaces you may browse.
**Load more** reads the next entries. **No change matches these filters.** calls for loosening
the filters; **You have not changed anything in the workspaces you can read yet.** describes
an empty personal list. A different person's page can be headed **Changes by …**. These activity
lists help locate changes without exposing the record's full before/after values.

## Authors, causes and destinations

Deactivated people and clients remain named using their current names. Changes made by refiroo
itself say **the engine**. For a job, the author is the person or client who requested it;
for publication changes, it is the person who published. A relationship entry identifies
the record at the other end. Publication and type-change entries may keep only the changed
values, so their earlier values can be unavailable.

The person's **Changes** page offers the last 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days and includes live
and change-set work, publications and permitted model work. Titles open the affected item
while it still exists; a deleted item has no current record to open.

A change set names its creator and the people who edited it. A publication names who
published and withdrew it. A job names its requester both in the list and on its page.
These names describe different responsibilities; the person publishing need not have prepared
every change.

A narrowed workspace Activity list offers **Show all activity** to clear its narrowing.
The wider result still includes only work you may read.

## What changed in a period

**What changed** above workspace **Activity** and a record's **History** can explain a period
in a few statements. It appears when a provider is enabled and you hold **Browse** and **Use
AI proposals** in the workspace. Opening the page sends nothing. Follow
[Explain a period in history](/docs/guide/use/explain-a-period-in-history/) to request an account
and check its sources.

The initial period is **Last 7 days** for a workspace and **Last 30 days** for a record.
**Choose dates** offers **From** and **To, included**; both chosen days are included, using your
browser's time zone. The first day must not follow the last. There is no fixed maximum period.

refiroo counts the live changes across the whole period: records created, changed, moved or
deleted by type, fields changed, relationships, jobs and publications, people, change-set events,
withdrawn publications and model activations. A publication can identify who prepared its work,
the preparation job and who published it. A staged record is counted when published, once;
record edits still sitting in an open change set are not counted as live changes. Events such
as creating or submitting that set can still be included. A record account concerns that
record's values, relationships and moves, rather than every record in the workspace. Counts can overlap: a record moved while a value
changed can appear in both counts. Do not add them as a total of different records.

**Explain this period** sends counts and model labels to the configured provider. Only the
values send level adds names of records, people, change sets and files. Names remain visible
in your fact lines whatever the send level. The explanation does not send record field values.
Requests may incur costs and are logged; [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) explains
permissions, content retention and provider privacy.

Each AI statement has numbered sources. A number leads to a fact counted by refiroo, not written
by the provider. **The facts** includes all facts, with **Show the other …** after the first ten.
The provider sees at most 40 facts of each kind and their true totals, so its short account is
not a replacement for the whole list. Statements without a valid source are removed and counted.
The note **Written by AI from the facts below** reminds you that the wording can be wrong.

![An account of a workspace period with numbered statements, facts and Show them](/docs/screens/use-history-explained.png)

**Show it** or **Show them** narrows Activity or the record's timeline to the changes counted
by that fact. Other facts offer **Open the change set** or **Open the job** where you may open
it. A job deleted after retention has no job link; a deleted record has no current name.
Use **Show all activity** or **Show all history** to leave the narrowing.

A period with no changes says so and sends nothing to AI. If **The account could not be written**
appears, the facts remain usable and **Try again** requests the wording again. A request that
cannot be made has its own error and retry. The same facts for the same period requested again within
an hour reuse the saved account without a second provider call. The preset periods end at the
time you ask: **Explain again** normally changes that end time and can make another paid call. The account itself is temporary,
not a permanent history entry. The browser's account is in English; it is not translated into
German. Requesting an explanation changes no record.

## Work prepared by an assistant

History separates who prepared work from who published it. Built-in assistant changes say
**Proposed by the AI assistant**, with the model when recorded, **Asked for by** the person who
requested the task, and **Edited by** a later editor when present. The mark survives later
edits of that prepared row and is kept in published history, including removals, after the
task expires. A task's proposal need not carry a confidence percentage. Mapping suggestions
can include confidence and a reason; replacing a mapping target removes that target's AI mark.

Work from an external connected assistant says **Prepared by an assistant:** followed by its
name, who asked and who edited when available. Its name is the one the assistant gave itself;
it is not proof of identity. The entry still names the person who published. The personal
Changes page has no separate assistant filter or mark, so inspect a record's History for this
detail. refiroo never turns an assistant's proposal into publication on its own.

![Live record history with an expanded update prepared by an assistant and attributed to a person](/docs/screens/use-history-assistant.png)

*Above: Chur Wiesental’s History attributes an Abbreviation update to Guide Admin and marks
it as prepared by Stops checker (guide). A separate entry below names changes made by that
assistant’s client.*

An external assistant can prepare and submit only change sets created by its own person or
client, not a colleague's. It can add or change records and relationships and set fields,
but cannot remove records or relationships, clear values, discard a set, withdraw a submission,
change the model, approve or publish. A person reviews the submitted work through
[change-set review](/docs/guide/use/review-what-a-change-set-changes/). Withdraw the request before editing a submitted change
set; a second-person policy still needs a different approver from
the person whose assistant submitted it. Correct mistaken additions yourself or have the
assistant prepare a new set. These external-assistant limits differ from the built-in workbook
task's fuller preparation abilities. See [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) before
allowing an assistant to read your workspace.
guide/src/content/docs/use/home.md:
---
title: Home
description: Find your workspaces, continue your work and see recent changes.
reader: steward
---

Select the refiroo name in the top bar to return to **Home**. It brings together the workspaces
you can read and the work waiting for you.

![Home with a greeting, workspace cards, open change sets and recent changes](/docs/screens/use-home.png)

*Above: Guide Admin can browse two workspaces. Graubünden has an open change set; Default has none.*

## Your workspaces

The default workspace comes first. Each card shows the workspace name, its model and release, your roles there and its applications.
The **Default** badge identifies the default workspace. Choose an application button to open its
starting view in that workspace. Follow [Switch workspace](/docs/guide/use/switch-workspace/)
and [Open an application](/docs/guide/use/open-an-application/) to check the destination.

The card's counts lead to your change sets or the open change sets available to publish. A count
of open work does not say that it is validated or ready for publication.
**Nothing open here** means there are no open change sets counted on that card.

Choose **Follow** to receive a notice when someone else publishes a change set in that workspace.
Your own publications do not send you a followed-workspace notice.
The button changes to **Following**; choose it again to stop following. Following neither grants
access nor changes the records. Notices appear in your [inbox](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/).

## Continue where you left off

After you have worked in an application, a **Continue where you left off** card can name the last
place and workspace. Select it to return there. Check the banner on arrival before editing:
access and available data may have changed since your last visit.

![Home with a Continue where you left off card](/docs/screens/use-home-continue.png)

*Above: the card returns Guide Admin to Domains in Default, the last place visited.*

## Work waiting for you

**Your change sets** lists your open proposals, newest change first, with how much each changes. Open one to continue editing
or reviewing it. Follow [Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/)
for validation, review and publication.

Where you may approve requests, **Waiting for your approval** lists submitted change sets, newest
first. Each entry names the change set, workspace and submitter, and shows when it was submitted.
Choose **Review** to open its changes and decision controls. An open-change-set count on a workspace
card does not mean those change sets have been submitted for approval.

![Home showing a submitted change set under Waiting for your approval](/docs/screens/appr-home-waiting.png)

*Above: fictional Rita Approver is a Data owner in Graubünden. Guide approval example was submitted
by Guide Admin; Review opens the request.*

Follow [Approve a change set](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/) to review, send back or approve
and publish. A person required to obtain a second person's approval cannot decide their own
request. The [inbox](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/) also carries notices of waiting requests and
of the decisions on your submissions.

**Your recent changes** lists your five latest actions. **See all your changes** opens the longer list,
with workspace, kind and period filters. See [History](/docs/use/history/) for what those entries mean.

The greeting names you and shows your roles. For the workspace-by-workspace detail, open your
[Account](/docs/use/account/). The avatar also opens theme choices and Sign out. The bell shows
unread notices and opens your [inbox](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/).

If Home reports a loading failure, retry it. If no workspace is available, ask an administrator
for Browse access to the workspace you need.

A saved address naming a workspace, application or record opens that place directly instead of
Home. If you may browse no workspace, Home says there is none yet beneath the instance's name;
it does not mean your sign-in failed. Ask an administrator for Browse access.

To manage following later, open **Settings › Notification email** and use **Stop following** beside
a workspace. Losing Browse access also stops its publication notices.

Following starts off. Losing Browse or deactivation pauses notices without deleting your
choice, so they can resume if access returns. **Stop following** deliberately removes the
choice. Follow [Follow a workspace](/docs/guide/use/follow-a-workspace/) for the steps and
[Notification settings](/docs/use/notifications-settings/) for email copies and digests.

A card can say **This version cannot open the workspace's model.** instead of offering
application buttons. Your data has not been deleted. Follow
[Open a retired or unavailable workspace](/docs/guide/use/open-a-retired-or-unavailable-workspace/)
to read the reason and find the responsible administrator.
guide/src/content/docs/use/importing-and:
---
title: Importing and exporting
description: Choose a file for editing or exchange, preview its changes and load it safely.
reader: steward
---

Export data to read or edit outside refiroo, then import it with a preview. Export needs
**Browse** in the workspace. Import needs **Bulk and import** and permission to write the
target record types in Live or a change set. The deployment must allow new jobs. Publications
and retired workspaces can be exported but cannot receive an import.

Use [Export records](/docs/guide/use/export-records/),
[Edit in Excel and import back](/docs/guide/use/edit-in-excel-and-import-back/), or
[Import a file](/docs/guide/use/import-a-file/).

## What an export contains

Open **Workspace actions › Export**. On a view, **What** starts with **This view** and its
name. This takes the view's search, supported filters, parent scope and chosen columns,
including matching rows beyond those on screen. The count line names its context and size
when known: rows × columns for a matrix, records for a tree or mapping grid.

Choose **The type**, **The application** or **The whole workspace** for whole types rather
than the view's narrowed selection. From **Settings › Data operations › Jobs**, choose types
in a workspace. **Valid on** optionally limits an export by business date; ordinary browser
lists have no equivalent selector. When a page's search is not included, the dialog says so.
A filter on a relationship's own values is not carried into a view export; read that notice
before assuming the file contains exactly the connections left on screen.

**Kind of file** offers **For editing in a spreadsheet** and, for a table view or a selection
of types, **Technical**. Other view kinds export as an editing workbook.
Technical exports offer **Excel (XLSX)**, **CSV** and **JSON Lines**. Choose **Between exported
records**, **All their relationships** or **None** for relationships. All their relationships
can refer to records outside the chosen record scope. Everything is read at one instant.
The job's file summary records its scope, counts, size and checksum. Failed or cancelled exports
have no downloadable file. Downloads remain subject to job and file retention.

## Workbook layouts

**For editing in a spreadsheet** makes an Excel (XLSX) workbook. Its shape follows the selection:

| Selection | What the workbook holds | What loads back |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Table view | The table's columns, labels and order, with optional related sheets. | Editable record values and relationships, according to the saved layout. |
| Matrix showing record fields | One row per row record; each column record has a group of cell fields, with hidden cell identities and versions. | The cell records only. Row labels are for reading. |
| Matrix showing links | One column per column record, listing linked records by a chosen text field, with dropdowns backed by a value sheet per column. | Connections within each row and column; value-sheet records where editing or creation is enabled. |
| Relationships table, rows | One row per connection, showing both records and the relationship's values. | Connection values; a new row without identities can connect two named records. |
| Relationships table, grid | One row per source record, with Linked and relationship values under each target. | Connection values; Yes can link a missing pair. No removes nothing. |
| Mapping grid | One row per source record, with its target in a relationship column. | The target relationship, as in a table workbook. |
| Tree | One sheet per type, with its parent by name. | Editable records and parent choices. |
| Type, application or workspace | One sheet per type, parents' types first, with fields, parents and relationships by name. | Editable values on each sheet; a connection between sheets loads from the later sheet only. |

A view enabling **Link existing** or **Unlink** uses the link-matrix layout, even when it also
enables **Create**. Otherwise the matrix shows its cell fields. Keep hidden identity and
version columns, including those that distinguish parents with the same name.

Every XLSX export, including a technical workbook, has **About this export** as its second
sheet. Read it for the view or scope, workspace, context, search and filters, export time,
counts, relationships and load-back rules. It is for reading and is ignored on import.
CSV and JSON Lines files have no sheets.

### Text in CSV files

In a CSV export, text beginning with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return gets one
extra leading single quote, so a spreadsheet shows it as text rather than a formula. The same
rule applies when one or more single quotes already precede that character. For example,
`=1+1` is written as `'=1+1`, and `'=1+1` as `''=1+1`.

Keep that added quote when returning an exported CSV. With **Profile: None**, import removes
exactly one protective quote from record names and text fields. Returning an unchanged export
therefore leaves the original values unchanged, including their original quotes. Other quotes
are kept. This reading applies to exported CSV layouts, not to an ordinary CSV read through a
stored profile. XLSX files are unaffected; their values need no added quote.

### Matrix cells and new records

Export does not ask where new matrix records go. The relationship's candidate rules limit
which groups can hold them. If the rules identify one group and it is missing, it is created
with the record. Otherwise the group holding the most of this view's records in the column
is used; a tie gives no choice. An unused group is never picked automatically, even if it is
the only one.

When neither the rules nor data give a place, refiroo can propose a new group named like the
groups this view uses in other columns, where the structure and rules allow it. In the browser,
review or edit its proposed name, or choose an existing group. An import preview says
**will create … under …**; confirming creates the group and record together. No model change
is needed. If no suitable place is found, a new record is refused with the column and reason.
Choose or prepare a group in the app before previewing again.

The main matrix sheet loads only its cells; value sheets load their records separately.
Empty or cleared cells change nothing; removing all
values or links in a cell is done in refiroo. In the record-field layout, a cell holding several
records is shown joined and not loaded back. Edit those records individually in the app.
In the link layout, a non-empty list replaces only that cell's connections: listed records are
linked, omitted records are unlinked, and other columns are left alone. Names containing a
semicolon are written and read with a comma instead. Keep that displayed form when editing.
Where the matrix also permits creation, an unknown value can create a record in the derived
or proposed group; otherwise the list must identify existing candidates.

### Value sheets and matching fields

For a link matrix, **What each cell lists** selects **Name** or a text field of its records.
The default is Name. The file records the field so it can be read back. A linked record with
no value in that field refuses the export; choose another field or supply the missing value.
The selected values need to distinguish records within each column for import to resolve them.

Each **Values · …** sheet lists the column's eligible and already-linked records, their fields
(except fields holding JSON), their group and hidden identities and versions. Its values back
the main-sheet dropdowns. With Edit or Create enabled, edits update by identity; where Create
is enabled, a new row creates a record. A row not selected in any cell still loads. With only
Link existing and Unlink, value sheets are for reading and do not load. A matrix showing the
record's own fields has no value sheets.

A main-cell value matching a value-sheet row refers to that record. Renames are recognised by
the new value and also the old one unless another sheet row now uses it. The same new value
in both places is one record. A value in neither the sheet nor existing records creates one
where allowed, supplying its name and the chosen field only. Other required values still
apply. Duplicate matching values are refused as ambiguous. Spreadsheet edits do not themselves
synchronise the two sheets; import resolves them together.

The preview's **How the file is read** shows matching fields, values matched, value-sheet
counts and where new records go. For an unrecorded reading, it guesses the field and marks
it **Guessed**, with a note when the choice is uncertain. Choosing another field runs the
preview again. **Save these fields in the profile**, where offered, keeps the reading for
later files. No records are written before **Load the file**. Follow
[Import a file](/docs/guide/use/import-a-file/#check-how-the-file-is-read).

For steps, see [Edit in Excel and import back](/docs/guide/use/edit-in-excel-and-import-back/).

## A workbook for people

For a table view, **For editing in a spreadsheet** makes a workbook shaped by your table: visible columns in their order,
readable labels and typed cells. **Advanced: columns and sheets** changes the columns, their
order, which field a relationship column shows and which relationships get separate sheets.
Related records are exported in full, even where the browser showed only a few chips.
Record identity and versions are held in hidden columns. Keep those columns and the workbook's
saved import information when editing. Cells choosing a single record offer dropdowns from
sheets of eligible records.

Columns marked **(not imported)** are for reading. A table relationship column that owns its
records is read-only; edit those records on their own sheet or in refiroo. An ambiguous or overlong relationship cell
becomes a read-only summary pointing to its sheet. Several owned records for one parent also
form a summary rather than an editable single value. Edit the appropriate sheet instead.

When imported with **Profile: None**, the workbook is read as exported. An untouched workbook
changes nothing; changed names, fields and added rows are loaded as edits. A record changed by
someone else since export is refused unless you deliberately choose the overwrite option.
A main-sheet relationship list replaces that whole set; connections still chosen keep their
identity and values. A relationship sheet adds or updates connections, but omitting a row does
not remove one.

**Blank ordinary field and owned-record cells leave values unchanged.** To clear such a value,
use refiroo's field editor. **An empty table cell replacing a relationship set empties that set**,
where its rules permit it. Check the preview carefully when clearing a relationship list.
A required connection still cannot be cleared.

An owned-record relationship can use **Columns per parent** to make a workbook for filling in.
Each chosen parent contributes columns for its owned record's fields. Filling an empty column
creates that record under its parent and connects it to the row's record. See
[Add a language with a workbook](/docs/guide/use/add-a-language-with-a-workbook/) for the generic
steps and an example. Excel permits at most 16,384 columns; a wider layout fails when the export
job runs. Reduce parents or fields and export again.

## Read a file through a profile

An import profile tells refiroo how sheets and columns become records, names, fields, parents
and relationships, and which values identify existing records. Choose a stored profile for a
CSV or workbook that was not exported by refiroo. Profile setup belongs to
[Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/); a steward can
[load its next version](/docs/guide/use/load-the-next-version-of-a-workbook/).

Under **Settings › Data operations › Import profiles**, **Upload the next version…** stores
an XLSX or CSV file and starts a job to read its sheets and columns. While waiting, the page
says **Checking [file name]: profiling its sheets, then reading it through the profile…**.
This reading step writes no records. If **The file could not be read** appears, follow its
reason and upload a corrected file. A file that is too large or is neither XLSX nor CSV is
refused. Checking and loading must wait until its analysis is finished.

The profile page reports **Columns**, **Values**, **Records** and **Profile against the active
release**. To inspect the source's sheets, detected lists, header rows, column statistics
and cell ranges while changing the mapping, a model administrator uses the draft's
[source pane](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/#source-file-and-draft). Those statistics show
filled and distinct values, candidate keys, frequent values, placeholders and shared values
with other columns or records in the comparison workspace; they are evidence to review.

A newer upload supersedes the earlier file for this profile in this workspace. The earlier
file is kept for the job retention period after replacement, then deleted. It does not replace
another workspace's upload. The stored file is shared with its uploader and holders of
**Bulk and import** in its workspace; a file naming no workspace requires that access at the
instance. Keep your own original if it needs to outlive this retention.

A missing or ambiguous related name is refused. Parents can be resolved from existing records
or the same file, and are loaded before children. Repeated keys with compatible filled cells,
in one sheet or several sheets of the file, combine into one record; conflicting filled values refuse all contributing rows. Blank cells
do not conflict with another row's supplied value. A profile without a stable key warns that
later uploads may create new records instead of finding earlier ones.

A profile can keep or delete records missing from the next file. Deletion of missing records
is allowed only in a change set, so review those removals before publication. A profile must
still fit the workspace's model; ask its model administrator to fix named problems.

## Preview and load

The import always previews first in the browser. Choose whether to **Load the rows that can
load** or **Load nothing unless every row loads**, and whether found records may be updated.
The preview reports creations, updates, unchanged and refused rows. Its column report shows
empty, converted, mapped and refused cells, and found, missing or ambiguous record matches.
A large file may be sampled; the page says how much was tried. Loading checks the whole file
against current data, so the final result can differ.

**Load the file** confirms; **Cancel import** ends the preview without writes. Expired previews
cannot load. Correct refused rows in the original file and resend the whole file: already
loaded rows should preview unchanged when their data and matching choices are unchanged.
Refused rows are listed on the job page; there is no download of just the refused rows.

For an export from another workspace, **Load them as this workspace's own** creates separate
records with stable identities derived for the destination. Parents and relationships stay
together; resending the file finds those copies. They do not stay linked to the originals.
**Refuse them** instead reports the source workspace on the refused rows.

Read [Jobs](/docs/use/jobs/) for progress, cancellation, access and retention.

## Read the preview's evidence

**The preview** counts **Created**, **Updated**, **Unchanged**, **Deleted**, **Refused items**
and **Rows**. **A sample** means only part of the file was tried. In **Rows in the preview**,
choose **All rows**, **Refused** or **Not loaded**. Read **Outcome** and **Why, or what it does**
for the individual rows; a refused cell gives its column and reason.

**How the file was read** explains each sheet and column:

| Count | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| Bound to | The field, name, parent or relationship receiving this column. |
| Cells and Empty | Whether the expected rows supplied anything to read. |
| Read and Value-mapped | Values successfully read or translated through the profile's value choices. |
| Refused | Cells that could not be used; correct their stated cause before loading. |
| Found, Not found and Ambiguous | Whether a name or key identified exactly one existing record. |

A **Check** marker calls attention to a column. The **Read as exported** summary identifies a
workbook using its saved import information. **This import** records the chosen file, profile
and load policy. After confirmation, **The result** reports **Applied items**, **Refused items**
and **Not loaded**. Read that result even when the preview looked right.

![Import preview with one refused Height cell, 115 unchanged rows and per-column reading counts](/docs/screens/import-preview-columns.png)

*Above: one row in the reference Stops workbook is refused because Height (m) contains
“not a number”. The column counts show 115 height values read and one refused; the preview
has written nothing.*

## Profiles and recurring keys

In **Settings › Data operations › Import profiles**, **Valid** means the profile fits its
model; **Needs a fix** means a named problem must be resolved. Neither guarantees that every
row in the next file is valid. **Not loaded yet** means no retained last load is shown.
**Load more profiles** continues the catalogue. If there are no profiles, ask a model
administrator to prepare one through [Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/).

**Last load** offers **Open the change set review** while its work is proposed, or
**Open the load's job** for the retained operation. A load can be missing here because it has
passed retention. Uploading the next file checks it without changing records. Accepting a
column rename or ignoring a new column changes the profile used for subsequent checks; review
those decisions with its owner. See [Load the next version of a workbook](/docs/guide/use/load-the-next-version-of-a-workbook/).

A matching key may combine several columns. Every component must be present and identify at
most one stored record. Fill incomplete keys or ask the profile owner to resolve ambiguous
combinations. Changing only a display name need not create a new record when a stable key still
finds the original.

An export uses one consistent reading of the data. If its worker restarts after a crash, it
starts the export again rather than appending new data to half of an old file. Follow the job
until it has a completed file. Home itself has no Import or Export action; open an application
or use Jobs. A record's History is a list of changes, not an earlier-state viewer, and offers
no restore or undo. See [History](/docs/use/history/).

## What the next file can change

A profile belongs to one model. Use it in a workspace running that model; a different model
needs its own suitable profile. A file carrying records from another workspace with a
different model cannot load them as counterparts: those rows are refused while other valid
rows can load under the chosen load policy.

The next-version check can recognise a renamed header when its column stays in the same
position and holds the same values. **Accept** saves that rename; **Ignore** saves the decision
not to load a new column. Each decision checks the file again before loading.

For a lookup allowing one related record, a changed value in the next file switches the
connection to the newly named record. Missing records are kept unless the profile says to
delete them. That deletion also removes their connections, but refuses a record that others
depend on. Review the refused items and the change set before publishing.

## File refusals and completion notices

A preview can refuse all rows participating in a parent cycle, rather than loading either
record into an invalid hierarchy. If the file cannot be read or does not fit the profile,
loading changes nothing. Correct the file or ask the profile owner to repair its mapping.

The tab that starts an import reports when its preview is ready and when loading finishes,
unless you already have that job open. A collection reloads after an import started in this
tab loads into it. For exports, the completion notice offers **Download** and the job page;
a failed or cancelled export instead reports that state. Keep the tab open for these notices,
or return to **Jobs** to inspect the result later.

A stored upload used by an import profile is visible to its uploader and to people allowed
to import in its workspace. Treat the file as shared with those workers when choosing what
to upload. Losing a write permission can stop a job at its next step; review its applied counts
before asking an authorised colleague to continue the work.

## Let the assistant prepare the import

When the assistant is enabled and you have the required access, **Import…** in the workspace
menu first opens **Load a workbook**. Give it one XLSX or CSV file, instructions, or both.
It proposes the model and load for review rather than publishing records. **Import without
the assistant…** opens the ordinary manual import. See
[Loading with the assistant](/docs/use/loading-with-the-assistant/) and
[Load a workbook with the assistant](/docs/guide/use/load-a-workbook-with-the-assistant/).
The whole file and your words go to Claude Code, turns can incur costs, and task files are
retained; [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) explains those rules.

## Remove an uploaded file or an import profile

Open **Settings › Data operations › Import profiles** and select the profile. People with
**Bulk and import** are offered the deletion buttons; without that access the buttons are absent.
Deleting either item does not undo a load or remove records already loaded into a workspace.

- **Delete the file…** asks **Delete <file name>?**. **Delete the file** removes that upload,
  its stored cells and the analysis of its sheets and columns. This analysis is not the saved
  import profile that maps the columns. A check still reading it is
  asked to stop. The import profile stays. Upload the file again before checking or loading it.
- **Delete the profile…** asks **Delete the profile <profile name>?**. **Delete the profile**
  removes the saved instructions for reading the workbook and returns you to the profile list.
  Loading the workbook again needs a new profile saved by installing a model draft that holds it;
  ask a model administrator to prepare this through [Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/).

Choose **Cancel** in either confirmation to keep the item. A refusal stays in the confirmation
with its reason. If someone changed the file or profile since you opened it, cancel, reload the
page and inspect the latest version before trying again. There is no undo button for either
deletion. Keep the original workbook outside refiroo if you need to upload it later.

![Import profile showing separate buttons to delete its uploaded file and the profile](/docs/screens/use-import-profile-delete-actions.png)

## Default file and preview limits

An import normally accepts a file of up to 200 MiB. Its preview tries at most 10,000 items;
**Load nothing unless every row loads** normally allows at most 10,000 items. Your operator
can change these limits. Read **Limits** on Jobs and the limit reported by the import form.
If a file exceeds the limit, split or reduce it, or agree a suitable limit with the operator.
If splitting a recurring workbook whose profile deletes missing records, ask its owner first:
each part could otherwise treat records in the other parts as missing.

Jobs and their downloadable files are normally retained for seven days. Download an export
before its **Kept until** time. A retained import profile can outlive its last load's job;
**Last load** is not an archive of every workbook loaded through it.

![Confirmation to remove an import profile while retaining previously loaded records](/docs/screens/use-import-profile-delete-confirm.png)
guide/src/content/docs/use/inbox-and-app:
---
title: Inbox and approvals
description: Read notifications and understand how change sets reach an approval decision.
reader: steward
---

The bell in the top bar opens your inbox. It tells you about work needing attention and results
of work you started. Approval notices lead an approver to a submitted change set.
Follow [Approve a change set](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/) for submitting and deciding.

## Read and manage notifications

The bell's count is the number of unread notices. Open it to see up to 20 unread notifications;
the panel indicates how many more remain. Use **See all notifications** for the rest.
**Mark all read** clears their unread state; **See all notifications** opens the full page.
You can also reach **Notifications** from the avatar menu.

![Inbox panel with unread notices, Mark all read and See all notifications](/docs/screens/use-inbox-panel.png)

*Above: Guide Admin has eight unread Batch finished notices from jobs they started.*

Notices include a change set waiting for your approval, approval or return of your submission,
a job that finished, failed or needs confirmation, and publications in workspaces you follow.
A notice is an invitation to inspect the result; a finished job may still have refused items.

![Notifications page with search, kind, workspace, read-state and sort controls](/docs/screens/use-notifications-page.png)

*Above: the reference account's notices are job results. One has been read; the others are highlighted.*

On **Notifications**, search by change set, comment, person or job. **Kind**, **Workspace** and
**Show** narrow the list; **Sort** chooses newest or oldest first. Filters cover the stored notices,
not just the rows you have scrolled to. Notices are kept for 90 days.

Opening a notice marks it read and opens its subject in the workspace it belongs to, where one
remains available. Completing a job’s confirmation also marks its notice read. A job notice
opens its state, result and items. An approval notice can remain after publication has consumed
the change set, so not every notice has an editable destination.

![A job opened from a Batch finished notice, showing its state and result](/docs/screens/use-notification-job.png)

*Above: the batch completed with 11 items already as asked and no changed items. Opening this job
marked its notice read.*

Tick notices to **Mark read**, **Mark unread** or **Delete** them. Shift selects a range; Cmd or
Ctrl adds one. **Select all** selects loaded notices, not every matching notice in storage.
At most 500 notices can be changed at once. Changing filters clears the selection.
**Delete all read…** opens **Delete all read notifications?**. Choose **Delete read
notifications** to permanently delete all your read notices, including those outside the
current filters, or **Cancel** to keep them. Unread notices and the jobs or change sets remain.
If an action fails, read the error and retry; clearing a notice does not fix its underlying job.

**Notification email settings** opens your mail choices. Where mail is configured and your account
has an email address, you can choose email notifications and their kinds. Turning mail off does
not turn off the inbox. If mail is unavailable, the settings page explains why.

![Notification email settings with mail unavailable and no followed workspaces](/docs/screens/settings-notifications.png)

*Above: mail is not configured on the reference instance, so the email choices are absent.
Workspaces I follow is empty; following starts from a workspace card on Home.*

## When a change needs approval

A workspace can require approval before publication and a different person to decide.
Administrators set these rules under [Approval policies](/docs/administer/approval-policies/).
To decide a request, you need **Approve publications**; the Data owner role includes it.
Check [Account](/docs/use/account/#what-you-can-do) for your own access.

![Workspace Approval tab with approval and second-person policy options](/docs/screens/use-approval-policy.png)

*Above: an earlier view of Graubünden’s Approval settings, with both policies off. The request
shown below uses approval with a second person required.*

With no approval requirement, people allowed to publish can do so directly. A person who prepares
work but cannot publish can submit it to an approver. When approval is required, direct publication
is available only to someone allowed to publish and approve their own work, with no second-person
requirement. That action records their approval as it publishes.

## From submission to decision

**Submit for publication** validates the change set and records its submitted version. An optional
comment gives the approver context. Submission does not change Live. The band says **waits for approval**. Open **Details** for the submitter and submitted version,
and the review’s **Decision** panel for the comment. The proposal cannot be edited while
it waits. **Withdraw request** ends the request and keeps the proposed work for editing; the
submitter or an authorised approver can withdraw it.

![Submitted change set with Waiting for approval, its comment and review and withdrawal controls](/docs/screens/appr-submitted.png)

*Above: Guide Admin submitted Guide approval example in Graubünden. Version 2 proposes a height
correction to Davos Platz; this earlier view keeps the submission comment in the banner.
In the current frame, read the comment in the review’s **Decision** panel.*

Approvers can find requests under **Waiting for your approval** on [Home](/docs/use/home/), or
through the bell's **Waiting for your approval** notice. Both lead to the review. Opening a
submitted change set also offers **Review and decide**.

![Approver's inbox with an unread Waiting for your approval notice](/docs/screens/appr-inbox-notice.png)

*Above: fictional approver Rita Approver receives a notice for Guide Admin's request.*

The review's **Decision** panel identifies who submitted which version and when, and shows their
comment. Below it, **Records** and **Relationships** show the proposed differences.

| Decision | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Approve and publish | Checks the current data again, applies the changes to Live and creates a publication immediately. Comment is optional. |
| Send back | Requires a Comment explaining what needs attention. Ends the pending request and keeps the change set for correction and another submission. Nothing is published. |

![Decision panel with submission details, Comment, Send back and Approve and publish above the changes](/docs/screens/appr-decision-panel.png)

*Above: Rita reviews Guide Admin's proposed change to Davos Platz. The empty Comment field says
Required to send back; approval does not require a comment.*

With the second-person rule on, the submitter sees **A second person must decide this request.**
instead of a Decision panel, even if they hold approval permission. They can inspect the changes
but must wait for another authorised approver.

## Sent back and submitted again

After **Send back**, the submitter receives a notice with the reason. The change-set banner names
the approver and repeats that reason. The proposal is editable again and **Submit for publication**
is available. The submitter can correct the work and submit again with a new comment. That is a
new request needing its own decision.

![Editable change set showing who sent it back and their reason](/docs/screens/appr-sent-back.png)

*Above: Rita asks Guide Admin to name the source of the new height. Review changes, Validate change
set and Submit for publication are available again; the correction has not reached Live.*

## Where the result appears

A successful approval publishes immediately and notifies the submitter. Under **Publications**,
the new snapshot is **Current** and names the person who published it. See
[Publications](/docs/use/publications/) for the saved result.

![Submitter's inbox with the approval notice above the earlier send-back notice](/docs/screens/appr-approved-notice.png)

*Above: Guide Admin's newest notice says Rita approved Guide approval example. The earlier
send-back notice remains below it; it is no longer the request's current state.*

Workspace **Activity** records the actions with who and when. Open **Settings**, **Workspaces**,
select the workspace and choose **Activity**. See [History](/docs/use/history/) for its filters.

![Workspace Activity showing change-set actions, the publication and the applied record correction](/docs/screens/appr-activity.png)

*Above: Graubünden's Activity after the submission, send back, resubmission and approval. The
visible latest entries include Publication 2 and Rita's published correction to Davos Platz.
Change-set actions use the general label Changed change set.*

Publication can still be refused because of a conflict or invalid combined data. A changed or
withdrawn request cannot be approved as the older submitted version. Reload, inspect the current
state and resolve the reported problem before retrying. The review also keeps the decision history.
Follow [Approve a change set](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/) for the steps, and
[Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) for how proposed work merges into Live.

## Email and following

Under **Settings › Notification email**, switch on **Email me when something arrives in my inbox**
to enable email where mail is configured and your account has an address. Choose **At once**,
**Digest** or **Off** for approval waiting, your approval decisions and your job notices.
Off stops only email; the inbox keeps receiving notices. Choose every morning or Mondays at
07:00 in your browser's time zone for digests, and check the next digest time shown. There is
no choice of another hour. A digest counts all eligible unread notices and lists the newest 50; if none remain, none is sent.

**Follow** on a Home workspace card adds notices when someone else publishes there. Your own
publications do not notify you through following. **Stop following** on Notification email ends
these notices; losing Browse access does too. If mail is unavailable or you have no address,
the page explains why and hides the email switch.

Administrators configure the publication rules on
[Approval policies](/docs/administer/approval-policies/). That page and its linked guide explain
saving the policy and establishing approvers; the submission and decision flow is above.

## When a notice has already been handled

Opening a job, move, migration or change-set review marks its notices read, including notices
arriving while you keep that subject open. A decision on a request, or confirmation or cancellation
of waiting work, also closes the waiting notice. A publication notice opens its publication
from Notifications or a digest while it is active and you have Browse. If it is no longer
active, it opens the workspace’s **Publications** instead. The bell also leads to
**Publications**. Opening marks the notice read; it does not restore lost Browse access.

For immediate email eligibility, digest counts and schedules, see
[Notification settings](/docs/use/notifications-settings/). A digest counts all eligible notices
but lists only the newest 50, and has no one-day cutoff. Job lines can include retained outcome
counts. **Stop following** removes a saved follow choice; losing access only suspends its notices.
Follow [Set up email notices](/docs/guide/use/set-up-email-notices/) or
[Follow a workspace](/docs/guide/use/follow-a-workspace/) to change these choices.

The **Submit for publication** dialog's **Comment (optional)** accepts up to 2,000 characters.
Choose **Submit** to validate and send the request, or **Cancel** to leave it editable.
**Submitted for publication. It waits for approval.** confirms submission. While waiting,
**Withdraw the request to edit it.** explains why controls are absent. **Request withdrawn.**
confirms that editing can resume; it does not discard the change set.

The change-set banner's ordinary write and model-version actions are explained in
[Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/#model-version-actions-on-the-banner).
For a person's activity, rather than inbox notices, see [History](/docs/use/history/).
guide/src/content/docs/use/jobs.md:
---
title: Jobs
description: Follow imports, exports and bulk work, inspect results and stop remaining work.
reader: steward
---

A job is work refiroo runs in the background, such as an import, export or change to many
records. Open **Settings › Data operations › Jobs** to find the jobs you may see across
workspaces, newest first. In **All jobs**, the list shows **Workspace**, **State**, **Items**, **Requested by**,
**Created**, **Finished** and **Actions**. Open a job to read its progress and results.

Follow [Follow and cancel a job](/docs/guide/use/follow-and-cancel-a-job/) for the steps.

## Jobs grouped under a task or a draft

Above the list, **Grouped** puts an assistant task's related work, including jobs queued by
its session, in one row. A model draft's jobs also form one row. A job with neither owner
remains a row of its own. **All jobs** shows the individual jobs instead. Your browser remembers
this choice when you return to Jobs.

The grouped table shows **Job or group**, **Workspace**, **Jobs**, **State**, **Latest** and
**Actions**. A group is labelled **Assistant task** or **Model draft** and named after its
workbook or draft. A workbook's extension appears beside its name. **Jobs** counts the group's
visible jobs; **State** gives counts for states with jobs, such as running, failed and completed.
**Latest** is the latest job time. These counts describe retained jobs you may see, not every
job ever started or every job in the instance.

Open the group name to see its jobs:

1. The heading names the workbook or draft. Above it, **Assistant task** or **Model draft**
   and the workspace identify the group; **‹ Jobs** returns to the main list.
2. **Summary of the group** gives the job count and latest time. **All** shows the total;
   state buttons show non-zero counts for **Running**, **Queued**, **Awaiting confirmation**,
   **Failed**, **Completed**, **Cancelled** or **Expired**. Select one to narrow the table;
   select **All** to restore every visible job. The selected state stays in the page's address.
3. The **Jobs** table shows **Job**, **State**, **Items**, **Requested by**, **Created**,
   **Finished** and **Actions**. Inspect processed, applied, rejected and unprocessed counts.
   **Refresh** reads again; **Load more jobs** continues the list. **Cancel** is offered
   for queued or running work where cancellation is available; it opens a confirmation.
4. **Open the task** or **Open the draft** opens the owning work. The button appears only
   after refiroo has confirmed you can read that task or draft. Seeing a group's jobs does
   not itself grant access to its owner; a missing button is not a stopped job.
5. Open a job to inspect its result. When opened from the group, its trail includes
   **‹ Assistant task: [name]** or **‹ Model draft: [name]**. Use that link to return to
   the group with the state choice preserved, or **Jobs** to return to the main list.

**Esc** goes up one level: job to the group it was opened from, then group to Jobs. A job
opened from the flat list returns directly to Jobs. Esc does not navigate while a dialog
is open or you are editing a field.

If the group says **This group has no jobs you can see**, its task or draft may have been
removed or its jobs may have expired. Return to Jobs. **No jobs in this state** means the
selected state has no visible rows; try **All** or **Refresh**. A read failure offers a retry;
it does not establish that the group is empty.

## States and results

A job can wait in the queue, run, wait for confirmation, complete, fail, be cancelled or expire.
**Cancel requested** means stopping has been requested, not that all work has stopped.
An import moves through **Reading the file**, **Previewing** and **Loading**. A waiting preview
has not applied its changes. **Load the file** confirms an import; **Apply** confirms a bulk
preview. Review the counts and item reasons before confirming.

Completion does not mean every row succeeded. Read applied, unchanged, rejected and unprocessed
counts and the item outcomes. A failure has **Why it failed**; a stopped job explains **What
stopped it**. Fix that cause before starting fresh work. A sample preview is informative, while
execution checks every item, the stored file, versions and the current context again.

An expired preview cannot be confirmed, even if a stale page still says it is waiting.
Start a new preview. The **Kept until** fact tells you when the job's retained results expire.
The list's **Limits** describes this deployment's batch, job and retention limits; do not rely
on a universal file size or item count.

## What a job's page shows

An import has its file/profile choices, row outcomes and column report. An export has **The
file**, with counts by type, format, size, checksum, context and **Download** after success.
An unsuccessful export has no file. Keep any file you need before its retention ends.

A copy or move shows records and relationships made, refused and not moved, breakdowns by type,
and outcomes filterable by reason. Source record names open in their original workspace.
Older retained jobs may lack relationship-type counts. A migration shows converted, type-changed,
removed and must-be-fixed counts. These operations are described under
[Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/) and [Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/).
A job without item outcomes instead explains what it belongs to and links there where allowed.

## Cancellation and access

Cancel queued, running or waiting work with the offered cancel button and its confirmation.
Cancellation stops future work; it does not roll back already committed chunks. All-or-nothing
work commits as one unit, while independent work can leave partial results. A colleague's edit
to a shared change set between chunks can stop the next chunk; earlier chunks remain.

Jobs run with the requester's current rights. Deactivation or losing a required permission can
fail work at its next step. You see your own jobs and jobs your permissions allow; knowing a
job's address does not grant access. A retired workspace refuses new data changes.

The tab that starts work reports progress and completion while open. The inbox can also receive
waiting and finished-job notices. Opening a job marks its notices read, including notices that
arrive while it stays open. Closing a page does not itself stop a running job.

![Completed export with state, retention, counts, file details and Download](/docs/screens/job-results-and-file.png)

## Read the job labels

| State | Meaning and next action |
| --- | --- |
| Queued | Waiting to start. Cancel if the work is no longer wanted. |
| Running | Work is in progress. Follow its counts or leave it running in the background. |
| Awaiting confirmation | A preview is ready; review it before Apply or Load the file. |
| Completed | Processing ended. Check the result and refused items before relying on it. |
| Failed | Work stopped with an error. Read Why it failed and any applied counts. |
| Cancelled | Cancellation has finished. Check what was applied before it stopped. |
| Expired | Retention ended. Start new work if you need another preview or file. |

The result label is separate: **Every item applied**, **Partly applied** or **Nothing applied**.
A failed independent chunk is rolled back, while earlier committed chunks stay applied.
Cancelled all-or-nothing work rolls back its transaction completely. **Not reached** items
can mean cancellation, failure, a model change or a colleague changing the change set. With
all-or-nothing work, an otherwise valid item can be unwritten because another was refused.

The list distinguishes **Batch**, **Import**, **Export**, **Workbook for people**, **Profile**,
**Profile check**, **Dry run**, **Inference**, **Mapping proposal**, **Migration** and **Move**.
Some belong to model-administration tasks; their pages link to that work. **Refresh** reloads
the list and **Load more jobs** continues it. **New export** starts a file; **New import**
appears when your permissions allow importing.

**State** names the workspace and requester and shows creation, start and finish times.
For an export, **The file** also records **Sheets**, its Live/change-set/publication scope,
**Change feed position**, **Valid on** when chosen and **Checksum (SHA-256)**. Use those facts
to distinguish similar retained files; the checksum identifies the completed file's contents.

**Cancel this job?** offers **Stop the job** or **Keep the job**. If it finished first, read the
refusal and refreshed state rather than assuming it was cancelled. **The change was not applied**
after confirmation leaves the preview waiting: cancel it and create a fresh preview against
current data. The old result remains readable until retention ends.

Copies keep their source identity so a later copy can update its earlier counterpart instead
of making another one. Moving a copy back can update the original, or recreate its original
identity if it was removed. Inspect the source links and results before publishing. A move's
source deletions wait for the target copy to be published first; the deletion proposal cannot
be published ahead of the copy it depends on. See [Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/)
for mapping design, or [Copying and moving records](/docs/use/copying-and-moving/)
for preparing and reviewing a transfer.

On a waiting preview's own page, **Cancel this import?** offers **Discard the import**,
or **Cancel this preview?** offers **Discard the preview**. **Keep the import** or **Keep the
preview** returns to the preview. Discarding writes nothing and leaves the preview readable
until expiry. On the Jobs list, the confirmation button is **Cancel job** instead.
Results and files are normally kept for seven days; your deployment's **Limits** and the job's
**Kept until** give the applicable retention.

guide/src/content/docs/use/lists-and-fil:
---
title: Lists, search and filters
description: Understand search, filter conditions, sorting, columns and navigation through long collections.
reader: steward
---

Use a collection's search and filters to find records across its whole list. The workspace
and the **Live**, change-set or publication context determine which data you search.
Follow [Find records](/docs/guide/use/find-records/) to narrow a list, or
[Continue a long list](/docs/guide/use/continue-a-long-list/) to reach a distant result.

## Search and combine conditions

![A collection narrowed by a date condition and a named relationship, with both shown as removable pills](/docs/screens/list-filter-pills.png)

*Above: Stops in Network, Graubünden, narrowed by Valid from and Operated by. The footer
shows the total for these conditions; the related-record chips identify each stop’s operator.*


Search matches names and fields the model makes searchable. It works together with filters;
a record must match the search and the applied conditions. **＋ Filter** groups the fields and
relationships offered by this view. Its search finds a field in a long menu. Each active
condition appears as a pill: open it to change it, or use **×** to remove it. **Clear all**
removes the filters. When both search and filters are active, **Clear search and filters**
removes both.

Text can be compared exactly, by containing text or by its beginning. Numbers and dates offer
comparisons and ranges; Yes/No fields offer the two values. **More** holds further conditions.
A missing optional value differs from a stored empty value. A range can show separate lower
and upper conditions; check both pills if a record is unexpectedly excluded.

A relationship filter can mean **Is any of** the records ticked, **Has none**, or **Has any**.
**Has any under** and **Has none under** use one ancestor and consider related records at any
depth below it. Candidate restrictions set by the model can narrow the records offered.
In Live, **Created** and **Updated** filter when a record was made or last changed.
They are different from its business validity dates. The browser has no control for viewing
all data as valid on a chosen business date.

On a phone, the condition editor opens as a sheet. Its **Show …** button includes the matching
count. An empty result says **No results match these filters**; clear or loosen conditions.
An empty collection instead says there are no records in this workspace yet. A failed read
is an error: retry it before concluding that nothing matches.

## Show or hide inactive records

A table can use a Yes/No field to mark inactive records. When the model chooses **Active**,
a record with **No** keeps its place in the list, with its name in a quieter colour and a grey
**Inactive** pill after it. If the field has another name, the pill says **Not** followed by
that name in lower case. Only **No** gets this mark; a missing value does not.

These records are shown by default. Beside **Filter**, **Hide inactive (N)** lets you narrow
the list by hiding exactly those marked records. Records with no value stay visible.
For another field name, the switch says **Hide not** followed by that name. The number counts records with **No** in this list after its search and other
filters; it is not the total for the workspace. The number is shown even when it is **0**.
The label can appear without a number while the count is loading or if that count cannot be read.

Turn on the switch to add a filter pill, such as **Active: not No**. The filter stays
in the page address, like your other conditions. Turn the switch off, or remove the pill
with **×**, to stop applying it. Choosing **Yes** for the same field in the ordinary
**＋ Filter** menu is different: that keeps only records with **Yes**, excluding records
with no value. The switch does not use that condition. If a record seems missing, check
its filter pill along with your other filters.

The mark does not change editing permissions. Where you may edit, change the value in its
cell or on the record as usual. A change set or publication uses its own values for the same
mark and switch; a publication remains read-only. A table without this model setting has
neither the mark nor the switch. See [Records](/docs/use/records/#edit-a-value-or-create-a-record)
for editing and [Find records](/docs/guide/use/find-records/) for narrowing a list.

## Sort and show columns

There is one sort at a time. Choose it from the sort menu or a sortable heading, then choose
**Ascending** or **Descending**. Without another selected order the usual order is by name;
a view can declare its initial sort. Missing field values come last, including when a list
contains types without that field. Structured fields and computed paths do not sort.
Created and updated times are not available where that context has no recorded timestamps.

**Display** chooses the shown columns and table density. Resizing a column changes how much
fits. The name column stays whole; columns that do not fit fold behind **Columns · n of m**.
Choose it to show all columns, scrolling sideways if needed. Other values stay on one line; an ellipsis marks a cut value. Hover, focus or long press to read
it in full. A related-record column shows coloured chips and **+N more** when some do not fit.
That count is not a button: widen the column or open the record to see all its connections.
A column with at most one related record can sort by its name. Multi-record columns and columns
showing a related record's field do not sort; use a relationship filter to narrow them.

## Long lists and saved position

The rows scroll inside the table while its headings and footer remain visible. The footer
shows the current range and total, page entry and start/end controls. Where available,
**Go to** seeks a value in the selected sort. The address keeps your search, filters, sort and
position, including when you return using **←** and the list’s name above a record’s title. These controls also work in change
sets and publications.

Only visible and nearby rows are drawn. The browser's Find command searches those drawn rows;
use the collection's own search to find a record anywhere in it. A later page can fail
independently: use its retry action and keep your conditions.

For actions on the results, see [Changing many records](/docs/use/changing-many-records/).
An export keeps the collection's supported filters and columns, but does not include its text
search; see [Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/).

## Display details and limits

In **Display**, the identity column is fixed and marked **(record identity)**. Other columns
have checkboxes. **Density** offers Default, Comfortable and Compact; **Per page** offers
10, 20, 50, 100 and the view's default where applicable. **Column width** offers **Narrow**,
**Wide** and **Reset display**. Choices stay on this device per view; rows per page stays in
the address too. Created/updated stamps are filters in Live rather than default table columns.

**Not set**, **Null** and **Empty text** distinguish missing, stored null and empty text.
Related-record chips open those records. Opening a record can take you to the application
where it belongs, even if its type was listed in the application you started from.
On phones, **Show all … columns** and **Show fewer columns** control extra columns.
Selecting text does not open or edit a row. Full-text popups close with Escape.

There are no named saved searches, saved filters or saved views. Keep the page address instead.
There is no multi-column sort, grouping or aggregation in the list, and no cross-collection
search page. **Find any record** in the top bar searches record names across the workspace;
a collection’s search stays within that collection. See [Appearance and devices](/docs/use/appearance-and-devices/)
for local keyboard commands.
