## Open, edit and recover a result

Choose a row to open its record; a related-record chip opens that connected record instead.
The record heading takes focus when the page opens. Choose **←** and the list’s name above
the title to return to the saved conditions and position. A failed panel can be retried without clearing the rest of the record.
For field and relationship edits from table cells, see [Records](/docs/use/records/#edit-a-value-or-create-a-record).
To select results for an action, see [Changing many records](/docs/use/changing-many-records/).

Numeric zero and **No** are actual values, not missing fields. Use the field's missing-value
condition when looking for records without a value. A view can offer several record types;
its search covers those types, rather than every collection in the application.

## Related values in columns

A related-record column can show the connected records' names, one of their fields, or a field
from an ancestor above them. The model chooses this presentation. A column showing a related
field does not sort. When a single-record column sorts by name, records without a connection
come last. These columns do not themselves offer filters; use the relationship conditions
in **＋ Filter** when the view declares them. Hiding a related-record column in **Display**
also stops reading its connections for that column.

Relationship chips follow the data context you are reading, including a change set or a
publication. The filter pill keeps the names of your chosen related records after a reload.
A Yes/No filter applies when you choose the value; other editors can require their apply action.

The sidebar scrolls independently of the table. Both short and long collections keep their
header and footer in view; the table fills the available height even with only a few records.

## Ask for filters in words

Where **Ask** is offered beside **Search**, you can describe the records you want and review
the ordinary filters the answer becomes. A partial answer waits for your acceptance. See
[Asking a list in words](/docs/use/ask-in-words/) and its
[step-by-step guide](/docs/guide/use/ask-a-list-in-words/). Your question and list definitions
go to the provider; short related lists can include names. Calls can incur costs and are
recorded: read [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) before sending.
guide/src/content/docs/use/loading-with-:
---
title: Loading with the assistant
description: Understand assistant proposals, checked records, saved layouts and the steps from acceptance to publication.
reader: steward
---

Give the assistant a workbook, instructions about existing records, or both. It prepares work
for you to review. Use [Load a workbook with the assistant](/docs/guide/use/load-a-workbook-with-the-assistant/)
for a file, or [Change records with the assistant](/docs/guide/use/change-records-with-the-assistant/)
for instructions alone. A task is the saved work you return to as it proposes, checks and loads.

## Access and information sent

The built-in assistant must be enabled by your operator. It uses Claude Code, independently
of the AI provider used by Search / Ask and mapping suggestions. It needs the send level values,
**Use AI proposals**, **Bulk and import**, **Work in change sets** and enabled background jobs.
Model changes also need the model permissions; installing a new release needs **Model release**
at instance level. Retired workspaces and publications cannot receive imports.

Claude Code receives your words, the workspace's model and the whole file, if supplied. It can
read the workspace records it needs, within your permissions and their application and type
restrictions. It never approves, publishes or activates a model. Turns can incur charges or
consume a subscription allowance. Tasks, workbooks and session transcripts are retained while
the work can continue and then cleaned up; the normal task retention is 90 days. Read
[AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) for costs, sending and retention before starting.

## What the assistant prepares

The dialog takes one XLSX or CSV file, within the deployment's import size limit. Instructions
are limited to 4,000 characters. Without a file, instructions are required. Images and documents
are not data files for this task. You cannot attach several files, schedule a task or transfer
its session to a colleague. Its requester and the workspace's administrators can read it.

When no saved layout fits, one session reads the workbook, the current model and the workspace's
records. It changes the model draft where needed and turns the file into proposed records and
relationships. It finds existing records by reading them, so explain which fields identify a
record when names alone are ambiguous. The engine checks every proposed record and relationship
against the draft's model and workspace data without saving the changes. The assistant writes
no import profile. One file row can supply several records or relationships.

The same instructions can produce different proposed structures on separate runs; inspect each
proposal rather than assuming it repeats a previous design. An update can leave the model unchanged and prepare only record changes. Instructions can also
ask for relationships or a model change. The assistant is limited to capabilities refiroo supports;
its notes explain when it cannot complete a request. A turn that runs beyond the session limit (30 minutes unless the operator changed it) is stopped like your Stop,
and the task goes back to where you can tell the assistant to go on or try again. While other tasks hold the assistant, the page says how many are ahead.

## Review the proposal

**The assistant’s proposal** says what it understood and lists the types it adds, changes or
loads, with attributes and record counts. For a proposal with a model draft, **Show the model
change** expands **The model: what changes**, including changes such as a field becoming optional.
A words-only task that needs no model change says **No change to the model.** It has no model
draft, model-change detail or model editor button.
For a workbook, **What the load does** shows new records, existing records matched, new
relationships, refused items and rows read. The type table separates **New**, **Matched**,
**Changed**, **Refused** and **Linked to**. A matched record can be changed or unchanged. Open a
type's row with a click, Enter or Space for example records with their values, links and source
cells. Examples show only some of the records the engine checked.

**One name twice in one type** identifies a name shared by records touched by the load and says
whether they sit at the top level or under parents. It is a finding, not proof that the records
are unwanted duplicates. Check it against the file and your intent. Expand **Where each part of
the file goes** for sheet and cell ranges and what they become.

Under **Checks**, read every **Needs attention** item. Check types holding records that the
proposal leaves out, any filled cells left out and **Columns left out**. Compare new records
with matched ones: an unexpected new record can mean an intended update failed to find its
record. A successful engine check does not prove the design means what you intended. Empty
cells hold no value; they do not by themselves mean a row was skipped.

![Workbook proposal showing the checked load summary, results by type, questions and acceptance controls](/docs/screens/use-assistant-proposal.png)

*Above: the workbook proposal for the Graubünden reference data, scrolled to What the load does
and its results by type. Questions shows the assistant’s assumed answer and the other choices.
Accept and load to change set is available; nothing has been installed or loaded.*

**Questions** shows the answers the assistant assumed, only for what a person decides. Keep every choice and the answers are recorded without another turn; change a choice and use **Answer and
design again**. **Tell the assistant what to change** followed by **Send to the assistant**
continues the same session with your correction. When there is a draft, **Open in the model
editor** lets you edit it directly; the session reads it again before continuing. It cannot change a draft
held by another assistant task and must use its own. Close in the editor returns to the task. The draft’s history records who asked for the
assistant’s model steps; it does not mark every model element as Proposed.

If the draft changed after the check, **What the load does** warns that accepting checks every
record again first and loads nothing if any is refused. Ask the assistant for a revised proposal
if the shown records no longer describe your intended result. A saved-layout check that predates
an edit must be renewed before loading. Concurrent task changes reload the latest state and ask
you to check before trying again.

## Accepting, loading and publishing

For a workbook, **Accept and load to change set** makes the engine install a release if the model changed,
open a change set and load exactly the checked records and relationships as one batch. No
assistant turn runs. With no model change, the change set uses the workspace's current release.
No model is activated and no records are published by this acceptance.

If an edited draft fails its new check, nothing is installed or loaded. If the data changed
since checking and any item is refused during loading, none of the batch is loaded and its
change set is discarded. The task names the refused records and their source cells. Tell the
assistant what to correct, then review and accept its revised proposal. A release already
installed before a load refusal can remain installed.

For a words-only task with no model change, **Accept** lets the session prepare a new change set
on the workspace's current release. It installs and activates nothing. Model-only and record-move
proposals keep **Accept the model** and the migration or staged-move endings described below.
A file whose records are all stored already is a normal outcome: the check shows every record as
already there, **Accept** ends the task loaded with nothing new, and the change set it leaves is empty
(discard it from the task). A session that loads without the engine's check and names an empty
change set is not reported as a successful load.

The result names the change set and its counts. **Review the change set** opens its normal
review. Check the actual rows and relationships, validate, then submit for approval or publish
as your access and the workspace’s policy allow. If the load uses a different model version,
review offers a combined move of the workspace and publication. A model administrator with
publication permission reviews the migration preview and confirms **Migrate and publish**;
a separate activation first is not required. See [the workbook load’s publication step](/docs/guide/use/load-a-workbook-with-the-assistant/).
The assistant does not confirm it. A second-person approval rule still applies to the person
who asked for the work.

The saved-layout path has its own **What the load would do** check and load button. Read
**What confirming does, in this order**: when that path changes the model, **Activate the model
and load** explicitly activates it as your confirmed action before loading the change set.
A subsequent load failure does not undo that model activation. A record load always waits
for publication to reach Live.

A task's bar below the top bar names the current step and next action. It follows you into
the model editor and change-set review opened from the task. You can leave while a turn works
and return through its entry under **Settings › Data operations › Jobs**; its completion is announced.
See [Jobs grouped under a task or a draft](/docs/use/jobs/#jobs-grouped-under-a-task-or-a-draft)
for the group’s state counts and **Open the task**.

## The next file and the saved profile

A workbook loaded from the assistant's checked records and relationships saves no import
profile. Send the next file of the same layout to the assistant again. Explain how its contents
correspond to records already held so the proposal can match them correctly.

A separately saved import profile can still load a matching file without an assistant session
or AI cost.

A fitting saved profile takes the engine's own path: you still review its proposal and row
check, but no assistant session starts. Sheets also present in the earlier file but deliberately
left out by the profile do not prevent reuse. A new sheet needs the assistant to review it. After the earlier task and its file expire,
a sheet the profile left out can also require a new session because that comparison is no
longer available. A saved layout can ask its unresolved file-value questions again on each repeat.
If **The saved layout does not fit this file** appears, **Read it with the assistant** starts
a session on that task and file. The saved-layout check also offers **Back to the proposal**
and a correction box. See [Load the next version of a workbook](/docs/guide/use/load-the-next-version-of-a-workbook/).

## A model change that moves records

The workspace menu's **Change this model…** asks what should change, with an optional workbook.
It additionally needs **Model authoring** and **Model release**. The proposal says what becomes
what and shows existing record counts. Review the model in the
[model editor](/docs/model/the-model-editor/) if you need to inspect its structure.
For the model administrator’s full task, follow
[Change a model with the assistant](/docs/guide/model/change-a-model-with-the-assistant/).

For whole types becoming other types, acceptance installs a release but moves no records.
**Preview the migration** opens the migration with the proposed choices. You can go **Back to
the proposal**. A person with Model release confirms it: the records move live with their IDs,
values, relationships and history. There is no change set or its approval step for that migration.
When the request changes only the model and asks nothing of the records (for example, adding views), the task ends the same way with a migration that moves no type: confirming it puts the workspace on the new model and every record stays as it is.

A whole-type move and a partial move need separate tasks.

For part of a type moving, the task normally shows **Three steps are yours**: activate a release
holding old and new types, review and publish the change set under the usual approval rules,
then activate the final release to remove the emptied types. If old types remain in the final
model, it shows **Two steps are yours** instead. The first activation moves no records; publishing
moves them. A remaining record in a type being removed blocks the final activation. Each step
appears when it is ready; someone with Model release performs activation. A large split can be
slow because the records are changed individually. See [Model migrations](/docs/model/migrations/).
If the task expires before the final activation, the installed release remains available under
Settings › Model so an administrator can complete the step.

## Stop, correct or end a task

Follow [Continue or correct an assistant task](/docs/guide/use/continue-an-assistant-task/) for the
buttons. These states need different decisions:

| What you see | How to continue |
| --- | --- |
| Working on it or Loading | **Stop** ends the turn. You can also leave the page while it runs. |
| A stopped correction with an earlier proposal | The last proposal returns with a note. The draft may already contain changes from the stopped turn: inspect it before continuing. Stop does not rewind the draft. |
| A stopped load | The change set being loaded is discarded and its jobs stopped. Return to the accepted proposal and tell the assistant how to continue. |
| The assistant stopped or You stopped the assistant | Read the task's notes. Use the words box, **Try again as it was** or **Go on as it was**, open the draft, or **Discard this task**. Even a session that never started can be tried again with corrected words. |
| The engine could not apply this proposal | Read the reason above the correction box, then tell the assistant what to change. |
| A loaded change set that is wrong | Use **Not what you wanted? Tell the assistant** and **Discard and load again**. Confirmation removes that entire change set, including hand edits. For a workbook load, the same session revises and checks the proposal; review it and choose **Accept and load to change set** before loading again. |
| A load you want to abandon | **Discard the change set** ends the task and removes that prepared work. Live records are unchanged. |
| A refused migration or activation | Read the engine's reason on the task and tell the assistant what to change. |
| Your access no longer permits the next step | The page names the permission needed and lets you copy the task link for a workspace administrator. |
| Published | The task confirms publication and offers **Change this model…** and **Ask about these records…** where your access allows. Start new work to correct published data. |
| Discarded | The session has ended. Use **Start again** in the journey bar or return to the workspace. |
| Expired or unknown task | The page explains it is not kept or does not exist and offers **Go to the workspaces**. |

The newest three task notes are shown; older notes are folded. **Discard this proposal** removes
the proposal and its draft; closing the proposal keeps it for later. Discarding a loaded task
also discards its change set. Unused model releases installed by a session are retired at its
end; releases still in use are kept. Published changes and their assistant origin remain in
[history](/docs/use/history/#work-prepared-by-an-assistant) after the task expires.

A refused workbook batch leaves no record or relationship changes and discards its change set.
Other task paths can leave a prepared change set after failure. If the task says it loaded
changes before stopping and offers **Review the change set**, open it before retrying: a failed
turn does not prove that no proposed work remains. Live is unchanged until publication.
guide/src/content/docs/use/mapping-grids:
---
title: Mapping grids
description: Understand source-to-target mappings, unmapped and ambiguous rows, replacement and removal.
reader: steward
---

Use a mapping grid to connect records on one side of a relationship to records on the other.
One use is connecting codes from another system to the records whose meaning they represent.
The model chooses both sides, their fields and the relationship; neither side has a fixed role
in refiroo. Follow [Map codes between systems](/docs/guide/use/map-codes-between-systems/) for the steps.

## Reading a mapping

Each row identifies a source record, its mapping state and its connected targets. Target chips use the target type’s colour and
show names with identifying fields chosen by the model. Read those fields before deciding that
two similar names mean the same thing.

Select the source record's name to open its record page. Each target chip opens that target's
record page. When editing is permitted, clicking elsewhere on the row opens **Change mapping**,
as do **Map** and **Change**.

The model may also show the name of a source record's nearest parent of a chosen type, even
several levels above it. The column heading is that type's name. Search looks at source names
and the source's displayed attributes, not these parent names.

Drag a column's right edge to change its width. With a keyboard, Tab to the edge and use the
Left or Right arrow key. refiroo remembers widths for this view in your browser on this device.
Rows keep their values on one line; a row with several targets lists them on separate lines.
If a value is cut off, point at the cell or move keyboard focus into it to see the full value
in a box beside the cell. The box usually appears below it and moves above when space is short.

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Unmapped | No target is connected through this view's relationship. |
| Mapped | At least one target is connected. When a row has several, the count says how many. |
| Ambiguous | More than one target is connected, on a view where a source may hold only one. |

A relationship decides what several targets mean. Where a source may hold many targets, such as
the "one" side of a one-to-many relationship, several targets are normal: the row is **Mapped**
with its count, and the view has no **Ambiguous** choice. **Ambiguous** appears only where a
source may hold at most one target, and describes multiple stored connections rather than
uncertainty about a suggested match. Decide whether one or several is correct for the data
before replacing anything. An unmapped row can be intentional.

![A mapping grid showing a source code mapped to two stops, other mapped codes and an unmapped code](/docs/screens/mapping-grid-codes-to-stops.png)

*Above: Codes to stops in Systems, searched for FICTIONAL, shows the invented Regional ticketing
system. T-0300 is Mapped (2), connected to Chur and Chur West; the other mapped codes each show
one stop. T-9999 is deliberately Unmapped, with Map available. This view allows several stops
per code, so its filters are All, Unmapped and Mapped. Select a name in the first column to open
the source record.*

**All**, **Unmapped**, **Mapped** and, where it applies, **Ambiguous** narrow the whole list, together with search.
An empty result says nothing about rows excluded by these conditions. A loading failure is not
an unmapped state; retry the read before editing.

## Choosing or clearing targets

**Map** on an unmapped row and **Change** on a filled row open **Change mapping**. Choosing a
target and saving sets that row's mapping to the chosen target. If several were connected,
the selection replaces them with one; it does not add another target alongside them.

Where offered, **Create new** followed by the target type opens a record creation form.
Creating a target and saving its mapping are distinct steps: review the selected target and
finish **Save mapping**. Cancelling the mapping does not undo a target already created.

**Remove mapping**, where available, clears the connection rather than deleting either record.
A required connection cannot be cleared. Changes are saved together or refused, so an unsuccessful
replacement does not leave a half-changed mapping. See [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/)
for candidate restrictions and number limits.

A mapping grid works with voluntary associations, not parent containment or required ownership.
To create owned related records across columns, use a [relation matrix](/docs/use/relation-matrices/).
To keep several targets, use the record's relationship controls rather than replacing the set
with one selection in the grid.

## Permissions, context and conflicts

Reading needs **Browse**. Saving needs **Edit live** or **Work in change sets** for the relevant
data. Reader can inspect; Contributor can prepare change-set work; Data steward and Data owner
can also edit Live. Scoped grants can restrict the types you change. Publications and retired
workspaces are read-only. See [Record permissions](/docs/use/records/#who-may-read-and-change-records).

In Live, a saved mapping applies immediately. In a change set it remains proposed until publication.
If someone changes the mapping after you read it, **Mapping conflict** shows the current mapping.
Review it before continuing with your selection or cancelling. Publishing also checks intervening
live changes; see [Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/).

The counts and **All**, **Unmapped**, **Mapped** and, where it applies, **Ambiguous** state choices describe the
whole matching list. Use them with search to find work beyond the visible rows. Target chips
preview the connected records so you can inspect identifying fields before replacing them.
An atomic replacement retains the existing relationship's identity and fields. Publishing a
change set refuses mappings that diverged from Live; review the current connections before
preparing another attempt.

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0. See [The example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/)
for sources and fictional additions.*

## More targets and newly created records

**Mapping status** groups **All**, **Unmapped**, **Mapped** and, where it applies, **Ambiguous**. A mapping row
counts eligible sources plus sources already connected, so changing candidate conditions does
not hide existing mappings. **Show all … targets for …** expands a row's remaining targets.

Creating a missing target asks for its application. Parent choices belong to that application;
if no required parent can stand there, creation is refused. Create or select a suitable parent
rather than choosing one from another application. Creating the target selects it in the mapping
form but does not save the mapping: finish **Save mapping** separately.

A replacement keeps the values of connections it retains when no new relationship values are
supplied. Explicit replacement values replace the whole collection of fields, and clearing
all is allowed only if the model accepts it. In the ordinary mapping picker, choosing a target
alone does not clear its existing relationship fields.

## Empty results and an unavailable view

**No results match these filters** means the mapping-state filter has no matching rows.
Choose **All** and clear other conditions to widen the list. **No results match this search**
means the search has no matches; change or clear it. **No … in this workspace yet** names the
source record type when there are no rows and neither a state filter nor search is applied.
Check that you are in the intended workspace and context before adding records.

**This mapping view references an object type that does not exist in the active model.**
means the view cannot be drawn. Reload after a model change. If it persists, give a model
administrator the view name and message so they can correct the model; changing mappings
cannot repair a missing type.

## Targets proposed by AI

**Propose targets** asks the configured AI provider to choose targets for unmapped sources.
It needs **Use AI proposals**, **Work in change sets**, a writable workspace and the send level
values. It is unavailable in a publication. Follow [Propose targets](/docs/guide/use/propose-targets/)
to prepare and review them.

Search and the chosen parent narrow which sources are considered. The provider receives source
and candidate target names and the fields this view shows. Only targets the grid permits are
candidates: all eligible targets when there are at most 100, otherwise each source's 20 closest
by name and searchable fields. Requests normally group 25 sources, or fewer for a small model
context. This shortlist can miss a good target; the proposal is help, not proof of a match.
Requests can cost money and their outcome is kept. See [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/)
for sending, access and retention.

Each accepted answer becomes an ordinary mapping in the chosen change set. Live data stays as
it was. **Proposed** under **Mapping status** shows sources with AI-proposed targets in that
change set. **Proposed by the AI** shows the confidence and reason; on a phone, open **Why?**
to read the reason. Confidence is the provider's estimate, not a guarantee. The operator sets
a minimum confidence, normally 0.5 out of 1; lower answers and invented or missing targets
are left unmapped.

![Proposed mappings in a change set, with suggested target stops and their confidence and reasons](/docs/screens/use-mapping-proposed.png)

Correct a wrong target through **Change** and **Save mapping**, or remove the mapping if allowed.
Changing the target removes its AI mark because the replacement is your choice. Publishing
uses the usual approval and conflict checks. The published relationship's history keeps the
proposal's origin and model, and separately names the person who published it.

The job's result counts **Proposed**, **Left unmapped: no likely target** and **Changed meanwhile,
not touched**. It also reports refused or unanswered rows when present. Concurrently mapped
sources are left alone. Failed calls produce warnings; their rows are not proposed. Earlier
successful batches can remain after a later failure. **Stop** likewise keeps proposals already
written. Inspect the change set before publishing even when the job ended early.
guide/src/content/docs/use/notifications:
---
title: Notification settings
description: Choose immediate email or digests, and manage the workspaces you follow.
reader: steward
---

Keep your inbox in refiroo and choose which notices also reach your email address. Open
**Settings › Notification email**, or **Notification email settings** on the Notifications
page. Follow [Set up email notices](/docs/guide/use/set-up-email-notices/) for the steps.
For the notices themselves, see [Inbox and approvals](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/).

## Email is your choice

**Email me when something arrives in my inbox** is off until you enable it. The page shows
the destination address. Under **How each kind reaches me**, choose **At once**, **Digest**
or **Off** for approval requests, decisions on your requests, jobs and other offered kinds.
These choices change only email: your inbox keeps every notice. Choices save as you make them;
read any error before assuming the new choice was stored.

If mail has not been configured or your account has no address, a sentence explains why no
email choice is offered. Ask an administrator about the missing setup or address. If email was
already on, the switch can remain visible so you can turn it off after mail becomes unavailable.
Email is for people's accounts, not clients used by other systems.

![Notification email for an account without an email address or followed workspaces](/docs/screens/notification-email-digest.png)

*Above: the reference account has no email address, so no email delivery choices are offered.
Its followed-workspaces list is also empty.*

**At once** sends an eligible unread notice once, provided it arrived since enabling email
and is less than 24 hours old. Previously read notices and notices from before enabling email
are not sent. Turning email off leaves inbox notices intact.

## A digest instead of separate messages

Choosing **Digest** for the first kind starts a daily schedule in your browser's time zone.
Under **The digest**, choose **Every morning at 07:00** or **Mondays at 07:00**. The page shows
the saved time zone and **Next digest**. There is no choice of another hour or an evening digest.
Enabling email recalculates its next time; changing the frequency or time zone moves it.
Saving the same schedule preserves its next time. With email off or no schedule, no next time
is shown. The browser supplies the time zone when you choose the schedule.

![Enabled notification email with delivery choices, digest frequency, time zone and next digest](/docs/screens/use-notification-email-digest-settings.png)

A digest counts all eligible unread, unhandled notices since email was enabled and lists the
newest 50, with links to the rest. Unlike immediate mail, it has no 24-hour cutoff. Job entries
can include applied and rejected counts while their results remain retained. Notices already
read or handled are omitted; nothing eligible means no message. A notice included in a digest
is not mailed again as a new digest entry.

Email uses fixed wording, kinds, times, counts and links. It contains no record, change-set,
workspace, person or file names. Digests do not require AI. If settings are refused, the prior
preferences remain; retry after checking the shown reason.

## Follow publication in a workspace

**Follow** on a workspace's Home card opts you into notices when someone else publishes a
change set there. Your own publication does not create a follower notice for you.
**Workspaces I follow** lists your choices with **Stop following**. Following requires Browse
and starts off. Selecting Follow again does not create duplicate subscriptions.

Losing Browse or deactivation stops notices while retaining your follow choice. Notices can
resume when access returns. Stop following to remove that choice deliberately. Following is
independent of whether email is available; its notices still appear in the inbox.
See [Follow a workspace](/docs/guide/use/follow-a-workspace/).

There is no browser view of a sent digest. Read the message in the receiving mailbox;
use **Notification email** to check its saved delivery choices and schedule.

## When email does not arrive

An unread notice alone is not enough: email must be enabled, the account active, a destination
address present and the instance able to send mail. A digest also needs a schedule and at
least one kind assigned to it. Choosing the first Digest kind saves a daily schedule with
your browser's time zone automatically. If that save is refused, your old choices remain;
read the error and retry rather than expecting a partly saved schedule.

Nothing eligible means no digest message. Check the inbox first: reading or handling a notice
can remove it from the next message. Turning a kind **Off** affects email only. There is no
interface-language or general account-locale chooser here; the digest time zone is a separate
schedule choice, not a language preference.

The unavailable-email messages are **Email is not set up for this installation, so there is
nothing to choose here.** and **Your account has no email address, so there is nothing to
choose here.** Neither means notifications are lost. Read them in **Notifications** and ask
an administrator to set up mail or correct your account's address.
---
title: Publications
description: Read saved workspace snapshots and understand Current and Withdrawn.
reader: steward
---

A **publication** keeps a workspace's records as they were after a successful publish. Open one
to read a saved result without changing Live. Follow
[Browse a publication](/docs/guide/use/browse-a-publication/) for the steps.

## What a publication keeps

Publishing a [change set](/docs/use/change-sets/) applies its authored changes over current live
data and creates a read-only snapshot. The snapshot retains the model release used for publication,
including the definitions and views for reading it. Later live corrections or model changes do
not rewrite its records. A publication is not an editable copy or a list of every earlier edit;
[History](/docs/use/history/) answers who changed what.

![Publications with a numbered snapshot, its model release, publisher and Current badge](/docs/screens/use-pub-list.png)

*Above: Publication 1 was created after Guide Admin published the correction to Thusis Süd.*

The **Publications** list is newest first. Each entry names its number within the workspace,
model version, publication time and publisher, along with:

- **Publication ID**, its stable identifier.
- **Started from**, the earlier publication the change set used, or Current live data.
- **Replaced as current**, the previous current publication, or No earlier publication.

Choose **Load older publications** when offered to read further back. **No publications yet**
means nothing has been published there; live data can still exist. A loading error needs a retry.

## Reading and status

**Open publication** opens the snapshot. Its purple banner names the publication and says it is
read-only. Search, filters and the views declared in that model help you inspect it. Editing
controls are unavailable. **Back to publications** returns to the list; **Live** returns to current data.
You need Browse access to the workspace to read its publications.

![A read-only publication searched for one record](/docs/screens/use-pub-snapshot.png)

*Above: Publication 1 shows Thusis Süd with Abbreviation THSD. The banner identifies the saved
model release and the read-only context.*

**Current** marks the designated publication. A newer publication replaces that designation;
older snapshots remain readable. Current does not mean that later direct live edits are included.
**Withdrawn** means an authorised person withdrew the current designation. Withdrawal keeps the
snapshot and Live unchanged and leaves no publication current; it does not select an older one.
With Publish permission, **Withdraw publication** is on the current publication's menu and asks
for confirmation.

## Starting work from a snapshot

With Work in change sets permission, the publication menu offers **Start a change set from this
publication**. Give it a **Change set name**, then choose **Create change set**. The result is editable
and keeps the snapshot's model release. This does not restore Live: only changes you deliberately
author can be published later. If its model differs from the workspace's current model, resolve
that difference before publishing. See [Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) and
[Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/).

For the actions on a saved snapshot, follow
[Start from an earlier publication](/docs/guide/use/start-from-an-earlier-publication/) or
[Withdraw a publication](/docs/guide/use/withdraw-a-publication/). Export is available where jobs
are enabled; Import and editing controls are absent. Snapshot pages do not show a Live History
panel. Reading the snapshot stays under its saved model even after later activations.
guide/src/content/docs/use/records.md:
---
title: Records
description: Understand records, their fields and relationships, validity, versions, history and access.
reader: steward
---

A record is one item of reference data: something your organisation names, describes and connects
to other items. Its record type defines the fields it holds, the relationships it may have and
where it belongs. The model defines these types; your records are the data kept using them.

For the steps to locate and inspect one, see [Find records](/docs/guide/use/find-records/).

For choosing the dataset and view, see [Workspaces](/docs/use/workspaces/) and [Applications](/docs/use/applications/).
For connected records and placement, see [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/) and
[Hierarchies](/docs/use/hierarchies/). For coverage across records, see
[Relation matrices](/docs/use/relation-matrices/) and [Fill in a relation matrix](/docs/guide/use/fill-in-a-relation-matrix/).


## Workspaces, applications and types

A **workspace** holds a set of reference data under a model release. An **application** groups
the types and views you work with. A **record type** defines one kind of item. The applications,
types and labels you see depend on your workspace's model.

A record belongs to a workspace and an application, and has a record type. A relationship may
connect it to a record in another application within the same workspace, where the model allows
that connection. Being in different applications does not make the records separate copies.

The workspace selector identifies the data you are working on. The context above the records
identifies **Live**, a **Change set**, or a publication. Live shows current data; a change set
holds proposed changes; a publication shows a saved, read-only snapshot. The same record can
therefore look different in these contexts. See [Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) for how
they fit together.

![Home showing a workspace card with three applications](/docs/screens/home.png)

*Above: the Graubünden workspace offers Network, Systems and Names. These are applications in
the example model; other models can define different applications and record types.*

## What a record holds

A record has a stable **ID** as well as its displayed name. Renaming it keeps its identity,
relationships and place in the hierarchy. Its ID is separate from a business code stored in a
field: changing a code does not create a different record.

**Fields** hold typed values, such as text, numbers, dates and Yes/No values. Zero and No are
values, rather than empty fields. Depending on the model, a field may be required, read-only,
unique, or limited to a range. A save that breaks a rule is refused with a reason. A blank optional
field means that no value has been set.

A model can hide a field from record forms and the fields panel. A hidden field is absent,
rather than an empty field you should fill. Hiding it does not delete its stored value.
Ask the model administrator if information needed for your task is missing. Read any help
text below a form field: it explains that field's use. The model can give a field different
help for different record types. Read-only fields can be shown but cannot be changed.

The model also chooses how the record's page presents it. Fields may appear in the heading or
in a details panel; other panels show children, relationships and history. For ways to edit a
single value or several fields together, see [Correct a record](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/).

![A record page with a heading, hierarchy path, fields and relationship tables](/docs/screens/stop-details.png)

*Above: Chur Wiesental is a Stop in the Network application of the Graubünden workspace.
Stop details holds its number, abbreviation and other fields; Modes and Operator show connected
records. This earlier view shows the ID and version directly in the heading; open **Details**
in the current header to see them.*

## Relationships and a place in the hierarchy

A **relationship** is a named connection between records. The model defines its meaning in each
direction, which types it connects, whether it is required and how many connections are allowed.
A connection can carry fields of its own. A relationship table shows connected records using
the fields and labels chosen by the model. In the Relationships panel, the connection's own
values follow the related record's columns. **Display** lists them under **Attributes of the
relationship**. They cannot be used to sort this panel; see [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/).

A **parent** gives a record its place in a hierarchy. Some types can stand at the top; others
need a parent of an allowed type. The line above a record’s title starts with **←** and the list’s name when you opened it from
a list, followed by its ancestors where the model shows them. Choose the list’s name to return. A parent is
more than an ordinary connection: changing it moves the record in the hierarchy and keeps the
parent connection consistent. An invalid parent or a move that creates a cycle is refused.

Relationships can express ownership or an association with an independent record. This matters
when deleting: a record that belongs to an owner can be removed with it, while an independent
record remains. The deletion section below explains the distinction.

See [Find records](/docs/guide/use/find-records/#inspect-the-record) for inspecting these panels, and
[Correct a record](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/#change-several-fields-together) for the form
that includes **Parent**. The model determines which parents and related records are available.

## Records that belong to another record

A model can define records that belong to an owner through a required relationship. Each owned
record has its own fields, identity, version and history. Its owner can be in another application
in the same workspace. This is a general relationship rule, not a feature tied to one domain.

A relationship panel on the owner's page lists the connected records. **No relationships yet**
means none are connected there. A [relation matrix](/docs/use/relation-matrices/) can compare
owners against column records and show their owned records in the cells, where the model declares
that view. Follow [Create an owned related record](/docs/guide/use/relate-records/#create-an-owned-related-record)
or [Fill in a relation matrix](/docs/guide/use/fill-in-a-relation-matrix/) for the steps.

![A record's related-record sections, one populated and one empty](/docs/screens/stop-relationships.png)

*Above: Chur Wiesental has two System codes and no Name translations. Regional ticketing
(FICTIONAL) is an invented example system; the other code belongs to Wikidata: stations.*

See [Translations as an example](/docs/examples/translations/) for one configuration of owned
records and a relation matrix. Languages, names and the rules connecting them come from that model.

## Validity periods

A record type can define a validity period using two date fields. The start is the first valid
date, including that day. The end is the first date on which the record is no longer valid,
excluding that day. An empty start leaves the beginning open; an empty end leaves the end open.
When both dates are set, the end must be later than the start.

For example, a stop with **Valid from** set to 1 April 2021 and **Valid to (exclusive)** set to
13 December 2026 is valid from 1 April 2021 through 12 December 2026. Those are the example
model's labels; other types can use different labels or have no validity period.

Validity describes the data's business dates. Setting an end date keeps the record, its identity
and its history. It does not delete the record or schedule a change set to publish on that date.
See [Correct a record](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/) for editing a date and
[Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) for coordinating
several date changes.

## Versions and refused saves

The version under **Details** in a record’s header protects it from being overwritten by an older edit.
When you save, refiroo checks the version you read. If someone else saved a change first, your
save is refused, even if you changed a different field on the same record. Their saved change
remains in place.

The field editor keeps your attempted value and shows **Current saved value** alongside the
refusal. Review the refreshed record before deciding whether to save again or cancel. Another
change before the next save can cause another refusal. Follow
[If someone else changed it first](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/#if-someone-else-changed-it-first)
for the recovery steps.

![An Abbreviation edit refused because the record changed in another session](/docs/screens/save-conflict.png)

*Above: another session changed Chur Depot Sand's Designation before this Abbreviation save.
The editor preserves the attempted abbreviation, shows the current saved value and reports
“The value was not saved” and “Object version has changed”.*

A record version is different from a model release, which defines the data's structure, and from
a publication number, which identifies a workspace snapshot. Work in a shared change set is also
protected by the change set's version; a colleague's intervening change can require a refresh.

## History

**History** shows what changed, who changed it and when, newest first. Expand an entry to read
its details. See [History](/docs/use/history/) for record events and activity across records,
and [See who changed what](/docs/guide/use/see-who-changed-what/) for the steps and filters.

## Deleting a record

**Delete record** on the record menu requests permanent removal. The confirmation describes what
is being removed. If there are dependent records or relationships, refiroo shows their impact
before the additional confirmation:

- Descendants in the hierarchy are removed with their parent.
- Records owned through required relationships are removed with their owner, including dependants
  in another application. Their dependants are included too.
- Relationships to independent records are removed, but those records and their hierarchies remain.

The impact lists affected records and relationships and gives their counts. Cancelling leaves
everything in place. If the record or the impact changes before confirmation, deletion is refused;
**Retry** obtains the current record so the deletion can be reviewed again. A required connection
cannot simply be removed on its own while leaving a dependant without its owner.

In Live, deletion takes effect immediately. In a change set, it remains a proposed deletion until
publication. Existing publications retain their snapshots. Ending a validity period is different
from deleting a record.

See [Correct a record](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/) for the record menu and editing context, and
[Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) for applying
proposed removals together.

## Who may read and change records

Access comes from roles granted to you directly or through a group. A grant covers a workspace,
or the whole installation. The relevant permissions are **Browse**, **Edit live** and
**Work in change sets**.

| Predefined role | Read records and history | Create, change and delete in Live | Create, change and delete in change sets |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reader | Yes | No | No |
| Contributor | Yes | No | Yes |
| Data steward | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Data owner | Yes | Yes | Yes |

An administrator can also define custom roles. Write permissions may be limited to particular
applications or record types. A deletion must be allowed for the dependent types it removes too.
**Browse** covers the workspace's data as a whole; it is not narrowed to selected types.
An administrator role alone does not give permission to read or edit reference data.

Your available controls reflect your access. Publications are always read-only, and a retired
workspace remains readable but refuses changes. The workspace's publication approval policy
does not by itself require approval for a direct live correction. See
[Correct a record](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/) for direct work and
[Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/#who-may-do-what) for publication permissions.

A narrowed grant permits a relationship change when you may write either connected record.
It does not permit changing unrelated records of a type outside your grant. A bulk load
refuses individual out-of-scope items; publishing a change set containing out-of-scope changes
refuses the publication as a whole. Check the proposal's types before asking someone to publish.

## Edit a value or create a record

Fields can hold text, long text, whole numbers, decimal numbers, Yes/No, dates, dates with times
or structured values. The model may require a value, limit a number's range, require at least
one of several fields, or require a unique value across the workspace. Separate relationship
rules can limit counting records beneath an ancestor; see [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/).
A missing value is different from No, zero or a deliberately stored empty value.

Click a value on the record page, or focus it and press Enter, to open its editor. Selecting
text to copy does not start an edit. Choose **Save** or press Enter to save where offered;
Escape cancels. Click an empty field to add a value. An optional value's trash button asks for
confirmation before clearing it. Read-only fields have no editing control.

The header's title and subtitle edit the same way. An empty subtitle offers **Add**.
Open **Details** in the header for the record’s ID, its copy button and version.
**Copy ID** is also in the record’s **⋯** menu. Use **Edit record** in the **⋯** menu
for the form containing all fields. A new record form saves its fields, allowed parent and
required relationships together: complete all required choices before choosing **Create**.
A refusal leaves the invalid record uncreated; correct the named field or connection.

In a table, use the cell's pencil to edit without opening the record. Optional values and
single relationships can have a trash button. These icons appear on hover and stay visible
on touch screens; the row's menu is the keyboard alternative. Clicking the value elsewhere
still opens the record. A success notice says whether you saved in Live or the open change set.
Ancestor fields, containment, owned relationships, computed fields and publications have no
cell editing icons. Relationship rows use tooltip-labelled icons for changing the other record,
editing the connection's fields or deleting it; a lock explains a required or parent-managed row.

There is no business-date filter in the browser. Validity fields describe business dates;
searching today's lists does not automatically select the records valid on another day.

## Propose instead of editing Live

A Contributor sees **Propose a change** on a record and **Propose a new …** on a collection.
The first use asks for a change-set name, then opens your proposal for editing. Later uses
continue your newest change set. The band names it, its change count and state. Open **Details**
for who started it, when, its version and model.
A Reader's band says **You can read this workspace** and whom to ask. With narrowed write
permissions, controls appear only on the allowed record types and the Live band names those types.

For several records, permitted collections offer selection and **Change values**,
**Change relationships** and **Delete** with a preview before applying. Deletion previews count
children and owned dependants by type, relationships removed and those reaching records that
stay. Review these separately from the number of selected records.

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0.*

## Clearing, uniqueness and related cells

Required fields need non-empty values; empty text does not meet the requirement. A model's
default fills a missing value on creation, rather than replacing an existing value on every
save. Workspace-wide uniqueness prevents two records holding the same nonempty unique value;
missing values and empty text do not reserve one. A conditional relationship rule can further
limit which records count within an ancestor; see [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/).

To clear an optional field, confirm **Remove value** in **Remove …?**. It makes the value unset
and keeps the record. If **Value removed; refresh needed** appears, removal succeeded but the
screen could not refresh. Choose **Retry refresh** and inspect the saved state before trying
another edit.

A multi-record relationship cell opens a checklist and saves additions and removals together.
See [Replace a record’s related records](/docs/guide/use/replace-a-records-related-records/).
For full workflows, use [Add a record](/docs/guide/use/add-a-record/),
[Delete a record](/docs/guide/use/delete-a-record/),
[Stop offering a value](/docs/guide/use/stop-offering-a-value/) or
[Propose a change](/docs/guide/use/propose-a-change/). For bulk policy and results, see
[Changing many records](/docs/use/changing-many-records/).

## When a record cannot open

**Object unavailable** is a failed read, not an empty record. Read its reason and choose
**Retry**, or **Back to list** to inspect another result. A record belonging to another
application follows that application's route where the model allows it. A record belonging
to another workspace cannot be read by silently substituting the workspace you have open.
Check the workspace and original address with its sender.

Read-only fields cannot be supplied on creation, changed later or cleared by an ordinary
edit. If a type requires **at least one of** several fields, keep one filled when changing
or removing another. For a related-record cell, a single-valued relationship opens its picker;
a many-valued one opens the complete checked set and saves its additions and removals together.
Computed fields, ancestor values, parent containment, ownership-managed connections and
publication cells have no ordinary table edit controls.

Different records' business validity periods may overlap. Ending a period does not turn the
ordinary list into a view of another date. Use **Valid on** when
[exporting a file](/docs/guide/use/export-records/) to request that business-date selection.
There is no record restore from History: review and save a new correction instead.
guide/src/content/docs/use/relation-matr:
---
title: Relation matrices
description: Compare related records across columns, understand cell states and find missing connections.
reader: steward
---

Use a relation matrix to compare many records against another set of records and see where
connections exist or are missing. For the steps to filter, create and correct cell records,
see [Fill in a relation matrix](/docs/guide/use/fill-in-a-relation-matrix/).

## Rows, columns and the records in a cell

The model defines the row type, the column type and the relationship being read. Each cell
shows the row's related records that sit under that column record in their hierarchy, possibly
several levels below it. A chip shows the first of the view's chosen cell fields holding text or a number, or the related
record's name when none does.

A language can be a column, but so can a system or another model-defined type. A matrix does
not automatically translate anything or create missing records.

Drag the right edge of the row-heading column or any record column to change its width.
With a keyboard, Tab to the edge and use the Left or Right arrow key. refiroo remembers these
widths for this view in your browser on this device. If a cell value is cut off, point at the
cell or move keyboard focus into it to read the full value in a box. The box usually appears
below the cell, or above it when space is short. Opening the cell still opens its usual dialog.

On a narrow screen, the matrix keeps all the columns currently shown. Scroll sideways to reach
those outside the screen; use the column chooser to work with a smaller selection.

![A matrix comparing operators against languages, with filled and missing cells](/docs/screens/matrix-operator-names.png)

*Above: Operator names in Names compares operators against five languages. French and German
cells contain related name records; many English, Italian and Romansh cells are None.*

![A matrix comparing municipalities against systems instead of languages](/docs/screens/matrix-municipalities-by-system.png)

*Above: Municipalities by system in Systems uses systems as columns and System codes as the
related records. This is the same view kind with a different configuration.*

## Cell states

Read the legend above the table. A model may define a condition for a related record to count,
such as a Yes/No field. This condition is separate from a record's validity dates unless the
model's rules make that connection. Not all states apply to every configuration.

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| One | Exactly one related record counts in this cell. |
| Several | More than one related record counts. This may be allowed. |
| Inactive | Related records exist, but none meets the condition for counting. This state applies when the relationship defines such a condition. |
| History only | No related record is present now, but an earlier publication held one. |
| None | No related record is present and the cell has no earlier-publication record to show. |
| Conflict | More than one record counts where the model permits only one. Inspect and resolve the extra counting records. |

Live writes refuse a second counting record where only one is allowed. A change set can
hold two before validation: the cell then shows **Conflict** with its count. Resolve the
extra counting record or connection and validate again before publishing. This state comes
from the relationship's one-per-column counting rule. A relationship cardinality limit also
restricts creation, but does not by itself give the cell a **Conflict** label.

**One** does not prove that every field is complete or that its content is correct. **None**
does not mean an existing record merely has an empty text field. **History only** refers to an
earlier publication, rather than every past edit in a record's history. Historical content in
a cell is read-only; where offered, **Create from this** uses it to prepare a new record.

## Filters and coverage

Search narrows the rows. **Filter** offers **Cell state** and a column chooser named after the
column type, followed by **to show**. A state filter finds rows with that state in at least one
chosen column across the whole list, including rows not yet scrolled into view.

By default, the matrix includes all records of its column type, even those that do not concern
the rows you are working on. Use the column chooser on its own, with **Any state**, to show only
the columns you need; **Show all** followed by the column type's plural name clears that selection.

The choice belongs to the page you have open, not to the view's saved settings, and does not
change what other people see. The page's address keeps the chosen columns and cell state, so a
bookmark or shared link opens the same selection. Opening the view again from the navigation
clears that selection; **Hide empty columns** may still leave columns out.

**Hide empty columns**, beside **Filter**, leaves out columns with no related record in any row
left by the current search and scope. A scope limits the rows to those under one record. The check
includes all those rows, not just the ones on screen. The column navigation skips empty columns,
so they do not take up places on each page of columns.

The switch is off by default. Like column widths, its setting is remembered for this view in
this browser on this device, including after a reload. Another device starts with it off.
In a change set or publication, it checks that change set's or publication's own records.

![A matrix with Hide empty columns on: only the French and German columns remain and a line says three empty columns are hidden, with Show all](/docs/screens/matrix-hide-empty-columns.png)

When columns are left out, a line below the toolbar says **N empty columns hidden**, or
**1 empty column hidden** for one. **Show all** on this line turns the switch off.
If you have chosen columns in **Filter**, those columns are shown regardless of the switch.
The switch then says **No effect while columns are chosen in Filter**. Its setting is kept
and takes effect again when you clear the column selection.

![The same matrix with the English column chosen in Filter: the switch stays on and says it has no effect while columns are chosen](/docs/screens/matrix-hide-empty-columns-chosen.png)

Choose the columns before interpreting results for cells in state **None**. If no columns were explicitly selected,
choosing a state uses the columns currently shown. A result with no matching rows means no
matches for that search, state and column selection; it does not prove coverage in omitted columns.
**Any state** removes the state restriction. Clearing the column selection also clears the state
restriction. Up to 20 selected columns can be shown at once; unselected columns can be browsed
with the column navigation when available.

![The matrix Filter panel showing cell states and a searchable column chooser](/docs/screens/matrix-filter-panel.png)

*Above: Municipality names offers Languages to show. Its legend defines counting as Active is
Yes. The same state filter can be used with columns representing systems.*

## What you can change from a cell

The model chooses the available actions: create a related record, edit its displayed fields,
link an existing record, or unlink it. Opening a populated cell shows a table, even when it
contains only one record. Each row identifies a linked record. Its displayed fields come first,
then a tinted **Attributes of the relationship** group holds values of its connection to the
matrix row. This separates a record's content from facts about the connection.

Use the filter box to find a row by its record name or displayed record fields. It does not
search the relationship's values. **Open** leads to the record's full page. **Unlink** asks
within that row: **Keep** cancels; **Unlink** removes only the connection. A required owner
connection cannot be removed on its own.

Where editing is permitted, change a value where it stands. A Yes or no checkbox saves with
one click. Other fields open a small editor over the cell, keeping the table in place. Enter
submits an ordinary single-line value; Escape cancels. A click outside closes an unchanged
record-field editor. Relationship-value editors also attempt a save when focus leaves them.
Review any error before closing. A save refreshes the cell and leaves the table open.

![A populated matrix cell with record fields, tinted relationship values and a small editor open](/docs/screens/matrix-cell-relationship-table-editor.png)

*Above: Municipalities by system in the Graubünden workspace. The Schmitten (GR) cell under
wikidata-municipalities contains one System code, Q65399. Confirmed is ticked, and the Note
editor is open over “Merged municipality, old code kept”. Open and Unlink belong to that row.*

A populated cell offers **Create** beside **Link existing** when the view permits those
actions and the cell may hold several records. A filled cell does not offer Create when
uniqueness is scoped to the column type, or the relationship lets the row connect to only one
record. That includes one-to-one, many-to-one read from its source, and one-to-many read from
its target. Empty, inactive and history-only cells can still offer creation.

An empty cell explains which row and column have no related record and offers **Link existing**
or **Create** where permitted. A read-only cell keeps the table for inspection without editing.
Historical content names its publication and remains read-only.

Creation fixes the row and column and asks where under the column the new record belongs.
Only places where the new record can meet the relationship's rules are offered. If the rules
identify a single group and it is missing, saving creates it with the record. Otherwise the
group already holding the most records used by this view in the column is selected; a tie
leaves no selection. A group holding none is never selected automatically, even as the only one.

If neither rules nor data give a place, refiroo can propose a new group using the type and
name of groups this view uses in other columns. The proposed name is editable and an existing
group can be chosen instead. Saving creates the group and record together. This uses the
current model; no model change is needed. A proposal is offered only where the structure,
required fields and relationship rules allow it. If no suitable place is found, choose or
prepare one in the app. See
[When a new group is proposed](/docs/guide/use/fill-in-a-relation-matrix/#when-a-new-group-is-proposed). The created record is listed in its container too.
The record and its connection are created together. Both Create and Link existing include **Attributes of the
relationship** when the pair carries values: fill these for the new connection, separately
from the record's fields. Linking instead uses an existing candidate. Where the relationship permits it, the same
record can be linked under several rows: these are separate connections to one shared record,
not copies. Disabled candidates explain why they cannot be linked. Unlinking keeps
the record, but cannot leave an owned record without a required owner.

For an inactive cell, inspect existing records before creating another. For a conflict, review
which records should count; do not assume several records are always wrong. All saves must satisfy
the model's rules, including any limit of one counting record per row and column. A refusal
explains that the row already has a record here and **only one may count**. Where offered,
**Open the … already here** takes you to that record; inspect it before creating another.

For example, a translation matrix can create a missing name under a language and allow only
one counting name for each row and language. A mapping matrix can instead reuse a code already
linked under another row, or create a separate code. These choices come from the model's
relationships and view actions. Connected systems see the new record and connection after
publication where their access exposes them. Reuse retains the record's identity under every
row; unlink removes a connection while leaving that record available elsewhere.

To work on the cells outside the browser, see
[Export records](/docs/guide/use/export-records/). The main matrix sheet loads only its cells;
clearing a cell does not remove its contents in refiroo. In a record-field workbook, cells
holding several records are skipped. A link workbook has value sheets for editing individual
records and loads non-empty lists of connections. See
[Matrix cells and new records](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/#matrix-cells-and-new-records).

## Who may edit, and refused saves

**Browse** allows reading. **Edit live** or **Work in change sets** allows the corresponding
writes, subject to scoped grants and the actions configured for the view. A read-only cell may
therefore still be readable on a record's page. See
[Record permissions](/docs/use/records/#who-may-read-and-change-records).
Publications and retired workspaces cannot be edited.

Successful Live saves apply immediately; change-set saves remain proposed. A duplicate refusal
can offer **Open the … already here** to inspect the existing record. **Changed elsewhere**
means the cell has been refreshed after another change: review it and your preserved input before
retrying. If that record is no longer in the cell, the dialog returns to its current contents.
A load error does not mean the cell is empty; retry the read.

See [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/) for ownership and candidates and
[Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) for reviewing and publishing proposed work.

A model administrator adds the matrix to the applications that need it. Its row, column and
cell types must be listed there; the records themselves remain in their own applications.
Showing a matrix does not move or duplicate them. A table in another application can therefore
list fewer records than the matrix reads through its relationships.

To restore an inactive cell, inspect the existing record and change the field that determines
whether it counts. For a history-only cell, **Create from this**, where offered, prepares a new
record from historical content; it does not edit the earlier publication. Check the new values
and required connections before saving. Use **Link existing** for a record already present,
and unlink only when the relationship's rules permit it.

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0. See [The example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/)
for sources and fictional additions.*

## Cell previews and editing details

A cell reports its full count but previews at most five records. Open the row's record to
inspect the complete relationship list. Conditions on the target end produce **Inactive** and
uniqueness **Conflict** states only when reading the relationship in its outgoing direction;
an incoming matrix does not apply those target-end states.

Focus a cell and press Enter or Space, or click it, to open its actions. The table offers inline value edits and row actions **Unlink** and **Open**; **Create …**,
**Link existing …** and **Create from this** appear where applicable.
When choosing a container, **Goes in** offers **Search places…**. Link or move choices can stay
visible but disabled with a reason such as **Already linked** or a cardinality limit.
**Does not count** identifies a candidate outside the cell's counting condition.

A conflict can say **Changed elsewhere** or **Not saved**, with a link to the affected record.
If a stale edit finds its record no longer belongs to this cell, the dialog explains and returns
to the cell's current actions. Inspect those before choosing another change. The page address
keeps search, column selection, state and row position. Leaving a dirty form asks whether to
discard unsaved changes; cancel that prompt to keep editing.

## Read the dialog and leave it safely

A conflict cell can show **Conflict (… )** with its count. Open the cell with Enter or Space.
Use **Open** on a row to inspect a record, or **Close** to leave its table. Link candidates can
stay visible but disabled with **Already linked** or a message that the record is already
linked to as many records as allowed. Choose another eligible candidate; searching again
does not remove that limit. **Does not count** identifies a record outside the counting condition.

**Not saved** reports a failed write; **Changed elsewhere** reports a conflict and refreshed
information. Inspect the current record before retrying. **Remove cell state …** and
**Remove chosen columns …** clear those restrictions. If leaving a changed form asks
**Discard your unsaved changes?**, stay to finish or confirm that you want to abandon the input.
The saved address retains matrix columns, state and position, rather than unsaved form values.
guide/src/content/docs/use/relationship-:
---
title: Relationships tables
description: Read and change the values of connections in rows or a grid.
reader: steward
---

Use a relationships table to work on connections between records, including values belonging
to each connection. A model administrator chooses the relationship, its directed pair of record
types, columns and layout. Any application can offer this view when its model declares it.
See [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/) for direction, ownership and allowed choices.

**Reference-data example:** the connection between a stop and an operator carries Local name,
Primary contact and Inspected on. The inspection date describes their connection. Changing it
does not change a date on the stop or the operator. The model chooses these fields.

## One row per relationship

Each row is one existing connection. It shows fields of the from record, fields of the to
record and the selected attributes of the relationship. A record with several connections
appears in several rows. Names open the corresponding records; endpoint columns identify the
records rather than editing them here.

Search narrows connections by their records. The view can offer equality filters on either
record's fields and the relationship's attributes, and sorting by the fields declared for the
view. Choose a sortable heading or **Sort**. A filter's empty choice removes that restriction.
The declared grouping can put rows beneath their from or to record, with a heading and count
of matching relationships. Scroll to continue reading the list; the heading can recur when a
window starts partway through a group.

**Display** chooses columns and the reading size. **Attributes of the relationship** separates
connection values from record fields. An editable relationship value opens its editor in the
cell; Enter submits a single-line value, leaving the editor attempts a save, and Escape cancels.
A Yes or no value saves when changed. A stale save shows the current saved relationship so you
can review it before retrying. Tick existing relationships to set one attribute across them;
see [Change relationship values in bulk](/docs/guide/use/change-relationship-values-in-bulk/#change-ticked-relationships-in-the-rows-layout).

![Relationships in rows with both endpoint fields, carried values and a counted group heading](/docs/screens/relationships-table-rows.png)

*Above: Stops and operators in the Network application of the Graubünden workspace, filtered
to Local name Station office and grouped by operator. Each group shows 5 relationships,
with Stop, Stop number and the relationship values alongside tickboxes.*

## Grid: each from record once

A grid puts each from record in one row. Each shown to record supplies a column group. Under
it are the relationship attributes chosen for this view. A group heading reads the record's
label followed by **n of m linked**, showing how many matching source records are connected
to that column record. These counts cover the filtered result, not just the rows on screen.
Both header rows stay visible while scrolling. Scroll sideways to reach further column groups.

A linked group shows its connection values. An empty value means that connection has no value
for the field; it is different from a hatched **Not linked** group. **+ Link** creates a
connection for that row and column where permitted. Linking still has to meet candidate and
number rules. It does not create either endpoint record.

Edit a linked value where it stands. A Yes or no checkbox saves in one click. Other values open
a small editor over the cell: Enter submits a single-line value, Escape cancels, and leaving
the editor attempts a save. The row refreshes after saving. If another person saved first,
review **Current saved relationship** before retrying; your stale value is not silently applied.

![Relationships grid with two header rows, linked counts and two stops selected](/docs/screens/relationships-grid-two-headers.png)

*Above: Stops by operator in the Graubünden workspace, filtered to Local name Station office.
Bus und Service AG (Chur) and Rhätische Bahn each show 5 of 10 linked. Two stops are ticked,
with 2 selected and Change relationship values in the selection bar. Hatched Not linked cells
include a + Link action; Operators and Display are above the grid.*

## Narrow rows and choose column records

The grid's row toolbar offers the from type's search and filter bar, with the same fields and
operators as that type's main view, plus the view's additional filter fields. Each non-JSON
relationship attribute shown by the view is also offered as a row filter. Such a filter finds
a row when a connection to a shown column record matches. With several relationship conditions,
the same connection must satisfy them together. Hidden column records do not supply a match.
See [Lists, search and filters](/docs/use/lists-and-filters/) for the operators.

Open the menu named after the to type's plural name to choose column records. It offers that
type's own search and filters and a searchable pick list under **… to show**. Choose particular
records or narrow their fields. At most 50 column groups appear at once. When more match, the
notice reports how many are shown out of the total; narrow the column-record filter to reach
the others. **Show all …** clears the column choices and restrictions, within that display limit.

**Display** chooses the from-record fields and the relationship attributes shown under each
column record. The row's name stays visible. Search, filters, column choices and display choices
belong to this page and stay in its address. They do not change the type's main view or another
person's view. Share or bookmark the address to return to those choices.

## Select records and change their connections together

Tick source rows, or select the loaded rows and choose **Select all N matching** when offered.
That includes matching records beyond those on screen; untick exceptions to leave them out.
**Change relationship values** sets or clears one attribute at all shown column records or one
chosen column record. Its preview distinguishes values that would change, values already held
and pairs that are not linked. Adding missing connections is a separate choice.
Follow [Change relationship values in bulk](/docs/guide/use/change-relationship-values-in-bulk/)
before applying a large selection.

## Live, change sets and publications

Live saves take effect immediately. In a change set, the grid marks affected connections as
